lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: uun. oyasumi.
lines.ja: ううん。おやすみ。
lines.kana: ううん。おやすみ。
lines.english: Nah. Night.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki is about to leave for work when Kenji points out that it's Saturday: no school for him, and no work for her.
Kenji is skipping school, so Yuki makes him go before she leaves for work.
Yuki's work finishes early today, so she asks Kenji to go shopping with her after work.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-3: Yuki finds Kenji still at home and thinks he's skipping school. Lines 4-7: she's off to work, it's busy, and she expects to get off around ten. Line 10: kyou, doyoubi da yo (it's Saturday). Line 12: that's why he isn't going to school, and line 14: Mom isn't at work, she's just out shopping. Line 15: so Yuki doesn't have to go to work either (shigoto ikanakute ii n da). B is wrong: Kenji never goes, because there's no school on a Saturday. C is wrong: Yuki has no work at all today; she asks Kenji to go shopping right now (line 17), and he says no and goes back to bed (line 18: uun. oyasumi).

questions.english: When Yuki finds Kenji at home, she tells him "minna mou gakkou itteru yo." Where does she say everyone else is?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、みんなが今どこにいると言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、みんながいまどこにいるといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, minna ga ima doko ni iru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: On their way to school right now.
At home, just about to leave for school.
Already at school.

questions.explanation: Line 3: gakkou itteru is the -teru form of iku, the state after going: they went and are there now, and mou (already) backs that up. A is wrong: on the way would be gakkou iku tochuu (or gakkou ni mukatteru), never itteru. B is wrong: about to leave is plain iku, as in ima kara gakkou iku. The same -teru state comes back in lines 13-14, where Yuki asks if Mom is at work (shigoto itteru n ja nai no?) and Kenji says she's out shopping (kaimono itteru dake). Elsewhere gakkou itteru can also mean 'attends school' (nihongo gakkou itteru: I go to a Japanese school).

questions.english: One weekday morning Kenji sees you heading for the door and asks, "a, mou deru no? doko iku no?" (Oh, you're leaving already? Where are you going?) You're off to work. Tell him.
questions.ja: あ、もう出るの？どこ行くの？
questions.kana: あ、もうでるの？どこいくの？
questions.romaji: a, mou deru no? doko iku no?
questions.answer: Say you're going to work, with shigoto and plain iku: shigoto iku yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: shigoto iku yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 仕事行くよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm going to work.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima kara shigoto itte kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 今から仕事行ってくるね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm off to work now. See you later.

questions.explanation: Heading off is plain iku: shigoto iku yo, the way Kenji asks in line 4 (kyou shigoto iku no?) and Yuki answers in line 5 (iku yo). itte kuru, 'go and come back', is the everyday I'm-off line. Don't say shigoto itteru here: that's the state, already at work, which is how Yuki asks about Mom in line 13 (shigoto itteru n ja nai no?). Casual speech drops ni; politely it's shigoto ni ikimasu.

questions.english: Kenji asks Yuki a 'what time' question about her work. What did he ask?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: What time will you get the job done?
choices.romaji: nanji ni shigoto o owaraseru no?

choices.english: What time do you get off work?
What time do you go to work?

questions.explanation: Line 6: shigoto nanji ni owaru no? For getting off work, the work itself ends: shigoto is the subject of owaru (with ga, dropped in casual speech), even though English says 'you finish'. A is the word-for-word 'you finish work': owaraseru means making something finish, so it's about getting a task done, not clocking off. C asks when she goes in (iku); Yuki is already heading out, and her answer is about the end of her day: juuji kana, kinou mo shigoto, juuji ni owatta shi (line 7).

questions.english: Yuki says to you, "kinou mo kaeri osokatta ne. nande?" (You got home late again yesterday. How come?) It's because work has been busy. Tell her.
questions.ja: 昨日も帰り遅かったね。なんで？
questions.kana: きのうもかえりおそかったね。なんで？
questions.romaji: kinou mo kaeri osokatta ne. nande?
questions.answer: Give work as the reason, with shigoto as the subject of isogashii: shigoto isogashii n da yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: shigoto isogashii n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 仕事忙しいんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: Work's been busy, that's why.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, shigoto ga isogashikute.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、仕事が忙しくて。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, work's just been so busy.

questions.explanation: English says 'I've been busy with work'; Japanese makes the work the subject: shigoto (ga) isogashii, as Yuki says in line 5 (shigoto metcha isogashii no) and Kenji in line 16 (shigoto isogashisugi da yo). The -kute form, shigoto ga isogashikute, trails off as the reason and is the standard excuse. Keep isogashii for people and their work or schedule: a crowded shop is konderu, not isogashii.

newWords.english: sis (what a younger sibling calls a big sister)
tough, rough (taihen da ne = that's rough)
just, only (kaimono itteru dake = she's just out shopping)
too, too much (isogashisugi = way too busy)
say (nan to iimashita ka = what did they say?)

script.title: A present from Tama
script.setting: A Sunday afternoon, the first fine day after three days of rain. Yuki has dropped in on her elderly neighbour, Satou-san, and they're sitting by his open garden doors. His cat, Tama, has been sulking in the corner.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: satou-san, koko, honto ni igokochi ga ii desu ne.
lines.ja: 佐藤さん、ここ、ほんとに居心地がいいですね。
lines.kana: さとうさん、ここ、ほんとにいごこちがいいですね。
lines.english: Satou-san, it's so cosy here.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. kyou wa yatto ame ga yande, kaze ga kimochi ii desu kara ne.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。今日はやっと雨がやんで、風が気持ちいいですからね。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。きょうはやっとあめがやんで、かぜがきもちいいですからね。
lines.english: Thank you. Well, the rain's finally stopped today, and the breeze feels lovely.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, honto ni kimochi ii. kyou wa watashi, kibun ga ii n desu.
lines.ja: ああ、ほんとに気持ちいい。今日は私、気分がいいんです。
lines.kana: ああ、ほんとにきもちいい。きょうはわたし、きぶんがいいんです。
lines.english: Ah, it really does feel nice. I'm in a good mood today.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: watashi mo, kyou wa kibun ga ii desu yo. demo, tama wa zutto kigen ga warui n desu.
lines.ja: 私も、今日は気分がいいですよ。でも、タマはずっと機嫌が悪いんです。
lines.kana: わたしも、きょうはきぶんがいいですよ。でも、たまはずっときげんがわるいんです。
lines.english: Me too, I'm in a good mood today. But Tama's been grumpy the whole time.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, tama-chan, kigen warui no? nande?
lines.ja: え、タマちゃん、機嫌悪いの？なんで？
lines.kana: え、たまちゃん、きげんわるいの？なんで？
lines.english: Oh, Tama-chan, are you in a bad mood? How come?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: mikka mo ame ga futte, zutto soto ni denakatta n desu yo. neko wa ame ga dame desu kara ne.
lines.ja: 三日も雨が降って、ずっと外に出なかったんですよ。猫は雨がだめですからね。
lines.kana: みっかもあめがふって、ずっとそとにでなかったんですよ。ねこはあめがだめですからね。
lines.english: It rained for three days, so she hasn't been outside at all. Cats can't stand the rain, you know.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tama-chan, ame, mou yanda yo. soto, kimochi ii yo.
lines.ja: タマちゃん、雨、もうやんだよ。外、気持ちいいよ。
lines.kana: たまちゃん、あめ、もうやんだよ。そと、きもちいいよ。
lines.english: Tama-chan, the rain's stopped now. It's lovely outside.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, soto ni demashita ne. yatto desu yo.
lines.ja: あ、外に出ましたね。やっとですよ。
lines.kana: あ、そとにでましたね。やっとですよ。
lines.english: Oh, she's gone out. Finally.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: watashi wa, mou chotto koko ni ite ii desu ka? igokochi ga ii node.
lines.ja: 私は、もうちょっとここにいていいですか？居心地がいいので。
lines.kana: わたしは、もうちょっとここにいていいですか？いごこちがいいので。
lines.english: Mind if I stay here a little longer myself? It's so cosy.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: douzo douzo, zutto ite ii desu yo. a, tama, mou modorimashita ne.
lines.ja: どうぞどうぞ、ずっといていいですよ。あ、タマ、もう戻りましたね。
lines.kana: どうぞどうぞ、ずっといていいですよ。あ、たま、もうもどりましたね。
lines.english: Of course, stay as long as you like. Oh, Tama's back already.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tama-chan, nani motteru no? e, mushi? kimochi warui!
lines.ja: タマちゃん、何持ってるの？え、虫？気持ち悪い！
lines.kana: たまちゃん、なにもってるの？え、むし？きもちわるい！
lines.english: Tama-chan, what have you got there? Huh, a bug? Gross!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: tama kara no purezento desu yo. mou kigen ii n desu ne.
lines.ja: タマからのプレゼントですよ。もう機嫌いいんですね。
lines.kana: たまからのぷれぜんとですよ。もうきげんいいんですね。
lines.english: It's a present from Tama. She's in a good mood already, I see.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou, tama-chan. demo, kore wa kimochi warui yo.
lines.ja: ありがとう、タマちゃん。でも、これは気持ち悪いよ。
lines.kana: ありがとう、たまちゃん。でも、これはきもちわるいよ。
lines.english: Thank you, Tama-chan. But this is gross.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sumimasen ne. kimochi warui desu yo ne.
lines.ja: すみませんね。気持ち悪いですよね。
lines.kana: すみませんね。きもちわるいですよね。
lines.english: Sorry about that. It is gross, isn't it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyou wa kibun yokatta noni.
lines.ja: 今日は気分よかったのに。
lines.kana: きょうはきぶんよかったのに。
lines.english: And I was in such a good mood today.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: tama wa, kigen ii n desu kedo ne.
lines.ja: タマは、機嫌いいんですけどね。
lines.kana: たまは、きげんいいんですけどね。
lines.english: Tama's in a fine mood, though.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Tama stays grumpy and won't go outside, even after the rain stops.
Tama goes outside, comes back with a bug for Yuki, and is in a good mood again.
Tama brings Satou-san a bug, and Yuki goes home feeling sick.

questions.explanation: Lines 4-6: Satou-san says Tama has been in a bad mood (kigen ga warui) because it rained for three days and she hasn't been out. Line 7: Yuki tells her the rain has stopped, and in line 8 she goes out. In lines 10-12 she's back with a bug, and Satou-san says it's a present from Tama and that she's in a good mood already (mou kigen ii). A is wrong: Tama goes out as soon as Yuki tells her the rain has stopped (line 8), and she cheers up. C is wrong: the bug is a present for Yuki (lines 11-12), and Yuki doesn't go home. In line 9 she asks to stay longer, and her kimochi warui means 'gross', not 'I feel sick'.

questions.english: It's a warm evening, and you and Kenta are sitting by the river when a breeze picks up. He says, "kaze dete kita ne. daijoubu?" (It's getting breezy. You okay?) Tell him you're fine: it feels nice.
questions.ja: 風出てきたね。大丈夫？
questions.kana: かぜでてきたね。だいじょうぶ？
questions.romaji: kaze dete kita ne. daijoubu?
questions.answer: Say you're fine and the breeze feels nice, with kimochi ii (ga usually drops in casual speech): un, daijoubu. kimochi ii yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daijoubu. kimochi ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大丈夫。気持ちいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm fine. It feels nice.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu. kaze ga kimochi ii ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫。風が気持ちいいね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm fine. The breeze feels lovely, doesn't it?

questions.explanation: kimochi ii is how something feels on your body: a breeze, a bath, a stretch. That's how it's used in lines 2, 3 and 7 (kaze ga kimochi ii, aa, honto ni kimochi ii, soto, kimochi ii yo). Don't say kibun ga ii here: that's your mood, as in lines 3-4. And a nice breeze isn't tanoshii (fun). Kenta is a friend, so answer casually; ne at the end asks him to agree, like the second model answer.

questions.english: Tama comes back carrying something, and Yuki cries, "e, mushi? kimochi warui!" What does she mean?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、なんで気持ち悪いと言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なんできもちわるいといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nande kimochi warui to iimashita ka?

choices.english: She thinks the bug Tama has brought is gross.
She suddenly feels unwell, as if she's coming down with a cold.
She thinks Tama is in a bad mood again.

questions.explanation: Line 11: Yuki says kimochi warui the moment she sees what Tama is carrying (e, mushi? a bug?), so here it means 'Gross!'. She says it again to Tama in line 13 (kore wa kimochi warui yo), and Satou-san agrees in line 14. B is wrong: kimochi warui can also mean queasy, but nothing has made Yuki ill, and for feeling unwell with a cold you'd say guai ga warui. C is wrong: a bad mood that shows is kigen ga warui, and by now Satou-san says the opposite, that Tama is already in a good mood (mou kigen ii, line 12).

questions.english: You've been smiling all afternoon, and Kenta says, "kyou, kigen ii ne. nande?" (You're in a good mood today. How come?) Tell him you're in a good mood, and why.
questions.ja: 今日、機嫌いいね。なんで？
questions.kana: きょう、きげんいいね。なんで？
questions.romaji: kyou, kigen ii ne. nande?
questions.answer: Talk about your own mood with kibun ii (kibun ga ii), not kigen: un, kyou wa kibun ii n da. Then give a reason.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kyou wa kibun ii n da. ame mo yanda shi.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、今日は気分いいんだ。雨もやんだし。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm in a good mood today. The rain's stopped, for one thing.

modelAnswers.romaji: datte, shigoto owatta kara. kibun ii n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: だって、仕事終わったから。気分いいんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: Well, work's done! I'm in a good mood.

questions.explanation: Kenta sees your mood from the outside, so he says kigen ii, the way Satou-san talks about Tama in lines 12 and 16. About your own mood you say kibun ga ii, or kibun ii in casual speech, as Yuki and Satou-san do in lines 3-4 (kyou wa watashi, kibun ga ii n desu); Yuki uses the past in line 15 (kyou wa kibun yokatta noni). Don't say kimochi ii: that's a physical feeling, like the breeze in line 2. n da gives an explanation, which suits a reply to nande.

questions.english: Yuki and Satou-san both say they're in a good mood today. Then Satou-san tells Yuki how Tama has been. What did he say?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Tama's been feeling sick the whole time.
choices.romaji: tama wa zutto kibun ga warui n desu

choices.english: Tama's been queasy (or gross) the whole time.
choices.romaji: tama wa zutto kimochi ga warui n desu

choices.english: Tama's been in a bad mood the whole time.
choices.romaji: tama wa zutto kigen ga warui n desu

questions.explanation: Line 4: 'demo, tama wa zutto kigen ga warui n desu.' A bad mood that others can see, in a person, a child or a cat, is kigen ga warui, and Yuki echoes it to the cat in line 5 (kigen warui no?). In the same line Satou-san uses kibun only for his own mood (kyou wa kibun ga ii desu yo). A is wrong: kibun ga warui is what English speakers tend to say for 'in a bad mood', but it means feeling sick or put off. B is wrong: kimochi ga warui means queasy or gross. It's what Yuki says about the bug (lines 11 and 13), not what Satou-san says about Tama.

questions.english: You've been chatting at Satou-san's house all afternoon. He asks, "mou kaerimasu ka?" (Are you heading home now?) Tell him you'd like to stay a little longer because it's so cosy here.
questions.ja: もう帰りますか？
questions.kana: もうかえりますか？
questions.romaji: mou kaerimasu ka?
questions.answer: Ask to stay a bit longer and give the reason with igokochi ga ii, politely: mou chotto ite ii desu ka? koko, igokochi ga ii node.

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, mou chotto ite ii desu ka? koko, igokochi ga ii node.
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、もうちょっといていいですか？ここ、居心地がいいので。
modelAnswers.english: No, could I stay a little longer? It's so cosy here.

modelAnswers.romaji: mada daijoubu desu. koko, honto ni igokochi ga ii n desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: まだ大丈夫です。ここ、ほんとに居心地がいいんですよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm fine for a while yet. It's really cosy here.

questions.explanation: igokochi ga ii is for a place you feel at ease in, as Yuki says of Satou-san's house in lines 1 and 9 (igokochi ga ii node). Don't reach for kaiteki (comfortable), which is physical comfort and sounds like an advert, or kimochi ii, which is how the breeze feels on your skin. Satou-san is an elderly neighbour and speaks politely, so answer in desu/masu; node gives the reason softly.

newWords.english: Tama, Satou-san's cat (Yuki calls her tama-chan; -chan is a friendly name ending)
say (nan to iimashita ka = what did they say?)

script.title: Too loud to read
script.setting: A rainy Saturday afternoon at the café where Sora works. There are no other customers, so he has been singing behind the counter. Mai, a regular, sits nearby with a book.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora-kun, chotto koe ookii yo. hon yomenai.
lines.ja: ソラくん、ちょっと声大きいよ。本読めない。
lines.kana: そらくん、ちょっとこえおおきいよ。ほんよめない。
lines.english: Sora, you're a bit loud. I can't read.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, gomen! ame futtete hima da kara, uta utatchatta.
lines.ja: あ、ごめん！雨降ってて暇だから、歌うたっちゃった。
lines.kana: あ、ごめん！あめふっててひまだから、うたうたっちゃった。
lines.english: Oh, sorry! It's raining and there's nothing to do, so I got carried away singing.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, ii yo. uta umai ne. nan no uta?
lines.ja: ううん、いいよ。歌うまいね。何の歌？
lines.kana: ううん、いいよ。うたうまいね。なんのうた？
lines.english: No, it's fine. You're a good singer. What's the song?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ima yatteru eiga no uta. kinou mita n da. mai-san wa mou mita?
lines.ja: 今やってる映画の歌。昨日見たんだ。マイさんはもう見た？
lines.kana: いまやってるえいがのうた。きのうみたんだ。まいさんはもうみた？
lines.english: It's from the film that's on right now. I saw it yesterday. Have you seen it yet, Mai?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, eiga wa mada mitenai. demo, kore, ano eiga no hon na no.
lines.ja: ううん、映画はまだ見てない。でも、これ、あの映画の本なの。
lines.kana: ううん、えいがはまだみてない。でも、これ、あのえいがのほんなの。
lines.english: No, I haven't seen the film yet. But this is the book it's based on.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, honto? jaa, hon yonde kara eiga miru no?
lines.ja: え、ほんと？じゃあ、本読んでから映画見るの？
lines.kana: え、ほんと？じゃあ、ほんよんでからえいがみるの？
lines.english: Wait, really? So you'll read the book first, then see the film?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. dakara, nani mo iwanaide ne.
lines.ja: うん。だから、何も言わないでね。
lines.kana: うん。だから、なにもいわないでね。
lines.english: Yep. So don't tell me anything, okay?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, iwanai. a, demo, minna de uta utau no ga metcha ii n da yo!
lines.ja: うん、言わない。あ、でも、みんなで歌うたうのがめっちゃいいんだよ！
lines.kana: うん、いわない。あ、でも、みんなでうたうたうのがめっちゃいいんだよ！
lines.english: Okay, I won't. Oh, but the bit where they all sing together is so good!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mou itteru yo!
lines.ja: もう言ってるよ！
lines.kana: もういってるよ！
lines.english: You're already telling me!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, gomen. mai-san wa? uta utau?
lines.ja: ごめん、ごめん。マイさんは？歌うたう？
lines.kana: ごめん、ごめん。まいさんは？うたうたう？
lines.english: Sorry, sorry. What about you, Mai? Do you sing?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, uta wa chotto. watashi wa e kaku no ga suki.
lines.ja: ううん、歌はちょっと。私は絵描くのが好き。
lines.kana: ううん、うたはちょっと。わたしはえかくのがすき。
lines.english: No, singing's not really my thing. I like drawing.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: honto? e kaku n da! mite ii?
lines.ja: ほんと？絵描くんだ！見ていい？
lines.kana: ほんと？えかくんだ！みていい？
lines.english: Really? You draw! Can I see?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, ii yo. kore.
lines.ja: うん、いいよ。これ。
lines.kana: うん、いいよ。これ。
lines.english: Um, okay. Here.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: waa! kore, boku?
lines.ja: わあ！これ、僕？
lines.kana: わあ！これ、ぼく？
lines.english: Whoa! Is this me?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. uta utatteru sora-kun.
lines.ja: うん。歌うたってるソラくん。
lines.kana: うん。うたうたってるそらくん。
lines.english: Yep. You, singing.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, itsu kaita no?
lines.ja: え、いつ描いたの？
lines.kana: え、いつかいたの？
lines.english: What? When did you draw this?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ima. koe ookikute, hon yomenakatta kara, e kaiteta no.
lines.ja: 今。声大きくて、本読めなかったから、絵描いてたの。
lines.kana: いま。こえおおきくて、ほんよめなかったから、えかいてたの。
lines.english: Just now. You were so loud I couldn't read, so I drew instead.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, gomen. demo, kono e, metcha ii!
lines.ja: あ、ごめん。でも、この絵、めっちゃいい！
lines.kana: あ、ごめん。でも、このえ、めっちゃいい！
lines.english: Oh, sorry. But this picture is amazing!

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora tells Mai how the film ends, so she gives up on the book and starts drawing instead.
Mai has already seen the film, so she sings its song with Sora and then shows him her drawings.
Sora's singing was too loud for Mai to read, so she drew a picture of him singing.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: the café is quiet, so Sora has been singing, and Mai says he is too loud for her to read (hon yomenai). Lines 13-15: she shows him a drawing, and it is him singing (uta utatteru sora-kun). Line 17 says why she drew it: he was so loud she couldn't read, so she drew (koe ookikute, hon yomenakatta kara, e kaiteta no). A is wrong: Sora only lets slip that everyone sings together (line 8), not the ending, and Mai stopped reading because of his singing (line 17). B is wrong: Mai hasn't seen the film (line 5: mada mitenai), and she doesn't sing (line 11: uta wa chotto).

questions.english: Sora says, "ashita mo ame da ne. uchi de nani suru?" (More rain tomorrow, huh. What'll you do at home?) You plan to stay in with a book. Tell him.
questions.ja: 明日も雨だね。うちで何する？
questions.kana: あしたもあめだね。うちでなにする？
questions.romaji: ashita mo ame da ne. uchi de nani suru?
questions.answer: Say you'll read a book, with hon and yomu: uchi de hon yomu yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: uchi de hon yomu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うちで本読むよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'll read a book at home.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita wa uchi de hon o yomimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 明日はうちで本を読みます。
modelAnswers.english: Tomorrow I'll stay home and read a book.

questions.explanation: A book takes yomu, the same verb whether you read silently or aloud. Casual speech drops o, as Mai and Sora do all through the scene: hon yomenai (line 1, I can't read), hon yonde kara (line 6, after reading the book), hon yomenakatta (line 17, I couldn't read). The plain form yomu covers a plan for tomorrow, since Japanese has no separate future tense. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Sora asks Mai if she has seen the film that's on right now. She answers, "uun, eiga wa mada mitenai." What does she mean?
questions.ja: マイさんは映画を見ましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはえいがをみましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa eiga o mimashita ka?

choices.english: She isn't going to watch it; the book is enough for her.
She hasn't seen it yet; she'll watch it once she has read the book.
She saw it last week, and now she's reading the book it came from.

questions.explanation: Line 5: mada mitenai means 'I haven't seen it yet'. The -te nai form with mada says it hasn't happened so far. Line 6 confirms the plan: Sora asks hon yonde kara eiga miru no? (So you'll read the book, then see the film?) and she says un. A is wrong: she does mean to see it, once she's read the book; 'I'm not going to watch it' would be minai. And don't say mada minai for 'I haven't watched it', the usual slip for English speakers: plain -nai with mada is a decision ('I'm not watching it yet'), not a report. C is wrong because Mai says uun (no). Sora is the one who has seen it, yesterday (line 4: kinou mita n da).

questions.english: Mai tells you, "watashi wa e kaku no ga suki. nani suru no ga suki?" (I like drawing. What do you like doing?) You love singing. Tell her.
questions.ja: 私は絵描くのが好き。何するのが好き？
questions.kana: わたしはえかくのがすき。なにするのがすき？
questions.romaji: watashi wa e kaku no ga suki. nani suru no ga suki?
questions.answer: Say you like singing, with uta and utau before no ga suki: uta utau no ga suki.

modelAnswers.romaji: uta utau no ga suki. metcha kimochi ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 歌うたうのが好き。めっちゃ気持ちいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: I like singing. It feels so good.

modelAnswers.romaji: uta o utau no ga suki desu.
modelAnswers.ja: 歌を歌うのが好きです。
modelAnswers.english: I like singing.

questions.explanation: Singing as a pastime is uta o utau. To English ears 'sing a song' sounds doubled, but uta utau is the everyday way to say 'singing'. Add no ga suki to say you like it, the same way Mai says e kaku no ga suki (line 11). Sora uses the same pair: uta utatchatta (line 2), mai-san wa? uta utau? (line 10). When the song is already clear, utau can stand alone, but for singing in general keep uta. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Sora asks Mai if she sings. She says singing isn't really her thing and tells him what she likes instead. What did she say?
questions.ja: マイさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I like drawing.
choices.romaji: watashi wa e kaku no ga suki.

choices.english: I like drawing (with hiku, as in drawing a line).
choices.romaji: watashi wa e hiku no ga suki.

choices.english: I like painting (with nuru, as in painting a wall).
choices.romaji: watashi wa e nuru no ga suki.

questions.explanation: Line 11: a picture takes kaku, whether it is drawn in pencil or painted in colour: e kaku no ga suki. Sora repeats it in line 12 (e kaku n da!), and Mai uses it again in line 17 (e kaiteta no). B carries English 'draw' straight across, but hiku draws a line (sen o hiku), not a picture. C carries over English 'paint', but nuru covers a surface with something, like paint on a wall or butter on toast; it doesn't make a picture. kaku here sounds the same as kaku 'write'. The noun e (picture) tells you which one is meant.

newWords.english: free, with nothing to do (hima da kara = there's nothing going on, so)
good at (uta umai ne = you're a good singer); also tasty
say, tell (nani mo iwanaide = don't tell me anything; mou itteru = you're already telling me)
like, love (e kaku no ga suki = I like drawing)

script.title: Already heard
script.setting: Evening at home. Okaasan gets back late from the shops after a long chat with Satou-san next door, just as Kenji has some news of his own.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: okaasan, kaeri osokatta ne.
lines.ja: お母さん、帰り遅かったね。
lines.kana: おかあさん、かえりおそかったね。
lines.english: Mum, you're back late.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: gomen ne. kaimono no kaeri ni, satou-san to hanashi o shiteta no.
lines.ja: ごめんね。買い物の帰りに、佐藤さんと話をしてたの。
lines.kana: ごめんね。かいもののかえりに、さとうさんとはなしをしてたの。
lines.english: Sorry. On my way back from the shops, I got talking with Satou-san.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: satou-san ka. hanashi nagai yo ne.
lines.ja: 佐藤さんか。話長いよね。
lines.kana: さとうさんか。はなしながいよね。
lines.english: Satou-san, huh. He does go on, doesn't he.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: honto ni ne. ichijikan, zutto hanashi kiiteta no yo.
lines.ja: ほんとにね。一時間、ずっと話聞いてたのよ。
lines.kana: ほんとにね。いちじかん、ずっとはなしきいてたのよ。
lines.english: Tell me about it. I was listening to him for a whole hour.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ichijikan? nan no hanashi shiteta no?
lines.ja: 一時間？何の話してたの？
lines.kana: いちじかん？なんのはなししてたの？
lines.english: An hour? What were you talking about?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: chotto ne.
lines.ja: ちょっとね。
lines.kana: ちょっとね。
lines.english: Oh, this and that.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: fuun. a, okaasan, chotto hanashi ga aru n da kedo.
lines.ja: ふーん。あ、お母さん、ちょっと話があるんだけど。
lines.kana: ふーん。あ、おかあさん、ちょっとはなしがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Huh. Oh, Mum, there's something I need to tell you.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hanashi ga aru tte, nani? nagai hanashi?
lines.ja: 話があるって、何？長い話？
lines.kana: はなしがあるって、なに？ながいはなし？
lines.english: Something to tell me? What is it? Is it a long one?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: uun. boku, satou-san ja nai kara, hanashi nagaku nai yo.
lines.ja: ううん。僕、佐藤さんじゃないから、話長くないよ。
lines.kana: ううん。ぼく、さとうさんじゃないから、はなしながくないよ。
lines.english: Nope. I'm not Satou-san. I don't go on and on.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hai hai. jaa, hanashi kiku yo.
lines.ja: はいはい。じゃあ、話聞くよ。
lines.kana: はいはい。じゃあ、はなしきくよ。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. Go on then, I'm listening.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ano ne, boku, kanojo ga dekita n da.
lines.ja: あのね、僕、彼女ができたんだ。
lines.kana: あのね、ぼく、かのじょができたんだ。
lines.english: So, um... I've got a girlfriend.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: a, sono hanashi, mou kiita yo.
lines.ja: あ、その話、もう聞いたよ。
lines.kana: あ、そのはなし、もうきいたよ。
lines.english: Oh, that. I've already heard.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e? nande?
lines.ja: え？なんで？
lines.kana: え？なんで？
lines.english: What? How?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: satou-san kara. kami ga nagakute, se ga takai ko da yo ne?
lines.ja: 佐藤さんから。髪が長くて、背が高い子だよね？
lines.kana: さとうさんから。かみがながくて、せがたかいこだよね？
lines.english: From Satou-san. Long hair, tall, right?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jaa, ichijikan mo boku no hanashi shiteta no?
lines.ja: じゃあ、一時間も僕の話してたの？
lines.kana: じゃあ、いちじかんもぼくのはなししてたの？
lines.english: Wait, so you spent a whole hour talking about me?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: un. sorede ne, okaasan kara mo hanashi ga aru no.
lines.ja: うん。それでね、お母さんからも話があるの。
lines.kana: うん。それでね、おかあさんからもはなしがあるの。
lines.english: Yep. And so, I've got something to talk to you about too.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ee, nagai hanashi? okaasan, hanashi nagai kara naa.
lines.ja: えー、長い話？お母さん、話長いからなあ。
lines.kana: えー、ながいはなし？おかあさん、はなしながいからなあ。
lines.english: Oh no, is it a long one? You do go on, Mum.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: nagai yo. sono ko no hanashi, zenbu kiku kara ne.
lines.ja: 長いよ。その子の話、全部聞くからね。
lines.kana: ながいよ。そのこのはなし、ぜんぶきくからね。
lines.english: A long one. I want to hear everything about this girl.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mum got back late from Satou-san's, and she's too tired to hear Kenji's news tonight.
Kenji tells Mum he has a girlfriend, and Mum says she'll pass the news on to Satou-san.
Kenji tells Mum he has a girlfriend, but she already knew: Satou-san told her during their hour-long chat.

questions.explanation: Line 11: Kenji's news is kanojo ga dekita (he's got a girlfriend). Line 12: Mum has already heard about it (sono hanashi, mou kiita yo), and line 14 says who from: satou-san kara, who even described the girl (long hair, tall). Line 15: so the hour Mum spent with Satou-san (lines 2-5) was about Kenji (ichijikan mo boku no hanashi shiteta no?). Lines 16-18: now Mum has her own talk for him: she wants to hear all about the girl. A is wrong: Mum isn't too tired; she says she'll listen (line 10: hanashi kiku yo) and wants to hear everything (line 18). B is wrong: the news went the other way, from Satou-san to Mum (line 14).

questions.english: You and Mum have been chatting about your little brother Kenji. He wanders in and asks, "nani? nani shiteta no?" (What? What were you two doing?) Tell him you were talking about him.
questions.ja: 何？何してたの？
questions.kana: なに？なにしてたの？
questions.romaji: nani? nani shiteta no?
questions.answer: Say who you were talking about with X no hanashi shiteta, using his name for X: kenji no hanashi shiteta no.

modelAnswers.romaji: kenji no hanashi shiteta no.
modelAnswers.ja: ケンジの話してたの。
modelAnswers.english: We were talking about you.

modelAnswers.romaji: kenji no hanashi o shiteta n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ケンジの話をしてたんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: We were talking about you, actually.

questions.explanation: Hanashi o suru takes the topic in front with no: X no hanashi shiteta = we were talking about X. Kenji asks it this way in line 5 (nan no hanashi shiteta no?) and line 15 (boku no hanashi shiteta no?). Casual speech drops o once hanashi has a word in front of it, as in the first model; the second keeps it and adds n da yo. Talking to Kenji, use his name rather than anata. The person you talked with goes with to: satou-san to hanashi o shiteta (line 2).

questions.english: When Kenji tells his mum he has a girlfriend, she says "a, sono hanashi, mou kiita yo." What does she mean?
questions.ja: お母さんは、何を聞いたんですか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、なにをきいたんですか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, nani o kiita n desu ka?

choices.english: She had already heard the news, from Satou-san.
She had already asked Satou-san about Kenji's girlfriend.
She had heard enough and wanted Kenji to stop talking.

questions.explanation: Line 12: hanashi o kiku is hearing about something as well as listening: sono hanashi, mou kiita yo = I've already heard about that. Line 14 says who from: satou-san kara (X kara kiku = hear it from X). B is kiku's other meaning, ask, which would be satou-san ni kiita; and it was Satou-san doing the talking while Mum listened for an hour (line 4: zutto hanashi kiiteta). C is wrong: Mum isn't cutting Kenji off; she offered to listen in line 10 (hanashi kiku yo) and in line 18 she wants to hear all of it (zenbu kiku kara ne).

questions.english: You call your old friend Kenta because there's something serious you need to talk to him about. He picks up: "moshimoshi? nani?" (Hello? What's up?) Tell him you need to talk, and ask if now is a good time.
questions.ja: もしもし？何？
questions.kana: もしもし？なに？
questions.romaji: moshimoshi? nani?
questions.answer: Open with chotto hanashi ga aru n da kedo, then ask ima ii?

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto hanashi ga aru n da kedo, ima ii?
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと話があるんだけど、今いい？
modelAnswers.english: I need to talk to you. Got a minute?

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto ohanashi ga aru n desu kedo, ima ii desu ka?
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっとお話があるんですけど、今いいですか？
modelAnswers.english: There's something I'd like to talk to you about. Do you have a moment?

questions.explanation: The everyday opener for a serious talk is chotto hanashi ga aru n da kedo, trailing off with n da kedo, exactly as Kenji says it in line 7; Mum uses the same phrase in line 16 (hanashi ga aru no). English 'I need to talk to you' pulls toward hanasu hitsuyou ga aru, which sounds stiff and official. Ima ii? (is now OK?) is the usual follow-up. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san: ohanashi ga aru n desu kedo.

questions.english: Mum says she got back late because she was talking with Satou-san. What did Kenji say about Satou-san?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Satou-san, huh. That's a long story, isn't it.
choices.romaji: satou-san ka. nagai hanashi da yo ne.

choices.english: Satou-san, huh. He does go on, doesn't he.
choices.romaji: satou-san ka. hanashi nagai yo ne.

choices.english: Satou-san, huh. He's loud, isn't he.
choices.romaji: satou-san ka. koe ookii yo ne.

questions.explanation: Line 3: X (wa) hanashi nagai, with ga dropped, is the stock grumble about a person who goes on and on. Kenji says it again about himself in line 9 (hanashi nagaku nai yo, I don't go on) and about Mum in line 17. A turns it round into nagai hanashi, which is one long talk or story: that's what Mum asks about Kenji's news in line 8 (nagai hanashi?) and Kenji asks about hers in line 17. It describes a talk, not a person, so it can't say Satou-san always goes on. C is a different complaint (koe ga ookii, he's loud); what kept Mum was how long he talked, a whole hour (line 4).

newWords.english: girlfriend (kanojo ga dekita = I've got a girlfriend)
girl, kid (sono ko = that girl; se ga takai ko = a tall girl)
too, also; after an amount, a whole (ichijikan mo = a whole hour)
quoting what was just said (hanashi ga aru tte, nani? = something to tell me? what?)

script.title: Free for football
script.setting: A weekday morning outside the flats. Kenta is running for the 8:15 train when the elderly neighbour, Satou-san, stops him for 'just a minute'. Satou-san takes his time getting to the point.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: uwa, mou hachiji? jikan nai!
lines.ja: うわ、もう八時？時間ない！
lines.kana: うわ、もうはちじ？じかんない！
lines.english: Ugh, eight already? I'm out of time!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, kenta-kun. ohayou gozaimasu. chotto ii desu ka?
lines.ja: あ、ケンタくん。おはようございます。ちょっといいですか？
lines.kana: あ、けんたくん。おはようございます。ちょっといいですか？
lines.english: Ah, Kenta. Good morning. Have you got a moment?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, satou-san, ohayou gozaimasu. sumimasen, ima chotto jikan ga nai n desu. hachiji juugofun no densha ni noranai to.
lines.ja: あ、佐藤さん、おはようございます。すみません、今ちょっと時間がないんです。八時十五分の電車に乗らないと。
lines.kana: あ、さとうさん、おはようございます。すみません、いまちょっとじかんがないんです。はちじじゅうごふんのでんしゃにのらないと。
lines.english: Oh, Satou-san, good morning. Sorry, I don't really have time right now. I've got to catch the 8:15.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ippun de owarimasu yo. nichiyoubi wa hima desu ka?
lines.ja: 一分で終わりますよ。日曜日は暇ですか？
lines.kana: いっぷんでおわりますよ。にちようびはひまですか？
lines.english: It'll only take a minute. Are you free on Sunday?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nichiyoubi desu ka? zutto shigoto ga isogashikute, doyou mo nichiyou mo hima ga nai n desu yo.
lines.ja: 日曜日ですか？ずっと仕事が忙しくて、土曜も日曜も暇がないんですよ。
lines.kana: にちようびですか？ずっとしごとがいそがしくて、どようもにちようもひまがないんですよ。
lines.english: Sunday? Work's been crazy for ages. I don't get any free time, Saturday or Sunday.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: aa, ima wa yoyuu ga nai n desu ne. nichiyoubi no sakkaa no chiketto ga nimai aru n desu kedo ne.
lines.ja: ああ、今は余裕がないんですね。日曜日のサッカーのチケットが二枚あるんですけどね。
lines.kana: ああ、いまはよゆうがないんですね。にちようびのさっかーのちけっとがにまいあるんですけどね。
lines.english: Ah, so you're swamped right now. Only, I've got two tickets for Sunday's football...

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, sakkaa? ikitai desu! demo, ima okane nai n desu yo.
lines.ja: え、サッカー？行きたいです！でも、今お金ないんですよ。
lines.kana: え、さっかー？いきたいです！でも、いまおかねないんですよ。
lines.english: Huh, football? I'd love to go! But I'm broke right now.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ichimai, gosen en desu kedo ne.
lines.ja: 一枚、五千円ですけどね。
lines.kana: いちまい、ごせんえんですけどね。
lines.english: Well, they're five thousand yen each...

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gosen en kaa. chotto okane ga tarinai desu.
lines.ja: 五千円かあ。ちょっとお金が足りないです。
lines.kana: ごせんえんかあ。ちょっとおかねがたりないです。
lines.english: Five thousand, huh. I'm a bit short.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: okane ga tarinai? iya iya, kenta-kun, okane wa ii n desu yo.
lines.ja: お金が足りない？いやいや、ケンタくん、お金はいいんですよ。
lines.kana: おかねがたりない？いやいや、けんたくん、おかねはいいんですよ。
lines.english: Short? No, no, Kenta. You don't need to pay.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, ii n desu ka? ima honto ni okane no yoyuu ga nakute.
lines.ja: え、いいんですか？今ほんとにお金の余裕がなくて。
lines.kana: え、いいんですか？いまほんとにおかねのよゆうがなくて。
lines.english: What, really? Money's really tight right now.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ii n desu yo. watashi mo mukashi wa, okane ga nakatta desu kara.
lines.ja: いいんですよ。私も昔は、お金がなかったですから。
lines.kana: いいんですよ。わたしもむかしは、おかねがなかったですから。
lines.english: It's fine. I was broke too, back in the day.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: satou-san, honto ni arigatou gozaimasu!
lines.ja: 佐藤さん、ほんとにありがとうございます！
lines.kana: さとうさん、ほんとにありがとうございます！
lines.english: Satou-san, thank you so much!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo, kenta-kun, doyou mo nichiyou mo hima ga nai n deshou?
lines.ja: でも、ケンタくん、土曜も日曜も暇がないんでしょう？
lines.kana: でも、けんたくん、どようもにちようもひまがないんでしょう？
lines.english: But Kenta, I thought you had no free time, Saturday or Sunday?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: iya, sakkaa nara hima arimasu!
lines.ja: いや、サッカーなら暇あります！
lines.kana: いや、さっかーならひまあります！
lines.english: No, for football I'm free!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hahaha. watashi wa ikanai node, sora-kun to douzo.
lines.ja: ははは。私は行かないので、ソラくんとどうぞ。
lines.kana: ははは。わたしはいかないので、そらくんとどうぞ。
lines.english: Ha ha ha. I'm not going, so take Sora with you.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hai! a, mou hachiji juppun! jikan nai! itte kimasu!
lines.ja: はい！あ、もう八時十分！時間ない！行ってきます！
lines.kana: はい！あ、もうはちじじゅっぷん！じかんない！いってきます！
lines.english: Will do! Oh, it's ten past eight already! I'm out of time! I'm off!

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Satou-san invites Kenta to Sunday's football, but Kenta can't afford a ticket, so he says no.
Kenta misses his train because Satou-san wants his help with something on Sunday.
Kenta says he has no free time and no money, but when Satou-san gives him the football tickets for free, he's suddenly free on Sunday.

questions.explanation: Lines 3 and 5: Kenta has no time right now (jikan ga nai) and no free time at weekends (hima ga nai). Line 7: he's broke (okane nai), and line 9: he's a bit short for a 5,000-yen ticket (okane ga tarinai). Line 10: Satou-san says he doesn't need to pay (okane wa ii n desu yo), and in line 16 he says he isn't going himself, so Kenta can take Sora. Line 15: for football, Kenta is suddenly free (sakkaa nara hima arimasu). A is wrong: Kenta can't afford the tickets, but he doesn't have to pay, and he takes them happily. B is wrong: Satou-san only wanted to give him the tickets, and at ten past eight (line 17) Kenta runs off for his 8:15 train. Nobody says he misses it.

questions.english: You're running for your train when Kenta catches you: "ne, ima chotto ii? hanashi ga aru n da kedo." (Hey, got a sec? I need to talk to you.) Tell him you've got no time right now.
questions.ja: ね、今ちょっといい？話があるんだけど。
questions.kana: ね、いまちょっといい？はなしがあるんだけど。
questions.romaji: ne, ima chotto ii? hanashi ga aru n da kedo.
questions.answer: Say you have no time right now with jikan and nai. Kenta's a friend, so keep it casual: gomen, ima jikan nai n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, ima jikan nai n da. densha ni noranai to.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今時間ないんだ。電車に乗らないと。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I don't have time right now. I've got to catch my train.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen! mou jikan nai!
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん！もう時間ない！
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry! I'm out of time!

questions.explanation: Time is something there is or isn't, so it's jikan ga nai, not jikan o motte nai. Kenta says it to himself in lines 1 and 17 (jikan nai!) and politely to Satou-san in line 3 (ima chotto jikan ga nai n desu). It's about right now, so use jikan, not hima: hima ga nai means no free time these days (line 5). Mou jikan nai! means 'I'm out of time!'. With a friend, drop ga and end with n da.

questions.english: Satou-san invites you over: "nichiyoubi, uchi ni kimasen ka?" (Would you like to come over on Sunday?) You've been working every weekend for a month. Apologise and say you've had no free time.
questions.ja: 日曜日、うちに来ませんか？
questions.kana: にちようび、うちにきませんか？
questions.romaji: nichiyoubi, uchi ni kimasen ka?
questions.answer: Apologise and say you've got no free time these days, with hima and nai, politely: sumimasen, zutto shigoto ga isogashikute, hima ga nai n desu.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, zutto shigoto ga isogashikute, hima ga nai n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、ずっと仕事が忙しくて、暇がないんです。
modelAnswers.english: I'm sorry, work's been so busy for ages. I've got no free time.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, doyou mo nichiyou mo hima ga nai n desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、土曜も日曜も暇がないんですよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I don't get any free time, Saturday or Sunday.

questions.explanation: hima ga nai means no free time these days. Kenta uses it for his weekends in line 5 (doyou mo nichiyou mo hima ga nai n desu yo), and Satou-san teases him with the same words in line 14. jikan ga nai is for right now or one thing, like Kenta rushing for the 8:15 in line 3. After a month of working weekends, it's hima. Satou-san is an elderly neighbour, so answer politely with n desu, and say sumimasen first to soften the no.

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "ne, ashita kaimono ni ikanai?" (Hey, want to go shopping tomorrow?) It's the end of the month and your bank account is empty. Tell him you're broke.
questions.ja: ね、明日買い物に行かない？
questions.kana: ね、あしたかいものにいかない？
questions.romaji: ne, ashita kaimono ni ikanai?
questions.answer: Say you're broke with okane and nai, casually: gomen, ima okane nai n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, ima okane nai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今お金ないんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'm broke right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: ikitai kedo, ima okane nai kara, gomen.
modelAnswers.ja: 行きたいけど、今お金ないから、ごめん。
modelAnswers.english: I'd love to, but I'm broke right now, so sorry.

questions.explanation: Being broke is okane (ga) nai. Kenta says it in line 7 (ima okane nai n desu yo), and Satou-san uses the past in line 12 (mukashi wa, okane ga nakatta). Okane o motte nai usually means you have no cash on you right now, not that you're broke. Okane ga tarinai would be short for one thing, like the 5,000-yen ticket in lines 9-10, but here you have no money for anything. Okane nai kara... gives it as the reason.

questions.english: When Satou-san says the tickets are 5,000 yen each, Kenta says "chotto okane ga tarinai desu." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンタさんのお金は？
questions.kana: けんたさんのおかねは？
questions.romaji: kenta-san no okane wa?

choices.english: He thinks 5,000 yen is too much to pay for a football ticket.
He doesn't have quite enough to pay for a 5,000-yen ticket.
He has no money at all, not even for his train.

questions.explanation: Line 9: okane ga tarinai means the money isn't enough, so he's short for one particular thing, here a 5,000-yen ticket. Chotto tarinai is 'a bit short'. Satou-san repeats it in line 10 (okane ga tarinai?) before telling him he doesn't need to pay. A would be takai (expensive), which nobody says. C goes too far. In line 7 Kenta does say he's broke (ima okane nai), but tarinai only says he can't cover this ticket, and he's still on his way to catch his train (lines 3 and 17).

questions.english: Satou-san says Kenta doesn't need to pay. Kenta is relieved. What does he say about his money?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: money's really tight right now
choices.romaji: ima honto ni okane no yoyuu ga nakute.

choices.english: I really can't 'afford' it right now (English verb)
I really don't hold any money to spare right now
choices.romaji: ima honto ni okane no yoyuu o motte nakute.

questions.explanation: Line 11: okane no yoyuu ga nai means no money to spare, money's tight. The -te form nakute trails off as a reason. In line 6 Satou-san uses yoyuu on its own (ima wa yoyuu ga nai n desu ne), meaning Kenta is swamped, with no time or energy to spare. B is wrong: Japanese has no verb for 'afford', and afoodo isn't a word. For one item you'd say kaenai (can't buy it), and for money in general okane no yoyuu ga nai. C is wrong: like time and money, yoyuu is something there is or isn't, so it takes ga nai, never o motte nai.

newWords.english: counter for flat things like tickets (ichimai = one, nimai = two)
long ago, back in the day
if it's...; when it comes to (sakkaa nara = for football)
say (nan to iimashita ka? = what did he say?)

script.title: Just a bit of air
script.setting: A stormy autumn Saturday at Kenta's flat. Yuki and Kenta had planned a bike ride, but the rain and wind have kept them in all day.

lines.romaji: uwaa, ame tsuyoku natte kita.

lines.kana: うわあ、あめつよくなってきた。
lines.english: Whoa, the rain's really coming down now.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kaze mo tsuyoi ne. kore ja, jitensha norenai yo.
lines.ja: 風も強いね。これじゃ、自転車乗れないよ。
lines.kana: かぜもつよいね。これじゃ、じてんしゃのれないよ。
lines.english: And it's windy, too. We can't go cycling in this.

lines.speaker: yuki

lines.kana: うん、あしたにしよう。きょうはあめつよいし。
lines.english: Yeah, let's make it tomorrow. The rain's so heavy today, anyway.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, ame yanda.
lines.ja: あ、雨やんだ。
lines.kana: あ、あめやんだ。
lines.english: Oh, the rain's stopped.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nande ima yamu no?
lines.ja: なんで今やむの？
lines.kana: なんでいまやむの？
lines.english: Why does it stop now, of all times?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: zutto uchi ni ita shi, chotto kaze ni atatte kuru.
lines.ja: ずっとうちにいたし、ちょっと風に当たってくる。
lines.kana: ずっとうちにいたし、ちょっとかぜにあたってくる。
lines.english: I've been stuck inside all day. I'm going to go and get some air.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: demo, mada kaze tsuyoi yo?
lines.ja: でも、まだ風強いよ？
lines.kana: でも、まだかぜつよいよ？
lines.english: But it's still windy out, you know.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: daijoubu. aa, ii kaze fuiteru. kimochi ii!
lines.ja: 大丈夫。ああ、いい風吹いてる。気持ちいい！
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。ああ、いいかぜふいてる。きもちいい！
lines.english: I'll be fine. Ahh, there's a lovely breeze. That feels great!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii kaze? tsumetai kaze fuiteru dake da yo.
lines.ja: いい風？冷たい風吹いてるだけだよ。
lines.kana: いいかぜ？つめたいかぜふいてるだけだよ。
lines.english: A lovely breeze? It's just a cold wind blowing.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sore ga ii n da yo.
lines.ja: それがいいんだよ。
lines.kana: それがいいんだよ。
lines.english: That's what's so nice about it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: zutto kaze ni atatteru to, kaze hiku yo.
lines.ja: ずっと風に当たってると、風邪ひくよ。
lines.kana: ずっとかぜにあたってると、かぜひくよ。
lines.english: Stay out in the wind too long and you'll catch a cold.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hikanai yo. hakkushon!
lines.ja: ひかないよ。はっくしょん！
lines.kana: ひかないよ。はっくしょん！
lines.english: I won't. Achoo!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, mou kaze hiita no?
lines.ja: え、もう風邪ひいたの？
lines.kana: え、もうかぜひいたの？
lines.english: What, you've caught a cold already?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hiitenai yo. chotto kaze ni atatta dake.
lines.ja: ひいてないよ。ちょっと風に当たっただけ。
lines.kana: ひいてないよ。ちょっとかぜにあたっただけ。
lines.english: I have not. I just got a bit of air.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou, haitte! ashita, jitensha noru n desho?
lines.ja: もう、入って！明日、自転車乗るんでしょ？
lines.kana: もう、はいって！あした、じてんしゃのるんでしょ？
lines.english: Honestly, get back inside! We're cycling tomorrow, aren't we?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hai hai. ashita, tenki ii to ii na.
lines.ja: はいはい。明日、天気いいといいな。
lines.kana: はいはい。あした、てんきいいといいな。
lines.english: Okay, okay. Hope the weather's nice tomorrow.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: The rain stops, so they go out on their bikes after all, wind or no wind.
Yuki goes out for some air in the cold wind, and Kenta warns her she'll catch a cold.
They put the bike ride off until tomorrow, and Kenta stands out in the cold wind and starts sneezing.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: the rain is heavy and it's windy too, so they can't ride (jitensha norenai). Lines 4-5: the weather is supposed to be nice tomorrow, so they move the ride to tomorrow (ashita ni shiyou). Line 6: the rain stops, but it's still windy (line 9). Line 8: Kenta goes out to get some air (kaze ni atatte kuru). Lines 11-13: Yuki says it's a cold wind and warns him he'll catch a cold, and in line 14 he sneezes (hakkushon). A is wrong: the ride stays tomorrow's plan (line 17: ashita, jitensha noru n desho?), and the wind is still strong (line 9). B swaps the two of them: Kenta is the one who goes out (line 8), and Yuki gives the warning (line 13).

questions.english: It's a bright, sunny morning. Your elderly neighbour Satou-san greets you in the street: "ohayou gozaimasu." Greet him back and say what nice weather it is.
questions.ja: おはようございます。
questions.kana: おはようございます。
questions.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu.
questions.answer: Greet him and remark on the weather with ii tenki, made polite with o- and desu: ohayou gozaimasu. ii otenki desu ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. ii otenki desu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: おはようございます。いいお天気ですね。
modelAnswers.english: Good morning. Lovely weather, isn't it?

modelAnswers.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. kyou wa tenki ga ii desu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: おはようございます。今日は天気がいいですね。
modelAnswers.english: Good morning. The weather's nice today, isn't it?

questions.explanation: Nice weather is ii tenki, or tenki ga ii; English 'beautiful weather' pushes kirei na tenki, which sounds odd. Yuki and Kenta use it casually in lines 3, 4 and 18 (kinou wa ii tenki datta noni naa / ashita wa tenki ii tte / tenki ii to ii na). To an older neighbour like Satou-san, add o- and desu: ii otenki desu ne is the standard remark after a morning greeting. Both models are polite: the first puts ii before the noun, the second uses the tenki ga ii pattern.

questions.english: Kenta says he's going out to get some air. What does Yuki say back?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: But it's still raining hard, you know.
But it's still windy, you know.
But the wind's still high, you know.

questions.explanation: Line 9: demo, mada kaze tsuyoi yo? Japanese has no adjective for 'windy': you say the wind is strong, kaze ga tsuyoi, with ga dropped in casual talk. A is the same frame with ame, which they used in lines 1 and 5, but the rain had just stopped (line 6: a, ame yanda), so it doesn't fit this moment. C turns English 'high winds' into Japanese word for word; takai means high, tall or expensive and is not used of wind.

questions.english: It's pouring where you are. Kenta calls you: "ima kara jitensha de iku ne!" (I'm heading over on my bike now!) Warn him that the rain's heavy.
questions.ja: 今から自転車で行くね！
questions.kana: いまからじてんしゃでいくね！
questions.romaji: ima kara jitensha de iku ne!
questions.answer: Warn him with ame (ga) tsuyoi: e, ame tsuyoi yo!

modelAnswers.romaji: e, ame tsuyoi yo! jitensha wa dame da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: え、雨強いよ！自転車はだめだよ。
modelAnswers.english: Wait, the rain's really heavy! No bike today.

modelAnswers.romaji: ame, metcha tsuyoku natte kita yo. densha de kite.
modelAnswers.ja: 雨、めっちゃ強くなってきたよ。電車で来て。
modelAnswers.english: The rain's really coming down now. Take the train.

questions.explanation: Heavy rain is strong rain: ame ga tsuyoi, not omoi ame, because omoi is only about weight. Tsuyoku natte kita is 'it's getting heavier', Yuki's opener in line 1; line 5 has the plain form (kyou wa ame tsuyoi shi). In line 2 Kenta answers in the same frame about the wind (kaze mo tsuyoi ne), and between them that's what puts the bike ride off.

questions.english: When Kenta steps outside, he says "aa, ii kaze fuiteru." What does he mean?
questions.ja: 外の風は？
questions.kana: そとのかぜは？
questions.romaji: soto no kaze wa?

choices.english: There's a nice breeze blowing, and he's enjoying it.
The wind has died down at last, so it's calm outside.
He's caught a slight cold, but he feels fine.

questions.explanation: Line 10: ii kaze fuiteru is 'a nice wind is blowing', a breeze. Fuku (fuiteru) is what wind does, and kimochi ii right after says he's enjoying it. Yuki uses the same verb to disagree in line 11 (tsumetai kaze fuiteru dake da yo: it's just a cold wind blowing). B is wrong: fuiteru means the wind is blowing right now, not dying down, and Yuki has just said it's still windy (line 9). C mixes up kaze (wind) with kaze (a cold), which sound the same: only the verb tells them apart. Fuku goes with the wind; a cold takes hiku, as in lines 13 and 15 (kaze hiku yo / mou kaze hiita no?).

questions.english: You're at a crowded party at Kenta's flat, and the room is hot and stuffy. You head for the door, and Kenta asks, "doko iku no?" (Where are you going?) Tell him you're just going to get some air.
questions.ja: どこ行くの？
questions.kana: どこいくの？
questions.romaji: doko iku no?
questions.answer: Say you're going to let the breeze hit you and come back, with kaze ni ataru + kuru: chotto kaze ni atatte kuru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto kaze ni atatte kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと風に当たってくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Just going to get some air.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto kaze ni atatte kimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと風に当たってきます。
modelAnswers.english: I'm just going to get some air.

questions.explanation: Nothing in 'get some air' leads to ataru: in Japanese you let the wind hit you, kaze ni ataru, and -te kuru adds 'and come back'. That's Kenta's line 8 (chotto kaze ni atatte kuru), and he says it again in line 16 (chotto kaze ni atatta dake). Keep the ni. Don't confuse it with kaze o hiku: that kaze is a cold, as in Yuki's warning in line 13 (zutto kaze ni atatteru to, kaze hiku yo). The second model is the polite version, for a work party with Tanaka-san.

newWords.english: they say, I heard (passing on news or a forecast: ashita wa tenki ii tte = they say it'll be nice tomorrow)
cold (to the touch); tsumetai kaze = a cold wind
just, only (kaze ni atatta dake = I just got some air)
catch a cold; this kaze (風邪) is a cold and sounds exactly like kaze (風), wind
say (nan to iimashita ka? = what did they say?)

Sora got his hair cut after work yesterday, and Kenta tells him to cut his nails before his movie date.
Kenta has a movie date today, so Sora checks him over and tells him to wash his face and cut his nails.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenta asks kami kitta? and Sora says kittenai yo, kami aratta dake (I didn't cut it, I just washed it). Lines 3-4: he meant to get it cut yesterday but couldn't (ikenakatta). Line 6: today he's seeing a movie with that girl. Lines 7-14: Kenta checks Sora's face, nails and hands. Lines 16-17: Sora asks Kenta the same question, and Kenta hasn't washed his face yet (kao wa mada da). B is wrong: Sora never got the haircut, because work was too busy (line 4). C swaps them: the date is Sora's (line 6), and it's Kenta who checks Sora over; Sora only turns the face question back on Kenta at the end.

questions.english: You've just got home. Kenta calls from the kitchen, "a, gohan dekita yo!" (Oh, food's ready!) Tell him you'll go and wash your hands first.
questions.ja: あ、ご飯できたよ！
questions.kana: あ、ごはんできたよ！
questions.romaji: a, gohan dekita yo!
questions.answer: Say you'll go and wash your hands, with te (o) arau in the te-form plus kuru: te aratte kuru.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, te aratte kuru.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、手洗ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: Okay, I'll go wash my hands.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, te o aratte kimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、手を洗ってきます。
modelAnswers.english: Then I'll go and wash my hands.

questions.explanation: Washing your hands is te o arau. Aratte kuru is 'go and wash, then come back', the same shape as Kenta's te aratte kite (line 13) and Sora's aratte kuru (line 8). Casual speech drops o (te aratte); the polite version keeps it. Sora answers Kenta in line 14 with te mo aratta yo (I washed my hands too), and Kenta uses it in line 17 (te wa aratta kedo). The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san or Satou-san.

questions.english: You've only just got up. Kenta asks, "ohayou. mada nemui?" (Morning. Still sleepy?) Say yes, and that you'll go and wash your face.
questions.ja: おはよう。まだ眠い？
questions.kana: おはよう。まだねむい？
questions.romaji: ohayou. mada nemui?
questions.answer: Say yes, then kao (o) aratte kuru: un, nemui. kao aratte kuru.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, nemui. kao aratte kuru.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、眠い。顔洗ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm sleepy. I'll go wash my face.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, mada nemui kara, chotto kao aratte kuru.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、まだ眠いから、ちょっと顔洗ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, still sleepy, so I'll just go wash my face.

questions.explanation: Washing your face is kao o arau, with the same arau as hands and hair. Splashing your face is the standard way to wake yourself up, so aratte kuru (I'll go and wash it) is the natural reply. Kenta asks kao mo aratta? in line 7, Sora says aratte kuru! in line 8, and Kenta checks kao aratte kita? in line 9. At the end Sora sends Kenta off the same way: kao aratte kite ne (line 18).

questions.english: Kenta asks Sora if he got a haircut, and Sora answers "kittenai yo. kami aratta dake." What had Sora done to his hair?
questions.ja: ソラさんの髪は？
questions.kana: そらさんのかみは？
questions.romaji: sora-san no kami wa?

choices.english: He'd had it trimmed just a little, so it barely looked different.
He'd cut it himself at home, because he couldn't get to the salon.
He'd only washed it; he hadn't cut it at all.

questions.explanation: Line 2: kittenai is 'I haven't cut it', and kami aratta dake is 'I just washed my hair'. Arau is the everyday verb for washing hair too; there's no separate shampoo verb. Kenta repeats it in line 5 (kami aratta dake de kekkou kawaru ne: just washing it makes quite a difference) and line 7 (dakara kami aratta n da). A is wrong: kittenai means he didn't cut it at all; even a small trim would be kitta (chotto kitta). B is wrong: he couldn't get to the salon (line 4: ikenakatta), but he didn't cut it anywhere. Washing was all he did.

questions.english: When Kenta first sees Sora, his hair looks different. What does Kenta ask him?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Huh? Did your hair get cut on you?
Huh? Did you get a haircut?
Huh? Did you wear your hair? (kita = wore)

questions.explanation: Line 1: kami kitta? is the stock 'did you get a haircut?'. Japanese says it even though a stylist does the cutting: line 3 shows Kenta thought Sora had gone to the salon (kami kiri ni iku). C uses kita, the past of the other kiru, 'wear' (fuku o kiru, kita). Cut is kitta, with the double t you hear as a tiny pause; wear is kita, with no pause. A, kirareta, is the passive. It makes the cut something done to you, the way you'd complain that a stylist took too much off. English 'have your hair cut' doesn't need a passive in Japanese; plain kitta covers a salon cut.

questions.english: Yuki phones while you're in the middle of cutting your nails. She asks, "moshimoshi? ima nani shiteru no?" (Hello? What are you up to right now?) Tell her.
questions.ja: もしもし？今何してるの？
questions.kana: もしもし？いまなにしてるの？
questions.romaji: moshimoshi? ima nani shiteru no?
questions.answer: Say you're cutting your nails, with tsume (o) kiru in the -teru form: tsume kitteru.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima? tsume kitteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 今？爪切ってるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Right now? I'm cutting my nails.

modelAnswers.romaji: tsume kitteta. nani?
modelAnswers.ja: 爪切ってた。何？
modelAnswers.english: I was cutting my nails. What's up?

questions.explanation: Cutting your nails is tsume o kiru, with the same kiru (cut) as kami o kiru. Kitteru is 'I'm cutting them right now'; kitteta is 'I was cutting them (until you called)'. Keep the double t: kiteru, with a single t, would be the 'wear' kiru. In the scene Kenta says tsume nagai yo, kittoki na yo (line 11), Sora says tsume kiranakya (line 12), and then tsume kitte, te mo aratta yo (line 14).

newWords.english: only, just (kami aratta dake = I just washed my hair)
girl, kid (ano ko = that girl, the one we both know about)
a meal, food (here: breakfast); also cooked rice
mom (okaasan ka yo = what are you, my mom?)
wear, put on (clothes); past kita. Not the kiru 'cut' (past kitta)
say (nan to iimashita ka = what did he say?)

script.title: An early start on Sunday
script.setting: Saturday night at the family home. Their mother has the bath ready and Yuki is about to get in, until Kenji comes out of the toilet and pushes in ahead of her.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ofuro dekita yo. kenji wa?
lines.ja: お風呂できたよ。ケンジは？
lines.kana: おふろできたよ。けんじは？
lines.english: The bath's ready. Where's Kenji?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: toire itteru yo.
lines.ja: トイレ行ってるよ。
lines.kana: トイレいってるよ。
lines.english: He's in the toilet.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, yuki, saki ni hairu?
lines.ja: じゃあ、ユキ、先に入る？
lines.kana: じゃあ、ゆき、さきにはいる？
lines.english: Then do you want to go first, Yuki?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, saki ni ofuro haitte kuru ne.
lines.ja: うん、先にお風呂入ってくるね。
lines.kana: うん、さきにおふろはいってくるね。
lines.english: Yeah, I'll go have my bath first.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, matte! boku ga saki ni shawaa abite kuru.
lines.ja: あ、待って！僕が先にシャワー浴びてくる。
lines.kana: あ、まって！ぼくがさきにシャワーあびてくる。
lines.english: Oh, wait! I'm going to go and shower first.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, kenji ga saki? nande?
lines.ja: え、ケンジが先？なんで？
lines.kana: え、けんじがさき？なんで？
lines.english: Huh, you first? How come?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ashita hayai n da. gomen!
lines.ja: 明日早いんだ。ごめん！
lines.kana: あしたはやいんだ。ごめん！
lines.english: I've got an early start tomorrow. Sorry!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ashita? nichiyoubi da yo?
lines.ja: 明日？日曜日だよ？
lines.kana: あした？にちようびだよ？
lines.english: Tomorrow? But it's Sunday.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: okaasan, kiite. kenji, shawaa abinagara uta utatteru.
lines.ja: お母さん、聞いて。ケンジ、シャワー浴びながら歌うたってる。
lines.kana: おかあさん、きいて。けんじ、シャワーあびながらうたうたってる。
lines.english: Mum, listen. Kenji's singing in the shower.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kibun ii n da ne. demo, mou sanjuppun da yo.
lines.ja: 気分いいんだね。でも、もう30分だよ。
lines.kana: きぶんいいんだね。でも、もうさんじゅっぷんだよ。
lines.english: Someone's in a good mood. But it's been thirty minutes already.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ofuro haitte ii yo.
lines.ja: お風呂入っていいよ。
lines.kana: おふろはいっていいよ。
lines.english: You can get in the bath now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: osoi yo! sanjuppun mo nani shiteta no?
lines.ja: 遅いよ！30分も何してたの？
lines.kana: おそいよ！さんじゅっぷんもなにしてたの？
lines.english: About time! What were you doing for thirty whole minutes?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shawaa abite, hige sotte, ha migaite.
lines.ja: シャワー浴びて、ひげ剃って、歯磨いて。
lines.kana: シャワーあびて、ひげそって、はみがいて。
lines.english: Showering, shaving, brushing my teeth.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hige sotta no? doko ni hige aru no?
lines.ja: ひげ剃ったの？どこにひげあるの？
lines.kana: ひげそったの？どこにひげあるの？
lines.english: You shaved? What beard?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: aru yo! koko ni chotto.
lines.ja: あるよ！ここにちょっと。
lines.kana: あるよ！ここにちょっと。
lines.english: I've got one! A bit, right here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ha mo zutto migaiteta shi. ne, ashita nani ga aru no?
lines.ja: 歯もずっと磨いてたし。ね、明日何があるの？
lines.kana: はもずっとみがいてたし。ね、あしたなにがあるの？
lines.english: And you were brushing your teeth forever. So what's happening tomorrow?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nani mo nai yo. a, chotto toire itte kuru.
lines.ja: 何もないよ。あ、ちょっとトイレ行ってくる。
lines.kana: なにもないよ。あ、ちょっとトイレいってくる。
lines.english: Nothing. Oh, I'm just going to the toilet.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: are wa deeto ne. yuki, ofuro haitchatte.
lines.ja: あれはデートね。ユキ、お風呂入っちゃって。
lines.kana: あれはデートね。ゆき、おふろはいっちゃって。
lines.english: That's a date, all right. Yuki, go on, get in the bath.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji has to be at school early tomorrow, so their mother lets him use the bath first, and Yuki waits half an hour.
Yuki sings in the bath for half an hour, so Kenji can't get in to shave and brush his teeth before his date.
Kenji pushes in ahead of Yuki and spends half an hour getting ready. He won't say what's happening tomorrow, but their mother guesses it's a date.

questions.explanation: In line 4 Yuki is about to have her bath, and in line 5 Kenji cuts in (matte! boku ga saki ni shawaa abite kuru). His reason in line 7 is an early start tomorrow (ashita hayai n da), but in line 8 their mother points out that tomorrow is Sunday. In lines 9-10 he's singing in the shower and has been in there for thirty minutes. In line 13 he says he showered, shaved and brushed his teeth. When Yuki asks what's happening tomorrow (line 16), he says nothing and escapes to the toilet (line 17), and their mother decides it's a date (line 18: are wa deeto ne). A is wrong: there's no school on a Sunday, and nobody let Kenji go first. He pushed in, and he only showered. B is wrong: Kenji is the one singing and taking thirty minutes, and Yuki is the one waiting.

questions.english: Their mother says the bath is ready and asks where Kenji is. Yuki says "toire itteru yo." Where is Kenji at that moment?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは今どこにいますか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはいまどこにいますか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa ima doko ni imasu ka?

choices.english: He's on his way to the toilet and will be there in a minute.
He's in the toilet right now. He went and hasn't come out yet.
He's in the bath, so Yuki can't use it yet.

questions.explanation: Line 2: toire itteru is iku in its -teru form. With iku, -teru means the person has gone and is there now, not 'is on the way'. So Kenji is in the toilet, and he comes out just in time to push in at line 5. A would be plain toire iku (he's about to go), not itteru. C is the English 'bathroom' getting in the way: in most Japanese homes the toilet is a separate room from the ofuro, so 'go to the bathroom' is toire ni iku. The bath is free, which is why their mother offers it to Yuki in line 3. Kenji's own line 17, chotto toire itte kuru, is the other shape: 'I'm just popping to the toilet (and I'll be back)'.

questions.english: You turn up at Kenta's flat soaked. He asks, "ame ni furareta no? daijoubu?" (Did you get caught in the rain? Are you okay?) Tell him you're fine and you'll go and take a shower.
questions.ja: 雨に降られたの？大丈夫？
questions.kana: あめにふられたの？だいじょうぶ？
questions.romaji: ame ni furareta no? daijoubu?
questions.answer: Say you're fine, then use shawaa with abiru, ideally in the -te kuru shape: un, daijoubu. chotto shawaa abite kuru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daijoubu. chotto shawaa abite kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大丈夫。ちょっとシャワー浴びてくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm fine. I'll just go and take a shower.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daijoubu. shawaa abite mo ii?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大丈夫。シャワー浴びてもいい？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm okay. Can I take a shower?

questions.explanation: A shower is water poured over you, so the verb is abiru. abite kuru means 'go and shower, then come back', the shape Kenji uses in line 5 (boku ga saki ni shawaa abite kuru). English 'take a shower' points to toru, but nobody says shawaa o toru. ofuro ni hairu is wrong here too: that's getting into a bath, and Kenta would have to fill one first. The second answer uses -te mo ii? to ask permission, which suits a shower in someone else's flat. Casual speech drops o, as both answers do.

questions.english: Your mother calls out, "ofuro dekita yo. dare ga saki?" (The bath's ready. Who's going first?) Say you'll go and have your bath first.
questions.ja: お風呂できたよ。誰が先？
questions.kana: おふろできたよ。だれがさき？
questions.romaji: ofuro dekita yo. dare ga saki?
questions.answer: Use ofuro with hairu, because a bath is something you get into: watashi! saki ni ofuro haitte kuru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: watashi! saki ni ofuro haitte kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 私！先にお風呂入ってくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Me! I'll go and have my bath first.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, watashi ga saki ni ofuro hairu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、私が先にお風呂入るね。
modelAnswers.english: Okay, I'll get in the bath first, then.

questions.explanation: You go into a bath, so it's ofuro (ni) hairu, and casual speech usually drops ni. This is Yuki's line 4 (saki ni ofuro haitte kuru ne). Kenji answers it in line 5 with the same frame and the other verb: saki ni shawaa abite kuru. A shower is poured over you (abiru) and a bath is gone into (hairu), so ofuro o abiru and ofuro o toru are both wrong. Their mother uses the same verb in line 18: ofuro haitchatte (go on, get in the bath).

questions.english: It's after lunch at the office, and you get up with your toothbrush. Yuki asks, "a, doko iku no?" (Oh, where are you off to?) Tell her you're just going to brush your teeth.
questions.ja: あ、どこ行くの？
questions.kana: あ、どこいくの？
questions.romaji: a, doko iku no?
questions.answer: Use ha with migaku, in the -te kuru shape: chotto ha migaite kuru.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto ha migaite kuru.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと歯磨いてくる。
modelAnswers.english: Just going to brush my teeth.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto ha o migaite kimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと歯を磨いてきます。
modelAnswers.english: I'm just going to brush my teeth.

questions.explanation: Teeth are polished, so the verb is migaku. Kenji uses it in lines 13 and 16 (ha migaite, ha mo zutto migaiteta). English speakers often say ha o arau ('wash'), but that's for hands and faces (te o arau, kao o arau). Teeth get migaku. With -te kuru you're saying you'll be right back. Lots of people in Japan brush their teeth at work after lunch. The second answer is the polite version, for Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Yuki asks Kenji what he was doing all that time, and he lists three things. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Showering, shaving, brushing my teeth.
choices.romaji: shawaa abite, hige sotte, ha migaite.

choices.english: Showering, trimming my beard, brushing my teeth.
choices.romaji: shawaa abite, hige kitte, ha migaite.

choices.english: Showering, shaving down my beard, brushing my teeth.
choices.romaji: shawaa abite, hige kezutte, ha migaite.

questions.explanation: Line 13: hige sotte. soru means shaving hair off with a razor, and in line 14 Yuki repeats it to tease him (hige sotta no? doko ni hige aru no?). B is what English 'cut' leads to, but hige o kiru means trimming a beard with scissors, not shaving it off. C is the dictionary trap: kezuru is the 'shave' of shaving wood or a pencil down, and it's never used for hair. Stubble and beards are always soru.

newWords.english: first, before the others (kenji ga saki? = you first?)
early (ashita hayai = I've got an early start tomorrow)
late, slow (osoi yo! = you took ages!)
shave down, whittle (wood, a pencil); never used for hair

script.title: Your Japanese is so good

speakers.name: Mai

lines.kana: じぶんでは、にほんごはすこしできますっていっていましたけどね。

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kinou, ema-san no hanashi mo kikimashita yo.
lines.ja: 昨日、エマさんの話も聞きましたよ。
lines.kana: きのう、えまさんのはなしもききましたよ。
lines.english: I sat down with Emma yesterday too, and heard what she had to say.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ema-san, nante itte imashita ka?
lines.ja: エマさん、何て言っていましたか？
lines.kana: えまさん、なんていっていましたか？
lines.english: What did Emma say?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san wa atama ga ii shi, shigoto mo dekiru shi, sensu mo ii tte.
lines.ja: 木村さんは頭がいいし、仕事もできるし、センスもいいって。
lines.kana: きむらさんはあたまがいいし、しごともできるし、センスもいいって。
