lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? watashi desu ka? atama ga ii no wa ema-san desu yo!
lines.ja: え？私ですか？頭がいいのはエマさんですよ！
lines.kana: え？わたしですか？あたまがいいのはえまさんですよ！
lines.english: What? Me? Emma's the smart one!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sore kara, kimura-san wa nihongo mo jouzu da tte.
lines.ja: それから、木村さんは日本語も上手だって。
lines.kana: それから、きむらさんはにほんごもじょうずだって。
lines.english: Oh, and that your Japanese is very good, too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: demo watashi, nihonjin desu yo!
lines.ja: でも私、日本人ですよ！
lines.kana: でもわたし、にほんじんですよ！
lines.english: But I'm Japanese!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: joudan desu yo. ema-san wa minna ni, nihongo jouzu desu ne tte iwarete imasu kara ne.
lines.ja: 冗談ですよ。エマさんはみんなに、日本語上手ですねって言われていますからね。
lines.kana: じょうだんですよ。えまさんはみんなに、にほんごじょうずですねっていわれていますからね。
lines.english: She was joking. Everyone's always telling her, 'Your Japanese is so good!'

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, ashita ema-san ni itte okimasu. iie, mada mada desu tte.
lines.ja: じゃあ、明日エマさんに言っておきます。いいえ、まだまだですって。
lines.kana: じゃあ、あしたえまさんにいっておきます。いいえ、まだまだですって。
lines.english: Then tomorrow I'll tell Emma: 'Oh no, I've still got a long way to go.'

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai says Emma only speaks a little Japanese, so Tanaka-san asks Mai to help her with it.
Mai praises Emma, and Tanaka-san tells her Emma said the same kind of things about Mai, even joking that Mai's Japanese is good.
Emma told Tanaka-san that Mai's Japanese is hard to follow, so Mai plans to speak to her more simply tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Tanaka-san asks how Emma is doing after her first month. In lines 4-10 Mai praises her: she's great at her job (shigoto ga dekiru), she has good taste in clothes (fuku no sensu mo ii), and her Japanese may even be better than Mai's (line 10). Line 11: Tanaka-san talked with Emma yesterday too, and line 13 gives what Emma said about Mai: atama ga ii, shigoto mo dekiru, sensu mo ii. In line 15 Emma also said Mai's Japanese is good, and line 17 explains it was a joke, because everyone says that to Emma. A is wrong: Emma is the one who says she speaks 'a little' (line 9), Mai says that isn't true (line 10), and nobody asks Mai to help. C is wrong: Emma praised Mai's Japanese as a joke. She didn't complain about it, and tomorrow Mai will joke back with iie, mada mada desu (line 18).

questions.english: Mai tells Tanaka-san that Emma is really good at her job. How does he agree?
questions.ja: 田中さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Yes, she's 'sumaato', after all.
Yes, her head is skilful, after all.
choices.romaji: ee, atama ga jouzu desu kara ne.

choices.english: Yes, she's smart, after all.
choices.romaji: ee, atama ga ii desu kara ne.

questions.explanation: Line 5: 'ee, atama ga ii desu kara ne.' Being smart is atama (head) with ii (good), and in casual speech ga drops (atama ii). The same pair comes back when Tanaka-san passes on what Emma said about Mai (line 13: atama ga ii shi) and when Mai answers (line 14: atama ga ii no wa ema-san desu yo). A is wrong: sumaato is the trap. In Japanese it means slim or sleek, so it would sound like a comment on Emma's figure. B is wrong: jouzu praises a skill done well, like the Japanese in lines 8 and 10 (nihongo mo sugoku jouzu). Being clever isn't a skill, so atama takes ii, never jouzu.

questions.english: Kenta has heard about your new coworker Emma and asks, "ema-san tte, nihongo dekiru no?" (Can Emma speak Japanese?) She speaks it really well. Tell him.
questions.ja: エマさんって、日本語できるの？
questions.kana: えまさんって、にほんごできるの？
questions.romaji: ema-san tte, nihongo dekiru no?
questions.answer: Go beyond dekiru and praise how well she speaks, with nihongo and jouzu. Kenta is a friend, so drop ga and answer casually: un, nihongo sugoku jouzu da yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, nihongo sugoku jouzu da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、日本語すごく上手だよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, her Japanese is really good.

modelAnswers.romaji: dekiru yo! nihongo, honto ni jouzu na n da.
modelAnswers.ja: できるよ！日本語、ほんとに上手なんだ。
modelAnswers.english: She sure can! Her Japanese is really good.

questions.explanation: Kenta asks with dekiru, which only says whether someone can speak it. Jouzu says she speaks it well, and that's what you want to tell him. Mai takes the same step in lines 9-10: Emma describes herself modestly with dekiru (nihongo wa sukoshi dekimasu, 'I speak a little'), and Mai corrects that to jouzu (sukoshi ja nai desu yo! nihongo, watashi yori jouzu kamo shiremasen). Jouzu is for praising someone else's skill, so it fits when you're talking about Emma. About your own Japanese you'd say sukoshi dekimasu, or mada mada desu when someone compliments you, which is the reply Mai jokes she'll give in line 18. Among friends, nihongo umai is also fine.

questions.english: Tanaka-san asks how Emma is getting on, and Mai says, "ema-san desu ka? sugoku shigoto ga dekiru n desu yo." What does Mai mean?
questions.ja: エマさんはどうですか？
questions.kana: えまさんはどうですか？
questions.romaji: ema-san wa dou desu ka?

choices.english: Emma is very capable: she's really good at her job.
Emma has a lot of work at the moment and is very busy.
Emma can now do the work by herself, without anyone's help.

questions.explanation: Line 4: shigoto ga dekiru is praise for a capable person, someone who is good at their job. Tanaka-san agrees that she's smart (line 5), and in line 13 Emma says the same about Mai (shigoto mo dekiru). It takes dekiru, not jouzu: jouzu praises a skill done well (nihongo ga jouzu), while shigoto ga dekiru says someone is capable. B is wrong: busy with work is shigoto ga isogashii, and nobody says Emma is busy. C is wrong: Mai isn't saying Emma can finally manage alone (that would be hitori de dekiru). She's praising how good Emma is at her job.

questions.english: Yuki holds up a new outfit: "mite mite! kinou, kaimono ni itte kita n da. kono fuku, dou?" (Look! I went shopping yesterday. What do you think of this?) You love it. Compliment her taste.
questions.ja: 見て見て！昨日、買い物に行ってきたんだ。この服、どう？
questions.kana: みてみて！きのう、かいものにいってきたんだ。このふく、どう？
questions.romaji: mite mite! kinou, kaimono ni itte kita n da. kono fuku, dou?
questions.answer: Praise her taste with sensu and ii. Yuki is a friend, so drop ga and answer casually: sensu ii ne!

modelAnswers.romaji: un, sugoku ii! sensu ii ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、すごくいい！センスいいね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it's great! You've got good taste.

modelAnswers.romaji: yuki tte, honto ni sensu ii yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ユキって、ほんとにセンスいいよね。
modelAnswers.english: You've really got great taste, Yuki.

questions.explanation: Taste in clothes is sensu with ii. Mai uses it about Emma in line 6 (fuku no sensu mo ii n desu yo), and Emma uses it about Mai in line 13 (sensu mo ii). Don't reach for aji: that's taste as in flavour. Also watch the false friend: sensu nai means 'no taste', not 'that doesn't make sense'. Yuki is talking casually, so drop ga; to Tanaka-san it would be sensu ga ii desu ne.

newWords.english: how, how about (dou desu ka? = how is she doing? / what do you think?)
clothes (fuku no sensu = taste in clothes)
say (itte imashita = said; iwarete imasu = gets told; itte okimasu = I'll tell her)
a joke (joudan desu yo = (she's) only joking)

script.title: Mom's busy Saturday
script.setting: A weekday evening. Yuki phones her mother to ask her out on Saturday, sure that she'll be free.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, okaasan? ne, doyoubi, dokka asobi ni ikanai?
lines.ja: もしもし、お母さん？ね、土曜日、どっか遊びに行かない？
lines.kana: もしもし、おかあさん？ね、どようび、どっかあそびにいかない？
lines.english: Hi, Mom? Hey, do you want to go out somewhere on Saturday?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: doyoubi? doyoubi wa ne, chotto isogashii no.
lines.ja: 土曜日？土曜日はね、ちょっと忙しいの。
lines.kana: どようび？どようびはね、ちょっといそがしいの。
lines.english: Saturday? Saturday I'm a bit busy, actually.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, nande? dokka asobi ni iku no?
lines.ja: え、なんで？どっか遊びに行くの？
lines.kana: え、なんで？どっかあそびにいくの？
lines.english: Huh, how come? Are you going out somewhere?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: juuji kara, satou-san to sanpo ni iku no.
lines.ja: 10時から、佐藤さんと散歩に行くの。
lines.kana: じゅうじから、さとうさんとさんぽにいくの。
lines.english: At ten I'm going for a walk with Satou-san.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sanpo ni iku dake desho?
lines.ja: 散歩に行くだけでしょ？
lines.kana: さんぽにいくだけでしょ？
lines.english: That's just a walk, though, right?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: uun. de, niji kara wa, tomodachi to eiga ni iku no.
lines.ja: ううん。で、2時からは、友達と映画に行くの。
lines.kana: ううん。で、にじからは、ともだちとえいがにいくの。
lines.english: Nope. Then at two, I'm going to the movies with a friend.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: eiga iku no? ii naa. watashi, doyoubi wa uchi de eiga miru dake da yo.
lines.ja: 映画行くの？いいなあ。私、土曜日はうちで映画見るだけだよ。
lines.kana: えいがいくの？いいなあ。わたし、どようびはうちでえいがみるだけだよ。
lines.english: You're going to the movies? Lucky you. All I'm doing on Saturday is watching a movie at home.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: eiga ni itte, shichiji kara wa minna de karaoke ni iku no.
lines.ja: 映画に行って、7時からはみんなでカラオケに行くの。
lines.kana: えいがにいって、しちじからはみんなでからおけにいくの。
lines.english: After the movie, at seven we're all going to karaoke.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto ni? okaasan ga karaoke iku no?
lines.ja: ほんとに？お母さんがカラオケ行くの？
lines.kana: ほんとに？おかあさんがからおけいくの？
lines.english: Seriously? You go to karaoke?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: iku yo. uta o utau no, kimochi ii n da kara.
lines.ja: 行くよ。歌を歌うの、気持ちいいんだから。
lines.kana: いくよ。うたをうたうの、きもちいいんだから。
lines.english: Of course I do. Singing feels great, you know.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: okaasan, watashi yori isogashii ne.
lines.ja: お母さん、私より忙しいね。
lines.kana: おかあさん、わたしよりいそがしいね。
lines.english: Mom, you're busier than I am.

lines.ja: じゃあ、ユキもカラオケ行く？
lines.kana: じゃあ、ゆきもからおけいく？

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: iku iku! jaa, shichiji ne.
lines.ja: 行く行く！じゃあ、7時ね。
lines.kana: いくいく！じゃあ、しちじね。
lines.english: I'm in! Seven, then.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, nichiyoubi wa hima da kara, yuki no uchi ni asobi ni iku ne.
lines.ja: で、日曜日は暇だから、ユキのうちに遊びに行くね。
lines.kana: で、にちようびはひまだから、ゆきのうちにあそびにいくね。
lines.english: And Sunday I'm free, so I'll come over to your place.

lines.ja: うちに？いいけど、何するの？
lines.kana: うちに？いいけど、なにするの？

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki to sanpo ni iku no. hachiji ni iku kara ne!
lines.ja: ユキと散歩に行くの。8時に行くからね！
lines.kana: ゆきとさんぽにいくの。はちじにいくからね！
lines.english: We'll go for a walk together. I'll be there at eight!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hachiji!? watashi no nichiyoubi mo, isogashiku natchatta.
lines.ja: 8時！？私の日曜日も、忙しくなっちゃった。
lines.kana: はちじ！？わたしのにちようびも、いそがしくなっちゃった。
lines.english: Eight?! Now my Sunday's busy too.

questions.english: What happens in this phone call?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Her mother is busy all Saturday, so Yuki stays in with a movie, and her mother will visit her on Sunday instead.
Yuki plans a Saturday of movies and karaoke for her mother, and on Sunday they'll both go walking with Satou-san.
Yuki asks her mother out, finds her Saturday is packed, joins her at karaoke, and gets booked for a Sunday walk.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Yuki asks her mother out (dokka asobi ni ikanai?). Lines 2-8: her mother's Saturday is full: a walk with Satou-san at ten, a movie with a friend at two, karaoke with everyone at seven. Lines 12-13: her mother asks Yuki to come to karaoke, and Yuki says iku iku. Lines 14-16: on Sunday her mother will come over to Yuki's place and take her for a walk at eight, so in line 17 Yuki's Sunday is busy too. A is wrong: watching a movie at home (line 7) was Yuki's plan before her mother asked her to karaoke, and in line 13 she says she'll come. B is wrong: the Saturday plans are her mother's own, not Yuki's. The walk with Satou-san is on Saturday at ten (line 4), and Sunday's walk is just Yuki and her mother (line 16).

questions.english: Kenta calls and asks, "nichiyoubi, uchi kuru? sora mo iru yo." (Want to come over on Sunday? Sora will be here too.) Say yes, you'll come over, using asobi ni iku.
questions.ja: 日曜日、うち来る？ソラもいるよ。
questions.kana: にちようび、うちくる？そらもいるよ。
questions.romaji: nichiyoubi, uchi kuru? sora mo iru yo.
questions.answer: Say you'll come over with asobi ni iku. Kenta asks with kuru, but you are the one going, so you answer with iku: un, asobi ni iku ne!

modelAnswers.romaji: un, asobi ni iku ne!
modelAnswers.ja: うん、遊びに行くね！
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll come over!

modelAnswers.romaji: iku iku! jaa, niji ni asobi ni iku yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 行く行く！じゃあ、2時に遊びに行くよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm in! I'll come over at two, then.

questions.explanation: asobi ni iku is also the everyday way to say you'll visit someone's place. In line 14 Yuki's mother says yuki no uchi ni asobi ni iku ne (I'll come over to your place), and in line 16 hachiji ni iku kara ne (I'll be there at eight). Kenta says kuru because you'd be coming to him, but you answer from where you are, so it's iku. English 'I'll come over' tempts asobi ni kuru, but that would mean Kenta is the one coming. Don't let English 'play' make asobi sound childish: adults say asobi ni iku all the time, for a visit like this or a fun day out. iku iku is the eager yes Yuki gives in line 13.

questions.english: Yuki's mother says, "niji kara wa, tomodachi to eiga ni iku no." What is she doing at two?
questions.ja: お母さんは2時から何をしますか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはにじからなにをしますか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa niji kara nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: Going out to the cinema with a friend.
Watching a movie at home with a friend.
Going over to a friend's place to watch a movie there.

questions.explanation: eiga ni iku is going out to see a film, at the cinema. Yuki takes it that way: eiga iku no? ii naa (line 7, You're going to the movies? Lucky you). In line 8 her mother goes straight on from the film to karaoke (eiga ni itte, then karaoke at seven). B is wrong: watching a film at home is eiga o miru, and that's Yuki's Saturday, not her mother's (line 7: uchi de eiga miru dake). C would be tomodachi no uchi de eiga o miru. eiga ni iku means the cinema, not a friend's place.

questions.english: You're putting your shoes on at the door, and Okaasan asks, "are, doko iku no?" (Oh, where are you off to?) Tell her you're just popping out for a walk.
questions.ja: あれ、どこ行くの？
questions.kana: あれ、どこいくの？
questions.romaji: are, doko iku no?
questions.answer: Say you're going for a walk with sanpo ni iku. The everyday line on the way out is chotto sanpo ni itte kuru (I'm popping out for a walk, back soon).

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto sanpo itte kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと散歩行ってくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Just popping out for a walk.

modelAnswers.romaji: tenki ii kara, chotto sanpo ni itte kuru.
modelAnswers.ja: 天気いいから、ちょっと散歩に行ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: It's nice out, so I'm going for a quick walk.

questions.explanation: sanpo is the walk, and you go on one: sanpo ni iku, as Yuki's mother says in line 4 (satou-san to sanpo ni iku no) and line 16 (yuki to sanpo ni iku no). Not sanpo o toru, copied from 'take a walk'. itte kuru (go and come back) is what you say on your way out the door, and casual speech often drops ni (sanpo itte kuru). The second model adds tenki ii (it's nice out), from an earlier chunk.

questions.english: Yuki's mother tells Yuki her plan for seven o'clock. What did she say?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: At seven we're all singing karaoke.
choices.romaji: shichiji kara wa minna de karaoke o utau no.

choices.english: At seven we're all going to karaoke.
choices.romaji: shichiji kara wa minna de karaoke ni iku no.

choices.english: At seven we're all going out.
choices.romaji: shichiji kara wa minna de asobi ni iku no.

questions.explanation: Line 8: shichiji kara wa minna de karaoke ni iku no. Karaoke is a place you go, so the noun goes straight before ni iku. Yuki echoes it in line 9 with ni dropped (okaasan ga karaoke iku no?), and her mother uses the same shape to invite her in line 12 (yuki mo karaoke iku?). A is 'sing karaoke' copied from English: karaoke o utau sounds off to many speakers. What you sing is uta, songs, which is how her mother puts it in line 10 (uta o utau no, kimochi ii n da kara). C is good Japanese for a night out, but it doesn't say where. Her mother names karaoke, and that's why Yuki is so surprised in line 9.

newWords.english: somewhere (casual for dokoka; dokka asobi ni ikanai? = want to go out somewhere?)
just, only (eiga miru dake = just watching a movie)
than (watashi yori isogashii = busier than me)

script.title: One more question

lines.kana: ねえちゃん、ちょっといい？しつもんがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Sis, got a sec? I've got a question.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii yo. nani?
lines.ja: いいよ。何？
lines.kana: いいよ。なに？
lines.english: Sure. What is it?

lines.speaker: kenji

lines.kana: ねえちゃんって、えいごはなせるよね？
lines.english: You can speak English, right?

lines.ja: あ、話すテストね。
lines.kana: あ、はなすてすとね。
lines.english: Oh, a speaking test.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: daijoubu. mijikai kotae de ii n da yo. demo, kotaenai no wa dame.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。短い答えでいいんだよ。でも、答えないのはダメ。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。みじかいこたえでいいんだよ。でも、こたえないのはだめ。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou. jaa, nanika shitsumon aru?
lines.ja: ありがとう。じゃあ、何か質問ある？
lines.kana: ありがとう。じゃあ、なにかしつもんある？
lines.english: Thank you. Now, any questions?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: uun, nai. metcha benkyou ni natta. jaa, oyasumi.
lines.ja: ううん、ない。めっちゃ勉強になった。じゃあ、おやすみ。
lines.kana: ううん、ない。めっちゃべんきょうになった。じゃあ、おやすみ。
lines.english: Nope. I learned loads. Okay, night.

lines.romaji: e, chotto! benkyou wa? tesuto, ashita da yo ne?
lines.ja: え、ちょっと！勉強は？テスト、明日だよね？
lines.kana: え、ちょっと！べんきょうは？てすと、あしただよね？
lines.english: Hey, hold on! What about studying? Your test is tomorrow, right?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shita yo. datte ima, benkyou ni natta mon.
lines.ja: したよ。だって今、勉強になったもん。
lines.kana: したよ。だっていま、べんきょうになったもん。
lines.english: I did study. I just learned loads, didn't I?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore wa benkyou shita tte iwanai no!
lines.ja: それは勉強したって言わないの！
lines.kana: それはべんきょうしたっていわないの！
lines.english: That doesn't count as studying!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, neechan. mou hitotsu shitsumon ga aru n da kedo.
lines.ja: あ、ねえちゃん。もう一つ質問があるんだけど。
lines.kana: あ、ねえちゃん。もうひとつしつもんがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Oh, Sis. I've got one more question.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nani? eigo?
lines.ja: 何？英語？
lines.kana: なに？えいご？
lines.english: What? About English?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: uun. onaka hetta. nanika aru?
lines.ja: ううん。お腹へった。何かある？
lines.kana: ううん。おなかへった。なにかある？
lines.english: Nope. I'm starving. Is there anything to eat?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sono shitsumon ni wa kotaemasen!
lines.ja: その質問には答えません！
lines.kana: そのしつもんにはこたえません！
lines.english: That is not a question I will be answering!

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki practises English questions with Kenji, and he stays up late studying for his test.
Yuki gives Kenji a tip for his speaking test; he calls that studying, says goodnight, then asks for food.
Kenji explains to Yuki how to answer questions in English at work, and she thanks him for it.

questions.explanation: Line 5: Kenji has a test tomorrow where he has to answer questions in English, and in line 7 he says he can't speak English, so he won't be able to answer them. Line 8: Yuki's tip: short answers are fine, but not answering is a no-no. Line 11: he says he learned loads (metcha benkyou ni natta) and says goodnight. Lines 12-14: when Yuki asks about studying, he claims that learning from her tip counts (ima benkyou ni natta mon), and she tells him it doesn't (sore wa benkyou shita tte iwanai no). Lines 15-18: his 'one more question' is that he's hungry, and she refuses to answer it. A is wrong: nobody practises any English, and Kenji heads off to bed (line 11: jaa, oyasumi) without studying. C swaps the two of them: Yuki is the one who speaks English at work (line 4), the test is Kenji's (line 5), and the tip comes from Yuki (line 8).

questions.english: At the end of a meeting, Tanaka-san asks the room, "dewa, nanika shitsumon wa arimasu ka?" (Well then, are there any questions?) You have one. Say so.
questions.ja: では、何か質問はありますか？
questions.kana: では、なにかしつもんはありますか？
questions.romaji: dewa, nanika shitsumon wa arimasu ka?
questions.answer: Say you have a question with shitsumon ga aru, in polite form for Tanaka-san: hai, hitotsu shitsumon ga arimasu.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, hitotsu shitsumon ga arimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、一つ質問があります。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, I have one question.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, sumimasen. shitsumon ga aru n desu kedo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、すみません。質問があるんですけど。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, excuse me. I have a question.

questions.explanation: A question you have is aru: shitsumon ga arimasu, or shitsumon ga aru n desu kedo to lead into it. English 'have' points to motsu, but shitsumon o motte imasu is not how it's said. Kenji opens with the casual version in line 1 (shitsumon ga aru n da kedo) and again in line 15 (mou hitotsu shitsumon ga aru n da kedo). Yuki's nanika shitsumon aru? in line 10 is the casual version of Tanaka-san's question, with ga dropped after nanika. Once you've said it, go on and ask: asking is shitsumon suru, or just kiku.

questions.english: Kenji tells Yuki why he's worried about tomorrow's test. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンジくんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-kun wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I won't be able to answer the questions (with o, as in English 'answer the questions').
I won't be able to ask any questions.
I won't be able to answer the questions.

questions.explanation: Line 7: boku, eigo hanasenai kara, shitsumon ni kotaerarenai yo. In Japanese you answer to a question, so shitsumon takes ni: shitsumon ni kotaeru, here in the can't-form kotaerarenai. Line 5 has the same ni (eigo de shitsumon ni kotaeru tesuto), and so does Yuki's last line (sono shitsumon ni wa kotaemasen). A is English 'answer the questions' put into Japanese word for word, with o: with kotaeru, o marks what you give as the answer (namae o kotaeru, give your name), never the question. B, shitsumon dekinai, means he can't ask questions. In the test the teacher asks, and Kenji's worry is answering.

questions.english: At work, Mai covers the phone with her hand and whispers, "ne, eigo dekiru? eigo no denwa na n da kedo." (Hey, can you do English? This call's in English.) You can speak a little. Tell her.
questions.ja: ね、英語できる？英語の電話なんだけど。
questions.kana: ね、えいごできる？えいごのでんわなんだけど。
questions.romaji: ne, eigo dekiru? eigo no denwa na n da kedo.
questions.answer: Say you can speak a little English, with hanasu in its can-form: un, eigo wa chotto dake hanaseru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, eigo wa chotto dake hanaseru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、英語はちょっとだけ話せるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I can speak a little English.

modelAnswers.romaji: eigo? sukoshi nara hanaseru kedo.
modelAnswers.ja: 英語？少しなら話せるけど。
modelAnswers.english: English? I can speak a bit, I guess.

questions.explanation: Being able to speak a language is the can-form of hanasu: hanaseru (polite hanasemasu). Kenji asks it that way in line 3 (eigo hanaseru yo ne?), Yuki answers hanaseru yo in line 4, and Kenji's hanasenai in line 7 is the negative. Plain hanasu says you do speak it, like Yuki's shigoto de mo hanashiteru (I speak it at work, line 4), not that you can. Mai's eigo dekiru? asks the same thing as eigo hanaseru?, so answering with hanaseru fits. eigo de hanasu would be talking in English right now.

questions.english: Yuki asks about studying, and Kenji answers, "shita yo. datte ima, benkyou ni natta mon." Has he actually studied for the test?
questions.ja: ケンジくんは、勉強しましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんは、べんきょうしましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-kun wa, benkyou shimashita ka?

choices.english: No. Yuki's tip taught him something, but he hasn't sat down and studied.
Yes. He studied on his own earlier that evening, before he asked Yuki.
Yes. He practised answering English questions with Yuki.

questions.explanation: benkyou ni natta means something was instructive: he learned from it. It's the thanks phrase he uses for Yuki's tip in line 9 (sore, benkyou ni naru) and line 11 (metcha benkyou ni natta). benkyou shita means he sat down and studied, and in line 13 Kenji passes one off as the other. Yuki's line 14, sore wa benkyou shita tte iwanai no, says exactly that: that isn't called studying. B is wrong: his only reason is what he learned just now (ima), and nobody mentions him studying earlier. C is wrong: Yuki only gave him a tip; they never practise, and he says goodnight right after (line 11).

newWords.english: big sister (what a younger brother or sister calls her; casual)
something, anything (nanika aru? = is there anything?)
say, call; X tte iwanai = that isn't called X

script.title: A quick recovery
script.setting: A weekday morning in the family kitchen. Okaasan and Yuki are getting ready for work when Kenji shuffles in and announces he's too ill for school.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: aa, koshi itai.
lines.ja: ああ、腰痛い。
lines.kana: ああ、こしいたい。
lines.english: Ugh, my back hurts.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: daijoubu? watashi mo kata kotteru. kinou zutto shigoto datta kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫？私も肩凝ってる。昨日ずっと仕事だったから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ？わたしもかたこってる。きのうずっとしごとだったから。
lines.english: You okay? Me too, my shoulders are all stiff. I was working all day yesterday.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: a, kenji, ohayou. mou shichiji han da yo.
lines.ja: あ、ケンジ、おはよう。もう七時半だよ。
lines.kana: あ、けんじ、おはよう。もうしちじはんだよ。
lines.english: Oh, Kenji, morning. It's already half past seven.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: kyou, gakkou ikanai. onaka itai.
lines.ja: 今日、学校行かない。お腹痛い。
lines.kana: きょう、がっこういかない。おなかいたい。
lines.english: I'm not going to school today. My stomach hurts.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e, onaka itai no? daijoubu?
lines.ja: え、お腹痛いの？大丈夫？
lines.kana: え、おなかいたいの？だいじょうぶ？
lines.english: Oh no, your stomach hurts? Are you all right?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: daijoubu ja nai. atama mo itai shi.
lines.ja: 大丈夫じゃない。頭も痛いし。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶじゃない。あたまもいたいし。
lines.english: No, I'm not. And my head hurts too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: atama mo itai no? nodo wa?
lines.ja: 頭も痛いの？喉は？
lines.kana: あたまもいたいの？のどは？
lines.english: Your head hurts too? What about your throat?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nodo mo, itai kana.
lines.ja: 喉も、痛いかな。
lines.kana: のども、いたいかな。
lines.english: My throat... hurts too, I guess?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kana? jibun no nodo da yo?
lines.ja: かな？自分の喉だよ？
lines.kana: かな？じぶんののどだよ？
lines.english: You guess? It's your own throat!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: itai. a, koshi mo itai. kata mo kotteru.
lines.ja: 痛い。あ、腰も痛い。肩も凝ってる。
lines.kana: いたい。あ、こしもいたい。かたもこってる。
lines.english: It hurts. Oh, and my back hurts. And my shoulders are stiff.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: koshi itai no wa okaasan da yo. kata kotteru no wa watashi!
lines.ja: 腰痛いのはお母さんだよ。肩凝ってるのは私！
lines.kana: こしいたいのはおかあさんだよ。かたこってるのはわたし！
lines.english: Mom's the one with the bad back! I'm the one with stiff shoulders!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo, okaasan mo yuki mo, shigoto ni iku n da yo.
lines.ja: でも、お母さんもユキも、仕事に行くんだよ。
lines.kana: でも、おかあさんもゆきも、しごとにいくんだよ。
lines.english: And still, Yuki and I are both going to work, you know.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ne, kenji. kyou, karaoke iku n ja nakatta?
lines.ja: ね、ケンジ。今日、カラオケ行くんじゃなかった？
lines.kana: ね、けんじ。きょう、からおけいくんじゃなかった？
lines.english: Hey, Kenji. Weren't you going to karaoke today?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, karaoke wa iku.
lines.ja: あ、カラオケは行く。
lines.kana: あ、からおけはいく。
lines.english: Oh, karaoke, yeah, I'm going to that.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e? nodo itai noni?
lines.ja: え？喉痛いのに？
lines.kana: え？のどいたいのに？
lines.english: Huh? With a sore throat?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: onaka mo nodo mo itai n da yo ne? jaa, karaoke mo dame ne.
lines.ja: お腹も喉も痛いんだよね？じゃあ、カラオケもダメね。
lines.kana: おなかものどもいたいんだよね？じゃあ、からおけもだめね。
lines.english: Your stomach and throat hurt, don't they? Then no karaoke either.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: onaka mo atama mo, mou itakunai.
lines.ja: お腹も頭も、もう痛くない。
lines.kana: おなかもあたまも、もういたくない。
lines.english: My stomach and my head don't hurt anymore.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, gakkou ni ikeru ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、学校に行けるね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、がっこうにいけるね。
lines.english: Well then, you can go to school, can't you?

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji really has a stomachache, so Okaasan lets him stay home from school but says no to karaoke.
Kenji says everything hurts so he can skip school, but once karaoke is off too, he's suddenly fine to go.
Kenji wants to skip karaoke because of his sore throat, so Yuki and Okaasan tell him to rest at home.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenji won't go to school because his stomach hurts (kyou, gakkou ikanai. onaka itai). Then the list grows: his head (line 6), his throat, though he isn't sure (line 8: nodo mo, itai kana), and even Okaasan's back and Yuki's shoulders (line 10), which Yuki points out in line 11. Lines 13-14: he still wants to go to karaoke (karaoke wa iku). In line 16 Okaasan says no karaoke either, and in line 17 nothing hurts any more (onaka mo atama mo, mou itakunai), so in line 18 he can go to school. A is wrong: he isn't really ill, since he gets better the moment karaoke is called off, and Okaasan never lets him stay home. C is wrong: Kenji wants to go to karaoke; Okaasan is the one who calls it off.

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "kyou, karaoke iku?" (Coming to karaoke today?) You've got a headache. Say you're not going, and why.
questions.ja: 今日、カラオケ行く？
questions.kana: きょう、からおけいく？
questions.romaji: kyou, karaoke iku?
questions.answer: Turn him down and give the reason with atama + itai, adding n da to explain: gomen, kyou wa ikanai. atama itai n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou wa ikanai. atama itai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日は行かない。頭痛いんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'm not going today. I've got a headache.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, kyou wa chotto atama ga itai n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、今日はちょっと頭が痛いんです。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I have a bit of a headache today.

questions.explanation: There is no 'have' in Japanese here: the head is what hurts, atama ga itai, and in casual talk ga drops (atama itai), as in Kenji's line 6 (atama mo itai shi) and Yuki's line 7 (atama mo itai no?). Don't build it with aru or motsu the way English uses 'have'. N da (n desu when polite) turns the headache into your reason for not coming. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: You put your chopsticks down after a few bites, and Okaasan asks, "e, mou gochisousama? daijoubu?" (What, finished already? Are you okay?) Tell her your stomach hurts.
questions.ja: え、もうごちそうさま？大丈夫？
questions.kana: え、もうごちそうさま？だいじょうぶ？
questions.romaji: e, mou gochisousama? daijoubu?
questions.answer: Say your stomach hurts with onaka + itai, ga dropped in casual talk: un, chotto onaka itai n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, chotto onaka itai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、ちょっとお腹痛いんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, my stomach hurts a bit.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, daijoubu ja nai. onaka itai.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、大丈夫じゃない。お腹痛い。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm not okay. My stomach hurts.

questions.explanation: The everyday tummy ache is onaka ga itai, usually onaka itai in casual talk, as in Kenji's line 4 (onaka itai) and Okaasan's line 5 (onaka itai no?). The dictionary word i (stomach) is heard too (i ga itai), but onaka is the everyday word, and the natural one at the table. N da makes it the reason you've stopped eating. The second model answers the daijoubu? part, the way Kenji does in line 6 (daijoubu ja nai).

questions.english: When Kenji says he's still going to karaoke, Yuki says "e? nodo itai noni?" What does she mean?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、何が言いたいですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なにがいいたいですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nani ga iitai desu ka?

choices.english: Singing at karaoke is what made his throat sore in the first place.
She'll go to karaoke in his place so he can rest his voice.
If his throat really hurt, he wouldn't be so keen to go and sing.

questions.explanation: Line 15: nodo itai is a sore throat, and noni is 'even though': 'even though your throat hurts?' A sore throat is exactly what keeps you away from karaoke, so Kenji's quick 'karaoke wa iku' (line 14) gives him away. It fits line 8, where he wasn't even sure his throat hurt (nodo mo, itai kana), and Yuki teased him for it (line 9: kana? jibun no nodo da yo?). A is wrong: nobody says how his throat got sore. B is wrong: Yuki never offers to go, and in line 16 Okaasan calls karaoke off.

questions.english: At the very start, Okaasan groans about where it hurts. What did she say?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Ugh, my back hurts.
Ugh, my upper back hurts.
Ugh, my back's gone stiff.

questions.explanation: Line 1: aa, koshi itai. Koshi is the lower back and hips, the part that aches after lifting or a long day, and what English means by plain 'my back hurts'. B is that English 'back' turned into senaka, which is the upper and middle back, higher than where Okaasan means. C borrows koru from Yuki's stiff shoulders in line 2 (kata kotteru), but Okaasan said itai: her back hurts. Yuki sorts the two out in line 11 (koshi itai no wa okaasan da yo. kata kotteru no wa watashi!).

questions.english: The morning after a long day at your desk, your coworker Mai asks, "kinou, zutto shigoto datta yo ne. daijoubu?" (You were working all day yesterday, right? You okay?) Say you're fine, but your shoulders are stiff.
questions.ja: 昨日、ずっと仕事だったよね。大丈夫？
questions.kana: きのう、ずっとしごとだったよね。だいじょうぶ？
questions.romaji: kinou, zutto shigoto datta yo ne. daijoubu?
questions.answer: Say you're fine, then use kata with the verb koru: un, daijoubu. demo, kata kotteru.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daijoubu. demo, kata kotteru.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大丈夫。でも、肩凝ってる。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm fine. My shoulders are stiff, though.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu desu. demo, chotto kata ga korimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫です。でも、ちょっと肩が凝りました。
modelAnswers.english: I'm fine. My shoulders have got a bit stiff, though.

questions.explanation: English says 'stiff', an adjective, but Japanese uses a verb: kata ga koru. Kotteru means they're stiff now and kotta / korimashita means they've gone stiff; there's no itai in it. That's Yuki's line 2, after a day of work (watashi mo kata kotteru), and Kenji's borrowed complaint in line 10 (kata mo kotteru). The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

newWords.english: say (nan to iimashita ka? = what did they say?; nani ga iitai? = what are they getting at?)

script.title: Who sent you over?
script.setting: A Saturday evening party at Kenta and Sora's flat. Yuki brought her coworker Mai, then spent the whole evening catching up with Kenta. Mai has been standing on her own when Sora comes over.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ano, sumimasen. yuki-san no tomodachi desu ka?
lines.ja: あの、すみません。ユキさんの友達ですか？
lines.kana: あの、すみません。ゆきさんのともだちですか？
lines.english: Um, excuse me. Are you a friend of Yuki's?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, hai. yuki-san to wa, shigoto de.
lines.ja: あ、はい。ユキさんとは、仕事で。
lines.kana: あ、はい。ゆきさんとは、しごとで。
lines.english: Oh, yes. We know each other from work.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: boku, sora desu. kenta to koko ni sunderu n desu. namae, oshiete moraemasu ka?
lines.ja: 僕、ソラです。ケンタとここに住んでるんです。名前、教えてもらえますか？
lines.kana: ぼく、そらです。けんたとここにすんでるんです。なまえ、おしえてもらえますか？
lines.english: I'm Sora. I live here with Kenta. Can I ask your name?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kimura mai desu. a, koe kakete kurete, arigatou gozaimasu.
lines.ja: 木村マイです。あ、声かけてくれて、ありがとうございます。
lines.kana: きむらまいです。あ、こえかけてくれて、ありがとうございます。
lines.english: I'm Mai Kimura. Oh, and thanks for coming over to say hi.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ie ie. yuki-san to kenta, zutto mukashi no hanashi shiteru n desu yo.
lines.ja: いえいえ。ユキさんとケンタ、ずっと昔の話してるんですよ。
lines.kana: いえいえ。ゆきさんとけんた、ずっとむかしのはなししてるんですよ。
lines.english: Not at all. Yuki and Kenta have been going on about the old days all evening.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ano futari, gakkou de tomodachi ni natta n desu yo ne. ii naa.
lines.ja: あの二人、学校で友達になったんですよね。いいなあ。
lines.kana: あのふたり、がっこうでともだちになったんですよね。いいなあ。
lines.english: Those two became friends at school, right? Lucky them.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii desu yo ne. boku, koko ni sunde ninen, tomodachi, kenta shika dekitenai n desu yo.
lines.ja: いいですよね。僕、ここに住んで二年、友達、ケンタしかできてないんですよ。
lines.kana: いいですよね。ぼく、ここにすんでにねん、ともだち、けんたしかできてないんですよ。
lines.english: I know, right? I've lived here two years, and Kenta's the only friend I've made.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: watashi mo desu. shigoto ga isogashikute, deai ga nai n desu.
lines.ja: 私もです。仕事が忙しくて、出会いがないんです。
lines.kana: わたしもです。しごとがいそがしくて、であいがないんです。
lines.english: Same here. Work keeps me so busy, I never meet anyone.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sore ni boku, jibun kara koe kakeru no, dame na n desu yo.
lines.ja: それに僕、自分から声かけるの、だめなんですよ。
lines.kana: それにぼく、じぶんからこえかけるの、だめなんですよ。
lines.english: Plus I'm hopeless at going up to people.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? demo, ima koe kakete kureta noni.
lines.ja: え？でも、今声かけてくれたのに。
lines.kana: え？でも、いまこえかけてくれたのに。
lines.english: Huh? But you just came over and talked to me.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, sore wa, kenta ga, yuki no tomodachi ni koe kakete tte.
lines.ja: あ、それは、ケンタが、ユキの友達に声かけてって。
lines.kana: あ、それは、けんたが、ゆきのともだちにこえかけてって。
lines.english: Oh, that. Kenta told me to go and talk to Yuki's friend.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, watashi mo desu! yuki-san ga, sora-san no namae oshiete kurete, koe kakete mite tte.
lines.ja: え、私もです！ユキさんが、ソラさんの名前教えてくれて、声かけてみてって。
lines.kana: え、わたしもです！ゆきさんが、そらさんのなまえおしえてくれて、こえかけてみてって。
lines.english: What, me too! Yuki told me your name and said I should try going over to you.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ano futari! jaa, kimura-san, kyou wa deai, arimashita ne.
lines.ja: あの二人！じゃあ、木村さん、今日は出会い、ありましたね。
lines.kana: あのふたり！じゃあ、きむらさん、きょうはであい、ありましたね。
lines.english: Those two! Well, Kimura-san, looks like you did meet someone today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, gomen ne! a, sora-kun, mai to hanashita?
lines.ja: マイ、ごめんね！あ、ソラくん、マイと話した？
lines.kana: まい、ごめんね！あ、そらくん、まいとはなした？
lines.english: Mai, sorry! Oh, Sora, have you talked to Mai?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: hai. namae mo oshiete moraimashita yo.
lines.ja: はい。名前も教えてもらいましたよ。
lines.kana: はい。なまえもおしえてもらいましたよ。
lines.english: Yep. She's even told me her name.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, mou? jaa, futari, tomodachi ni natta no?
lines.ja: え、もう？じゃあ、二人、友達になったの？
lines.kana: え、もう？じゃあ、ふたり、ともだちになったの？
lines.english: What, already? So, are you two friends now?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, tomodachi dekita yo. yuki-san to kenta-san no okage de ne.
lines.ja: うん、友達できたよ。ユキさんとケンタさんのおかげでね。
lines.kana: うん、ともだちできたよ。ゆきさんとけんたさんのおかげでね。
lines.english: Yep, I've made a friend. All thanks to you and Kenta.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: desho? kyou wa ii deai ga aru kamo tte, itta jan.
lines.ja: でしょ？今日はいい出会いがあるかもって、言ったじゃん。
lines.kana: でしょ？きょうはいいであいがあるかもって、いったじゃん。
lines.english: See? I told you you might meet someone nice today.

questions.english: What happens at the party?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora comes over to talk to Mai; they find out Kenta and Yuki each told them to talk to the other, and they end up friends.
Mai goes over to Sora because Yuki told her to, and they find out they went to the same school.
Sora asks Mai her name, but she's upset when she finds out Kenta sent him over.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: Sora goes up to Mai and asks her name, and she thanks him for coming over (koe kakete kurete). Line 11: Kenta told him to (yuki no tomodachi ni koe kakete tte). Line 12: Yuki told Mai the same about Sora (koe kakete mite tte). Lines 16-17: Yuki asks if they're friends now, and Mai says she's made a friend (tomodachi dekita yo). B is wrong: Sora is the one who comes over (line 10: ima koe kakete kureta noni), and the school is where Yuki and Kenta became friends (line 6). C is wrong: Mai isn't upset. She says Yuki did the same thing to her (line 12: watashi mo desu!), and in line 17 she thanks them both, with a wink (okage de ne).

questions.english: You moved to a new town a month ago. Kenta asks, "koko ni kite, mou ikkagetsu da ne. tomodachi wa?" (It's been a month since you got here. Any friends?) You've made a couple. Tell him.
questions.ja: ここに来て、もう一か月だね。友達は？
questions.kana: ここにきて、もういっかげつだね。ともだちは？
questions.romaji: koko ni kite, mou ikkagetsu da ne. tomodachi wa?
questions.answer: Say friends have come along, with dekiru in the past: un, tomodachi dekita yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, mou tomodachi dekita yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、もう友達できたよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I've already made some friends.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, tomodachi ga dekimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、友達ができました。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, I've made some friends.

questions.explanation: Gaining friends takes tomodachi ga dekiru, and once it has happened it's past: dekita. That's Mai's line 17 (un, tomodachi dekita yo), and line 7 has the not-yet version (kenta shika dekitenai: Kenta's the only one I've made). English 'make' pulls toward tomodachi o tsukuru, but that's for setting out to make friends (tomodachi tsukuritai), not for saying you have some. tomodachi ni natta needs a particular person (X to tomodachi ni natta), and Kenta asked about friends in general. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Satou-san.

questions.english: Yuki comes back and finds Sora already knows Mai's name. What does she ask the two of them?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: So, did you two go and make friends?
So, did you two make someone your friend?
choices.romaji: jaa, futari, tomodachi ni shita no?

choices.english: So, are you two friends now?
choices.romaji: jaa, futari, tomodachi ni natta no?

questions.explanation: Line 16: Yuki asks whether the two of them have become friends with each other, so it's tomodachi ni naru: futari, tomodachi ni natta no? It's the same shape as line 6, where Mai says Yuki and Kenta gakkou de tomodachi ni natta (became friends at school). Mai answers from her own side in line 17 (tomodachi dekita yo: I've made a friend), but that's her reply, not Yuki's question. A is English 'make friends' turned into tsukuru: natives say tomodachi tsukuritai for wanting to go out and find friends, not for two people who've just hit it off. B is 'make' turned into ni suru, the 'make' partner of ni naru: tomodachi ni suru sounds like turning someone into your friend, not two people becoming friends.

questions.english: You're at Yuki's party, and a woman you haven't met (it's Mai) comes over and says, "a, hajimemashite. yuki-san no tomodachi desu." (Oh, hi. I'm a friend of Yuki's.) She hasn't said her name. Ask her what it is.
questions.ja: あ、はじめまして。ユキさんの友達です。
questions.kana: あ、はじめまして。ゆきさんのともだちです。
questions.romaji: a, hajimemashite. yuki-san no tomodachi desu.
questions.answer: Ask her to tell you her name, with oshieru: namae, oshiete moraemasu ka?

modelAnswers.romaji: hajimemashite. namae, oshiete moraemasu ka?
modelAnswers.ja: はじめまして。名前、教えてもらえますか？
modelAnswers.english: Nice to meet you. Could I ask your name?

modelAnswers.romaji: yoroshiku. namae oshiete kureru?
modelAnswers.ja: よろしく。名前教えてくれる？
modelAnswers.english: Nice to meet you. What's your name?

questions.explanation: Asking someone to tell you their name takes oshieru, the verb for passing on information: Sora does exactly this in line 3 (namae, oshiete moraemasu ka?). English 'tell me your name' points to iu, but namae o iu is saying a name out loud, not sharing it with someone. Line 12 has the same verb for passing a name along: yuki-san ga sora-san no namae oshiete kurete (Yuki told me your name). The second model is the casual version, once a party has loosened up.

questions.english: At a party, Mai keeps glancing over at Sora but doesn't move. She tells you, "sora-kun to hanashitai kedo, jibun kara wa chotto." (I'd like to talk to Sora, but going over myself is a bit...) Encourage her to go up to him.
questions.ja: ソラくんと話したいけど、自分からはちょっと。
questions.kana: そらくんとはなしたいけど、じぶんからはちょっと。
questions.romaji: sora-kun to hanashitai kedo, jibun kara wa chotto.
questions.answer: Tell her to go and speak to him, with koe o kakeru: koe kakete mite yo!

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu da yo. koe kakete mite yo!
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫だよ。声かけてみてよ！
modelAnswers.english: You'll be fine. Go and say hi!

modelAnswers.romaji: jibun kara koe kakete mitara?
modelAnswers.ja: 自分から声かけてみたら？
modelAnswers.english: Why don't you go up to him yourself?

questions.explanation: Going up to someone to start a conversation is koe o kakeru, literally putting your voice on them. Yuki says the same thing to Mai in line 12 (koe kakete mite: try going over to him), and Sora admits in line 9 that he's bad at it (jibun kara koe kakeru no, dame). English 'talk to' leads to hanasu, which is fine once you're talking: Mai already said she wants to hanasu with him. Getting the conversation started is koe kakeru.

questions.english: Mai tells Sora that work keeps her busy, and then says "deai ga nai n desu." What does she mean?
questions.ja: マイさんは、何がないんですか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、なにがないんですか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, nani ga nai n desu ka?

choices.english: She's so busy she never gets to see her friends.
She never gets the chance to meet anyone new.
She hasn't had a chance to talk to anyone at the party tonight.

questions.explanation: Line 8: a deai is an encounter with someone new, and deai ga nai is the stock complaint 'I never meet anyone'. Her life is work and home, with no new people in it, the same as Sora, whose only friend in two years is Kenta (line 7). A is English 'I never meet anyone' taken literally (dare ni mo awanai), which sounds like she never sees people at all, and she still sees Yuki. C is about tonight, but Mai is talking about life in general. Sora turns it around in line 13 (kyou wa deai, arimashita ne: well, you met someone today), and Yuki in line 18 (ii deai ga aru kamo: you might meet someone nice).

newWords.english: long ago, the old days (mukashi no hanashi = talk about old times)
two people; the two of them (ano futari = those two)
only (with a negative: kenta shika dekitenai = Kenta's the only one I've made)
thanks to (X no okage de = thanks to X)

script.title: Mom knows this tune
script.setting: A rainy Saturday at home. Kenji's soccer with his friends is rained off, so he has been on his video game all morning when his mother comes into the living room, where the old family piano stands.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji, mada geemu shiteru no?
lines.ja: ケンジ、まだゲームしてるの？
lines.kana: けんじ、まだげーむしてるの？
lines.english: Kenji, are you still on that game?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. datte, ame futteru shi.
lines.ja: うん。だって、雨降ってるし。
lines.kana: うん。だって、あめふってるし。
lines.english: Yeah. I mean, it's raining.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kyou wa sakkaa shinai no?
lines.ja: 今日はサッカーしないの？
lines.kana: きょうはさっかーしないの？
lines.english: No soccer today?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shinai yo. minna mo uchi de geemu shiteru.
lines.ja: しないよ。みんなも家でゲームしてる。
lines.kana: しないよ。みんなもうちでげーむしてる。
lines.english: Nope. Everyone else is at home gaming too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, piano hiite miru? mukashi naratteta n da kara.
lines.ja: じゃあ、ピアノ弾いてみる？昔習ってたんだから。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ぴあのひいてみる？むかしならってたんだから。
lines.english: Then why not have a go on the piano? You took lessons, after all.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: naratteta kedo, mou hikenai yo. zutto hiitenai shi.
lines.ja: 習ってたけど、もう弾けないよ。ずっと弾いてないし。
lines.kana: ならってたけど、もうひけないよ。ずっとひいてないし。
lines.english: I did, but I can't play anymore. I haven't touched it in ages.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: okaasan mo mukashi, piano naratteta n da yo.
lines.ja: お母さんも昔、ピアノ習ってたんだよ。
lines.kana: おかあさんもむかし、ぴあのならってたんだよ。
lines.english: I took piano lessons too, you know, back in the day.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, honto ni? okaasan, piano hikeru no?
lines.ja: え、ほんとに？お母さん、ピアノ弾けるの？
lines.kana: え、ほんとに？おかあさん、ぴあのひけるの？
lines.english: Wait, really? Mom, you can play the piano?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hikeru yo. jaa, chotto hiku ne.
lines.ja: 弾けるよ。じゃあ、ちょっと弾くね。
lines.kana: ひけるよ。じゃあ、ちょっとひくね。
lines.english: Of course I can. Here, I'll play you a bit.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e! sore, kono geemu no kyoku da!
lines.ja: え！それ、このゲームの曲だ！
lines.kana: え！それ、このげーむのきょくだ！
lines.english: Whoa! That's the music from this game!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: un. kenji ga zutto geemu shiteru kara, oboechatta.
lines.ja: うん。ケンジがずっとゲームしてるから、覚えちゃった。
lines.kana: うん。けんじがずっとげーむしてるから、おぼえちゃった。
lines.english: Yep. You're on that game all the time, so I picked it up.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: okaasan, metcha jouzu da ne.
lines.ja: お母さん、めっちゃ上手だね。
lines.kana: おかあさん、めっちゃじょうずだね。
lines.english: Mom, you're really good.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji mo hiite miru? oshieru yo.
lines.ja: ケンジも弾いてみる？教えるよ。
lines.kana: けんじもひいてみる？おしえるよ。
lines.english: Want to try playing it? I'll teach you.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un! a, ame yanda. jaa, sakkaa suru!
lines.ja: うん！あ、雨やんだ。じゃあ、サッカーする！
lines.kana: うん！あ、あめやんだ。じゃあ、さっかーする！
lines.english: Yeah! Oh, the rain's stopped. Right, I'm off to play soccer!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e? piano wa?
lines.ja: え？ピアノは？
lines.kana: え？ぴあのは？
lines.english: What? What about the piano?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ashita hiku! itte kimasu!
lines.ja: 明日弾く！行ってきます！
lines.kana: あしたひく！いってきます！
lines.english: I'll play tomorrow! Bye!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hai hai. ki o tsukete ne.
lines.ja: はいはい。気をつけてね。
lines.kana: はいはい。きをつけてね。
lines.english: Yes, yes. Be careful, okay?

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji's mom finds out he can still play the piano, and he plays her the music from his game before going out to play soccer.
Kenji's mom tells him to stop gaming and go to his piano lesson, but he goes to play soccer with his friends instead.
Kenji is gaming because of the rain. His mom plays his game's music on the piano and offers to teach him, but when the rain stops he runs off to play soccer.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: soccer is off because it's raining (ame futteru shi, sakkaa shinai no? / shinai yo), so Kenji is gaming. Lines 7-9: his mom took piano lessons too (piano naratteta) and can still play (hikeru yo). Lines 10-11: what she plays is the music from his game, which she picked up from hearing it all the time. Line 13: she offers to teach him (oshieru yo). Lines 14-16: the rain stops (ame yanda), he goes to play soccer (sakkaa suru!) and puts the piano off till tomorrow (ashita hiku!). A is wrong: Kenji says he can't play anymore (line 6: mou hikenai yo), and it's his mom who plays. B is wrong: there's no lesson today. The lessons were long ago (mukashi naratteta), and his mom only suggests he try the piano at home.

questions.english: Kenji is amazed that his mom can play the music from his game. She says "kenji ga zutto geemu shiteru kara, oboechatta." How does she know the tune?
questions.ja: なんでお母さんはこの曲が弾けるんですか？
questions.kana: なんでおかあさんはこのきょくがひけるんですか？
questions.romaji: nande okaasan wa kono kyoku ga hikeru n desu ka?

choices.english: Kenji is on that game all the time, and she picked the tune up from hearing it.
She plays the game herself when Kenji isn't around.
She learned it in her piano lessons years ago.

questions.explanation: Line 11: kenji ga zutto geemu shiteru is 'Kenji is gaming all the time': geemu (o) suru in its -teru form, with zutto for 'constantly'. Because the game music is always on, it stuck (oboechatta). B is wrong: kenji ga makes Kenji the one gaming, not her. C mixes up the two kinds of learning: she did take piano lessons as a girl (line 7: piano naratteta), but she picked this tune up by ear, which is oboeru, not narau.

questions.english: Kenta asks, "kinou, nani shiteta?" (What were you up to yesterday?) You spent the day playing soccer with friends. Tell him.
questions.ja: 昨日、何してた？
questions.kana: きのう、なにしてた？
questions.romaji: kinou, nani shiteta?
questions.answer: Say you were playing soccer, using sakkaa with suru in its -teta form: tomodachi to sakkaa shiteta yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: tomodachi to sakkaa shiteta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 友達とサッカーしてたよ。
modelAnswers.english: I was playing soccer with friends.

modelAnswers.romaji: kinou wa tomodachi to sakkaa o shitemashita.
modelAnswers.ja: 昨日は友達とサッカーをしてました。
modelAnswers.english: Yesterday I was playing soccer with friends.

questions.explanation: A sport takes suru: sakkaa (o) suru, with o usually dropped in casual talk, as in line 3 (kyou wa sakkaa shinai no?) and line 14 (jaa, sakkaa suru!). Shiteta is 'was doing'. Don't let English 'play' pull you to asobu: sakkaa o asobu isn't Japanese, and tomodachi to asonda only says you hung out with friends, not what you did. The polite version suits someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: When Kenji hears that his mom took piano lessons too, what does he ask her?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは、お母さんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんは、おかあさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa, okaasan ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Mom, do you do piano?
Mom, you can play the piano?
Mom, you can play around on the piano?

questions.explanation: Line 8: okaasan, piano hikeru no? Hiku is the verb for actually playing a keyboard or string instrument, and hikeru is 'can play'. His mom answers with the same word (line 9: hikeru yo). A carries suru over from sports and games (sakkaa shinai no?, geemu shiteru). With an instrument, suru or yaru only names it as a hobby, and it doesn't ask whether she can play. C is English 'play' turned into asobu, which means playing around or having fun; you don't asobu an instrument.

questions.english: Mai hears you play a few bars on a piano and asks, "e, piano hikeru no?" (Wait, you can play the piano?) Tell her you took piano lessons back in the day.
questions.ja: え、ピアノ弾けるの？
questions.kana: え、ぴあのひけるの？
questions.romaji: e, piano hikeru no?
questions.answer: Say you used to take lessons, using piano with narau in its -teta form: un, mukashi piano naratteta n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, mukashi piano naratteta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、昔ピアノ習ってたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I took piano lessons back in the day.

modelAnswers.romaji: piano wa mukashi naratteta kara, chotto hikeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ピアノは昔習ってたから、ちょっと弾けるよ。
modelAnswers.english: I took piano lessons years ago, so I can play a bit.

questions.explanation: Lessons with a teacher are narau, and naratteta is 'used to take lessons', as Kenji and his mom both say (line 5: mukashi naratteta n da kara; line 6: naratteta kedo; line 7: okaasan mo mukashi piano naratteta). Mai asked with hiku (hikeru no?), but narau tells her where the skill came from. Don't say piano o benkyou shita, which sounds like studying it as a school subject. Don't say oboeta either: that is picking something up by yourself, the way Okaasan picked up the game tune (line 11: oboechatta).

newWords.english: long ago, back in the day (mukashi naratteta = used to take lessons)
pick up, memorise (oboechatta = it stuck, I picked it up)
play around, have fun (not used for sports or instruments)

script.title: Both a bit off
script.setting: A weekday morning outside the apartment building. Satou-san is back from his morning walk and runs into Kenta, who is heading to work and doesn't look well.

speakers.name: Boss
speakers.voice: male, 50s, brisk but friendly, heard over the phone

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu, kenta-san. oya, guai ga warusou desu ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます、ケンタさん。おや、具合が悪そうですね。
lines.kana: おはようございます、けんたさん。おや、ぐあいがわるそうですね。
lines.english: Good morning, Kenta. Oh dear, you don't look well.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. kinou kara chotto guai ga warukute.
lines.ja: おはようございます。昨日からちょっと具合が悪くて。
lines.kana: おはようございます。きのうからちょっとぐあいがわるくて。
lines.english: Morning. I've been feeling a bit unwell since yesterday.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kibun ga warui n desu ka?
lines.ja: 気分が悪いんですか？
lines.kana: きぶんがわるいんですか？
lines.english: Do you feel sick?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: iie, ima wa daijoubu desu. demo kinou, densha ga kondete, kibun ga waruku natchatte.
lines.ja: いいえ、今は大丈夫です。でも昨日、電車が混んでて、気分が悪くなっちゃって。
lines.kana: いいえ、いまはだいじょうぶです。でもきのう、でんしゃがこんでて、きぶんがわるくなっちゃって。
lines.english: No, I'm all right now. But yesterday the train was packed, and I started feeling sick.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: guai ga warui noni, oshigoto ni iku n desu ka?
lines.ja: 具合が悪いのに、お仕事に行くんですか？
lines.kana: ぐあいがわるいのに、おしごとにいくんですか？
lines.english: You're not well, and you're still going to work?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hai. kyou wa yasumenai n desu yo.
lines.ja: はい。今日は休めないんですよ。
lines.kana: はい。きょうはやすめないんですよ。
lines.english: Yeah. I can't take today off.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: dame desu yo. densha ni nottara, mata kibun ga waruku narimasu yo.
lines.ja: だめですよ。電車に乗ったら、また気分が悪くなりますよ。
lines.kana: だめですよ。でんしゃにのったら、またきぶんがわるくなりますよ。

questions.kana: なにがありましたか？

choices.english: Kenta isn't well, but his boss says he can't have the day off, so he heads for the train.
Satou-san isn't well, so Kenta stays home from work to keep him company on his walk.
Kenta isn't well. Satou-san talks him out of going to work, and Kenta calls in sick on his glitchy phone.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenta isn't well (guai ga warusou / guai ga warukute). In line 6 he says he can't take today off, but Satou-san warns him he'll feel sick on the train again (line 7), so he decides to stay home (line 8: kyou wa yasumimasu). His phone is acting up (lines 8-10), but the call goes through: he calls in sick (line 11) and his boss tells him to take the day off (line 12). A is wrong because the boss says ii yo, kyou wa yasunde (sure, take the day off). B is wrong because Satou-san is the one in good shape (line 15: saikin, choushi ga ii n desu yo). Kenta only says he might take up walks once he's better (line 16).

questions.english: Your friend Yuki asks, "ne, kyou karaoke ikanai?" (Hey, want to go to karaoke today?) You're not feeling great. Say sorry and tell her you're feeling a bit unwell.
questions.ja: ね、今日カラオケ行かない？
questions.kana: ね、きょうからおけいかない？
questions.romaji: ne, kyou karaoke ikanai?
questions.answer: Turn her down with guai ga warui, softened with chotto: gomen, kyou wa chotto guai warui n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou wa chotto guai warui n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日はちょっと具合悪いんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'm not feeling too great today.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen ne, kinou kara chotto guai ga warukute.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんね、昨日からちょっと具合が悪くて。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've been feeling a bit unwell since yesterday.

questions.explanation: Guai ga warui is the everyday 'I'm not feeling well'. Kenta uses it with Satou-san in line 2 (kinou kara chotto guai ga warukute), and Satou-san sees it on his face in line 1 (guai ga warusou). Chotto softens it, and with a friend ga often drops (guai warui). The n da gives your reason for saying no. Byouki desu would sound like you have an actual illness. Taichou ga warui also works, but it's the more careful word you'd keep for work.

questions.english: It's a workday morning and you feel unwell. You phone your manager, Tanaka-san, and he picks up: "hai, tanaka desu. ohayou gozaimasu." (Hello, Tanaka speaking. Good morning.) Tell him you're not feeling well and ask for the day off.
questions.ja: はい、田中です。おはようございます。
questions.kana: はい、たなかです。おはようございます。
questions.romaji: hai, tanaka desu. ohayou gozaimasu.
questions.answer: Use the work-safe taichou ga warui and ask for the day off: sumimasen, kyou wa taichou ga warui node, yasumasete kudasai.

modelAnswers.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. sumimasen, kyou wa taichou ga warui node, yasumasete kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: おはようございます。すみません、今日は体調が悪いので、休ませてください。
modelAnswers.english: Good morning. I'm sorry, I'm not feeling well today. Could I take the day off?

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, kinou kara chotto taichou ga warui n desu. kyou wa yasunde mo ii desu ka?
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、昨日からちょっと体調が悪いんです。今日は休んでもいいですか？
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've been a bit under the weather since yesterday. Would it be all right if I took today off?

questions.explanation: At work, taichou ga warui is the safe phrase for calling in sick. Kenta tells his neighbour guai ga warui (line 2), but on the phone to his boss he switches to taichou ga warui (line 11: kyou wa taichou ga warui node, yasumasete kudasai), and his boss repeats it back (line 12). Node gives the reason politely. Yasumasete kudasai asks to be let off, and yasunde mo ii desu ka asks permission. Guai ga warui would be understood, but taichou is the careful word for your manager.

questions.english: After deciding to stay home, Kenta takes out his phone and frowns at it. What does he say?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、スマホを見て、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、すまほをみて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, sumaho o mite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: My phone's broken.
My phone's acting up.
My phone's working nicely.

questions.explanation: Line 8: sumaho no choushi warui naa. Choushi ga warui is for a device that still works, just badly. A is what English 'my phone's broken' turns into, but kowareta means it broke and has stopped working. Kenta's phone still works: he makes his call on it in line 11, and he says it's been acting up for ages (line 10: zutto choushi ga warui n desu). C is the opposite, choushi ga ii (working well). That doesn't fit his puzzled 'are?' or Satou-san's joke in line 9 that Kenta and his phone are both off (kenta-san mo sumaho mo, choushi ga warui n desu ne).

questions.english: When Kenta asks about his walk, Satou-san says "saikin, choushi ga ii n desu yo." What does he mean?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、最近どうですか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、さいきんどうですか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, saikin dou desu ka?

choices.english: He's been in good shape lately, thanks to his daily walks.
He's in a good mood this morning because the weather is nice.
His phone has been working well lately, unlike Kenta's.

questions.explanation: Line 15: said about yourself, choushi ga ii means you're in good shape. Satou-san gives the reason straight away: mainichi sanpo ni itte imasu kara (I go for a walk every day). Kenta picks it up in line 16: choushi ga yoku nattara (once I'm feeling better). B is a mood, which would be kigen ga ii or kibun ga ii, and nobody mentions the weather. C: choushi does work for devices (Kenta's sumaho no choushi warui, line 8), but Satou-san says nothing about a phone. He's talking about himself and his walks.

questions.english: You and Mai are squeezed onto a packed train, and you start to feel sick. Mai asks, "densha, sugoku konderu ne. daijoubu?" (The train's so packed. You okay?) Tell her you're feeling a bit sick.
questions.ja: 電車、すごく混んでるね。大丈夫？
questions.kana: でんしゃ、すごくこんでるね。だいじょうぶ？
questions.romaji: densha, sugoku konderu ne. daijoubu?
questions.answer: Say no, you feel sick, with kibun ga warui: uun, chotto kibun ga warui.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, chotto kibun ga warui.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、ちょっと気分が悪い。
modelAnswers.english: No, I feel a bit sick.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, chotto kibun ga waruku natte kita.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、ちょっと気分が悪くなってきた。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm starting to feel a bit sick.

questions.explanation: Kibun ga warui is feeling sick or faint right now, in a crowd or a stuffy train. That's what happened to Kenta yesterday (line 4: densha ga kondete, kibun ga waruku natchatte), and Satou-san warns it will happen again (line 7). Waruku natte kita says it's coming on. It isn't English 'I feel bad', which is guilt (warui na). Guai ga warui is general unwellness, not this sudden 'I'm going to be sick' feeling.

newWords.english: take time off; rest (yasumenai = can't take off; yasumasete kudasai = please let me have the day off)
get crowded (densha ga kondete = the train was packed)
oh my, oh dear (an older speaker's mild surprise; oya oya)

questions.english: What happens with Yuki's movie plan?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki's Friday meeting is put off, so she and Kenji go to the movie on Friday night.
Kenji's exam is postponed, so they go to the movie on Sunday, and Kenji studies on Saturday instead.
Kenji's exam is pushed back a week, which frees up Sunday, but then work comes up for Yuki, so the movie moves to next week.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-5: Yuki wants to take Kenji to a movie, but he has class on Saturday (line 2), he's studying on Sunday for Monday's exam (line 4), and she has a meeting till eight on Friday (line 5). Line 8: the exam is postponed to next week, so Sunday opens up (line 9: jaa, nichiyoubi, eiga iku?). Then Tanaka-san's message brings Sunday work for Yuki (line 13: kyuu ni shigoto haitchatta), so the movie moves to next week (line 15: raishuu de ii?), and Kenji plans games instead of studying (lines 16-18). A is wrong: Yuki's meeting never moves; the thing that gets postponed is Kenji's exam. B is wrong: they never get to Sunday's movie, because Yuki's work comes up (line 13), and Kenji's Saturday is class (line 2), not studying.

questions.english: Sora asks you, "ashita, hima? asobi ni ikanai?" (Free tomorrow? Want to go out?) You've got class tomorrow. Tell him.
questions.ja: 明日、暇？遊びに行かない？
questions.kana: あした、ひま？あそびにいかない？
questions.romaji: ashita, hima? asobi ni ikanai?
questions.answer: Say you have class, with jugyou and aru (ga can drop): gomen, ashita wa jugyou aru n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, ashita wa jugyou aru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、明日は授業あるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got class tomorrow.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, ashita wa jugyou ga aru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、明日は授業があるんです。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I have class tomorrow.

questions.explanation: A class on your timetable just exists: jugyou ga aru, with ga usually dropped, as in Kenji's line 2 (doyoubi wa jugyou aru) and Yuki's line 3 (e, doyoubi mo jugyou aru no?). English 'have class' tempts jugyou o motsu, but that is a teacher's teaching load, not a student going to class. n da turns it into the reason you can't go. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Satou-san.

questions.english: Yuki suggests Friday, then remembers why she can't do it. What did she say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Oh, that's no good. I've got a meeting till eight.
choices.romaji: a, dame. hachiji made kaigi aru n datta.

choices.english: Oh, that's no good. I'm holding a meeting till eight.
choices.romaji: a, dame. hachiji made kaigi motteru n datta.

choices.english: Oh, that's no good. I need a meeting till eight.
choices.romaji: a, dame. hachiji made kaigi ga iru n datta.

questions.explanation: Line 5: a meeting on your calendar just exists, so it's kaigi ga aru (ga dropped, as usual in casual speech), and n datta adds 'oh right, I'd forgotten'. Kenji uses the same phrase in line 12 (mata kaigi aru no?). B puts English 'have' into Japanese with motsu: kaigi o motsu is at best a stiff 'hold a meeting', never a meeting you're going to. C swaps aru for iru, which is for people and animals; after a thing it's heard as iru 'need', so kaigi ga iru sounds like 'I need a meeting'. Meetings, classes and exams all take aru.

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "nichiyoubi, uchi ni asobi ni konai?" (Want to come over to ours on Sunday?) You've got an exam on Monday. Turn him down.
questions.ja: 日曜日、うちに遊びに来ない？
questions.kana: にちようび、うちにあそびにこない？
questions.romaji: nichiyoubi, uchi ni asobi ni konai?
questions.answer: Say you have an exam on Monday, with shiken and aru: gomen, getsuyoubi shiken aru kara.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, getsuyoubi shiken aru kara, benkyou suru.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、月曜日試験あるから、勉強する。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got an exam on Monday, so I'm studying.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, getsuyoubi ni shiken ga aru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、月曜日に試験があるんです。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I have an exam on Monday.

questions.explanation: An exam on your calendar just exists: shiken ga aru, as in Kenji's line 4 (getsuyoubi, shiken aru kara) and Yuki's line 17 (shiken, raishuu aru n desho?). Not shiken o motsu. Sitting the exam is shiken o ukeru, but to turn down a plan you only need to say it's there. kara gives the reason, just as Kenji does in line 4. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Satou-san.

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "doyoubi no sakkaa, kuru yo ne?" (You're coming to football on Saturday, right?) Work has come up for you on Saturday. Tell him.
questions.ja: 土曜日のサッカー、来るよね？
questions.kana: どようびのさっかー、くるよね？
questions.romaji: doyoubi no sakkaa, kuru yo ne?
questions.answer: Say work came up, with shigoto and hairu in the past: gomen, doyoubi kyuu ni shigoto haitchatta.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, doyoubi kyuu ni shigoto haitchatta.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、土曜日急に仕事入っちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, work's suddenly come up on Saturday.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, doyoubi wa kyuu ni shigoto ga haitchaimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、土曜日は急に仕事が入っちゃいました。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, something's come up at work on Saturday.

questions.explanation: When work lands on a day you'd kept free, the work goes into your schedule by itself: shigoto ga hairu, with the work as the subject and no 'I' doing anything. Yuki says it in line 13 (nichiyoubi, kyuu ni shigoto haitchatta) and Kenji repeats it in line 14 (nichiyoubi ni shigoto haitta no?). -chatta adds 'sorry, it couldn't be helped'. Kaigi ga aru would only fit a meeting that was already on your calendar; Yuki makes that difference in line 13 (kaigi ja nakute...). The second model is the polite version, for someone you speak politely to.

questions.english: Kenji reads a message from school about his Monday exam. What happened to the exam?
questions.ja: 月曜日の試験は？
questions.kana: げつようびのしけんは？
questions.romaji: getsuyoubi no shiken wa?

It's been put off until next week.

questions.explanation: Line 8: raishuu ni enki ni natta is 'got postponed to next week': the exam becomes postponed, and nobody in the sentence does the postponing. Yuki checks it in line 17 (shiken, raishuu aru n desho?), and Kenji repeats enki ni natta in line 18. A would be chuushi ni natta (called off), and Yuki's line 17 shows there is still an exam. C makes Kenji the one doing it, but he is only reading news from school (line 6: a, gakkou kara da). English 'was postponed' tempts the passive enki sareta, which sounds like an official notice; in conversation it's enki ni natta.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: The rain ruins Kenta's new cookbook, so Sora cheers him up by offering to cook dinner.
Sora is disappointed to win only an umbrella, but it keeps Kenta's new book dry in the rain, and Kenta says he'll cook for him.
Sora wins a cookbook he has no use for, so he swaps it with Kenta for an umbrella.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Kenta wins a book in the draw, and line 3 says it's a cookbook. Sora only wins an umbrella (lines 5-6), and they already have five at home (line 8), so he feels unlucky (line 10: boku wa honto ni un warui naa). Then it starts raining and Kenta is worried the book will be ruined (line 11). Sora puts up his umbrella and Kenta gets under it (lines 12-13). Sora decides he's the lucky one after all (line 14), and Kenta says he'll cook for him from the book (line 15). A is wrong: the book never gets ruined, because the umbrella keeps it dry. Sora also doesn't cook (line 4: ryouri shinai). C is wrong: Kenta won the cookbook and Sora won the umbrella, and nobody swaps prizes.

questions.english: Yuki's little brother Kenji tells you how his exam went: "kyou shiken datta n da kedo, kinou benkyou shita no ga deta n da." (I had an exam today, and the stuff I studied yesterday came up.) Tell him he was lucky.
questions.ja: 今日試験だったんだけど、昨日勉強したのが出たんだ。
questions.kana: きょうしけんだったんだけど、きのうべんきょうしたのがでたんだ。
questions.romaji: kyou shiken datta n da kedo, kinou benkyou shita no ga deta n da.
questions.answer: Tell him he was lucky with luck as the subject: un ii ne! (ga dropped). Or, since it's already happened, use the past: un ga yokatta ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: e, un ii ne!
modelAnswers.ja: え、運いいね！
modelAnswers.english: Oh, lucky you!

modelAnswers.romaji: sore wa un ga yokatta ne.
modelAnswers.ja: それは運がよかったね。
modelAnswers.english: That was lucky.

questions.explanation: Sora says the first answer to Kenta in line 2 (e, honto ni? un ii ne!) when Kenta wins the book. In line 14 he keeps ga: honto ni un ga ii no wa boku da ne. In Japanese the luck is the subject (un ga ii: the luck is good), so you don't put 'lucky' on the person the way English does. The past of ii is yokatta, so 'that was lucky' is un ga yokatta, never un iikatta. 'Good luck!' before an exam is ganbatte and has nothing to do with un. Here the exam is already over, so you're commenting on luck that has already happened.

questions.english: Sora shows Kenta the umbrella he won and says they already have five at home. Kenta says "aa, sore wa un warukatta ne." What does Kenta mean?
questions.ja: 運悪かったねって、何ですか？
questions.kana: うんわるかったねって、なんですか？
questions.romaji: un warukatta ne tte, nan desu ka?

choices.english: That was a bad choice. Sora should have gone for a different prize.
That's a bad umbrella. It probably won't last in the rain.
That was just bad luck. It's nobody's fault he got another umbrella.

questions.explanation: Line 9: un warukatta ne is the usual way to console someone. The luck was bad (warukatta is the past of warui), and ga is dropped. On its own, warui can mean poor quality or at fault, but with un it is only about luck. A is wrong: prizes are won in a draw, not chosen (atatta, lines 1 and 5), and Kenta isn't blaming Sora. B is wrong: Kenta says nothing against the umbrella, and it works fine when the rain comes (lines 12-13). Sora answers in line 10 with both phrases in one frame: kenta wa un ii yo ne. boku wa honto ni un warui naa.

questions.english: When the rain starts and Sora puts up his umbrella, Kenta thanks him. What did Kenta say about the umbrella?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Your umbrella really came in handy.
choices.romaji: sora no kasa, metcha yaku ni tatta ne.

choices.english: Your umbrella was really convenient.
choices.romaji: sora no kasa, metcha benri datta ne.

choices.english: Your umbrella really did me good.
choices.romaji: sora no kasa, metcha tame ni natta ne.

questions.explanation: Line 13: yaku ni tatta, the past of yaku ni tatsu, says the umbrella actually helped: it kept Kenta's new book out of the rain. B is what you get by translating the English word 'useful' as benri. Benri means handy or convenient to use, like a shop close to home. It describes how easy something is to use, not that it just got you out of trouble. C is the chunk's other phrase, tame ni naru. That one is for a book, a talk or a show that does you good over time, the way Kenta describes the cookbook in line 3. An umbrella can help you, but it doesn't teach you anything. Lines 3 and 7 already set the two apart: the book is tame ni naru, and the umbrella is yaku ni tatsu.

questions.english: Yuki sees the book you're carrying and asks, "sono hon, mou yonda? ii hon?" (Have you read that book yet? Is it any good?) Tell her it's really worthwhile.
questions.ja: その本、もう読んだ？いい本？
questions.kana: そのほん、もうよんだ？いいほん？
questions.romaji: sono hon, mou yonda? ii hon?
questions.answer: Say it's worth reading with tame ni naru, keeping ni: un, sugoku tame ni naru yo. Before a noun it becomes tame ni naru hon.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, sugoku tame ni naru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、すごくためになるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it's really worthwhile.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kekkou tame ni naru hon da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、けっこうためになる本だよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it's a pretty worthwhile book.

questions.explanation: Kenta says the same thing about the cookbook in line 3 (kekkou tame ni naru n da yo). Sora turns it round in line 4 (yonde mo tame ni naranai naa) and again in line 16 (boku no tame ni mo naru ne). Tame ni naru says a book, show or talk is good for you, something you come away from knowing more. Yaku ni tatsu is practical help with a task, like the umbrella in line 13. Ni stays even in casual speech. This is not the grammar -tame ni (in order to): here tame means benefit, and the phrase ends in naru.

newWords.english: cooking; a dish (ryouri no hon = a cookbook; ryouri suru = to cook)
to be won in a draw (hon ga atatta = I won a book; nani ga atatta? = what did you win?)
to make, to cook (ryouri tsukuru = cook a meal)

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki was out drinking last night, so Mai gives her water and tells her to skip tonight's plans.
Yuki couldn't sleep after a late-night coffee, and she agrees to stick to tea at tonight's drinks with Kenta.
Yuki couldn't sleep after a late-night coffee, so she cancels tonight's drinks with Kenta and goes home early.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Mai guesses Yuki was out drinking (osake nonda n desho), but in line 4 Yuki says she wasn't: her work wasn't finished, so she had a coffee at ten at night. In line 10 she remembers she's drinking with Kenta and the others tonight, and after Mai's teasing about her 'just one' (line 13) she decides in line 14: konban, osake wa nomanai. ocha dake nomu. A is Mai's wrong guess from line 3. C goes too far: Yuki still goes out tonight, she just won't drink alcohol; going home and straight to bed is Mai's advice for afterwards (line 15).

questions.english: The morning after a night out, Kenta groans: "Ugh, I drank too much last night. My head hurts." Tell him to drink some water.
questions.ja: ああ、昨日飲みすぎた。頭痛い。
questions.kana: ああ、きのうのみすぎた。あたまいたい。
questions.romaji: aa, kinou nomisugita. atama itai.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu? mizu nonda?
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫？水飲んだ？

modelAnswers.romaji: mizu nonde ne. kyou wa osake nomanaide ne.
