modelAnswers.english: Make sure you drink some water. And no drinking today, okay?

questions.explanation: Drinking water takes the same nomu as every other drink: Mai says mizu nonde (line 7) and uchi ni kaettara, mizu nonde sugu nete ne (line 15), and Yuki promises mizu mo nomu kara (line 12). After a night of drinking, mizu nonda? and mizu nonde ne are what friends say to look after you. Kenta's nomisugita uses nomu on its own: once drinking is the topic, nomu by itself means alcohol. For 'have' a drink, don't reach for motsu or aru; it's always nomu.

questions.english: It's eleven at night at Kenta's flat, and he says: "I'm making coffee. Want some?" Turn it down: tell him you can't sleep if you drink coffee at night.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. demo, yoru koohii nomu to nerenai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。でも、夜コーヒー飲むと寝れないんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. But I can't sleep if I drink coffee at night.

modelAnswers.english: No, I'm good. If I have coffee now, I won't be able to sleep.

questions.explanation: Mai says exactly this in line 5: watashi mo, yoru koohii nomu to nerenai n da. Yuki uses the same verb for her late cup in line 4 (yoru juuji ni koohii nonjatta) and asks koohii, ippai dake nonde ii? in line 16. Kenta's ireru is the making (koohii o ireru, ocha o ireru); what you'd be doing is drinking it, so your answer takes nomu.

questions.english: What did Yuki want to drink tonight with Kenta and the others?
questions.ja: ユキさんは今晩、何を飲みたかったですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはこんばん、なにをのみたかったですか？

choices.english: Just tea
Japanese sake, the rice wine
One beer

questions.explanation: Line 10: konban, kenta-tachi to osake nomu n da. When Mai objects, Yuki says biiru ippai dake (just one beer, line 12). osake means alcohol in general (beer, wine, highballs); Japanese rice wine specifically is nihonshu. So B is the trap of hearing osake as 'sake'. A is what she agrees to in line 14 (ocha dake nomu) after Mai teases her, not what she wanted.

questions.english: When Yuki says she'd rather have coffee than water, what does Mai offer her instead?
questions.ja: マイさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Then want some tea?
Then want some black tea?
Then want to go out for a cuppa?

questions.explanation: Line 9: jaa, ocha nomu? asoko ni mugicha aru yo. Yuki takes it in line 10 (un, ocha nomu). ocha is Japanese tea: green tea or, as here, barley tea (mugicha). B, koucha, is black tea, which is what English 'tea' usually means, but ocha on its own means Japanese tea, not black tea, and koucha isn't what's on offer. C, ocha shinai?, is an invitation to go out to a cafe for a break; Mai isn't suggesting going anywhere, she's offering the tea that's right there in the office.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?

questions.kana: なにがありましたか？

choices.english: Kenta cooks dinner, but Sora takes a long bath and it goes cold. Then Sora admits he has already eaten, but he eats Kenta's food anyway.
Sora cooks dinner for Kenta, but Kenta takes a long bath and the food goes cold.
Kenta cooks dinner, but Sora has already eaten, so he goes to bed and Kenta eats alone.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-4: Kenta is making dinner (gohan, mou sugu dekiru yo; kenta ga gohan tsukutte kureteru no?). Line 5: Sora wants a bath first, and in line 10, thirty minutes later, the food has gone cold (gohan, samechatta yo). Line 13: Sora admits he already ate before coming home (mou gohan tabete kichatta), but in lines 15 and 17 he eats anyway (kenta no gohan wa taberu yo! ... samete mo oishii!). B swaps the two: Kenta is the one cooking and Sora is the one in the bath. C is wrong: Sora doesn't go to bed. He sits down and eats Kenta's dinner even though he's full (line 17: un, ippai. demo...).

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "ne, mou gohan tabeta?" (Hey, have you eaten yet?) You haven't eaten yet. Tell him.
questions.ja: ね、もうご飯食べた？
questions.kana: ね、もうごはんたべた？
questions.romaji: ne, mou gohan tabeta?
questions.answer: Say not yet, using mada and the negative of taberu's -teru form: uun, mada gohan tabetenai. Don't say tabenakatta: that means you skipped the meal.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, mada gohan tabetenai.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、まだご飯食べてない。
modelAnswers.english: No, I haven't eaten yet.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, gohan mada tabetenai n da. onaka suita yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、ご飯まだ食べてないんだ。おなかすいたよ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I haven't had dinner yet. I'm starving.

questions.explanation: gohan is any meal, not only rice: in this scene Kenta's gohan is hamburger steak (line 4). For 'not yet', Japanese uses mada with the negative -teru form, exactly as Kenta says in line 4 (boku mo mada gohan tabetenai n da). tabenakatta would mean you didn't eat the meal at all, not that you haven't got to it yet. If you had already eaten, you'd say un, tabeta, or, like Sora in line 13, mou gohan tabete kichatta (I already ate before I got here).

questions.english: At the end, Kenta says, "ashita wa sora ga gohan tsukutte ne." What does he want Sora to do tomorrow?
questions.ja: ケンタは明日、ソラに何をしてほしいですか？
questions.kana: けんたはあした、そらになにをしてほしいですか？
questions.romaji: kenta wa ashita, sora ni nani o shite hoshii desu ka?

choices.english: Cook just the rice, while Kenta makes the rest of the meal.
Come straight home after work so they can eat together.
Make dinner for the two of them.

questions.explanation: gohan tsukuru means 'cook a meal, make dinner': tomorrow Sora cooks, the way Kenta did tonight (line 14: gohan tsukutta noni, 'I made dinner!'). A is the rice trap: gohan here is the whole meal, and tonight's was hamburger steak. Cooking just the rice would be gohan o taku. B: Kenta says nothing about Sora coming home. His jab comes in the next sentence: gohan dekitara, boku wa sugu iku kara (the second dinner's ready, I'll be right there), unlike Sora and his thirty-minute bath.

questions.english: While Sora is in the bath, Kenta finishes cooking and calls out to him. What does he shout?
questions.ja: ケンタは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Dinner's preparation! (a stab at 'dinner's ready')
Dinner's ready!
Dinner's over! (we've finished eating)

questions.explanation: Line 8: sora! gohan dekita yo! The kitchen call uses dekiru in the past: the meal has been made, so it's ready. A is what you get by translating 'ready' with junbi. Japanese would say gohan no junbi ga dekita, which still uses dekiru, and the everyday call is simply gohan dekita yo. C, gohan owatta, means the meal is over and everyone has finished eating, which is the opposite moment. Notice the tense: in line 2 Kenta said mou sugu dekiru yo. Non-past dekiru means it'll be ready very soon, not that it's ready now.

questions.english: Dinner is hot on the table. Sora says, "jaa, chotto ofuro haitte kuru ne." (Right, I'm just going to hop in the bath.) Tell him the food will get cold.
questions.ja: じゃあ、ちょっとお風呂入ってくるね。
questions.kana: じゃあ、ちょっとおふろはいってくるね。
questions.romaji: jaa, chotto ofuro haitte kuru ne.
questions.answer: Warn him using the -chau form of sameru: e, ima? gohan samechau yo. Not samuku naru: samui is for the weather and for how a person feels.

modelAnswers.romaji: e, ima? gohan samechau yo.
modelAnswers.ja: え、今？ご飯冷めちゃうよ。
modelAnswers.english: What, now? The food'll get cold.

modelAnswers.romaji: gohan samechau kara, tabete kara ni shite yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ご飯冷めちゃうから、食べてからにしてよ。
modelAnswers.english: The food'll get cold, so have your bath after you eat.

questions.explanation: When hot food loses its heat, the verb is sameru. samechau adds 'and that would be a shame', which is why it's the usual warning. Kenta says it in line 6, and half an hour later he says it in the past in line 10 (gohan, samechatta yo). In the same scene Sora says samukatta and samukute (lines 1 and 5). That's samui, used for the cold weather outside and for how he feels, never for food. In line 17 Sora even eats the food cold: samete mo oishii (it's good even cold).

newWords.english: I'm home (said when you get home)
welcome back (said to someone getting home)

script.title: Whose cold was it?
script.setting: A weekday evening. Okaasan, in bed with a cold, leaves Yuki a voicemail about the weekend. Later Yuki calls back and gets Okaasan's voicemail too.

lines.romaji: de ne, senshuu kaetta toki, watashi, chotto taichou kuzushiteta yo ne?

questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Okaasan asks Yuki to come home this weekend and look after Kenji, who is ill in bed.
Yuki can't come home this weekend because she has a cold, and she doesn't want to give it to Kenji.
Okaasan tells Yuki not to come home so she won't catch the family's cold, and Yuki replies that Kenji probably caught it from her in the first place.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenji caught a cold (kenji ga ne, kaze hiichatta no) and Okaasan caught it from him (okaasan ni mo utsutchatta no). Lines 3-4: Yuki was due home this weekend, but Okaasan tells her not to come (kaette konaide ne), or she'll catch it too (kitara, yuki ni mo utsuru yo). Lines 11-12: Yuki was run down when she came home last week, and she thinks her cold spread to Kenji (watashi no kaze, kenji ni utsutchatta n da to omou). A is wrong: Okaasan asks her not to come (line 4). B is wrong: it's Okaasan who calls off the visit, and Yuki's cold was last week (line 11: kuzushiteta), already passed on to Kenji (line 12).

questions.english: Okaasan phones you and hears your croaky voice. She asks, "e, sono koe, dou shita no?" (Oh, what's happened to your voice?) Tell her you've caught a cold.
questions.ja: え、その声、どうしたの？
questions.kana: え、そのこえ、どうしたの？
questions.romaji: e, sono koe, dou shita no?
questions.answer: Say you've caught a cold with kaze and hiku, in the past: kaze hiichatta.

modelAnswers.romaji: kaze hiichatta.
modelAnswers.ja: 風邪ひいちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: I've caught a cold.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kinou kara kaze hiiteru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、昨日から風邪ひいてるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I've had a cold since yesterday.

questions.explanation: A cold is 'pulled' with hiku, not caught with toru or tsukamu (catching a ball). Kaze hiichatta is how Okaasan breaks the news about Kenji in line 1. Kaze hiiteru (line 6: kaze hiiteru noni) is having a cold right now, so kinou kara kaze hiiteru is 'I've had a cold since yesterday'. Kaze ga utsutta would only fit if you were saying who gave it to you.

questions.english: You have a cold, and Yuki asks, "kaze? doko de hiita no?" (A cold? Where did you pick that up?) Your friend had one last week. Tell her you caught it from your friend.
questions.ja: 風邪？どこでひいたの？
questions.kana: かぜ？どこでひいたの？
questions.romaji: kaze? doko de hiita no?
questions.answer: Say your friend's cold spread to you, with kaze ga utsuru: tomodachi no kaze ga utsutta n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: tomodachi no kaze ga utsutta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 友達の風邪がうつったんだ。
modelAnswers.english: I caught my friend's cold.

modelAnswers.romaji: tomodachi kara utsutchatta.
modelAnswers.ja: 友達からうつっちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: I caught it off a friend.

questions.explanation: Kaze o hiku is just getting a cold. When it comes from someone, the cold moves to you: kaze ga utsuru, with no or kara for whose it was. Okaasan says it in line 2 (kenji no kaze, okaasan ni mo utsutchatta) and Yuki in line 12 (watashi no kaze, kenji ni utsutchatta). Yuki asked with hiita, but kaze hiita on its own wouldn't say where it came from.

questions.english: Okaasan tells Yuki that she and Kenji haven't 'byouki ni natta'. What does she mean?
questions.ja: お母さんとケンジは、大丈夫なんですか？
questions.kana: おかあさんとけんじは、だいじょうぶなんですか？
questions.romaji: okaasan to kenji wa, daijoubu na n desu ka?

choices.english: It's nothing serious: they've come down with something, but it isn't a real illness.
They haven't seen a doctor yet, so they don't know what illness it is.
They were ill last week, but they've both got better now.

questions.explanation: Line 5: byouki ni natta wake ja nakute, chotto taichou kuzushita dake. Byouki ni naru sounds like falling properly ill, so Okaasan says it isn't that; they're just a bit run down (taichou kuzushita) with a cold and an upset stomach (lines 2 and 6). B is wrong: she never mentions a doctor, and she knows it's Kenji's cold. C is wrong: her throat is still sore (line 2: nodo ga itakute); last week is when Yuki was run down (line 11).

questions.english: You missed work yesterday with a passing bug. Yuki asks, "kinou inakatta ne. dou shita no?" (You weren't in yesterday. What happened?) Tell her you were a bit under the weather.
questions.ja: 昨日いなかったね。どうしたの？
questions.kana: きのういなかったね。どうしたの？
questions.romaji: kinou inakatta ne. dou shita no?
questions.answer: Say you came down with something minor, with taichou and kuzusu: chotto taichou kuzushichatte.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto taichou kuzushichatte.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと体調崩しちゃって。
modelAnswers.english: I came down with a little something.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto taichou kuzushite ne. demo, mou daijoubu.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと体調崩してね。でも、もう大丈夫。
modelAnswers.english: I was a bit under the weather. I'm fine now, though.

questions.explanation: For a passing bug, the everyday explanation is taichou (o) kuzushita, as in line 5 (chotto taichou kuzushita dake) and line 11 (chotto taichou kuzushiteta). Byouki ni natta would sound like a real illness and worry her. Taichou ga warukatta only describes how you felt; kuzusu is coming down with it.

questions.english: Okaasan says Kenji ate three ice creams even though he has a cold. What does she say happened to his stomach?
questions.ja: お母さんは、ケンジのお腹について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、けんじのおなかについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, kenji no onaka ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: his stomach got run down too
he's upset his stomach too
his stomach fell ill too
choices.romaji: onaka mo byouki ni natta no yo

questions.explanation: Line 6: onaka mo kowashita no yo. The stomach is 'broken' with kowasu, with Kenji as the one who broke it; mo stands in for o, meaning his stomach too, on top of the cold. Yuki says it again in line 10 (sore wa onaka kowasu yo). A is wrong: kuzusu goes with taichou, your health in general (line 5: taichou kuzushita); for the stomach it's kowasu. C is wrong: byouki ni naru is for a person falling properly ill, not a stomach, and Okaasan has just said this isn't a real illness (line 5).

when, (at) the time (kaetta toki = when I came home)
get well soon, take care (said to someone who's ill)

lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、くつぬいでいい？

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki and Kenji get caught in the rain on the way to the shops, so they come home and change out of their wet clothes.
Kenji takes too long getting dressed, so Yuki goes shopping without him and he goes back to bed.
Rain puts off the shopping, so Kenji gets undressed and goes back to bed; then the rain stops, and Yuki tells him to get dressed again.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: Kenji is dressed and puts his shoes on (kiteru yo / ima kutsu haku kara / haita yo). Line 5: it starts raining just as they're leaving (ame futte kita), and in line 7 Yuki puts the shopping off till tomorrow (ashita ni shiyou ka). Lines 8-12: shoes off, clothes off, back to bed (oyasumi). Line 13: the rain stops (ame yanda yo), and in line 15 Yuki tells him to get dressed again (mou ikkai fuku kite, kutsu haite!). A is wrong: they never leave the house, so nobody gets wet; the rain starts at the door (line 5). B is wrong: Kenji is ready in time (line 4: haita yo), and Yuki doesn't go without him: she wants him dressed again and out of the door in ten minutes (lines 15 and 17).

questions.english: Yuki calls out "fuku kita?" and Kenji answers "kiteru yo." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは今、どうですか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはいま、どうですか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa ima, dou desu ka?

choices.english: He has already come down and is waiting at the door.
His clothes are already on; the shoes are what he's doing now.
He's in the middle of getting dressed and will be done soon.

questions.explanation: Line 2: kiteru is a state, 'I have them on', not 'I'm putting them on now'. That's why he adds ima kutsu haku kara: shoes are the one thing left. C reads -teru like English '-ing', but with kiru, -teru means the clothes are already on. A hears kiteru as 'has come' (来てる): the same sounds, but that one falls after ki (KI-te-ru) while 'wearing' is flat (ki-TE-RU), and Yuki has just asked fuku kita? (did you get dressed?).

questions.english: You're dressed, but your shoes aren't on yet. Yuki calls from the front door: "mou deru yo! mada?" (We're leaving! Still not ready?) Tell her you're putting your shoes on now.
questions.ja: もう出るよ！まだ？
questions.kana: もうでるよ！まだ？
questions.romaji: mou deru yo! mada?
questions.answer: Say you're putting your shoes on now with haku: ima kutsu haku kara!

modelAnswers.romaji: ima kutsu haku kara!
modelAnswers.ja: 今靴履くから！
modelAnswers.english: I'm putting my shoes on now!

modelAnswers.romaji: fuku wa kiteru. ato wa kutsu haku dake.
modelAnswers.ja: 服は着てる。あとは靴履くだけ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm dressed. I just have to put my shoes on.

questions.explanation: Anything you step into goes on with haku, so shoes are kutsu o haku, never kutsu o kiru, even though English says 'wear' for both. Kenji does exactly this in line 2 (kiteru yo. ima kutsu haku kara): clothes with kiru, shoes with haku. Plain haku is 'putting them on now'; haiteru would mean they're already on, like Yuki's line 3 (watashi wa mou kutsu haiteru yo).

questions.english: When Yuki puts off the shopping, Kenji asks her something about his shoes. What did he ask?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Then can I take my shoes off?
Then can I pick up my shoes?
Then can I put my shoes on?

questions.explanation: Line 8: shoes come off with nugu, so Kenji asks kutsu nuide ii?, and Yuki answers watashi mo nugu (line 9: I'm taking mine off too). B is English 'take off' turned into toru: kutsu totte sounds like picking the shoes up or passing them to someone, not getting them off your feet. C is the opposite verb: haku puts shoes on, and Kenji already had his on (line 4: haita yo); with the shopping off, he wants them off.

questions.english: You come home soaked. Yuki says: "e, ame ni furareta no? kaze hiku yo!" (Oh, did you get caught in the rain? You'll catch a cold!) Tell her you'll get out of your clothes right away.
questions.ja: え、雨に降られたの？風邪ひくよ！
questions.kana: え、あめにふられたの？かぜひくよ！
questions.romaji: e, ame ni furareta no? kaze hiku yo!
questions.answer: Say you'll take your clothes off right away with nugu: un, sugu fuku nugu.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, sugu fuku nugu.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、すぐ服脱ぐ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll get out of these clothes right away.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, fuku nuide, ofuro hairu.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、服脱いで、お風呂入る。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll get these clothes off and have a bath.

questions.explanation: Whatever goes on with kiru or haku comes off with nugu, so clothes are fuku o nugu, as in Kenji's line 10 (fuku mo nuide, mou ikkai neru) and line 14 (mou fuku mo kutsu mo nuijatta yo). fuku o toru would sound like picking your clothes up (fuku totte = pass me my clothes). The same nugu took the shoes off in lines 8-9, so one verb undoes both kiru and haku.

newWords.english: decide on, go with (ashita ni shiyou = let's make it tomorrow)
take, pick up; pass (fuku totte = pass me my clothes)

script.title: The music next door
script.setting: A Saturday morning in the corridor of their apartment building. Yuki is heading out when Satou-san, the elderly neighbour on the other side of her thin wall, stops her. She's sure he's about to complain about her music.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, yuki-san, ohayou gozaimasu. chotto ii desu ka?
lines.ja: あ、ユキさん、おはようございます。ちょっといいですか？
lines.kana: あ、ゆきさん、おはようございます。ちょっといいですか？
lines.english: Ah, Yuki-san, good morning. Have you got a moment?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. hai, dou shimashita?
lines.ja: おはようございます。はい、どうしました？
lines.kana: おはようございます。はい、どうしました？
lines.english: Good morning. Sure, what is it?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yoru, yoku ongaku o kakete imasu yo ne.
lines.ja: 夜、よく音楽をかけていますよね。
lines.kana: よる、よくおんがくをかけていますよね。
lines.english: You often have music on in the evenings, don't you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, sumimasen! urusakatta desu ka?
lines.ja: あ、すみません！うるさかったですか？
lines.kana: あ、すみません！うるさかったですか？
lines.english: Oh, I'm sorry! Was it too loud?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: iie, sou ja nai n desu. kinou no yoru wa ongaku o kakete inakatta node, dou shita no kana to omotte.
lines.ja: いいえ、そうじゃないんです。昨日の夜は音楽をかけていなかったので、どうしたのかなと思って。
lines.kana: いいえ、そうじゃないんです。きのうのよるはおんがくをかけていなかったので、どうしたのかなとおもって。
lines.english: No, it's not that. Last night you didn't have any music on, so I wondered if something was wrong.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, kinou wa kaeri ga osokatta n desu. demo satou-san, watashi no ongaku, kiiteru n desu ka?
lines.ja: あ、昨日は帰りが遅かったんです。でも佐藤さん、私の音楽、聞いてるんですか？
lines.kana: あ、きのうはかえりがおそかったんです。でもさとうさん、わたしのおんがく、きいてるんですか？
lines.english: Oh, I got home late last night. But Satou-san, you listen to my music?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai. saikin wa, terebi o minai n desu yo.
lines.ja: はい。最近は、テレビを見ないんですよ。
lines.kana: はい。さいきんは、テレビをみないんですよ。
lines.english: I do. I don't watch TV these days, you see.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: doushite desu ka? asa mo yoru mo, nyuusu o mite imashita yo ne.
lines.ja: どうしてですか？朝も夜も、ニュースを見ていましたよね。
lines.kana: どうしてですか？あさもよるも、ニュースをみていましたよね。
lines.english: How come? You used to have the news on morning and night.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore ga, nyuusu o miru to, warui hanashi bakari de.
lines.ja: それが、ニュースを見ると、悪い話ばかりで。
lines.kana: それが、ニュースをみると、わるいはなしばかりで。
lines.english: The thing is, whenever I watch the news, it's nothing but bad stories.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, sou desu ne. jaa, channeru o kaetara dou desu ka?
lines.ja: ああ、そうですね。じゃあ、チャンネルを変えたらどうですか？
lines.kana: ああ、そうですね。じゃあ、チャンネルをかえたらどうですか？
lines.english: Ah, that's true. Well, how about changing the channel?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: channeru o kaete mo, doko mo nyuusu bakari desu yo. dakara, yuki-san no ongaku o kiku no ga tanoshimi na n desu.
lines.ja: チャンネルを変えても、どこもニュースばかりですよ。だから、ユキさんの音楽を聞くのが楽しみなんです。
lines.kana: チャンネルをかえても、どこもニュースばかりですよ。だから、ゆきさんのおんがくをきくのがたのしみなんです。
lines.english: Even if I change the channel, it's news everywhere. So listening to your music is what I look forward to.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou datta n desu ka. watashi mo terebi wa minai node, itsumo ongaku o kaketeru n desu.
lines.ja: そうだったんですか。私もテレビは見ないので、いつも音楽をかけてるんです。
lines.kana: そうだったんですか。わたしもテレビはみないので、いつもおんがくをかけてるんです。
lines.english: Oh, so that's why. I don't watch TV either, so I always have music on.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kinou wa, terebi mo minai shi, ongaku mo nai shi, chotto sabishikatta desu yo.
lines.ja: 昨日は、テレビも見ないし、音楽もないし、ちょっと寂しかったですよ。
lines.kana: きのうは、テレビもみないし、おんがくもないし、ちょっとさびしかったですよ。
lines.english: So last night, with no TV and no music, it was a bit lonely.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sumimasen! jaa, kyou wa uchi ni kaettara, sugu ongaku o kakemasu ne.
lines.ja: すみません！じゃあ、今日はうちに帰ったら、すぐ音楽をかけますね。
lines.kana: すみません！じゃあ、きょうはうちにかえったら、すぐおんがくをかけますね。
lines.english: I'm sorry! Then today I'll put music on the minute I get home.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. tanoshimi ni shite imasu.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。楽しみにしています。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。たのしみにしています。
lines.english: Thank you. I'll look forward to it.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Satou-san tells Yuki her music was too loud last night, and she promises to turn it down from now on.
Satou-san's TV only shows the news, so Yuki offers to come round tonight and change the channel for him.
Satou-san has stopped watching TV because the news is all bad. He enjoys Yuki's music and missed it last night, and she promises to put it on as soon as she gets home.

questions.explanation: Lines 3-5: Satou-san brings up Yuki's music, but not to complain (iie, sou ja nai n desu). Last night she had none on, and he wondered if something was wrong. Lines 7-11: he doesn't watch TV these days, because the news is all bad stories and every channel is news, so listening to her music is what he looks forward to. Line 13: last night was a bit lonely. Line 14: she'll put music on as soon as she gets home today. A is wrong: Yuki asks if it was too loud (line 4), but he says that's not it, and there was no music at all last night (line 5). B is wrong: changing the channel is Yuki's suggestion (line 10), he says every channel is news anyway (line 11), and what she offers is music, not a visit.

questions.english: Mai asks you, "uchi ni kaettara, itsumo nani shiteru no?" (What do you usually do once you get home?) Tell her you watch TV.
questions.ja: うちに帰ったら、いつも何してるの？
questions.kana: うちにかえったら、いつもなにしてるの？
questions.romaji: uchi ni kaettara, itsumo nani shiteru no?
questions.answer: Say you watch TV, with terebi and miru in the -teru form for something you do as a routine: terebi miteru kana.

modelAnswers.romaji: terebi miteru kana.
modelAnswers.ja: テレビ見てるかな。
modelAnswers.english: I guess I watch TV.

modelAnswers.romaji: itsumo terebi o mite imasu.
modelAnswers.ja: いつもテレビを見ています。
modelAnswers.english: I usually watch TV.

questions.explanation: TV takes miru, the same 'watch' verb as the news. The -teru form (miteru, polite mite imasu) is what you do as a routine, like Yuki's itsumo ongaku o kaketeru in line 12. Satou-san uses the negative in line 7 (saikin wa, terebi o minai n desu), and so does Yuki in line 12 (terebi wa minai node). Casual speech drops o, and kana softens it to 'I guess'. The polite model is for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: After saying every channel is news, Satou-san tells Yuki what he looks forward to instead. What did he say?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは何が楽しみだと言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんはなにがたのしみだといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa nani ga tanoshimi da to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Listening to your music is what I look forward to.
choices.romaji: yuki-san no ongaku o kiku no ga tanoshimi na n desu.

choices.english: Asking your music is what I look forward to.
choices.romaji: yuki-san no ongaku ni kiku no ga tanoshimi na n desu.

choices.english: Putting your music on is what I look forward to.
choices.romaji: yuki-san no ongaku o kakeru no ga tanoshimi na n desu.

questions.explanation: Line 11: ongaku o kiku is listening to music, and Satou-san is the one listening, from next door. B turns English 'listen to' into ni. With ni, kiku means asking someone (sensei ni kiku), so it would mean asking her music something. Listening takes o, or a dropped o, as in Yuki's line 6 (watashi no ongaku, kiiteru n desu ka?). C uses kakeru, putting music on, which is Yuki's part (lines 3, 12 and 14): she puts it on, and he listens.

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "ne, kesa no nyuusu mita? yabakatta yo." (Did you see the news this morning? It was crazy.) You haven't. Tell him you haven't seen the news this morning, and ask what happened.
questions.ja: ね、今朝のニュース見た？やばかったよ。
questions.kana: ね、けさのニュースみた？やばかったよ。
questions.romaji: ne, kesa no nyuusu mita? yabakatta yo.
questions.answer: Say no, with nyuusu and miru in the -te nai form ('haven't seen'): uun, kesa wa nyuusu mitenai. nani ga atta no?

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, kesa wa nyuusu mitenai. nani ga atta no?
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、今朝はニュース見てない。何があったの？
modelAnswers.english: No, I haven't seen the news this morning. What happened?

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, kesa wa nyuusu o mite imasen. nani ka atta n desu ka?
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、今朝はニュースを見ていません。何かあったんですか？
modelAnswers.english: No, I haven't seen the news this morning. Did something happen?

questions.explanation: The news takes miru, just like TV, and that covers a news app on your phone too. Yuki and Satou-san use it in lines 8-9 (nyuusu o mite imashita yo ne / nyuusu o miru to). Mitenai (polite mite imasen) is 'haven't seen it', the natural reply when something is news to you, and kesa wa means 'this morning, at least'. Kiku is only for the news on the radio. The polite model is for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: You're at Kenta's flat and he's cooking. He says, "gohan, mou sugu dekiru kara ne." (The food'll be ready soon.) Ask if it's okay to put some music on.
questions.ja: ご飯、もうすぐできるからね。
questions.kana: ごはん、もうすぐできるからね。
questions.romaji: gohan, mou sugu dekiru kara ne.
questions.answer: Ask permission with ongaku and kakeru in the -te form plus ii?: jaa, ongaku kakete ii?

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, ongaku kakete ii?
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、音楽かけていい？
modelAnswers.english: Okay. Mind if I put some music on?

modelAnswers.romaji: ongaku kakete mo ii? nani ga ii?
modelAnswers.ja: 音楽かけてもいい？何がいい？
modelAnswers.english: Mind if I put some music on? What do you feel like?

questions.explanation: Starting music on a speaker is ongaku o kakeru, Yuki's habit in lines 3, 12 and 14 (sugu ongaku o kakemasu ne). English 'play' is not asobu here (that's play for fun) and not hiku (playing an instrument). It isn't ongaku o kiku either: that's the listening, which is Satou-san's part (lines 6 and 11). Kakete ii? and kakete mo ii? both ask 'is it okay if I...?', and casual speech drops o.

questions.english: When Satou-san says the news is nothing but bad stories, Yuki asks, "jaa, channeru o kaetara dou desu ka?" What is she suggesting?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何をしたらいいと言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなにをしたらいいといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nani o shitara ii to iimashita ka?

choices.english: That he stop watching TV for a while.
That he switch to a different channel.
That he head back home for now.

questions.explanation: Line 10: channeru o kaeru is changing the channel, and kaetara dou desu ka? is 'how about changing it?'. Satou-san's reply in line 11 confirms it: channeru o kaete mo, doko mo nyuusu bakari (even if I change the channel, it's news everywhere). A is what he already does (line 7: saikin wa, terebi o minai n desu). That would be terebi o minai, with no channel in it. C mixes up kaeru 'change' with kaeru 'go home'. Going home is kaettara, with a double t, as in Yuki's line 14 (uchi ni kaettara); changing is kaetara, with one.

newWords.english: noisy, too loud (urusakatta desu ka? = was it too loud?)
something to look forward to (tanoshimi ni shite imasu = I'm looking forward to it)

script.title: The cat who opens doors
script.setting: Saturday evening. Mai is away for the weekend, and Sora, Kenta's flatmate, is staying at her flat to look after her cat, Mochi. Mai phones to see how it's going.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, sora-kun? mochi, daijoubu?
lines.ja: もしもし、ソラくん？モチ、大丈夫？
lines.kana: もしもし、そらくん？もち、だいじょうぶ？
lines.english: Hi, Sora? How's Mochi?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, daijoubu da yo. demo ne, heya no doa, shimete mo shimete mo aku n da yo.
lines.ja: うん、大丈夫だよ。でもね、部屋のドア、閉めても閉めても開くんだよ。
lines.kana: うん、だいじょうぶだよ。でもね、へやのどあ、しめてもしめてもあくんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, she's fine. But listen, the door to the room keeps opening, however many times I shut it.

questions.explanation: Line 2: the room door keeps opening however often Sora shuts it. Line 5: Mai explains that Mochi opens doors by herself (jibun de doa akeru), and in line 7 tells him to lock the front door so she can't get out. Lines 8-10: Sora isn't sure he locked it, checks, and finds the door shut and locked (doa shimatteru, kagi mo kakatteru). Lines 12-14: the room door opens again, and Sora sees Mochi do it (mochi ga doa aketa). A is wrong: the front door was shut and locked (line 10), and Mochi was in the flat (line 14). B is wrong: Sora is the one shutting the room door (line 2), Mochi is the one opening it, and Mai tells him he doesn't need to shut it anymore (line 15).

questions.explanation: Someone opening a door is doa (o) akeru, so a request is doa akete, made softer with kureru or moraeru. Not doa aite: aku is what the door does with nobody doing it (line 12: heya no doa ga aita), so you can't ask a person to do it.

Doa shimeta (shimeru) would mean you shut it yourself, but you only found it shut. Doa ga shimeteru isn't Japanese: with ga, the verb is shimaru.

questions.explanation: Locking up is kagi (o) kakeru: you put the lock on, so the object is kagi, not doa. Mai says it in line 7 (genkan no doa wa kagi kakete ne) and line 15 (genkan wa kagi kakete ne!), and Sora panics about it in line 8 (kagi kaketa kke?). Kagi shimete ne is just as common in casual speech. Not kagi kakatteru: that's the state, 'it's locked', which is Sora's reply in line 16.

questions.romaji: sora-kun wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I told you, it's locked! (kakeru, the act of locking, with ga)
I've locked the door (rokku suru), I told you!
I told you, it's locked!

questions.explanation: Line 16: kagi kakatteru, the -teru form of kakaru: the lock is on. Sora found it that way in line 10 (kagi mo kakatteru yo), so he's describing how it is, not doing anything. A, kagi ga kaketeru, is the usual mistake for 'it's locked': kakeru is the act of locking, as in Mai's kagi kakete ne (lines 7 and 15), and with ga the verb is kakaru. B, rokku suru, is mostly for cars and phones, and it makes the door the thing you lock; at the front door it's the kagi that kakaru.

choices.english: Kenji was supposed to keep an eye on the curry but had his music on, and his mother is the one who smells it burning.
Kenji didn't hear his mother calling him to dinner. While she's telling him off, he hears a noise and smells burning: she'd left the curry on the stove. It's only a little burnt.
Kenji hears a noise and smells something burning, but his mother says it's nothing, and the curry burns so badly they can't eat it.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Okaasan told him again and again (nando mo itta noni), but he had music on and didn't notice (ongaku kiitete, zenzen ki tsukanakatta). Lines 8-10: Kenji hears a noise (oto shinakatta?) and then smells burning (kogeta nioi mo shinai?). Line 11: it's the curry, and line 13: it's only a little burnt (chotto kogeta dake). A is wrong: Kenji was up in his room, and he is the one who smells the burning (line 10); his mother hadn't noticed (line 14). C is wrong: she says there was no noise (line 9), but she agrees about the smell (line 11: honto da), and the curry is fine to eat: Kenji calls it saikou in line 16.

questions.english: You walk into the kitchen while Okaasan is cooking. She says "gohan, mou sugu dekiru yo." (Dinner's nearly ready.) Something smells great. Tell her.
questions.ja: ご飯、もうすぐできるよ。
questions.kana: ごはん、もうすぐできるよ。
questions.romaji: gohan, mou sugu dekiru yo.
questions.answer: Make the smell the subject and use suru, not kagu: a, ii nioi suru!

modelAnswers.romaji: a, nanka ii nioi suru!
modelAnswers.ja: あ、なんかいい匂いする！
modelAnswers.english: Ooh, something smells good!

modelAnswers.romaji: un, ii nioi suru ne. kyou, karee?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、いい匂いするね。今日、カレー？
modelAnswers.english: Mm, that smells good. Is it curry tonight?

questions.explanation: Kenji says exactly this in line 6: a, nanka ii nioi suru. The smell is the subject and suru reports it; ga is usually dropped in casual speech. Don't reach for kagu (sniff): that's smelling on purpose, not a smell reaching you. Visiting someone like Satou-san, the polite version keeps ga: ii nioi ga shimasu ne.

questions.english: When Kenji first senses something is wrong, what does he ask his mother?
questions.ja: ケンジ君はお母さんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんはおかあさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-kun wa okaasan ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Did you just listen to a noise? (kiku: listening on purpose)
Didn't you just smell something?
Did you just hear something? (lit. 'wasn't there a noise?')

questions.explanation: Line 8: ima, nanka oto shinakatta? The noise is the subject and suru reports it: oto shita is 'there was a noise', here as a 'wasn't there...?' question, and his mother answers with the same verb (line 9: oto? shinakatta yo). A is the English 'did you hear a noise' built with kiku, but kiku is listening on purpose, like ongaku kiitete in line 2; for a sound that just reached you, natives say oto shita (or oto ga kikoeta). B is the smell version, but the smell comes later: in line 10 Kenji says kogeta nioi mo shinai?, with mo ('too') because it comes on top of the noise.

questions.english: Okaasan phones you, but the line is bad. She says "moshimoshi? are? moshimoshi?" Ask her if she can hear you.
questions.ja: もしもし？あれ？もしもし？
questions.kana: もしもし？あれ？もしもし？
questions.romaji: moshimoshi? are? moshimoshi?
questions.answer: Ask with kikoeru and your voice as the subject: moshimoshi, koe kikoeru? Not kiiteru? (are you listening?).

modelAnswers.romaji: moshimoshi, koe kikoeru?
modelAnswers.ja: もしもし、声聞こえる？
modelAnswers.english: Hello? Can you hear me?

modelAnswers.romaji: okaasan, koe kikoeteru?
modelAnswers.ja: お母さん、声聞こえてる？
modelAnswers.english: Mum, can you hear me?

questions.explanation: On a call, the question is whether your voice is reaching her, so the verb is kikoeru with koe as the subject: koe kikoeru? or koe kikoeteru?. Okaasan asks the same thing in line 1 (okaasan no koe, kikoenakatta?). Don't say kiiteru?: that's 'are you listening?', and Kenji's comeback in line 4 turns on exactly this difference (kiiteru yo! koe ga kikoenakatta dake da yo: 'I do listen, I just couldn't hear you'). On a work call, make it polite: koe kikoemasu ka?

questions.english: In the kitchen, Kenji says to his mother "okaasan mo, zenzen ki tsukanakatta ne." What does he mean?
questions.ja: どういうことですか？
questions.kana: どういうことですか？
questions.romaji: dou iu koto desu ka?

choices.english: She hadn't noticed the curry burning either, just as he hadn't noticed her calling.
She wasn't careful when she rushed down to the kitchen.
She doesn't listen to him either.

questions.explanation: Line 14: ki tsukanakatta is the past negative of ki ga tsuku, 'didn't notice', with ga dropped. The mo ('you too') points back to line 2, where Kenji said the same about not noticing her calling (zenzen ki tsukanakatta); now she hadn't noticed the burning smell. She takes the point in line 15: ki ga tsuite kurete, arigatou (thanks for noticing). B mixes it up with ki o tsukeru (be careful), which sounds almost the same: Kenji did shout ki o tsukete! as she ran downstairs (line 12), but that's a different phrase. C would be kikanai or kiitenakatta (not listening), which is her complaint about him in line 3, not his about her.

script.title: An hour of babysitting
script.setting: A Saturday morning outside Kenta's building. Kenta is minding his sister's month-old baby for the first time, and it won't stop crying. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, comes out and hears it.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nakanaide, nakanaide. sugu kaette kuru kara ne.
lines.ja: 泣かないで、泣かないで。すぐ帰ってくるからね。
lines.kana: なかないで、なかないで。すぐかえってくるからね。
lines.english: Don't cry, don't cry. She'll be back soon, okay?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-san, ohayou gozaimasu. are? okosan ga ita n desu ka?
lines.ja: ケンタさん、おはようございます。あれ？お子さんがいたんですか？
lines.kana: けんたさん、おはようございます。あれ？おこさんがいたんですか？
lines.english: Good morning, Kenta-san. Oh? I didn't know you had a child.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, ohayou gozaimasu. iya, boku wa kodomo inai desu yo. sengetsu, ane ni kodomo ga umareta n desu.
lines.ja: あ、おはようございます。いや、僕は子供いないですよ。先月、姉に子供が生まれたんです。
lines.kana: あ、おはようございます。いや、ぼくはこどもいないですよ。せんげつ、あねにこどもがうまれたんです。
lines.english: Oh, good morning. No, I don't have any kids. My sister had a baby last month.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: aa, oneesan no okosan desu ka. omedetou gozaimasu.
lines.ja: ああ、お姉さんのお子さんですか。おめでとうございます。
lines.kana: ああ、おねえさんのおこさんですか。おめでとうございます。
lines.english: Ah, it's your sister's little one. Congratulations.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. ane, kodomo ga umarete kara, zutto jikan ga nakute. kyou yatto, kami kiri ni itteru n desu.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。姉、子供が生まれてから、ずっと時間がなくて。今日やっと、髪切りに行ってるんです。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。あね、こどもがうまれてから、ずっとじかんがなくて。きょうやっと、かみきりにいってるんです。
lines.english: Thank you. Since the baby came, my sister hasn't had a minute to herself. Today she's finally gone to get her hair cut.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore de, kenta-san ga mendou o miteru n desu ka. demo, sugoku naitemasu ne.
lines.ja: それで、ケンタさんが面倒を見てるんですか。でも、すごく泣いてますね。
lines.kana: それで、けんたさんがめんどうをみてるんですか。でも、すごくないてますね。
lines.english: So that's why you're looking after the baby. The little one's really crying, though.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sou na n desu. ane ga dete, mada ichijikan na n desu kedo. kodomo sodateru no tte, taihen desu ne.
lines.ja: そうなんです。姉が出て、まだ一時間なんですけど。子供育てるのって、大変ですね。
lines.kana: そうなんです。あねがでて、まだいちじかんなんですけど。こどもそだてるのって、たいへんですね。
lines.english: It is. My sister's only been gone an hour, but raising kids sure is hard work.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: haha. kodomo ga otona ni naru made, nijuunen arimasu yo. chotto, ii desu ka?
lines.ja: はは。子供が大人になるまで、二十年ありますよ。ちょっと、いいですか？
lines.kana: はは。こどもがおとなになるまで、にじゅうねんありますよ。ちょっと、いいですか？
lines.english: Ha ha. It's twenty years until a child grows up, you know. May I?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? a, hai. douzo.
lines.ja: え？あ、はい。どうぞ。
lines.kana: え？あ、はい。どうぞ。
lines.english: Huh? Oh, sure. Here.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ne? mou naitenai deshou?
lines.ja: ね？もう泣いてないでしょう？
lines.kana: ね？もうないてないでしょう？
lines.english: See? No more crying.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, sugoi! satou-san, okosan iru n desu ka?
lines.ja: え、すごい！佐藤さん、お子さんいるんですか？
lines.kana: え、すごい！さとうさん、おこさんいるんですか？
lines.english: Wow, amazing! Satou-san, do you have kids?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai, sannin imasu yo. minna mou otona ni natte, uchi o demashita kedo ne.
lines.ja: はい、三人いますよ。みんなもう大人になって、うちを出ましたけどね。
lines.kana: はい、さんにんいますよ。みんなもうおとなになって、うちをでましたけどね。
lines.english: Yes, three. They're all grown up now and have left home, mind you.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sannin mo! kodomo sannin sodateta n desu ka. sugoi naa.
lines.ja: 三人も！子供三人育てたんですか。すごいなあ。
lines.kana: さんにんも！こどもさんにんそだてたんですか。すごいなあ。
lines.english: Three! You raised three kids? That's amazing.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: iya iya, kodomo no mendou o miteta no wa, zutto tsuma datta n desu. watashi wa shigoto bakkari de.
lines.ja: いやいや、子供の面倒を見てたのは、ずっと妻だったんです。私は仕事ばっかりで。
lines.kana: いやいや、こどものめんどうをみてたのは、ずっとつまだったんです。わたしはしごとばっかりで。
lines.english: Oh no, no. It was always my wife who looked after the kids. I was working all the time.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? demo, ima no, sugokatta desu yo.
lines.ja: え？でも、今の、すごかったですよ。
lines.kana: え？でも、いまの、すごかったですよ。
lines.english: Really? But what you just did was amazing.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: mago ga umarete kara, maishuu mendou o miteru n desu. kodomo o sodateru no ga taihen da tte, yatto wakarimashita yo.
lines.ja: 孫が生まれてから、毎週面倒を見てるんです。子供を育てるのが大変だって、やっと分かりましたよ。
lines.kana: まごがうまれてから、まいしゅうめんどうをみてるんです。こどもをそだてるのがたいへんだって、やっとわかりましたよ。
lines.english: Since my grandchild was born, I've looked after them every week. Only now have I learned how hard it is to raise kids.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jaa, ane ga kaette kuru made, mendou mite moraemasen ka? onegai shimasu!
lines.ja: じゃあ、姉が帰ってくるまで、面倒見てもらえませんか？お願いします！
lines.kana: じゃあ、あねがかえってくるまで、めんどうみてもらえませんか？おねがいします！
lines.english: Then could you look after the baby until my sister gets back? Please!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: haha, ii desu yo. demo, kenta-san mo koko ni ite kudasai ne.
lines.ja: はは、いいですよ。でも、ケンタさんもここにいてくださいね。
lines.kana: はは、いいですよ。でも、けんたさんもここにいてくださいね。
lines.english: Ha ha, all right. But you're staying here too, Kenta-san.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenta has just become a father, and Satou-san gives him tips on raising kids.
Satou-san asks Kenta to look after his grandchild for the morning.
Satou-san settles the baby Kenta is minding for his sister, and Kenta asks him to help until she's back.

questions.explanation: Line 3: the baby isn't Kenta's. He has no kids (kodomo inai), and his sister had a baby last month (ane ni kodomo ga umareta). Line 5: she has finally gone to get her hair cut, so Kenta is looking after the baby (line 6). Lines 8-10: Satou-san takes the baby and it stops crying (mou naitenai deshou?). Line 17: Kenta asks him to look after it until his sister gets back (mendou mite moraemasen ka?), and in line 18 he agrees, as long as Kenta stays too. A is wrong: Kenta says he has no kids (line 3), and the tips idea is turned on its head when Satou-san admits his wife did the looking after (line 14). B is wrong: Satou-san looks after his grandchild every week (line 16), but today it's Kenta who asks Satou-san for help.

questions.english: Satou-san gets talking with you outside the building and asks, "okosan wa iru n desu ka?" (Do you have children?) Answer him using kodomo and iru: say you don't have any, or how many you have.
questions.ja: お子さんはいるんですか？
questions.kana: おこさんはいるんですか？
questions.romaji: okosan wa iru n desu ka?
questions.answer: Use kodomo with iru, the verb for people: kodomo wa inai n desu (I don't have any), or kodomo ga hitori imasu (I have one), with the number after kodomo.

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, kodomo wa inai n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、子供はいないんです。
modelAnswers.english: No, I don't have any children.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, kodomo ga hitori imasu. sengetsu umareta n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、子供が一人います。先月生まれたんです。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, I have one. Born just last month.

questions.explanation: Children, like brothers and sisters, take iru, the verb for people and animals. Don't use aru (for things) or kodomo o motte imasu (a word-for-word 'have'). Satou-san asks with iru in line 2 (okosan ga ita n desu ka?), Kenta answers kodomo inai in line 3 and asks okosan iru n desu ka? in line 11, and Satou-san answers sannin imasu in line 12, with the number before the verb. Say okosan for someone else's children and kodomo for your own. Satou-san speaks politely, so answer politely.

questions.english: When Satou-san asks if the baby is Kenta's, how does Kenta explain whose it is?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、お姉さんのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、おねえさんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, oneesan no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: my sister 'had' a child (motsu, hold or own)
my sister had a baby (a baby was born to her)
my sister 'had' a child (aru, the verb for things)

questions.explanation: Line 3: 'sengetsu, ane ni kodomo ga umareta n desu.' The baby is the subject of umareru (be born) and the parent takes ni, which is how Japanese shares birth news. Kenta uses it again in line 5 (kodomo ga umarete kara, since the baby was born). A is wrong: kodomo o motsu is about being a parent as a stage of life (kodomo o motte kara, since becoming a parent), not news of a birth, and motta on its own sounds like she picked something up. C is wrong: aru is for things, and kodomo ga atta isn't said for having a baby.

questions.english: After one hour, Kenta says raising kids is hard work. Satou-san laughs and says, "kodomo ga otona ni naru made, nijuunen arimasu yo." What does he mean?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、何が言いたかったんですか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、なにがいいたかったんですか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, nani ga iitakatta n desu ka?

choices.english: Kenta has only just started: it takes twenty years for a child to grow up.
Kenta needs another twenty years before he's grown-up enough to have kids.
His own children grew up twenty years ago, so he's forgotten how hard it is.

questions.explanation: Line 8: otona ni naru is 'become an adult, grow up', and made is 'until', so a child takes twenty years to grow up. After Kenta's single hour (line 7), Satou-san is gently teasing him: the hard part has only just begun. In line 12 he uses it about his own children: minna mou otona ni natte (they're all grown up now). B is wrong: otona ni naru can also mean acting more grown-up, but the subject here is kodomo (a child), not Kenta. C is wrong: he never says when his children grew up, and in line 16 he says he has only now learned how hard raising kids is.

questions.english: That evening Kenta tells you, "kyou, zutto ane no kodomo no mendou miteta n da. tsukareta." (I was looking after my sister's baby all day. I'm worn out.) Sympathise using kodomo and sodateru: say raising kids must be tough.
questions.ja: 今日、ずっと姉の子供の面倒見てたんだ。疲れた。
questions.kana: きょう、ずっとあねのこどものめんどうみてたんだ。つかれた。
questions.romaji: kyou, zutto ane no kodomo no mendou miteta n da. tsukareta.
questions.answer: Say raising kids is tough with kodomo (o) sodateru and taihen: kodomo sodateru no tte taihen da yo ne. In casual speech o drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: otsukare! kodomo sodateru no tte, taihen da yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: お疲れ！子供育てるのって、大変だよね。
modelAnswers.english: Well done! Raising kids is tough, isn't it.

modelAnswers.romaji: kodomo sodateru no, honto ni taihen na n da ne. oneesan, sugoi naa.
modelAnswers.ja: 子供育てるの、ほんとに大変なんだね。お姉さん、すごいなあ。
modelAnswers.english: Raising kids really is tough, huh. Your sister's amazing.

questions.explanation: sodateru is raising children over the years, with kodomo as its object. Kenta says it in line 7 (kodomo sodateru no tte, taihen desu ne) and line 13 (kodomo sannin sodateta), and Satou-san in line 16 (kodomo o sodateru no ga taihen da tte). Its partner sodatsu is the child's side, growing up (toukyou de sodatta, I grew up in Tokyo), so it doesn't fit here. Kenta is your friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: Kenta tells you, "ashita mo ane ga kaimono ni iku n da kedo, boku, shigoto na n da. dou shiyou." (My sister's going shopping again tomorrow, but I've got work. What do I do?) Offer to look after the baby, using mendou and miru.
questions.ja: 明日も姉が買い物に行くんだけど、僕、仕事なんだ。どうしよう。
questions.kana: あしたもあねがかいものにいくんだけど、ぼく、しごとなんだ。どうしよう。
questions.romaji: ashita mo ane ga kaimono ni iku n da kedo, boku, shigoto na n da. dou shiyou.
questions.answer: Offer with mendou (o) miru: watashi ga mendou miru yo (I'll look after the baby), or the favour form mendou mite ageru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, ashita wa watashi ga mendou miru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、明日は私が面倒見るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Then I'll look after the baby tomorrow.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo, kodomo no mendou nara mite ageru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ、子供の面倒なら見てあげるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sure, I can look after the baby for you.

questions.explanation: mendou o miru is looking after someone and taking responsibility for them: babies, kids, grandchildren. Satou-san uses it in line 6 (kenta-san ga mendou o miteru), line 14 (kodomo no mendou o miteta) and line 16 (maishuu mendou o miteru), and Kenta asks for it in line 17 (mendou mite moraemasen ka?). In casual speech o drops (mendou miru). Don't mix it up with mendokusai (what a hassle): same mendou, opposite feel. Kenta is a friend, so casual is right.

newWords.english: someone else's child (polite; say kodomo for your own)
my older sister (oneesan: someone else's older sister)
cry (naiteru: is crying; nakanaide: don't cry)
until (ane ga kaette kuru made = until my sister gets back)

script.title: Curry with a fever
script.setting: Saturday morning. Kenta phones Yuki to fix a time for the movie they planned, but she is in bed feeling awful.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? kyou no eiga, nanji ni suru?
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？今日の映画、何時にする？
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？きょうのえいが、なんじにする？
lines.english: Hey, Yuki? What time do you want to do the movie today?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, kenta. gomen, kyou, nanka darukute.
lines.ja: あ、ケンタ。ごめん、今日、なんかだるくて。
lines.kana: あ、けんた。ごめん、きょう、なんかだるくて。
lines.english: Oh, Kenta. Sorry, today I'm kind of... not feeling it.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: darui? e, eiga iku no ga darui no? hidoi naa.
lines.ja: だるい？え、映画行くのがだるいの？ひどいなあ。
lines.kana: だるい？え、えいがいくのがだるいの？ひどいなあ。
lines.english: Not feeling it? What, you can't be bothered to go to the movie? Harsh.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou ja nakute, karada ga darui no! kinou no yoru, netsu deta n da.
lines.ja: そうじゃなくて、体がだるいの！昨日の夜、熱出たんだ。
lines.kana: そうじゃなくて、からだがだるいの！きのうのよる、ねつでたんだ。
lines.english: Not like that! I mean my body feels all heavy. I came down with a fever last night.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, netsu deta no? daijoubu?
lines.ja: え、熱出たの？大丈夫？
lines.kana: え、ねつでたの？だいじょうぶ？
lines.english: Wait, you got a fever? Are you okay?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uun, mada sanjuuhachido mo netsu aru.
lines.ja: ううん、まだ38度も熱ある。
lines.kana: ううん、まださんじゅうはちどもねつある。
lines.english: Not really. I've still got a fever of 38.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: uwa, takai ne. seki toka wa?
lines.ja: うわ、高いね。咳とかは？
lines.kana: うわ、たかいね。せきとかは？
lines.english: Yikes, that's high. Any cough or anything?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: seki mo deru shi, hanamizu mo deru shi, mou saiaku.
lines.ja: 咳も出るし、鼻水も出るし、もう最悪。
lines.kana: せきもでるし、はなみずもでるし、もうさいあく。
lines.english: I've got a cough, my nose is running... it's the worst.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sokka, kaze hiichatta n da.
lines.ja: そっか、風邪ひいちゃったんだ。
lines.kana: そっか、かぜひいちゃったんだ。
lines.english: Ah, so you've caught a cold.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. a, kenta mo kinou, seki deteta yo ne?
lines.ja: うん。あ、ケンタも昨日、咳出てたよね？
lines.kana: うん。あ、けんたもきのう、せきでてたよね？
lines.english: Yeah. Oh, wait. You had a cough yesterday too, didn't you?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? a, un. hanamizu mo deteta. netsu wa denakatta kedo.
lines.ja: え？あ、うん。鼻水も出てた。熱は出なかったけど。
lines.kana: え？あ、うん。はなみずもでてた。ねつはでなかったけど。
lines.english: Huh? Oh, yeah. And a runny nose. I didn't get a fever, though.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore da! kenta no kaze ga utsutta n da!
lines.ja: それだ！ケンタの風邪がうつったんだ！
lines.kana: それだ！けんたのかぜがうつったんだ！
lines.english: That's it! I caught your cold!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gomen! eiga wa raishuu ikou. nanka tsukutte motte iku yo.
lines.ja: ごめん！映画は来週行こう。なんか作って持っていくよ。
lines.kana: ごめん！えいがはらいしゅういこう。なんかつくってもっていくよ。
lines.english: Sorry! Let's do the movie next week. I'll cook something and bring it over.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto? jaa, kenta no karee ga ii.
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、ケンタのカレーがいい。
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、けんたのカレーがいい。
lines.english: Really? Then I want your curry.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: karee? netsu aru noni?
lines.ja: カレー？熱あるのに？
lines.kana: カレー？ねつあるのに？
lines.english: Curry? When you've got a fever?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. karada wa darui kedo, karee nara taberareru.
lines.ja: うん。体はだるいけど、カレーなら食べられる。
lines.kana: うん。からだはだるいけど、カレーならたべられる。
lines.english: Yep. My body feels like lead, but curry I can always manage.

questions.english: What happens in this phone call?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki can't be bothered to go to the movie today, so Kenta gets annoyed and goes without her.
Kenta has caught Yuki's cold, so she offers to cook curry and bring it to him.
Yuki is sick, probably with Kenta's cold, so the movie moves to next week and Kenta will bring her food.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-4: Yuki's 'nanka darukute' is not about the movie, as Kenta guesses in line 3; she means karada ga darui, and a fever came on last night (netsu deta). Lines 6-8: she still has a fever of 38, a cough and a runny nose. Lines 10-12: Kenta had a cough and a runny nose yesterday, so she decides she caught his cold (kenta no kaze ga utsutta). Line 13: the movie moves to next week (eiga wa raishuu ikou) and Kenta will cook something and bring it over; line 14: she asks for his curry. A is Kenta's misreading, which Yuki corrects in line 4 (sou ja nakute), and nobody goes without her. B swaps the two: it is Yuki who caught Kenta's cold (line 12), and Kenta is the one cooking (lines 13-14: kenta no karee).

questions.english: Now you're the one in bed with the cold. Kenta drops by with curry and asks, "netsu wa dou?" (How's the fever?) It hasn't gone down. Tell him you still have a fever.
questions.ja: 熱はどう？
questions.kana: ねつはどう？
questions.romaji: netsu wa dou?
questions.answer: Say the fever is still there, with netsu and aru: un, mada netsu aru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, mada netsu aru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、まだ熱あるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I've still got a fever.

modelAnswers.romaji: mada chotto netsu aru. sanjuunanado.
modelAnswers.ja: まだちょっと熱ある。37度。
modelAnswers.english: Still a bit of a fever. 37.

questions.explanation: A fever you have right now is netsu ga aru: the fever 'exists'. That is Yuki's 'mada sanjuuhachido mo netsu aru' in line 6 and Kenta's 'netsu aru noni?' in line 15. English 'have' pulls toward motsu, but you never netsu o motsu. And netsu deta (line 4) is the moment it came on, not the fever you still have; in casual speech ga drops: netsu aru.

questions.english: When Yuki tells Kenta what happened last night, what does she say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、昨日の夜のことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、きのうのよるのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, kinou no yoru no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Last night I turned into a fever.
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, netsu ni natta n da.

choices.english: I came down with a fever last night.
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, netsu deta n da.

choices.english: Last night I received a fever.
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, netsu moratta n da.

questions.explanation: Line 4: kinou no yoru, netsu deta n da, and Kenta echoes it in line 5 (e, netsu deta no?). A fever 'comes out': netsu ga deru, with the past deta for the moment it came on. A, netsu ni naru, is English 'get' read as 'become'; Japanese doesn't say it. C, morau, is 'get' word for word; with illness it is only for catching a cold from someone (kenta no kaze moratta), never for a fever itself. For the cold she caught from Kenta, Yuki uses kaze ga utsuru (line 12).

questions.english: A few days later you've caught it too. Yuki phones, hears you coughing, and asks, "kaze hiita no? netsu aru?" (Did you catch a cold? Got a fever?) You have no fever, but you do have a cough. Tell her.
questions.ja: 風邪ひいたの？熱ある？
questions.kana: かぜひいたの？ねつある？
questions.romaji: kaze hiita no? netsu aru?
questions.answer: Say no fever, but a cough with seki and deru: netsu wa nai kedo, seki ga deru n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, netsu wa nai kedo, seki ga deru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、熱はないけど、咳が出るんだ。
modelAnswers.english: No, no fever, but I've got a cough.

modelAnswers.romaji: netsu wa nai. demo, seki ga sugoku deru.
modelAnswers.ja: 熱はない。でも、咳がすごく出る。
modelAnswers.english: No fever. But I'm coughing a lot.

questions.explanation: A cough 'comes out' like a fever does: seki ga deru, the same deru as Yuki's 'seki mo deru shi' in line 8 and her 'seki deteta yo ne?' to Kenta in line 10. English 'have a cough' pulls toward motsu, which isn't used; a cough that keeps coming takes deru (a clinic may also ask seki wa arimasu ka?). For coughing at this very moment, seki shiteru also works. Netsu wa nai is the negative of netsu ga aru.

questions.english: Next week at the movie, Yuki is still getting over her cold. She catches you staring and asks, "nani? nani miteru no?" (What? What are you looking at?) Her nose is running. Tell her.
questions.ja: なに？なに見てるの？
questions.kana: なに？なにみてるの？
questions.romaji: nani? nani miteru no?
questions.answer: Tell her her nose is running, with hanamizu and deru in the -teru form: hanamizu deteru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: hanamizu deteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 鼻水出てるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Your nose is running.

modelAnswers.romaji: yuki, hanamizu deteru. daijoubu?
modelAnswers.ja: ユキ、鼻水出てる。大丈夫？
modelAnswers.english: Yuki, your nose is running. You okay?

questions.explanation: A runny nose is hanamizu ga deru, 'nose water comes out'; English 'runny' has nothing to copy. Deteru is 'is coming out right now', as Kenta's 'hanamizu mo deteta' in line 11 is 'was running'. Yuki uses the plain form for her symptoms in line 8 (hanamizu mo deru shi). Between friends ga drops: hanamizu deteru yo.

questions.english: Kenta first thinks Yuki doesn't feel like going out. Then she says "sou ja nakute, karada ga darui no!" What does she mean?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、今どうですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、いまどうですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, ima dou desu ka?

choices.english: Her body feels heavy and run-down, the way it does when you're getting sick.
Going out today feels like too much of a drag.
She's worn out from doing too much yesterday.

questions.explanation: Line 4: karada ga darui is the heavy, sluggish feeling with no clear cause, and she adds straight away that a fever came on last night. She says it again in line 16 (karada wa darui kedo, karee nara taberareru). B is Kenta's misreading in line 3: darui on its own about something you have to do (eiga iku no ga darui) is a casual 'what a drag', which is why Yuki says sou ja nakute. C would be tsukareta, tired from effort; Yuki mentions no effort, only the fever, the cough and the runny nose.

newWords.english: kind of, sort of (filler); something (nanka tsukutte = make something)

lines.kana: もう！じぶんであけて！

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenta wakes Sora because he's late for work at twelve, and Sora hurries out into the rain.
Kenta wakes Sora for a shift that turns out to be next week; once everything is shut again, Sora can't get back to sleep.
Sora wants the window open because his room smells of alcohol, but Kenta shuts it when it starts to rain.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-6: Kenta gets Sora up by opening the curtains and then the window. Line 9: he thinks Sora has work at twelve today, but in line 10 Sora says that's next week (sore raishuu da yo). Kenta apologises and closes the curtains (lines 11 and 13), and shuts the window once it starts raining (lines 14-15). Line 16: by now Sora is wide awake (mou nerarenai) and wants the curtains open again, and in line 17 Kenta tells him to do it himself. A is wrong: there is no work today, and nobody goes out. C is wrong: it's Kenta who opens the window because of the smell (lines 5-7); Sora wants it shut because he's cold (lines 6 and 12).

questions.english: You're round at Kenta's. He walks in from the kitchen and says, "uwa, kono heya atsui ne." (Whew, it's hot in this room.) Offer to open the window.
questions.ja: うわ、この部屋暑いね。
questions.kana: うわ、このへやあついね。
questions.romaji: uwa, kono heya atsui ne.
questions.answer: Offer with mado and akeru, as a question: mado akete ii? (mind if I open the window?) or mado akeyou ka? (shall I open the window?).

modelAnswers.romaji: un. mado akete ii?
modelAnswers.ja: うん。窓開けていい？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah. Mind if I open the window?

modelAnswers.romaji: atsui ne. mado akeyou ka?
modelAnswers.ja: 暑いね。窓開けようか？
modelAnswers.english: It really is. Shall I open the window?

questions.explanation: Someone opening a window uses akeru, the verb Kenta uses in line 5 (mado mo akeru ne) and Sora throws back at him in line 6 (nande mado akeru no?). As an offer it's usually a question: akete ii? asks if it's okay, akeyou ka? offers to do it. Don't say mado aiteru here: that describes a window that is already open, not you opening it.

questions.english: Sora is shivering on the sofa and says, "samui! mado aiteru yo!" (It's freezing! The window's open!) You opened it earlier. Say sorry and that you'll shut it.
questions.ja: 寒い！窓開いてるよ！
questions.kana: さむい！まどあいてるよ！
questions.romaji: samui! mado aiteru yo!
questions.answer: Apologise and say you'll close it, with mado and shimeru: gomen, mado shimeru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, mado shimeru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、窓閉めるね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'll shut the window.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen. ima mado shimeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん。今窓閉めるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry. I'll close the window right now.

questions.explanation: Sora's aiteru describes the window's state: it's open. What you do about it is shimeru, someone shutting it, as Sora asks in lines 12 and 14 (mado mo shimete, mado shimete!) and Kenta reports in line 15 (mado shimeta yo). Not mado shimaru: shimaru is the window itself closing (mado shimatteru, the window is shut), not someone shutting it.

questions.english: When Kenta lets the daylight in, what does Sora shout?
questions.ja: ソラさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Argh, that's bright! Draw the curtains! (hiku, pull)
Argh, that's bright! Curtains, shut! (shimaru, shutting on their own)
Argh, that's bright! Close the curtains!

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenta has just opened the curtains (line 3: kaaten akeru yo) and the light hurts (mabushii), so Sora wants them shut: kaaten shimete. A is English 'draw the curtains' put into Japanese word for word (hiku, pull). Japanese does have kaaten o hiku, but it's mostly written and, like 'draw', it doesn't say which way, so in speech people name the direction with shimeru or akeru. B uses shimaru, the curtains shutting on their own, like doa ga shimaru (kaaten shimatteru = the curtains are shut), so it can't ask someone to shut them; that takes shimeru. Kenta closes them with the same verb in lines 11 and 13 (kaaten shimeru ne, kaaten wa shimeta kedo), and Sora only asks for the opposite, kaaten akete, at the very end, once he's given up on sleep (line 16).

newWords.english: dazzling, too bright (light in your eyes)

lines.kana: で、けんたくんから「ふたりとも、ずっとスマホいじってたね」ってきた。
lines.english: And Kenta wrote back: "You two were on your phones the whole time, huh."

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki wants Saturday's photos to send to Kenta, but Mai was on her phone all day and didn't take any.
Each of them has photos of the other on her phone all day, and Mai has already sent hers to Kenta.
Mai is upset that Yuki took photos of her without asking, so Yuki promises not to send them to Kenta.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Yuki asks Mai to send the Saturday photos. Lines 2-4: Mai's photos show Yuki on her phone the whole day (zutto sumaho ijitteta). Lines 7-10: Yuki's photos show Mai on hers too, looking at pictures of her cat. Line 14: Mai sent her photos to Kenta this morning, before she sent them to Yuki, and in line 16 Kenta writes back teasing them both. A is wrong because Mai did take photos (she shows them in line 2), and it's Yuki who doesn't want them sent to Kenta (line 13). C is wrong because Mai only says she didn't notice the photo being taken (line 8); she isn't upset, and the photos Yuki doesn't want sent are Mai's photos of her.

questions.english: You're out for a walk with Kenta when he stops and says: "Look! This place is amazing." Ask him to take a photo of you here.
questions.ja: 見て！ここ、すごいね。
questions.kana: みて！ここ、すごいね。
questions.romaji: mite! koko, sugoi ne.
questions.answer: Ask for a photo with shashin (o) toru in the te-form request: koko de shashin totte! or the softer shashin totte moraeru?

modelAnswers.romaji: nee, koko de shashin totte!
modelAnswers.ja: ねえ、ここで写真撮って！
modelAnswers.english: Hey, take a picture of me here!

modelAnswers.romaji: honto da. shashin totte moraeru?
modelAnswers.ja: ほんとだ。写真撮ってもらえる？
modelAnswers.english: You're right. Could you take a picture of me?

questions.explanation: For photos, English 'take' really is toru: Mai says kondo wa minna de shashin torou (line 12), and Yuki talks about the photos she took, jibun de totta shashin (line 5) and watashi ga totta shashin (line 7). It's the one 'take' that works this way: medicine is kusuri o nomu and a train is densha ni noru. Don't say shashin o morau: that means getting a photo from someone. To ask, use the te-form (shashin totte) or -te moraeru? to sound softer.

questions.english: Mai says Yuki was on her phone the whole time. What does Yuki say she was actually doing on it?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、スマホで何をしていましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、スマホでなにをしていましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, sumaho de nani o shite imashita ka?

choices.english: Sending the photos to Kenta.
Taking more photos of everyone.
Looking at the photos she had taken.

questions.explanation: Line 5: jibun de totta shashin, miteta n da yo. miteta is shashin o miru, looking at photos. totta only says which photos: the ones she had taken herself. B mixes up the two verbs. A is okuru, which comes up later, when Mai says she has already sent her photos to Kenta (line 14). Mai's comeback in line 6 is that looking at photos on your phone all day still counts as sumaho o ijiru, and she then makes the same excuse herself in line 10 (neko no shashin miteta no).

questions.english: When Mai shows Yuki the photos, what does she say Yuki was doing all day?
questions.ja: マイさんは、土曜日のユキさんについて、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、どようびのゆきさんについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, doyoubi no yuki-san ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: You were on your phone the whole time.
You were using your phone the whole time.
You were playing on your phone the whole time.

questions.explanation: Line 4: tenki yokatta noni, yuki, zutto sumaho ijitteta yo. Being idly on your phone is sumaho (o) ijiru, and about someone else it carries a mild complaint, as it does here. Mai says it again in line 6 and Kenta does in line 16. B, tsukau, is 'use' word for word. It would be understood, but it sounds like using the phone for a task, such as a call or a map. C, sumaho de asobu, means playing games on it, and nobody was doing that: Yuki was looking at her photos and Mai at photos of her cat.

questions.english: Mai tells you: "Some of yesterday's photos came out really well." Ask her to send them to you.
questions.ja: 昨日の写真、すごくいいのあるよ。
questions.kana: きのうのしゃしん、すごくいいのあるよ。
questions.romaji: kinou no shashin, sugoku ii no aru yo.
questions.answer: Ask with okuru as a request: shashin okutte, or okutte kurenai? to be softer. The person you send to takes ni: watashi ni mo okutte.

modelAnswers.romaji: honto? jaa, sono shashin okutte!
modelAnswers.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、その写真送って！
modelAnswers.english: Really? Then send them to me!

modelAnswers.romaji: sugoi! watashi ni mo shashin okutte kurenai?
modelAnswers.ja: すごい！私にも写真送ってくれない？
