lines.kana: え、くらい！けんじ、いるの？
lines.english: Huh, it's dark! Kenji, are you home?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un, iru yo.
lines.ja: うん、いるよ。
lines.kana: うん、いるよ。
lines.english: Yeah, I'm here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nande denki tsukenaide geemu shiteru no?
lines.ja: なんで電気つけないでゲームしてるの？
lines.kana: なんででんきつけないでげーむしてるの？
lines.english: Why are you playing games without putting the light on?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: denki, tsukenai n ja nakute, tsukanai n da yo.
lines.ja: 電気、つけないんじゃなくて、つかないんだよ。
lines.kana: でんき、つけないんじゃなくて、つかないんだよ。
lines.english: It's not that I'm not putting the light on. It won't come on.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, tsukanai no? rimokon wa?
lines.ja: え、つかないの？リモコンは？
lines.kana: え、つかないの？りもこんは？
lines.english: What, it won't come on? What about the remote?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: kore. botan, nando mo oshita kedo, dame.
lines.ja: これ。ボタン、何度も押したけど、だめ。
lines.kana: これ。ぼたん、なんどもおしたけど、だめ。
lines.english: Here. I've pressed the button over and over. Nothing.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto da. botan oshite mo, denki tsukanai. denchi kana?
lines.ja: ほんとだ。ボタン押しても、電気つかない。電池かな？
lines.kana: ほんとだ。ぼたんおしても、でんきつかない。でんちかな？
lines.english: You're right. I press the button and the light doesn't come on. The batteries, maybe?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: denchi wa kinou kaeta yo.
lines.ja: 電池は昨日替えたよ。
lines.kana: でんちはきのうかえたよ。
lines.english: I changed the batteries yesterday.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, nande darou. a! kinou no yoru, denki keshita no, kenji?
lines.ja: じゃあ、なんでだろう。あ！昨日の夜、電気消したの、ケンジ？
lines.kana: じゃあ、なんでだろう。あ！きのうのよる、でんきけしたの、けんじ？
lines.english: Then why...? Oh! Kenji, was it you who turned the light off last night?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. asoko no suitchi de keshita.
lines.ja: うん。あそこのスイッチで消した。
lines.kana: うん。あそこのすいっちでけした。
lines.english: Yeah. I turned it off at the switch over there.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore da yo! suitchi de denki keshitara, rimokon no botan oshite mo tsukanai no.
lines.ja: それだよ！スイッチで電気消したら、リモコンのボタン押してもつかないの。
lines.kana: それだよ！すいっちででんきけしたら、りもこんのぼたんおしてもつかないの。
lines.english: That's it! If you turn the light off at the switch, it won't come on however much you press the remote.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, sou na no?
lines.ja: え、そうなの？
lines.kana: え、そうなの？
lines.english: Wait, really?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou. jaa, asoko no suitchi de tsukete mite.
lines.ja: そう。じゃあ、あそこのスイッチでつけてみて。
lines.kana: そう。じゃあ、あそこのすいっちでつけてみて。
lines.english: Yep. Go on, try putting it on with that switch over there.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, tsuita! sugee.
lines.ja: あ、ついた！すげえ。
lines.kana: あ、ついた！すげえ。
lines.english: Oh, it came on! Nice.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: desho? ato, kenji no heya, denki tsuiteru yo.
lines.ja: でしょ？あと、ケンジの部屋、電気ついてるよ。
lines.kana: でしょ？あと、けんじのへや、でんきついてるよ。
lines.english: Told you. Oh, and the light's on in your room.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ee. keshite kite. kaaten mo shimetoite.
lines.ja: えー。消してきて。カーテンも閉めといて。
lines.kana: えー。けしてきて。かーてんもしめといて。
lines.english: Ugh. Go turn it off for me. And shut the curtains while you're there.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jibun de yatte! denki wa rimokon de keshite ne!
lines.ja: 自分でやって！電気はリモコンで消してね！
lines.kana: じぶんでやって！でんきはりもこんでけしてね！
lines.english: Do it yourself! And use the remote to turn the light off!

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: The remote's batteries were dead, so Yuki put new ones in and the light came on.
The light wouldn't come on from the remote because Kenji had turned it off at the wall switch last night. Turning it on at the switch fixed it.
Kenji was playing in the dark on purpose, so Yuki turned the light on at the switch herself.

questions.explanation: Lines 4-7: the light won't come on (tsukanai), however often Kenji and then Yuki press the remote's button. Lines 9-11: Kenji turned it off at the switch last night (suitchi de keshita), and once that happens the remote can't turn it back on. Lines 13-14: Kenji turns it on at the switch and it comes on (a, tsuita!). A is wrong: Kenji changed the batteries yesterday (line 8: denchi wa kinou kaeta yo), so they weren't the problem. C is wrong: Kenji wasn't choosing the dark (line 4: tsukenai n ja nakute, tsukanai). Also, Kenji turns it on at the switch, not Yuki.

questions.english: You walk into a room with Yuki in the evening, and she says, "kono heya, kurai ne." (This room's dark, isn't it?) Offer to put the light on.
questions.ja: この部屋、暗いね。
questions.kana: このへや、くらいね。
questions.romaji: kono heya, kurai ne.
questions.answer: Offer with denki and tsukeru in its 'shall I?' form: un, denki tsukeyou ka?

modelAnswers.romaji: un, denki tsukeyou ka?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、電気つけようか？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah. Shall I put the light on?

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, denki tsukeru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、電気つけるね。
modelAnswers.english: I'll put the light on, then.

questions.explanation: A light goes on with tsukeru. Yuki asks why Kenji is playing with the light off (line 3: nande denki tsukenaide...?) and later tells him asoko no suitchi de tsukete mite (line 13). tsukeyou ka? offers to do it, and tsukeru ne says you're doing it now. Don't carry akeru (open) over from doors, and don't say denki o ireru: ireru goes with suitchi (switch) or dengen (power), not with the light itself.

questions.english: Yuki suddenly guesses what went wrong. What does she ask Kenji?
questions.ja: ユキさんはケンジさんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはけんじさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa kenji-san ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Did you shut the light last night, Kenji? (shimeru, the door verb)
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, denki shimeta no, kenji?

choices.english: Did you cut off the power last night, Kenji?
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, denki tometa no, kenji?

choices.english: Was it you who turned the light off last night, Kenji?
choices.romaji: kinou no yoru, denki keshita no, kenji?

questions.explanation: Line 9: kinou no yoru, denki keshita no, kenji? A light goes off with kesu, and Kenji answers with the same verb in line 10 (suitchi de keshita). A is 'shut' put into Japanese: shimeru is for doors, windows and curtains. Kenji uses it for the curtains in line 16 (kaaten mo shimetoite), right after keshite kite for his light. B, denki o tomeru, means cutting off the power supply (what happens when the bill isn't paid), not switching off a light.

questions.english: Yuki asks Kenji why he's playing games without putting the light on. From his answer, why is the room dark?
questions.ja: 部屋はなんで暗いんですか？
questions.kana: へやはなんでくらいんですか？
questions.romaji: heya wa nande kurai n desu ka?

choices.english: Kenji has tried to put it on, but the light won't come on.
Kenji likes playing games in the dark, so he's left the light off.
Kenji forgot to put the light on because he was busy with his game.

questions.explanation: Line 4: denki, tsukenai n ja nakute, tsukanai n da yo. tsukenai (from tsukeru) is a person not putting it on, which is what Yuki assumed in line 3. tsukanai (from tsuku) is the light itself not coming on, and that is what's happening: he has pressed the remote's button over and over (line 6). The light takes tsuku all through the scene: tsuita when it finally comes on (line 14) and tsuiteru for the one left on in his room (line 15). B and C are both the tsukenai that Kenji denies: it isn't that he chose not to, or forgot. He tried and it won't work.

questions.english: Yuki hands you the light's remote and says, "kore de denki tsukete." (Put the light on with this.) It has lots of buttons. Ask her which one to press.
questions.ja: これで電気つけて。
questions.kana: これででんきつけて。
questions.romaji: kore de denki tsukete.
questions.answer: Ask which button with dono botan and osu: dono botan osu no?

modelAnswers.romaji: dono botan osu no?
modelAnswers.ja: どのボタン押すの？
modelAnswers.english: Which button do I press?

modelAnswers.romaji: dono botan o oseba ii?
modelAnswers.ja: どのボタンを押せばいい？
modelAnswers.english: Which button should I press?

questions.explanation: You press a button with osu. Kenji says botan, nando mo oshita kedo (line 6), Yuki says botan oshite mo, denki tsukanai (line 7), and in line 11 she says rimokon no botan oshite mo tsukanai no. Casual speech drops the o (botan osu no?). Pressing the button is osu; what the light does is tsuku, and what you do to it is tsukeru. The same botan o osu works for lifts, the stop button on a bus and ticket machines.

newWords.english: remote control (here, for the ceiling light)
switch (here, the light switch on the wall)
stop; denki o tomeru = cut off the power supply (only in a quiz choice)

script.title: Saved by a late train
script.setting: Late at night on a city station platform. Yuki, kept late at work, runs up for the last train home and finds her elderly neighbour Satou-san already waiting.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, satou-san! konban wa. juuichiji han no densha, mou dechaimashita ka?
lines.ja: あ、佐藤さん！こんばんは。十一時半の電車、もう出ちゃいましたか？
lines.kana: あ、さとうさん！こんばんは。じゅういちじはんのでんしゃ、もうでちゃいましたか？
lines.english: Oh, Satou-san! Good evening. Has the eleven-thirty train gone already?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: aa, yuki-san. mada dete imasen yo. densha ga okurete iru n desu.
lines.ja: ああ、ユキさん。まだ出ていませんよ。電車が遅れているんです。
lines.kana: ああ、ゆきさん。まだでていませんよ。でんしゃがおくれているんです。
lines.english: Ah, Yuki-san. No, it hasn't left yet. The train's running late.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hontou desu ka? aa, maniatta. densha ni okurechau to omotte, zutto hashitta n desu.
lines.ja: 本当ですか？ああ、間に合った。電車に遅れちゃうと思って、ずっと走ったんです。
lines.kana: ほんとうですか？ああ、まにあった。でんしゃにおくれちゃうとおもって、ずっとはしったんです。
lines.english: Really? Oh, I made it. I thought I was going to miss the train, so I ran the whole way.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: daijoubu desu ka? konna jikan made, oshigoto desu ka?
lines.ja: 大丈夫ですか？こんな時間まで、お仕事ですか？
lines.kana: だいじょうぶですか？こんなじかんまで、おしごとですか？
lines.english: Are you all right? Have you been at work this late?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai. shigoto ga owaranakute, shuuden ga nakunaru ka to omoimashita.
lines.ja: はい。仕事が終わらなくて、終電がなくなるかと思いました。
lines.kana: はい。しごとがおわらなくて、しゅうでんがなくなるかとおもいました。
lines.english: Yes. I couldn't get away from work, and I thought the last train would be gone.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. watashi wa hisashiburi ni, tomodachi to osake o nonde imashita.
lines.ja: そうですか。私は久しぶりに、友達とお酒を飲んでいました。
lines.kana: そうですか。わたしはひさしぶりに、ともだちとおさけをのんでいました。
lines.english: I see. I was out having drinks with a friend, first time in ages.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii desu ne! satou-san mo, kyou wa kaeri ga osoi n desu ne.
lines.ja: いいですね！佐藤さんも、今日は帰りが遅いんですね。
lines.kana: いいですね！さとうさんも、きょうはかえりがおそいんですね。
lines.english: How nice! So you're getting home late tonight too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: iya, shuuden ga nakunaru kara tte, juuichiji ni wa omise o deta n desu yo.
lines.ja: いや、終電がなくなるからって、十一時にはお店を出たんですよ。
lines.kana: いや、しゅうでんがなくなるからって、じゅういちじにはおみせをでたんですよ。
lines.english: Well, no. I told my friend I'd miss the last train, and I was out of the bar by eleven.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, juuichiji ni? jaa, zutto koko ni ita n desu ka?
lines.ja: え、十一時に？じゃあ、ずっとここにいたんですか？
lines.kana: え、じゅういちじに？じゃあ、ずっとここにいたんですか？
lines.english: What, at eleven? So you've been here this whole time?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai. densha ni okureru no ga iya de ne. demo, densha ga okurete, mada koko ni iru n desu.
lines.ja: はい。電車に遅れるのが嫌でね。でも、電車が遅れて、まだここにいるんです。
lines.kana: はい。でんしゃにおくれるのがいやでね。でも、でんしゃがおくれて、まだここにいるんです。
lines.english: Yes. I can't stand missing a train, you see. But the train's late, so here I still am.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: densha, nanji ni deru kana. chotto mite mimasu ne.
lines.ja: 電車、何時に出るかな。ちょっと見てみますね。
lines.kana: でんしゃ、なんじにでるかな。ちょっとみてみますね。
lines.english: I wonder what time it'll leave. Let me check.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: onegai shimasu. sumaho wa nigate na n desu yo.
lines.ja: お願いします。スマホは苦手なんですよ。
lines.kana: おねがいします。すまほはにがてなんですよ。
lines.english: Please do. I'm hopeless with smartphones.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, juuichiji gojuppun ni demasu tte. mou sugu desu yo.
lines.ja: あ、十一時五十分に出ますって。もうすぐですよ。
lines.kana: あ、じゅういちじごじゅっぷんにでますって。もうすぐですよ。
lines.english: Oh, it says it leaves at eleven fifty. Any minute now.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, yuki-san wa, densha ga okureta kara maniatta n desu ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、ユキさんは、電車が遅れたから間に合ったんですね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ゆきさんは、でんしゃがおくれたからまにあったんですね。
lines.english: So you only made it because the train was late, Yuki-san.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou na n desu. densha ga okuretenakattara, shuuden nakunattemashita.
lines.ja: そうなんです。電車が遅れてなかったら、終電なくなってました。
lines.kana: そうなんです。でんしゃがおくれてなかったら、しゅうでんなくなってました。
lines.english: That's right. If the train hadn't been late, I'd have missed the last train.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: watashi wa, mou sukoshi omise ni ireba yokatta desu ne.
lines.ja: 私は、もう少しお店にいればよかったですね。
lines.kana: わたしは、もうすこしおみせにいればよかったですね。
lines.english: As for me, I should have stayed at the bar a little longer.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, densha kimashita yo! satou-san, kaerimashou.
lines.ja: あ、電車来ましたよ！佐藤さん、帰りましょう。
lines.kana: あ、でんしゃきましたよ！さとうさん、かえりましょう。
lines.english: Oh, here comes the train! Let's go home, Satou-san.

questions.english: What happened on the platform?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: The last train had already left, so Yuki and Satou-san had to find another way home.
Yuki left work early and got there with time to spare, while Satou-san only just made the train.
Yuki thought she'd missed the last train, but it was running late, so she made it; Satou-san had left his drinks early and was still waiting.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-3: Yuki asks if the eleven-thirty has gone; it hasn't, because the train is running late (densha ga okurete iru n desu), so she made it (aa, maniatta). Line 5: work kept her and she thought the last train would be gone. Lines 8-10: Satou-san left the bar at eleven so he wouldn't lose the last train, and because of the delay he's still waiting. Lines 14-15 spell out the irony: she made it only because the train was late. A is wrong: the train hadn't left (line 2: mada dete imasen), and it pulls in at the end (line 17). B swaps the two: Yuki was kept at work and ran (lines 3 and 5); it was Satou-san who came early (lines 8-10).

questions.english: Yuki asks whether the eleven-thirty train has gone. What does Satou-san say about the train?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、電車について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、でんしゃについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, densha ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: The train is running late.
choices.romaji: densha ga okurete iru n desu.

choices.english: We're late for the train.
choices.romaji: densha ni okurete iru n desu.

choices.english: The train is late (the word for people late to school or work).
choices.romaji: densha ga chikoku shite iru n desu.

questions.explanation: Line 2: densha ga okurete iru n desu. With ga, the train is the one running behind, which is why it hasn't left. The same ga okureru comes back in line 10 (densha ga okurete) and line 15 (densha ga okuretenakattara). B swaps ga for ni: densha ni okureru is a person being late for the train, which is what Yuki was afraid of in line 3 (densha ni okurechau) and what Satou-san hates in line 10 (densha ni okureru no ga iya). C uses chikoku, which is people arriving late for school or work; a train doesn't chikoku suru.

questions.english: This morning you ran for the eight o'clock train and just made it. At work, Yuki says: "kesa, hashitteta ne! hachiji no densha, dou datta?" (You were running this morning! How did it go with the eight o'clock train?) Tell her you made it.
questions.ja: 今朝、走ってたね！八時の電車、どうだった？
questions.kana: けさ、はしってたね！はちじのでんしゃ、どうだった？
questions.romaji: kesa, hashitteta ne! hachiji no densha, dou datta?
questions.answer: Say you made it in time with maniau in the past: un, maniatta yo!

modelAnswers.romaji: un, maniatta yo!
modelAnswers.ja: うん、間に合ったよ！
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I made it!

modelAnswers.romaji: un, hashitte densha ni maniatta.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、走って電車に間に合った。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I ran and made the train.

questions.explanation: Getting there in time for a train is densha ni maniau, literally being in time for it. Yuki says it to herself in line 3 (aa, maniatta) and Satou-san says it in line 14 (densha ga okureta kara maniatta). Once everyone knows which train, the noun drops and maniatta alone is the usual answer. Not densha o tsukamaeta or densha o totta, which are English 'catch' and 'take' word for word. If you hadn't made it, you'd say maniawanakatta, not misu shita.

questions.english: You're on the platform with Satou-san. He asks: "densha wa nanji desu ka ne?" (What time is the train, I wonder?) Your phone says it leaves at ten fifteen. Tell him.
questions.ja: 電車は何時ですかね？
questions.kana: でんしゃはなんじですかね？
questions.romaji: densha wa nanji desu ka ne?
questions.answer: Give the time with deru, politely since it's Satou-san: juuji juugofun ni demasu yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: juuji juugofun ni demasu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 十時十五分に出ますよ。
modelAnswers.english: It leaves at ten fifteen.

modelAnswers.romaji: densha wa juuji juugofun ni demasu tte.
modelAnswers.ja: 電車は十時十五分に出ますって。
modelAnswers.english: It says the train leaves at ten fifteen.

questions.explanation: A train leaving is deru, the same verb as leaving the house. Yuki asks mou dechaimashita ka? in line 1 and reads the time off her phone in line 13 (juuichiji gojuppun ni demasu tte). Not densha ga hanareru or densha ga saru: those describe it pulling away from the platform, not the departure time. The -tte in the second answer passes on what the app says, just as Yuki does in line 13.

questions.english: Yuki arrives out of breath and says "densha ni okurechau to omotte, zutto hashitta n desu." What was she afraid of?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、なんで走ったんですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なんではしったんですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nande hashitta n desu ka?

choices.english: That the train would run late and she'd get home after midnight.
That she'd get there too late and the train would leave without her.
That the last train would be too crowded to get on.

questions.explanation: Line 3: densha ni okureru, with ni, is you being late for the train, and since a train doesn't wait, late means missed; -chau adds 'I'm going to end up...'. Satou-san uses the same ni okureru in line 10 for why he came so early. A swaps the particle: densha ga okureru is the train running late, which is what actually happened (line 2) and what saved her (lines 14-15). C: nobody mentions crowds; her worry was the time, and in line 5 she says she thought the last train would be gone.

questions.english: It's late, you're out for drinks with Yuki, and your last train leaves soon. She says: "e, mou kaeru no? mou sukoshi nomou yo!" (What, going already? Stay for a bit more!) Say no: your last train will be gone.
questions.ja: え、もう帰るの？もう少し飲もうよ！
questions.kana: え、もうかえるの？もうすこしのもうよ！
questions.romaji: e, mou kaeru no? mou sukoshi nomou yo!
questions.answer: Turn her down with shuuden (ga) nakunaru: gomen, shuuden nakunatchau kara, mou kaeru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, shuuden nakunatchau kara, mou kaeru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、終電なくなっちゃうから、もう帰るね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, the last train'll be gone, so I'm heading home.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, shuuden ga nakunaru kara, kyou wa kaeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、終電がなくなるから、今日は帰るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nah, the last train will be gone, so I'm going home tonight.

questions.explanation: Japanese makes the last train the subject: shuuden ga nakunaru, the last train 'is gone', so there's no way home. It's exactly what Satou-san told his friend in line 8 (shuuden ga nakunaru kara tte), and Yuki uses it in lines 5 and 15. Not shuuden o misu suru: misu is a mistake. -chau in nakunatchau adds 'it'll be gone before I know it'; casual speech drops the ga.

script.title: The wrong medicine
script.setting: Saturday afternoon at the flat Sora shares with Kenta. Kenta has told Mai that Sora is ill in bed, so she drops by to check on him.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora, daijoubu? kenta kara kiita yo. netsu ga aru n da tte?
lines.ja: ソラ、大丈夫？ケンタから聞いたよ。熱があるんだって？
lines.kana: そら、だいじょうぶ？けんたからきいたよ。ねつがあるんだって？
lines.english: Sora, are you OK? Kenta told me. You've got a fever?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. kinou kara. nodo mo itai shi, saiaku da yo.
lines.ja: うん。昨日から。喉も痛いし、最悪だよ。
lines.kana: うん。きのうから。のどもいたいし、さいあくだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, since yesterday. My throat hurts too. It's awful.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: byouin wa? itta?
lines.ja: 病院は？行った？
lines.kana: びょういんは？いった？
lines.english: What about the doctor? Have you been?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: byouin wa ittenai. demo, kusuri nonderu kara daijoubu.
lines.ja: 病院は行ってない。でも、薬飲んでるから大丈夫。
lines.kana: びょういんはいってない。でも、くすりのんでるからだいじょうぶ。
lines.english: No, I haven't. But I'm taking medicine, so I'm fine.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou na n da. de, kusuri wa kiita?
lines.ja: そうなんだ。で、薬は効いた？
lines.kana: そうなんだ。で、くすりはきいた？
lines.english: I see. So, has the medicine helped?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uun, zenzen kikanai n da yo. kono kusuri, kinou kara nonderu noni.
lines.ja: ううん、全然効かないんだよ。この薬、昨日から飲んでるのに。
lines.kana: ううん、ぜんぜんきかないんだよ。このくすり、きのうからのんでるのに。
lines.english: Nope, it's not doing a thing. And I've been taking it since yesterday.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: chotto misete. e, kore, onaka no kusuri da yo!
lines.ja: ちょっと見せて。え、これ、お腹の薬だよ！
lines.kana: ちょっとみせて。え、これ、おなかのくすりだよ！
lines.english: Let me see. Wait, this is stomach medicine!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uso! kenta ga kaze no kusuri da tte itteta noni.
lines.ja: うそ！ケンタが風邪の薬だって言ってたのに。
lines.kana: うそ！けんたがかぜのくすりだっていってたのに。
lines.english: No way! Kenta told me it was cold medicine!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: onaka no kusuri ja, kikanai yo. kaze no kusuri motte kita kara, kore nonde.
lines.ja: お腹の薬じゃ、効かないよ。風邪の薬持ってきたから、これ飲んで。
lines.kana: おなかのくすりじゃ、きかないよ。かぜのくすりもってきたから、これのんで。
lines.english: Stomach medicine won't do anything for that. I brought some cold medicine, so take this.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: arigatou. kono kusuri wa kiku no?
lines.ja: ありがとう。この薬は効くの？
lines.kana: ありがとう。このくすりはきくの？
lines.english: Thanks. And does this one actually work?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, yoku kiku yo. watashi, kaze hiitara itsumo kono kusuri da yo.
lines.ja: うん、よく効くよ。私、風邪ひいたらいつもこの薬だよ。
lines.kana: うん、よくきくよ。わたし、かぜひいたらいつもこのくすりだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, it works really well. Whenever I catch a cold, this is what I take.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, nomu ne. a, kusuri, mou kiite kita ki ga suru.
lines.ja: じゃあ、飲むね。あ、薬、もう効いてきた気がする。
lines.kana: じゃあ、のむね。あ、くすり、もうきいてきたきがする。
lines.english: Okay, down it goes. Oh, I think it's kicking in already.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kusuri, ima nonda bakkari desho. ashita mo netsu ga attara, byouin itte ne.
lines.ja: 薬、今飲んだばっかりでしょ。明日も熱があったら、病院行ってね。
lines.kana: くすり、いまのんだばっかりでしょ。あしたもねつがあったら、びょういんいってね。
lines.english: You only just took it. If you've still got a fever tomorrow, go and see a doctor, OK?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ee, byouin, hitori de iku no iya da naa.
lines.ja: えー、病院、一人で行くの嫌だなあ。
lines.kana: えー、びょういん、ひとりでいくのいやだなあ。
lines.english: Ugh, the doctor's? I hate going on my own.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, watashi mo iku yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、私も行くよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、わたしもいくよ。
lines.english: Then I'll come with you.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: honto? jaa, ashita mo netsu ga aru to ii naa.
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、明日も熱があるといいなあ。
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、あしたもねつがあるといいなあ。
lines.english: Really? Then I hope I've still got a fever tomorrow.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mou, nani itteru no. ii kara, nete.
lines.ja: もう、何言ってるの。いいから、寝て。
lines.kana: もう、なにいってるの。いいから、ねて。
lines.english: Oh, honestly. Just go to sleep.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora saw a doctor, but the medicine he was given there isn't working, so Mai brings him a different one.
Mai brings Sora the wrong medicine by mistake, so he decides to go to the doctor on his own tomorrow.
Sora has been taking stomach medicine for his cold, so Mai gives him cold medicine and offers to go to the doctor with him.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Sora hasn't been to the doctor (byouin wa ittenai), but he's taking medicine. Line 6: it isn't working at all (zenzen kikanai). Line 7: Mai looks and sees it's stomach medicine (onaka no kusuri), which Kenta had told him was cold medicine (line 8). Line 9: she gives him the cold medicine she brought. Line 13: if he still has a fever tomorrow he should see a doctor, and when he says he hates going on his own (line 14), she says she'll come too (line 15: watashi mo iku yo). A is wrong: Sora hasn't been to the doctor at all (line 4), and the medicine that didn't work came from Kenta. B is wrong: the wrong medicine was Kenta's, and Mai brought the right one. Sora doesn't want to go to the doctor on his own (line 14), so Mai offers to go with him.

questions.english: Kenta (whose stomach medicine Sora was taking) says to you, "kinou kara zutto onaka ga itai n da yo ne. dou shiyou." Tell him to see a doctor, using byouin ni iku.
questions.ja: 昨日からずっとお腹が痛いんだよね。どうしよう。
questions.kana: きのうからずっとおなかがいたいんだよね。どうしよう。
questions.romaji: kinou kara zutto onaka ga itai n da yo ne. dou shiyou.
questions.answer: Tell him to go to the byouin: byouin itta hou ga ii yo (you should see a doctor), or suggest it with byouin ni itte mitara? With a friend, ni usually drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: sore, byouin itta hou ga ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: それ、病院行った方がいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: You should get that looked at by a doctor.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, kyou byouin ni itte mitara?
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、今日病院に行ってみたら？
modelAnswers.english: Then why not go and see a doctor today?

questions.explanation: In the scene Mai asks byouin wa? itta? (line 3) and tells Sora byouin itte ne (line 13), and Sora answers byouin wa ittenai (line 4). Byouin is any doctor's clinic, not just a big hospital, so it's the normal word even for a stomachache or a cold. The verb is iku: English 'see a doctor' pulls toward isha o miru or isha ni au, which Japanese doesn't say for a visit. Advice takes -ta hou ga ii, and between friends ni usually drops (byouin itta hou ga ii yo). Kenta is a friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: You've had a headache all afternoon. Mai notices and says, "atama itai no? kusuri aru yo." Answer using kusuri o nomu: ask if you can take some, or say you've already taken some.
questions.ja: 頭痛いの？薬あるよ。
questions.kana: あたまいたいの？くすりあるよ。
questions.romaji: atama itai no? kusuri aru yo.
questions.answer: Pair kusuri with nomu: sono kusuri, nonde mo ii? (can I take some of that?) or mou kusuri nonda (I've already taken something). In casual speech o drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: honto? arigatou. jaa, sono kusuri, nonde mo ii?
modelAnswers.ja: ほんと？ありがとう。じゃあ、その薬、飲んでもいい？
modelAnswers.english: Really? Thanks. Can I take some, then?

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. demo daijoubu, mou kusuri nonda kara.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。でも大丈夫、もう薬飲んだから。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks, but I'm OK. I've already taken something.

questions.explanation: Medicine takes nomu, the verb for drinking, even when it's a pill: Sora says kusuri nonderu (line 4) and kono kusuri, kinou kara nonderu noni (line 6), and Mai tells him kore nonde (line 9). English 'take' pulls toward toru, but kusuri o toru means picking the medicine up or fetching it, not swallowing it. In casual speech o drops (kusuri nonda). Mai is a friend, so a casual answer fits.

questions.english: Sora tells Mai he's been taking medicine. She asks, "de, kusuri wa kiita?" What is she asking?
questions.ja: マイさんは、何を聞きましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、なにをききましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, nani o kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Whether he asked anyone what the medicine was for.
Whether the medicine has made him feel any better.
Whether he'd heard of that medicine before.

questions.explanation: Line 5: de, kusuri wa kiita? With medicine as the subject, kiku means 'take effect', so Mai is asking whether it has worked. Sora's answer settles it: zenzen kikanai n da yo (line 6), it isn't doing anything. Mai later says stomach medicine won't work (line 9: onaka no kusuri ja, kikanai yo), and Sora asks of the new one, kono kusuri wa kiku no? (line 10). A and C hear the other kiku, 'ask' or 'hear', which sounds exactly the same: Mai uses that one in line 1 (kenta kara kiita yo, Kenta told me), and this question itself uses it (nani o kikimashita ka, what did she ask?). For 'the medicine works', don't reach for hataraku (work at a job): it's kusuri ga kiku, and as it kicks in, kiite kita (line 12).

newWords.english: (not) at all, with a negative (zenzen kikanai: isn't working at all)
have only just done (nonda bakkari: only just took it)
(with a sigh) oh, honestly; come on

script.title: Not close, apparently
script.setting: A weeknight at home. Okaasan hasn't heard from Yuki for a week and is starting to worry; Kenji is slumped on the sofa with his phone.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji, yuki kara renraku kita?
lines.ja: ケンジ、ユキから連絡来た？
lines.kana: けんじ、ゆきかられんらくきた？
lines.english: Kenji, have you heard from Yuki?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un, kesa kita kedo.
lines.ja: うん、今朝来たけど。
lines.kana: うん、けさきたけど。
lines.english: Yeah, this morning. Why?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e, kenji ni wa renraku kuru no? okaasan ni wa senshuu kara konai no yo.
lines.ja: え、ケンジには連絡来るの？お母さんには先週から来ないのよ。
lines.kana: え、けんじにはれんらくくるの？おかあさんにはせんしゅうからこないのよ。
lines.english: Wait, she gets in touch with you? I haven't heard a thing from her since last week.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shigoto isogashii n ja nai?
lines.ja: 仕事忙しいんじゃない？
lines.kana: しごといそがしいんじゃない？
lines.english: Maybe she's just busy with work?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo, denwa shite mo denai shi, renraku torenai no yo.
lines.ja: でも、電話しても出ないし、連絡取れないのよ。
lines.kana: でも、でんわしてもでないし、れんらくとれないのよ。
lines.english: But she doesn't pick up when I call. I just can't get hold of her.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ore ni wa mainichi renraku kuru kedo.
lines.ja: 俺には毎日連絡来るけど。
lines.kana: おれにはまいにちれんらくくるけど。
lines.english: Well, I hear from her every day.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mainichi renraku totteru no? itsu kara sonna ni naka ii no?
lines.ja: 毎日連絡取ってるの？いつからそんなに仲いいの？
lines.kana: まいにちれんらくとってるの？いつからそんなになかいいの？
lines.english: You two are in touch every day? Since when are you so close?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: betsu ni naka yokunai yo. geemu no hanashi bakkari da shi.
lines.ja: 別に仲良くないよ。ゲームの話ばっかりだし。
lines.kana: べつになかよくないよ。げーむのはなしばっかりだし。
lines.english: We're not close or anything. It's all just game stuff.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou? mukashi wa sugoku naka warukatta noni ne.
lines.ja: そう？昔はすごく仲悪かったのにね。
lines.kana: そう？むかしはすごくなかわるかったのにね。
lines.english: Oh, really? You two used to get on so badly, too.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jaa, okaasan ga neechan to naka waruku natta n ja nai?
lines.ja: じゃあ、お母さんが姉ちゃんと仲悪くなったんじゃない？
lines.kana: じゃあ、おかあさんがねえちゃんとなかわるくなったんじゃない？
lines.english: So maybe it's you she's fallen out with.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: naka warukunai wa yo! senshuu mo futari de kaimono ni itta no yo.
lines.ja: 仲悪くないわよ！先週も二人で買い物に行ったのよ。
lines.kana: なかわるくないわよ！せんしゅうもふたりでかいものにいったのよ。
lines.english: We are not on bad terms! We went shopping together just last week.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: okaasan, sumaho.
lines.ja: お母さん、スマホ。
lines.kana: おかあさん、すまほ。
lines.english: Mom, your phone.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: a! yuki kara renraku kita!
lines.ja: あ！ユキから連絡来た！
lines.kana: あ！ゆきかられんらくきた！
lines.english: Oh! It's a message from Yuki!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nante?
lines.ja: なんて？
lines.kana: なんて？
lines.english: What's she say?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shigoto isogashikute gomen tte. shuumatsu kaeru tte!
lines.ja: 仕事忙しくてごめんって。週末帰るって！
lines.kana: しごといそがしくてごめんって。しゅうまつかえるって！
lines.english: She says sorry, work's been busy. And she's coming home this weekend!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: yokatta ne, renraku torete.
lines.ja: よかったね、連絡取れて。
lines.kana: よかったね、れんらくとれて。
lines.english: Good, so you got hold of her.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ato, kenji to geemu shitai tte. yappari naka ii n ja nai.
lines.ja: あと、ケンジとゲームしたいって。やっぱり仲いいんじゃない。
lines.kana: あと、けんじとげーむしたいって。やっぱりなかいいんじゃない。
lines.english: And she wants to play games with you. See, you two do get along.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: dakara, naka yokunai tte.
lines.ja: だから、仲良くないって。
lines.kana: だから、なかよくないって。
lines.english: Like I said, we're not close.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji and Yuki have fallen out, so Okaasan tells Kenji to call his sister and make up before the weekend.
Okaasan can't get hold of Yuki, so Kenji phones her; Yuki picks up and says she'll go shopping with Okaasan at the weekend.
Okaasan hasn't heard from Yuki since last week, though Kenji hears from her every day. Then Yuki messages: work's been busy, and she's coming home this weekend.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-6: Okaasan has heard nothing since last week and can't reach Yuki (line 3: okaasan ni wa senshuu kara konai no yo; line 5: renraku torenai no yo), but Kenji hears from her every day (line 6: ore ni wa mainichi renraku kuru kedo). Lines 13-15: a message arrives (a! yuki kara renraku kita!): sorry, work's been busy, and she's coming home at the weekend (shuumatsu kaeru tte). A is wrong: Kenji and Yuki only got on badly in the old days (line 9: mukashi wa), they're in touch every day now, and nobody is told to call anyone. B is wrong: nobody phones Yuki in the scene; she messages Okaasan herself, and the shopping trip was last week (line 11: senshuu mo futari de kaimono ni itta no yo).

questions.english: Sora asks you, "ne, kenta to yuki-san tte, mukashi kara no tomodachi na n da tte?" (Hey, I hear Kenta and Yuki have been friends for ages?) They have, and they still get on really well. Tell him they're close.
questions.ja: ね、ケンタとユキさんって、昔からの友達なんだって？
questions.kana: ね、けんたとゆきさんって、むかしからのともだちなんだって？
questions.romaji: ne, kenta to yuki-san tte, mukashi kara no tomodachi na n da tte?
questions.answer: Say their relationship is good with naka ga ii (ga can drop in speech): un, ano futari, sugoku naka ii yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, ano futari, sugoku naka ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、あの二人、すごく仲いいよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, those two are really close.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, ano futari wa sugoku naka ga ii n desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、あの二人はすごく仲がいいんですよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, those two get on really well.

questions.explanation: English 'get along' sends you looking for a verb, but Japanese says the relationship (naka) is good: naka ga ii. Okaasan asks it in line 7 (itsu kara sonna ni naka ii no?) and says it again in line 17 (yappari naka ii n ja nai). Kenji's denial in lines 8 and 18 is the negative, naka yokunai: ii turns into yo- when it changes form. nakayoku suru is the action, being nice to each other (nakayoku shite ne), so it doesn't describe how two people get on. And 'close' here is not chikai, which is near in distance. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Kenji teases his mother: "jaa, okaasan ga yuki to naka waruku natta n ja nai?" What is he suggesting?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: That Okaasan has been feeling unwell, so Yuki is leaving her to rest.
That Okaasan and Yuki have fallen out, and that's why Yuki isn't getting in touch.
That Okaasan has been in a bad mood lately, so Yuki doesn't feel like calling her.

questions.explanation: Line 10: naka ga warui is about how two people get on (neechan to = with his big sister, Yuki), and waruku natta means it has become bad: they've fallen out. Kenji is joking that this, not work, is why Yuki has gone quiet, and Okaasan protests in line 11 (naka warukunai wa yo!) that the two of them went shopping just last week. A would be guai ga warui (feeling unwell) and C kigen ga warui (in a bad mood): both describe one person, and neither has naka. Okaasan used the same phrase about the past in line 9: mukashi wa sugoku naka warukatta, Kenji and Yuki used to get on badly.

questions.english: Okaasan asks you, "yuki wa shuumatsu nanji ni kaeru no? kiite kureta?" (What time is Yuki getting home this weekend? Did you ask her?) You've called her several times, but she isn't picking up. Tell your mother you can't get hold of her.
questions.ja: ユキは週末何時に帰るの？聞いてくれた？
questions.kana: ゆきはしゅうまつなんじにかえるの？きいてくれた？
questions.romaji: yuki wa shuumatsu nanji ni kaeru no? kiite kureta?
questions.answer: Say you can't reach her with the can-form of toru: renraku torenai n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: nando mo denwa shita kedo, renraku torenai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 何度も電話したけど、連絡取れないんだ。
modelAnswers.english: I've called her loads of times, but I can't get hold of her.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, mada renraku torenai yo. denwa shite mo denai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、まだ連絡取れないよ。電話しても出ないんだ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I still can't reach her. She doesn't pick up.

questions.explanation: Getting through to someone, or staying in touch with them over time, is renraku o toru. Here it's the can-form torenai, 'I can't get hold of her', just as Okaasan says in line 5 (denwa shite mo denai shi, renraku torenai no yo). Okaasan uses the ongoing form in line 7 (mainichi renraku totteru no? = you're in touch every day?), and Kenji the positive in line 16 when the message finally comes (yokatta ne, renraku torete). English 'contact her' or 'keep in touch' points to renraku suru, but that is sending one message or making one call (mata renraku suru ne): renraku shita only says you sent something, not that you couldn't reach her.

questions.english: Right at the start, Okaasan asks Kenji about his sister. What did she ask?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji, have you heard from Yuki?
Kenji, did Yuki tell you (about it)?
Kenji, did you get in touch with Yuki?

questions.explanation: Line 1: renraku ga kuru (ga dropped, past kita) is a message or call coming to you, with the sender marked by kara: yuki kara renraku kita? = have you heard from Yuki? Kenji answers with the same verb in line 2 (un, kesa kita kedo), and Okaasan uses it again in line 3 (okaasan ni wa senshuu kara konai no yo) and line 13 when the message arrives (a! yuki kara renraku kita!). B is English 'hear from' put into Japanese: yuki kara kiita means being told something by Yuki, a piece of news, not getting a message from her. C turns it round: renraku shita? asks whether Kenji contacted Yuki, but Okaasan wants to know whether Yuki has been in touch, which is why Kenji's answer is kita, not shita.

newWords.english: phone call; denwa suru = call (denwa shite mo denai = she doesn't pick up when I call)
I, me (casual, mostly men and boys)
not particularly (betsu ni naka yokunai = we're not close or anything)
the old days, back then (mukashi wa = used to)
two people, the two of them (futari de = the two of us together)
just as I thought; after all

script.title: Curry for shogi
script.setting: A weekday evening. Kenta doesn't pick up, so Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, leaves him a voicemail. The day before, Kenta had brought him some homemade curry.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, kenta-kun? satou desu.
lines.ja: もしもし、ケンタくん？佐藤です。
lines.kana: もしもし、けんたくん？さとうです。
lines.english: Hello, Kenta? It's Satou.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kinou wa, oishii karee o arigatou gozaimashita. onaka ippai ni narimashita.
lines.ja: 昨日は、おいしいカレーをありがとうございました。お腹いっぱいになりました。
lines.kana: きのうは、おいしいかれーをありがとうございました。おなかいっぱいになりました。
lines.english: Thank you for the delicious curry yesterday. I ate until I was full.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hontou ni ki ni itte, kesa mo tabemashita yo.
lines.ja: 本当に気に入って、今朝も食べましたよ。
lines.kana: ほんとうにきにいって、けさもたべましたよ。
lines.english: I loved it so much, I had some again this morning.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hitotsu ki ni natta n desu ga, ano karee, nani ga haitte ita n desu ka?
lines.ja: 一つ気になったんですが、あのカレー、何が入っていたんですか？
lines.kana: ひとつきになったんですが、あのかれー、なにがはいっていたんですか？
lines.english: One thing made me curious, though. What was in that curry?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: totemo ki ni itta node, jibun de mo tsukutte mitai n desu.
lines.ja: とても気に入ったので、自分でも作ってみたいんです。
lines.kana: とてもきにいったので、じぶんでもつくってみたいんです。
lines.english: I liked it so much that I'd like to try making it myself.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: zutto, ryouri ni kyoumi ga atta n desu. demo, gohan o tsukuru no wa, jishin ga nakute ne.
lines.ja: ずっと、料理に興味があったんです。でも、ご飯を作るのは、自信がなくてね。
lines.kana: ずっと、りょうりにきょうみがあったんです。でも、ごはんをつくるのは、じしんがなくてね。
lines.english: I've always been interested in cooking. But I've never felt confident making meals, you see.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-kun, karee no tsukurikata, oshiete moraemasen ka?
lines.ja: ケンタくん、カレーの作り方、教えてもらえませんか？
lines.kana: けんたくん、かれーのつくりかた、おしえてもらえませんか？
lines.english: Kenta, could you teach me how to make that curry?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou ieba, kenta-kun, shougi ni kyoumi ga aru tte itte imashita yo ne.
lines.ja: そういえば、ケンタくん、将棋に興味があるって言っていましたよね。
lines.kana: そういえば、けんたくん、しょうぎにきょうみがあるっていっていましたよね。
lines.english: Oh, and come to think of it, you said you were interested in shogi, didn't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: shougi nara, jishin ga arimasu kara, watashi ga oshiemasu yo.
lines.ja: 将棋なら、自信がありますから、私が教えますよ。
lines.kana: しょうぎなら、じしんがありますから、わたしがおしえますよ。
lines.english: Shogi, on the other hand, I'm confident at, so I'll teach you.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: doyoubi wa dou desu ka? konna ni shuumatsu o tanoshimi ni suru no wa, hisashiburi desu.
lines.ja: 土曜日はどうですか？こんなに週末を楽しみにするのは、久しぶりです。
lines.kana: どようびはどうですか？こんなにしゅうまつをたのしみにするのは、ひさしぶりです。
lines.english: How's Saturday for you? It's been a long time since I looked forward to a weekend this much.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-kun mo, shougi, ki ni itte kureru to ii n desu ga.
lines.ja: ケンタくんも、将棋、気に入ってくれるといいんですが。
lines.kana: けんたくんも、しょうぎ、きにいってくれるといいんですが。
lines.english: I hope you'll take to shogi, too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, doyoubi, tanoshimi ni shite imasu. shitsurei shimasu.
lines.ja: じゃあ、土曜日、楽しみにしています。失礼します。
lines.kana: じゃあ、どようび、たのしみにしています。しつれいします。
lines.english: Well then, I'm looking forward to Saturday. Goodbye for now.

questions.english: What does Satou-san want to do?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、何がしたいんですか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、なにがしたいんですか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, nani ga shitai n desu ka?

choices.english: Find out what was in Kenta's curry, because something in it didn't agree with him.
Swap lessons: Kenta teaches him shogi, and he teaches Kenta to make curry.
Learn to make Kenta's curry, and teach Kenta shogi in return, on Saturday.

questions.explanation: Lines 3 and 5: Satou-san loved Kenta's curry (ki ni itte, ki ni itta) and wants to try making it himself. Line 7: he asks Kenta to teach him how (karee no tsukurikata, oshiete moraemasen ka?). Lines 8-9: Kenta once said he was interested in shogi, and Satou-san is confident at shogi, so he'll do the teaching there (watashi ga oshiemasu yo). Line 10: he suggests Saturday, and line 12 closes with doyoubi, tanoshimi ni shite imasu. A is wrong: in line 4 'hitotsu ki ni natta' means one thing made him curious. He asks what was in the curry because he wants to make it (line 5), not because something bothered him. B swaps the roles: Satou-san is the one who isn't confident about cooking (line 6) and who is confident at shogi (line 9).

questions.english: Satou-san says, "hontou ni ki ni itte, kesa mo tabemashita yo." How did he feel about the curry?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、カレーをどう思いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、かれーをどうおもいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, karee o dou omoimashita ka?

choices.english: He really loved it.
Something about it bothered him.
He felt sure he could make it himself.

questions.explanation: Line 3: ki ni iru is taking a liking to something, and once it has happened Japanese uses the past or -te form, even where English says 'I love it': ki ni itte here, ki ni itta in line 5. He loved it so much he ate it again this morning (kesa mo tabemashita) and wants to make it himself (line 5). B is ki ni naru, which sounds close: in line 4 he does say 'hitotsu ki ni natta n desu ga', but that's 'one thing made me curious' about what was in it, and it's natta, not itta. C is the opposite of line 6, where he says he has no confidence making meals (jishin ga nakute).

questions.english: Satou-san says how he has always felt about cooking. What did he say?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、料理について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、りょうりについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, ryouri ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I've always been confident about cooking
choices.romaji: zutto, ryouri ni jishin ga atta

choices.english: I've always been interested in cooking
choices.romaji: zutto, ryouri ni kyoumi ga atta

choices.english: I've always been 'interest' in cooking (a calque of 'interested')

questions.explanation: Line 6: 'zutto, ryouri ni kyoumi ga atta n desu'. In Japanese the interest exists (kyoumi ga aru, here past atta), and the topic takes ni: ryouri ni. He uses it again in line 8 about Kenta (shougi ni kyoumi ga aru). A swaps in the chunk's contrast partner, jishin: he says the opposite about cooking in the same line (jishin ga nakute, no confidence). C is the English adjective turned into kyoumi + desu, which Japanese doesn't say; you don't 'be' interest, you have it (kyoumi ga aru).

questions.english: Kenta asks you, "doyoubi, uchi de karee tsukuru kedo, kuru?" (I'm making curry at my place on Saturday. Want to come?) Say yes, and that you're looking forward to it.
questions.ja: 土曜日、うちでカレー作るけど、来る？
questions.kana: どようび、うちでかれーつくるけど、くる？
questions.romaji: doyoubi, uchi de karee tsukuru kedo, kuru?
questions.answer: Say you'll come and that you're looking forward to it with tanoshimi ni shiteru, the -te ru form for how you feel now. What you're looking forward to can go first, with o dropped (kenta no karee, tanoshimi ni shiteru).

modelAnswers.romaji: iku iku! tanoshimi ni shiteru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 行く行く！楽しみにしてるね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm in! Looking forward to it.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, iku! kenta no karee, tanoshimi ni shiteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、行く！ケンタのカレー、楽しみにしてるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll come! I'm looking forward to your curry.

questions.explanation: Satou-san closes with 'doyoubi, tanoshimi ni shite imasu' (line 12), and in line 10 says 'konna ni shuumatsu o tanoshimi ni suru no wa, hisashiburi desu'. English 'look forward to' has no matching verb: Japanese makes the event a pleasure ahead, tanoshimi ni suru, in the -te ru form for how you feel now (shiteru; polite shite imasu). Don't say matenai for 'I can't wait': it sounds like you've run out of patience. Kenta asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Imagine you're Kenta. On Saturday, Satou-san sets out the shogi board and asks, "kenta-kun, shougi wa tsuyoi desu ka?" (Are you any good at shogi?) You've hardly ever played. Tell him you're not confident.
questions.ja: ケンタくん、将棋は強いですか？
questions.kana: けんたくん、しょうぎはつよいですか？
questions.romaji: kenta-kun, shougi wa tsuyoi desu ka?
questions.answer: Say you're not confident with jishin and nai: jishin nai desu (ga dropped) or jishin ga arimasen. Stay polite: he's your older neighbour.

modelAnswers.romaji: iya, jishin nai desu. oshiete kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: いや、自信ないです。教えてください。
modelAnswers.english: Oh no, I'm not confident. Please teach me.

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, mada jishin ga arimasen. yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、まだ自信がありません。よろしくお願いします。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm not confident yet. I'm in your hands.

questions.explanation: Satou-san says 'jishin ga nakute' about cooking (line 6) and 'jishin ga arimasu' about shogi (line 9). English 'confident' is an adjective, but in Japanese confidence is something you have or don't: jishin (ga) aru / nai, with ga often dropped (jishin nai desu). Don't say jishin desu, which sounds like 'It's an earthquake!' (jishin also means earthquake), and a bare wakarimasen just means 'I don't know'. He's an older neighbour, so keep it polite.

newWords.english: how to make something (tsukuru + -kata, way of)

script.title: Not ready yet
script.setting: Saturday evening at Kenta and Sora's flat. Yuki has come to pick Kenta up for dinner at Mai's. He promised to bring homemade gyoza, and they aren't done yet.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenta, junbi dekita? sorosoro deru yo.
lines.ja: ケンタ、準備できた？そろそろ出るよ。
lines.kana: けんた、じゅんびできた？そろそろでるよ。
lines.english: Kenta, are you ready? We need to head out soon.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gomen, mou chotto. gyouza ga mada na n da.
lines.ja: ごめん、もうちょっと。餃子がまだなんだ。
lines.kana: ごめん、もうちょっと。ぎょうざがまだなんだ。
lines.english: Sorry, nearly there. The gyoza aren't done yet.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, mada tsukutteru no? gyouza tte, jikan kakaru yo ne?
lines.ja: え、まだ作ってるの？餃子って、時間かかるよね？
lines.kana: え、まだつくってるの？ぎょうざって、じかんかかるよね？
lines.english: What, you're still making them? Gyoza take ages, don't they?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jikan mo da kedo, tsutsumu no ga tema kakaru n da yo.
lines.ja: 時間もだけど、包むのが手間かかるんだよ。
lines.kana: じかんもだけど、つつむのがてまかかるんだよ。
lines.english: Time, sure, but it's the wrapping that's such a fiddly job.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ato dore gurai kakaru?
lines.ja: あとどれぐらいかかる？
lines.kana: あとどれぐらいかかる？
lines.english: How much longer will it take?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nijuppun gurai kana.
lines.ja: 二十分ぐらいかな。
lines.kana: にじゅっぷんぐらいかな。
lines.english: About twenty minutes, I guess.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nijuppun mo? mai no uchi made ichijikan kakaru n da yo. densha ni maniawanai yo.
lines.ja: 二十分も？マイの家まで一時間かかるんだよ。電車に間に合わないよ。
lines.kana: にじゅっぷんも？まいのうちまでいちじかんかかるんだよ。でんしゃにまにあわないよ。
lines.english: Twenty whole minutes? It takes an hour to get to Mai's. We'll miss our train.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jaa, tetsudatte! futari nara hayai yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、手伝って！二人なら早いよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、てつだって！ふたりならはやいよ。
lines.english: Then give me a hand! It'll go quicker with two of us.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou! tema kakaru no, nigate na n da kedo.
lines.ja: もう！手間かかるの、苦手なんだけど。
lines.kana: もう！てまかかるの、にがてなんだけど。
lines.english: Ugh! I'm hopeless at fiddly stuff.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: daijoubu. mite, kou yatte, kou.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。見て、こうやって、こう。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。みて、こうやって、こう。
lines.english: You'll be fine. Watch: like this, then this.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, dekinai! kore, honto ni tema kakaru ne.
lines.ja: え、できない！これ、ほんとに手間かかるね。
lines.kana: え、できない！これ、ほんとにてまかかるね。
lines.english: What? I can't do it! These really are a lot of work.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku mo kyonen no imagoro wa, ikko ni gofun mo kakatteta yo.
lines.ja: 僕も去年の今ごろは、一個に五分もかかってたよ。
lines.kana: ぼくもきょねんのいまごろは、いっこにごふんもかかってたよ。
lines.english: This time last year, I was taking five whole minutes per gyoza too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyonen no imagoro? e, mou ichinen tatta n da.
lines.ja: 去年の今ごろ？え、もう一年経ったんだ。
lines.kana: きょねんのいまごろ？え、もういちねんたったんだ。
lines.english: This time last year? Wow, so it's been a year already.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un. ichinen kakatte, yatto jouzu ni natta n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。一年かかって、やっと上手になったんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。いちねんかかって、やっとじょうずになったんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah. It took me a year to finally get good at it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sokka. jikan tatsu no hayai ne.
lines.ja: そっか。時間経つの早いね。
lines.kana: そっか。じかんたつのはやいね。
lines.english: Huh. Time flies, doesn't it.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yatto junbi dekita! a, mou sanjuppun tatteru. gomen!
lines.ja: やっと準備できた！あ、もう三十分経ってる。ごめん！
lines.kana: やっとじゅんびできた！あ、もうさんじゅっぷんたってる。ごめん！
lines.english: Ready at last! Oh, it's been thirty minutes already. Sorry!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: daijoubu. ima mai kara renraku kita yo. mai mo mada junbi dekitenai tte.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。今マイから連絡来たよ。マイもまだ準備できてないって。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。いままいかられんらくきたよ。まいもまだじゅんびできてないって。
lines.english: It's fine. Mai just messaged. She says she isn't ready yet either.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nan da. jaa, mou chotto tsukureru ne.
lines.ja: なんだ。じゃあ、もうちょっと作れるね。
lines.kana: なんだ。じゃあ、もうちょっとつくれるね。
lines.english: Oh, is that all? Then I can make a few more.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenta was ready on time, but they missed their train because Yuki took so long wrapping gyoza.
The gyoza took so long that Kenta called off the dinner, and Yuki went to Mai's on her own.
Kenta wasn't ready because the gyoza weren't done. Yuki helped, it ran half an hour over, and then Mai messaged that she wasn't ready either.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenta isn't ready because the gyoza aren't done (gyouza ga mada na n da). Line 7: Yuki worries they'll miss the train. Lines 8-11: Kenta gets her to help wrap them. Line 16: he's finally ready, but thirty minutes have gone by (mou sanjuppun tatteru). Line 17: Mai has messaged that she isn't ready yet either (mai mo mada junbi dekitenai tte), so there's no rush, and in line 18 Kenta decides he can make a few more. A is wrong: Kenta wasn't ready (line 2), and nobody says they missed the train. B is wrong: nobody calls anything off; Yuki stays and helps, and Mai's message just means there's time to spare.

questions.english: When Yuki arrives at Kenta's flat, what does she ask him?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、ケンタさんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、けんたさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, kenta-san ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenta, can you get ready?
Kenta, are you ready?
Kenta, are you going to get ready?

questions.explanation: Line 1: kenta, junbi dekita? Japanese asks whether getting ready is done, so the question is in the past: dekita? = are you ready (yet)? Kenta answers in the same frame in line 16 (yatto junbi dekita!), and Mai's message in line 17 is mai mo mada junbi dekitenai (she isn't ready yet either). A copies English 'are you ready?' into the present: junbi dekiru? asks whether he is able to get ready. C, junbi suru?, asks whether he's going to start getting ready: junbi suru is doing the preparing, junbi ga dekiru is being done with it.

questions.english: Kenta asks you how long it takes to get from your place to his: "uchi kara koko made, dore gurai?" It's about thirty minutes by train. Tell him.
questions.ja: 家からここまで、どれぐらい？
questions.kana: うちからここまで、どれぐらい？
questions.romaji: uchi kara koko made, dore gurai?
questions.answer: Give the time with kakaru: densha de sanjuppun gurai kakaru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: densha de sanjuppun gurai kakaru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 電車で三十分ぐらいかかるよ。
modelAnswers.english: About thirty minutes by train.

modelAnswers.romaji: kekkou jikan kakaru yo. densha de sanjuppun gurai.
modelAnswers.ja: けっこう時間かかるよ。電車で三十分ぐらい。
modelAnswers.english: It takes a while. About thirty minutes by train.

questions.explanation: How long something takes is kakaru, with the amount where jikan would go: Yuki's mai no uchi made ichijikan kakaru (line 7) and ato dore gurai kakaru? (line 5), Kenta's ikko ni gofun mo kakatteta (line 12). On its own, jikan kakaru means 'it takes a while' (line 3), as in the second model answer. Don't reach for toru, English 'take': jikan o toru means making time for someone. And not tatsu: sanjuppun tatta would mean thirty minutes have gone by (line 16).

questions.english: When the gyoza are finally done, Kenta says "a, mou sanjuppun tatteru. gomen!" What does he mean?
questions.ja: 「もう三十分経ってる」は、どういう意味ですか？
questions.kana: 「もうさんじゅっぷんたってる」は、どういういみですか？
questions.romaji: mou sanjuppun tatteru wa, dou iu imi desu ka?

choices.english: Thirty minutes have already gone by while they were making the gyoza.
The gyoza will take another thirty minutes.
It takes thirty minutes to get to Mai's place.

questions.explanation: Line 16: tatsu is time going by, so mou sanjuppun tatteru = it's already been thirty minutes (in line 6 he guessed about twenty). B would be ato sanjuppun kakaru: kakaru is how long a job still takes, as in Yuki's ato dore gurai kakaru? (line 5), and the gyoza are already done. C mixes in the trip: Yuki said it takes an hour to get to Mai's, with kakaru (line 7: ichijikan kakaru). The same pair comes up in lines 13-14: mou ichinen tatta (a year has gone by) against ichinen kakatte (it took a year).

questions.english: Yuki, still fighting with a gyoza, asks you: "ne, gyouza tsukutta koto aru? dou datta?" You have made them, and it was a lot of fiddly work. Tell her.
questions.ja: ね、餃子作ったことある？どうだった？
questions.kana: ね、ぎょうざつくったことある？どうだった？
questions.romaji: ne, gyouza tsukutta koto aru? dou datta?
questions.answer: Say you have, and that it was fiddly work, with tema and kakaru: aru yo. demo, kekkou tema kakatta.

modelAnswers.romaji: aru yo. demo, kekkou tema kakatta.
modelAnswers.ja: あるよ。でも、けっこう手間かかった。
modelAnswers.english: I have. It was quite a lot of work, though.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, aru. tsutsumu no ga metcha tema kakaru yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、ある。包むのがめっちゃ手間かかるよね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I have. Wrapping them is such a hassle, right?

questions.explanation: A fiddly, slow chore like wrapping gyoza is tema ga kakaru, with the same kakaru as jikan ga kakaru: Kenta in line 4 (tsutsumu no ga tema kakaru n da yo), Yuki in lines 9 and 11. English 'it takes a lot of effort' points to doryoku, but doryoku is effort as in trying hard (doryoku shita = I worked hard at it), not a chore being a hassle. jikan kakatta would only say it took a long time; tema is the fiddliness, which Kenta sets apart from time in line 4 (jikan mo da kedo...).

script.title: Just a bit under the kotatsu
script.setting: A winter morning in Kenta and Sora's flat. Sora's alarm has been going off in his room, and Kenta finds him asleep under the kotatsu.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora, okite! sora no heya de, mezamashi zutto natteru yo!
lines.ja: ソラ、起きて！ソラの部屋で、目覚ましずっと鳴ってるよ！
lines.kana: そら、おきて！そらのへやで、めざましずっとなってるよ！
lines.english: Sora, wake up! Your alarm's been going off in your room forever!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: n? a, kenta. ohayou.
lines.ja: ん？あ、ケンタ。おはよう。
lines.kana: ん？あ、けんた。おはよう。
lines.english: Hm? Oh, Kenta. Morning.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nande kotatsu de neteru no? futon ni hairanakatta no?
lines.ja: なんでこたつで寝てるの？布団に入らなかったの？
lines.kana: なんでこたつでねてるの？ふとんにはいらなかったの？
lines.english: Why are you sleeping in the kotatsu? Didn't you go to bed?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. ofuro haitte, futon ni hairu mae ni, chotto dake kotatsu ni haitta n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。お風呂入って、布団に入る前に、ちょっとだけこたつに入ったんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。おふろはいって、ふとんにはいるまえに、ちょっとだけこたつにはいったんだよ。
lines.english: Nope. After my bath, I got under the kotatsu for just a bit before going to bed.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: de, nechatta n da.
lines.ja: で、寝ちゃったんだ。
lines.kana: で、ねちゃったんだ。
lines.english: And then you fell asleep.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sou. yoji ni ikkai, me ga sameta n da kedo, kimochi yokute okirenakatta.
lines.ja: そう。四時に一回、目が覚めたんだけど、気持ちよくて起きれなかった。
lines.kana: そう。よじにいっかい、めがさめたんだけど、きもちよくておきれなかった。
lines.english: Yep. I woke up once at four, but it felt so nice I couldn't get up.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kaze hiku yo, sore.
lines.ja: 風邪ひくよ、それ。
lines.kana: かぜひくよ、それ。
lines.english: You'll catch a cold doing that.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kaze wa hiitenai kedo, iya na yume mita. shigoto ni okureru yume.
lines.ja: 風邪はひいてないけど、嫌な夢見た。仕事に遅れる夢。
lines.kana: かぜはひいてないけど、いやなゆめみた。しごとにおくれるゆめ。
lines.english: I haven't caught a cold, but I had a horrible dream. I was late for work.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: aa, kotatsu de neru to, iya na yume miru tte iu yo ne.
lines.ja: ああ、こたつで寝ると、嫌な夢見るって言うよね。
lines.kana: ああ、こたつでねると、いやなゆめみるっていうよね。
lines.english: Oh yeah, they say you get bad dreams if you sleep in the kotatsu.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a! shigoto, hachiji kara da! ima nanji?
lines.ja: あ！仕事、八時からだ！今何時？
lines.kana: あ！しごと、はちじからだ！いまなんじ？
lines.english: Oh! Work starts at eight! What time is it?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: shichiji han da yo.
lines.ja: 七時半だよ。
lines.kana: しちじはんだよ。
lines.english: Half past seven.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: yabai! mezamashi, shichiji ni kaketa noni!
lines.ja: やばい！目覚まし、七時にかけたのに！
lines.kana: やばい！めざまし、しちじにかけたのに！
lines.english: Oh no! I set my alarm for seven!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: dakara, zutto natteru tte. sono mezamashi de, boku wa me ga sameta n da kedo ne.
lines.ja: だから、ずっと鳴ってるって。その目覚ましで、僕は目が覚めたんだけどね。
lines.kana: だから、ずっとなってるって。そのめざましで、ぼくはめがさめたんだけどね。
lines.english: I told you, it's been going off this whole time. That alarm's what woke me up, you know.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen! a, shigoto, kyou ja nakute ashita da.
lines.ja: ごめん！あ、仕事、今日じゃなくて明日だ。
lines.kana: ごめん！あ、しごと、きょうじゃなくてあしただ。
lines.english: Sorry! Oh. Work isn't today. It's tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? jaa, nande mezamashi kaketa no?
lines.ja: え？じゃあ、なんで目覚ましかけたの？
lines.kana: え？じゃあ、なんでめざましかけたの？
lines.english: What? Then why did you set an alarm?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kyou da to omotteta. ne, kenta mo kotatsu hairu?
lines.ja: 今日だと思ってた。ね、ケンタもこたつ入る？
lines.kana: きょうだとおもってた。ね、けんたもこたつはいる？
lines.english: I thought it was today. Hey, want to get under the kotatsu too?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: iya, boku wa futon ni haitte, mou ikkai neru. oyasumi.
lines.ja: いや、僕は布団に入って、もう一回寝る。おやすみ。
lines.kana: いや、ぼくはふとんにはいって、もういっかいねる。おやすみ。
lines.english: Nah, I'm getting back into bed and going back to sleep. Night.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: oyasumi. ii yume mite ne.
lines.ja: おやすみ。いい夢見てね。
lines.kana: おやすみ。いいゆめみてね。
lines.english: Night. Sweet dreams.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora's alarm never went off, so Kenta woke him just in time for work.
Sora fell asleep under the kotatsu and panicked about work, but his shift is actually tomorrow.
Sora slept through his alarm under the kotatsu and ended up late for his shift.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Sora got under the kotatsu 'just for a bit' before bed (chotto dake kotatsu ni haitta), and line 6: he woke at four but couldn't get up. After his bad dream about being late (line 8), he remembers work starts at eight (line 10) and panics, because it's half past seven (lines 11-12). In line 14 he realises work is tomorrow, not today (kyou ja nakute ashita da), and in line 17 Kenta goes back to bed. A is wrong: the alarm did go off; it has been ringing in Sora's room the whole time (lines 1 and 13), and it woke Kenta up. C is wrong: being late for work only happened in Sora's dream (line 8); his shift is tomorrow (line 14).

questions.english: Sora tells Kenta about the dream he had under the kotatsu. What did he say?
questions.ja: ソラさんは、夢について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんは、ゆめについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa, yume ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: 'There was a bad dream' (aru, word for word)
'I held a bad dream' (motsu, word for word)
'I saw a bad dream' (miru, word for word)

questions.explanation: Line 8: iya na yume mita. A dream you have in your sleep is 'seen': yume o miru, here with o dropped and in the past, mita. Kenta uses it again in line 9 (iya na yume miru tte iu yo ne), and Sora signs off with it in line 18 (ii yume mite ne, sweet dreams). A is wrong: yume ga aru (past yume ga atta) is having a dream in the sense of an ambition, like 'I have a dream', not something you see asleep. B is wrong: yume o motsu is also about ambitions (holding a dream for the future); English 'have' doesn't turn into motsu for dreams in your sleep.

questions.english: Sora says, "yoji ni ikkai, me ga sameta n da kedo, kimochi yokute okirenakatta." What happened at four o'clock?
questions.ja: 四時に、ソラさんはどうしましたか？
questions.kana: よじに、そらさんはどうしましたか？
questions.romaji: yoji ni, sora-san wa dou shimashita ka?

choices.english: He woke up for a moment, but stayed right where he was under the kotatsu.
He got up, had a bath, and went back under the kotatsu.
His alarm went off, but he slept right through it.

questions.explanation: Line 6: me ga sameta is only the waking, his eyes opening; getting out of bed is okiru, and Sora says okirenakatta (I couldn't get up) because the kotatsu felt so nice (kimochi yokute). English 'woke up' covers both, but Japanese splits them: me ga sameta kedo, okirenakatta. B is wrong: the bath came before he got under the kotatsu (line 4: ofuro haitte), and he never got up. C is wrong: his alarm was set for seven (line 12), not four; at four he woke on his own. Kenta's line 13 shows waking because of an alarm: sono mezamashi de, boku wa me ga sameta.

questions.english: Late at night you're dozing off under the kotatsu. Kenta says, "kotatsu de neru to, kaze hiku yo." (Sleep in the kotatsu and you'll catch a cold.) Tell him you'll get into bed now.
questions.ja: こたつで寝ると、風邪ひくよ。
questions.kana: こたつでねると、かぜひくよ。
questions.romaji: kotatsu de neru to, kaze hiku yo.
questions.answer: Say you'll get into bed with futon ni hairu: wakatta, mou futon ni hairu yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: wakatta. mou futon ni hairu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 分かった。もう布団に入るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Okay. I'm getting into bed now.

modelAnswers.romaji: sou da ne. sorosoro futon ni hairu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: そうだね。そろそろ布団に入るよ。
modelAnswers.english: You're right. Time I got into bed.

questions.explanation: Getting into bed is going in: futon ni hairu, with the same hairu as ofuro ni hairu and kotatsu ni hairu. Sora strings all three together in line 4 (ofuro haitte, futon ni hairu mae ni, chotto dake kotatsu ni haitta), and Kenta says it in line 17 (futon ni haitte, mou ikkai neru). It means getting under the covers, not yet being asleep; the sleeping itself is neru. In casual speech ni can drop (futon hairu).

questions.english: Kenta checks on you the night before an early shift: "ashita, shigoto hachiji kara da yo ne? okireru?" (Work's at eight tomorrow, right? Will you manage to get up?) Tell him you'll set an alarm, or that you already have.
questions.ja: 明日、仕事八時からだよね？起きれる？
questions.kana: あした、しごとはちじからだよね？おきれる？
questions.romaji: ashita, shigoto hachiji kara da yo ne? okireru?
questions.answer: Use mezamashi with kakeru: un, mezamashi kaketoku yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, mezamashi kaketoku yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、目覚ましかけとくよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll set an alarm.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu. rokuji ni mezamashi kaketa kara.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫。六時に目覚ましかけたから。
modelAnswers.english: I'll be fine. I've set my alarm for six.

questions.explanation: Alarms are set with kakeru: mezamashi o kakeru, often said the night before as mezamashi kaketoku (-toku = do it in advance). Sora uses it in line 12 (mezamashi, shichiji ni kaketa noni) and Kenta in line 15 (nande mezamashi kaketa no?). English 'set' gives no hint of kakeru; mezamashi o oku would only mean putting the clock down somewhere. For a phone alarm, araamu o setto suru is also fine.

questions.english: You're at home with the kotatsu on. Sora comes in from outside and says, "aa, samukatta! soto, metcha samui yo." (Brr, that was cold! It's freezing out there.) Tell him to get under the kotatsu, or suggest you both do.
questions.ja: ああ、寒かった！外、めっちゃ寒いよ。
questions.kana: ああ、さむかった！そと、めっちゃさむいよ。
questions.romaji: aa, samukatta! soto, metcha samui yo.
questions.answer: Invite him in with kotatsu ni hairu: kotatsu haitte! (get in) or kotatsu ni hairou yo (let's get in).

modelAnswers.romaji: kotatsu haitte! kimochi ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: こたつ入って！気持ちいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: Get under the kotatsu! It's lovely.

modelAnswers.romaji: sou na n da. jaa, kotatsu ni hairou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: そうなんだ。じゃあ、こたつに入ろうよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh yeah? Then let's get under the kotatsu.

questions.explanation: You go into a kotatsu just like a bath or a bed: kotatsu ni hairu. Sora uses it in line 4 (chotto dake kotatsu ni haitta) and line 16 (kenta mo kotatsu hairu?), dropping ni the second time, as casual speech does. English 'under' tempts kotatsu no shita, but the verb is simply hairu. Sleeping in it is a different phrase, kotatsu de neru (lines 3 and 9).

newWords.english: ring, go off (an alarm, a phone)

script.title: Tonight, not tomorrow
script.setting: Early evening at the office. Yuki and Mai are about to go out for dinner when they hear thunder the forecast never mentioned.

lines.kana: ね、まい、きょうごはんいかない？

lines.speaker: mai

lines.kana: そうだよね。ちょっとみてみる。え！たいふう、こんばんくるって！

lines.kana: え、こんばん？てんきよほう、はずれてばっかり！

lines.kana: だよね！あれ？ちょっとゆれてない？

lines.ja: うん。でも、そういう予報は当たるんだよね。
