lines.english: Yeah. But those are always the ones that turn out right.

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: The typhoon is due tomorrow, as forecast, so they go to dinner tonight before it arrives.
Dinner is called off: the typhoon turns out to be coming tonight, not tomorrow, there's a small earthquake, and Mai heads home to her cat, who's scared of thunder.
A big earthquake hits Chiba, so Yuki and Mai stay late at the office together until it's safe.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Yuki suggests dinner and Mai says yes (line 2). Then they hear thunder (lines 2 and 4), though the forecast said no rain (line 3). Line 7: the news says the typhoon is coming tonight, not tomorrow (taifuu, konban kuru tte!). Lines 9-12: a small earthquake (ookii jishin ja nakute yokatta). Lines 14-15: Mai asks to go home because her cat is scared of thunder, and Yuki moves dinner to next week (gohan wa raishuu ne). A is wrong: the forecast said tomorrow, but the news says tonight (lines 6-8), and dinner is off. C is wrong: the quake in Chiba wasn't a big one (line 12), and Mai goes home rather than staying.

questions.english: Mai asks you, "ne, ashita, kaimono ikanai?" (Want to go shopping tomorrow?) You've heard a typhoon is coming tomorrow. Tell her.
questions.ja: ね、明日、買い物行かない？
questions.kana: ね、あした、かいものいかない？
questions.romaji: ne, ashita, kaimono ikanai?
questions.answer: Say a typhoon is coming tomorrow, with taifuu and kuru: demo, ashita taifuu kuru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: demo, ashita taifuu kuru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: でも、明日台風来るよ。
modelAnswers.english: But there's a typhoon coming tomorrow.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita wa taifuu ga kuru tte.
modelAnswers.ja: 明日は台風が来るって。
modelAnswers.english: They say a typhoon's coming tomorrow.

questions.explanation: A typhoon comes: kuru. English 'a typhoon hits' pushes you to utsu or ataru, which don't work with the typhoon as the subject. The scene uses the same pair in line 6 (taifuu kuru no, ashita ja nakatta?) and line 7 (taifuu, konban kuru tte!). The second answer adds tte, 'they say', the way Yuki passes on the news in line 7. Ataru only works the other way round, with your plans as the subject: ryokou ga taifuu ni atatchatta (our trip ran into a typhoon).

questions.english: Once the shaking is over, Yuki wonders about the earthquake. What does she say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、地震のあと何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、じしんのあとなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, jishin no ato nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I wonder where that earthquake rang out.
choices.romaji: ima no jishin, doko de natta no kana.

choices.english: I wonder where that earthquake struck.
choices.romaji: ima no jishin, doko o utta no kana.

choices.english: I wonder where that earthquake happened.
choices.romaji: ima no jishin, doko de okita no kana.

questions.explanation: Line 11: Yuki says ima no jishin, doko de okita no kana, and Mai answers with the same verb in line 12 (chiba de okita tte). An earthquake happens: okiru. A uses naru, the verb thunder takes (line 4: kaminari natteru); an earthquake doesn't ring. B is English 'strike' or 'hit' put into Japanese: utsu is hitting with a hand or a bat, and an earthquake never utsu. While it shakes, people just shout jishin da!, as Mai does in line 10. Yuki lines up all three verbs in line 13: taifuu wa kuru, kaminari wa natteru, jishin mo okita.

questions.english: Yuki doubts there's any thunder, because the forecast said no rain. Mai answers, "demo, kiite. honto ni kaminari natteru yo." What can she hear?
questions.ja: マイさんは、何が聞こえましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、なにがきこえましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, nani ga kikoemashita ka?

choices.english: Thunder: it's rumbling outside right now.
Nothing yet: the sky is turning stormy, and thunder is on its way.
A bolt of lightning that has just hit something near the office.

questions.explanation: Line 4: kaminari natteru is naru 鳴る, 'make a sound', the verb a phone or an alarm takes, in its -teru form: thunder is rumbling right now. In line 2 Mai heard one clap (ima, kaminari natta?), and by line 4 it's still going. B mixes it up with naru 'become': the two sound alike, but 'ring' is said flat (na-RU) while 'become' falls (NA-ru), and nobody says the weather is turning into thunder. C would be kaminari ga ochita (lightning struck); nothing in the scene was hit.

questions.english: Mai looks out at a dry street and says, "kyou, ame furu tte itteta noni, furanakatta ne." (They said it would rain today, but it didn't.) Agree, and grumble that the forecast got it wrong.
questions.ja: 今日、雨降るって言ってたのに、降らなかったね。
questions.kana: きょう、あめふるっていってたのに、ふらなかったね。
questions.romaji: kyou, ame furu tte itteta noni, furanakatta ne.
questions.answer: Say the forecast missed, with tenki yohou and hazureru in the past: un, tenki yohou hazureta ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, tenki yohou hazureta ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、天気予報外れたね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, the forecast got it wrong.

modelAnswers.romaji: tenki yohou, mata hazureta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 天気予報、また外れたよ。
modelAnswers.english: The forecast was wrong again.

questions.explanation: A forecast misses (hazureru) or hits (ataru), like a guess. As a grumble it's almost always past, hazureta, as Yuki says in line 5 (tenki yohou, mata hazureta ne); Mai's hazurete bakkari in line 8 means it keeps getting things wrong. Not machigaeru: that's a person making a slip, so yohou ga machigaeta doesn't work. The opposite comes at the end: Mai hopes the typhoon forecast is wrong this time (line 16: hazurete hoshii naa), and Yuki says those are the ones that turn out right (line 17: sou iu yohou wa ataru n da yo ne).

newWords.english: again (mata hazureta = got it wrong again)
Chiba, the prefecture just east of Tokyo
be right, hit the mark (a forecast, a guess); the opposite of hazureru

script.title: Nicer than he seems
script.setting: A weekday morning at the office. Mai (Kimura-san at work) is quiet at her desk the day after a meeting with Yamamoto-san, a blunt colleague from another team. Her manager, Tanaka-san, stops by.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san, kyou wa genki nai desu ne. kibun demo warui n desu ka?
lines.ja: 木村さん、今日は元気ないですね。気分でも悪いんですか？
lines.kana: きむらさん、きょうはげんきないですね。きぶんでもわるいんですか？
lines.english: Kimura-san, you seem down today. Are you feeling sick or something?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, iie, daijoubu desu. kinou, yamamoto-san to kaigi datta n desu kedo.
lines.ja: あ、いいえ、大丈夫です。昨日、山本さんと会議だったんですけど。
lines.kana: あ、いいえ、だいじょうぶです。きのう、やまもとさんとかいぎだったんですけど。
lines.english: Oh, no, I'm fine. It's just that I had a meeting with Yamamoto-san yesterday.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: aa, yamamoto-san desu ka. nante iwareta n desu ka?
lines.ja: ああ、山本さんですか。何て言われたんですか？
lines.kana: ああ、やまもとさんですか。なんていわれたんですか？
lines.english: Ah, Yamamoto-san. What did he say to you?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: watashi no shigoto o mite, kore, dame desu ne tte. sore dake de, sugu dete itchatta n desu.
lines.ja: 私の仕事を見て、これ、ダメですねって。それだけで、すぐ出て行っちゃったんです。
lines.kana: わたしのしごとをみて、これ、だめですねって。それだけで、すぐでていっちゃったんです。
lines.english: He looked at my work and said, "This won't do." Just that, and then he walked straight out.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sorede, ki ni shiteta n desu ne.
lines.ja: それで、気にしてたんですね。
lines.kana: それで、きにしてたんですね。
lines.english: So that's what's been bothering you.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai. sumimasen, seikaku warui no kana tte, chotto omotchaimashita.
lines.ja: はい。すみません、性格悪いのかなって、ちょっと思っちゃいました。
lines.kana: はい。すみません、せいかくわるいのかなって、ちょっとおもっちゃいました。
lines.english: Yes. I'm sorry, but I did kind of wonder if he's just mean.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: yamamoto-san wa, dare ni demo sou na n desu yo. kanji wa chotto warui desu kedo, seikaku wa ii n desu.
lines.ja: 山本さんは、誰にでもそうなんですよ。感じはちょっと悪いですけど、性格はいいんです。
lines.kana: やまもとさんは、だれにでもそうなんですよ。かんじはちょっとわるいですけど、せいかくはいいんです。
lines.english: Yamamoto-san is like that with everyone. He comes across as a bit unfriendly, but he's a good person.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, sou na n desu ka?
lines.ja: え、そうなんですか？
lines.kana: え、そうなんですか？
lines.english: Oh, is he?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kesa wa, yamamoto-san mo genki nakatta n desu yo.
lines.ja: 今朝は、山本さんも元気なかったんですよ。
lines.kana: けさは、やまもとさんもげんきなかったんですよ。
lines.english: And this morning, Yamamoto-san seemed down too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? yamamoto-san mo desu ka?
lines.ja: え？山本さんもですか？
lines.kana: え？やまもとさんもですか？
lines.english: What? Him too?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san ni, kinou wa gomen tte ittoite kudasai, tte. sugoku ki ni shitemashita yo.
lines.ja: 木村さんに、昨日はごめんって言っといてください、って。すごく気にしてましたよ。
lines.kana: きむらさんに、きのうはごめんっていっといてください、って。すごくきにしてましたよ。
lines.english: He asked me to tell you he's sorry about yesterday. It was really bothering him.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou datta n desu ka. shiranakatta desu.
lines.ja: そうだったんですか。知らなかったです。
lines.kana: そうだったんですか。しらなかったです。
lines.english: Oh, I see. I had no idea.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ato, kimura-san wa kanji ga ii shi, shigoto mo dekiru tte, ittemashita yo.
lines.ja: あと、木村さんは感じがいいし、仕事もできるって、言ってましたよ。
lines.kana: あと、きむらさんはかんじがいいし、しごともできるって、いってましたよ。
lines.english: Oh, and he said you're pleasant to work with, and good at your job, too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yamamoto-san, hontou wa seikaku ii n desu ne.
lines.ja: 山本さん、本当は性格いいんですね。
lines.kana: やまもとさん、ほんとうはせいかくいいんですね。
lines.english: So Yamamoto-san is actually a nice person underneath.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou na n desu. kanji wa ii kedo seikaku ga warui hito mo imasu kara ne.
lines.ja: そうなんです。感じはいいけど性格が悪い人もいますからね。
lines.kana: そうなんです。かんじはいいけどせいかくがわるいひともいますからね。
lines.english: That's right. After all, some people are pleasant on the surface but mean underneath.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou desu ne. yamamoto-san mo genki nai nara, ima kara koe o kakete kimasu.
lines.ja: そうですね。山本さんも元気ないなら、今から声をかけてきます。
lines.kana: そうですね。やまもとさんもげんきないなら、いまからこえをかけてきます。
lines.english: That's true. If Yamamoto-san's feeling down too, I'll go and have a word with him now.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ii desu ne. a, demo, shigoto wa mou ichido mite kudasai ne. yamamoto-san no dame wa, hontou ni dame desu kara.
lines.ja: いいですね。あ、でも、仕事はもう一度見てくださいね。山本さんのダメは、本当にダメですから。
lines.kana: いいですね。あ、でも、しごとはもういちどみてくださいね。やまもとさんのだめは、ほんとうにだめですから。
lines.english: Good idea. Oh, but do look over your work again. When Yamamoto-san says it won't do, it really won't.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Tanaka-san warns Mai that Yamamoto-san seems pleasant but is mean underneath.
Mai feels sick after a long meeting, so Tanaka-san tells her to take it easy.
Mai thought Yamamoto-san was mean, but he felt bad about yesterday and had praised her.

questions.explanation: Lines 4-6: after the meeting Yamamoto-san only said 'kore, dame desu ne' (this won't do) and walked out, so Mai wondered if he was mean (seikaku warui no kana). Lines 9-13: Tanaka-san tells her Yamamoto-san was down too, asked him to pass on a 'sorry' (gomen), and said Mai is pleasant to work with and good at her job. In line 16 she decides to go and speak to him. A turns Tanaka-san's point around: he says Yamamoto-san comes across as unfriendly but is a good person (line 7). The people who are pleasant but mean (line 15) are other people, not him. B is wrong: Tanaka-san does ask if she feels sick (kibun demo warui n desu ka?), but in line 2 she says she's fine. She's down (genki nai), not ill.

questions.english: Yuki is about to work with Yamamoto-san for the first time, and she asks you what he's like. Tell her he's a good person underneath, using seikaku.
questions.ja: 山本さんって、どんな人？
questions.kana: やまもとさんって、どんなひと？
questions.romaji: yamamoto-san tte, donna hito?
questions.answer: Say he's a nice person with seikaku ii (ga drops in casual speech), or seikaku no ii hito before a noun. You can set it against how he comes across, the way Tanaka-san does: kanji wa chotto warui kedo, seikaku wa ii.

modelAnswers.romaji: kanji wa chotto warui kedo, seikaku wa ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 感じはちょっと悪いけど、性格はいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: He comes across a bit unfriendly, but he's a good guy.

modelAnswers.romaji: seikaku no ii hito da yo. hanashite miru to wakaru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 性格のいい人だよ。話してみるとわかるよ。
modelAnswers.english: He's a nice person. You'll see once you talk to him.

questions.explanation: Seikaku is who someone is underneath, so seikaku ga ii is the plain way to say someone is a good, kind person. Tanaka-san uses it in line 7 (seikaku wa ii n desu), right after kanji wa chotto warui (he comes across as a bit unfriendly), and Mai says it in line 14 (hontou wa seikaku ii n desu ne). Keep seikaku first: ii seikaku shiteru ne usually sounds sarcastic ('you've got some nerve'). Yuki asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Tanaka-san sees the meeting has been bothering her, what does Mai say she wondered about Yamamoto-san?
questions.ja: 木村さんは、山本さんについて、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: きむらさんは、やまもとさんについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kimura-san wa, yamamoto-san ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: maybe he's a bad person
maybe he's just mean
maybe he has a bad personality (word for word)
choices.romaji: warui seikaku o motteru no kana

questions.explanation: Line 6: 'seikaku warui no kana tte, chotto omotchaimashita' (I kind of wondered if he's just mean), with ga dropped as usual. Seikaku ga warui judges what someone is like by nature, so it's a strong thing to say, which is why Mai says sumimasen first. Tanaka-san uses it again in line 15 (seikaku ga warui hito). A is wrong: warui hito judges someone as a bad person in the moral sense, like a crook, and Mai only meant he might be mean. C is a word-for-word calque of 'have a bad personality': Japanese doesn't hold a personality with motsu. Seikaku is the subject and warui describes it.

questions.english: Tanaka-san passes on what Yamamoto-san said about Mai: 'kimura-san wa kanji ga ii shi, shigoto mo dekiru.' What did he mean by kanji ga ii?
questions.ja: 感じがいいって、どういう意味ですか？
questions.kana: かんじがいいって、どういういみですか？
questions.romaji: kanji ga ii tte, dou iu imi desu ka?

choices.english: She's pleasant to deal with.
Her handwriting is neat.
She's always in a good mood.

questions.explanation: Line 13: kanji (感じ) here is the impression someone's manner gives, so kanji ga ii means she's pleasant to deal with. Tanaka-san sets it against seikaku in line 15 (kanji wa ii kedo seikaku ga warui hito: pleasant on the surface but mean underneath), and in line 7 he says Yamamoto-san himself comes across as a bit unfriendly (kanji wa chotto warui). B mixes it up with kanji (漢字), the Chinese characters, which sound the same; nobody mentions writing. C would be kibun ga ii (in a good mood), which is about how she feels at a given moment, not the impression she makes on people.

questions.english: Your friend Kenta flops onto the sofa with a big sigh and says this. Tell him he seems down and ask what's wrong, using genki.
questions.ja: はあ。今日は何もしたくないなあ。
questions.kana: はあ。きょうはなにもしたくないなあ。
questions.romaji: haa. kyou wa nanimo shitakunai naa.
questions.answer: Say genki nai ne (genki ga nai with ga dropped) to tell him he seems down, then ask dou shita no? Don't say genki ja nai, which leans toward 'unwell', or kibun warui, which means feeling sick.

modelAnswers.romaji: genki nai ne. dou shita no?
modelAnswers.ja: 元気ないね。どうしたの？
modelAnswers.english: You seem down. What's up?

modelAnswers.romaji: kenta, kyou zutto genki nai ne. daijoubu?
modelAnswers.ja: ケンタ、今日ずっと元気ないね。大丈夫？
modelAnswers.english: Kenta, you've seemed down all day. You okay?

questions.explanation: Genki ga nai is how someone seems right now: low and flat. Tanaka-san opens with it in line 1 (kyou wa genki nai desu ne), says it about Yamamoto-san in line 9 (genki nakatta), and Mai uses it in line 16 (genki nai nara). Tanaka-san's follow-up in line 1, kibun demo warui n desu ka? (are you feeling sick?), asks about something different, and Mai says she's fine. Kenta is a friend, so casual genki nai ne fits. To Tanaka-san you'd say genki nai desu ne.

newWords.english: person (seikaku no ii hito: a nice person)

script.title: His lying face
script.setting: A weekday evening. Yuki's mother leaves her a voicemail about Kenji, who has been coming home late all week.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? okaasan da kedo. kenji, konshuu zutto kaeri ga osoi no.
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？お母さんだけど。ケンジ、今週ずっと帰りが遅いの。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？おかあさんだけど。けんじ、こんしゅうずっとかえりがおそいの。
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? It's Mum. Kenji's been coming home late all week.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: tomodachi to benkyou shiteru tte iu kedo, are wa uso tsuiteru kao yo.
lines.ja: 友達と勉強してるって言うけど、あれは嘘ついてる顔よ。
lines.kana: ともだちとべんきょうしてるっていうけど、あれはうそついてるかおよ。
lines.english: He says he's studying with friends, but I know that face. He's lying.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kinou mo juuichiji made kaette konakatta kara, monku itta no.
lines.ja: 昨日も十一時まで帰ってこなかったから、文句言ったの。
lines.kana: きのうもじゅういちじまでかえってこなかったから、もんくいったの。
lines.english: Yesterday he didn't get in till eleven again, so I complained to him about it.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou shitara, monku bakkari iwanaide yo. boku mo shigoto ga isogashii n da kara tte.
lines.ja: そうしたら、「文句ばっかり言わないでよ。僕も仕事が忙しいんだから」って。
lines.kana: そうしたら、「もんくばっかりいわないでよ。ぼくもしごとがいそがしいんだから」って。
lines.english: And he goes, "Stop complaining all the time. I'm busy with work too, you know."

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shigoto tte nani yo. mou, sonna joudan itte.
lines.ja: 仕事って何よ。もう、そんな冗談言って。
lines.kana: しごとってなによ。もう、そんなじょうだんいって。
lines.english: Work? What work? Honestly, cracking jokes like that.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: gomen ne, guchi bakkari itte. kenji ni monku itte mo, kiite kurenai kara.
lines.ja: ごめんね、愚痴ばっかり言って。ケンジに文句言っても、聞いてくれないから。
lines.kana: ごめんね、ぐちばっかりいって。けんじにもんくいっても、きいてくれないから。
lines.english: Sorry, all I'm doing is moaning. Complaining to Kenji gets me nowhere. He doesn't listen.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, kesa satou-san ni mo guchi ittara ne, kenji, keeki no omise de baito shiteru n da tte!
lines.ja: で、今朝佐藤さんにも愚痴言ったらね、ケンジ、ケーキのお店でバイトしてるんだって！
lines.kana: で、けささとうさんにもぐちいったらね、けんじ、けーきのおみせでばいとしてるんだって！
lines.english: So this morning I was moaning to Satou-san too, and he says Kenji's got a part-time job at a cake shop!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: raishuu, okaasan no tanjoubi desho? dakara uso tsuiteta no ne.
lines.ja: 来週、お母さんの誕生日でしょ？だから嘘ついてたのね。
lines.kana: らいしゅう、おかあさんのたんじょうびでしょ？だからうそついてたのね。
lines.english: It's my birthday next week, isn't it? So that's why he was lying.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shigoto ga isogashii tte, joudan itteta n ja nakatta no ne.
lines.ja: 仕事が忙しいって、冗談言ってたんじゃなかったのね。
lines.kana: しごとがいそがしいって、じょうだんいってたんじゃなかったのね。
lines.english: And all that about being busy with work. He wasn't joking after all.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki mo shitteta n desho? zutto okaasan ni naisho ni shiteta no ne.
lines.ja: ユキも知ってたんでしょ？ずっとお母さんに内緒にしてたのね。
lines.kana: ゆきもしってたんでしょ？ずっとおかあさんにないしょにしてたのね。
lines.english: You knew too, didn't you? You've been keeping it from me all this time.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kono hanashi, kenji ni wa naisho ni shite ne. raishuu wa, bikkuri shita kao suru kara.
lines.ja: この話、ケンジには内緒にしてね。来週は、びっくりした顔するから。
lines.kana: このはなし、けんじにはないしょにしてね。らいしゅうは、びっくりしたかおするから。
lines.english: Don't say a word of this to Kenji, okay? Next week I'll put on my surprised face.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: okaasan mo uso tsuku no, jouzu ja nai kedo ne. jaa ne.
lines.ja: お母さんも嘘つくの、上手じゃないけどね。じゃあね。
lines.kana: おかあさんもうそつくの、じょうずじゃないけどね。じゃあね。
lines.english: Mind you, I'm not much good at lying either. Bye!

questions.english: What does Okaasan find out, and what is she going to do?
questions.ja: お母さんは何がわかりましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなにがわかりましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nani ga wakarimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji has been out at karaoke with his friends, and she wants Yuki to have a word with him.
Kenji's late nights are a part-time job at a cake shop, because her birthday is coming, and she'll pretend she doesn't know.
Kenji really has been studying with friends, and she feels bad for complaining at him.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenji has been late all week and says he's studying with friends, but Okaasan is sure he's lying (uso tsuiteru kao). Line 7: Satou-san tells her Kenji has a part-time job at a cake shop. Line 8: her birthday is next week, so that's why he lied (dakara uso tsuiteta no ne). Line 11: she asks Yuki not to tell Kenji (kenji ni wa naisho ni shite ne) and says she'll put on a surprised face. A is wrong: karaoke never comes up, and far from asking Yuki to talk to Kenji, she asks her to say nothing. C is wrong: he wasn't studying, he was working (line 7), and her only apology is to Yuki, for moaning (line 6: gomen ne, guchi bakkari itte).

questions.english: You've told Kenta you've started getting up at five every morning. He doesn't buy it: "e, mainichi goji ni okiteru no? uso desho?" (Wait, you're up at five every day? You're kidding, right?) Tell him you're not lying.
questions.ja: え、毎日五時に起きてるの？嘘でしょ？
questions.kana: え、まいにちごじにおきてるの？うそでしょ？
questions.romaji: e, mainichi goji ni okiteru no? uso desho?
questions.answer: Deny it with uso o tsuku in the negative -teru form: honto da yo. uso tsuitenai yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: honto da yo. uso tsuitenai yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ほんとだよ。嘘ついてないよ。
modelAnswers.english: It's true. I'm not lying.

modelAnswers.romaji: uso tsuitenai tte! honto ni goji ni okiteru n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 嘘ついてないって！ほんとに五時に起きてるんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm not lying, I swear! I really do get up at five.

questions.explanation: Lying takes tsuku: uso o tsuku, here as uso tsuitenai (I'm not lying), with o dropped as usual in casual speech. Okaasan uses the same verb in line 2 (uso tsuiteru kao), line 8 (uso tsuiteta) and line 12 (uso tsuku no). English 'tell a lie' points to iu, and natives do say uso bakkari itte, but the set phrase for lying is tsuku. Kenta's uso desho? on its own just means 'you're kidding, right?', so the verb has to come from you. To someone like Satou-san you'd say uso wa tsuitemasen.

questions.english: Okaasan says, "shigoto ga isogashii tte, joudan itteta n ja nakatta no ne." What has she realised?
questions.ja: ケンジの「仕事が忙しい」は、どういうことでしたか？
questions.kana: けんじの「しごとがいそがしい」は、どういうことでしたか？
questions.romaji: kenji no shigoto ga isogashii wa, dou iu koto deshita ka?

choices.english: Kenji was teasing her, because she's the one who's always busy.
Kenji has stopped joking around and started taking his studies seriously.
Kenji wasn't joking when he said he was busy with work: he really does have a job.

questions.explanation: Line 9: joudan itteta n ja nakatta = he wasn't joking. In line 4 Kenji said boku mo shigoto ga isogashii n da kara, and in line 5 Okaasan brushed it off as a joke (shigoto tte nani yo. mou, sonna joudan itte). Line 7 shows it was true: he has a part-time job at a cake shop. Jokes are said, with iu (joudan o iu), not made (joudan o tsukuru doesn't work). A is wrong: nobody mentions Okaasan's own work; the 'joke' was a high schooler claiming to be busy with work. B is wrong: he wasn't studying at all (line 7), and the line is about something he said, not about him getting serious.

questions.english: When Okaasan had a go at him for coming home late, what did Kenji say back?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは、お母さんに何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんは、おかあさんになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa, okaasan ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Stop complaining all the time.
Stop doing complaints all the time (monku with suru).
Stop moaning about your lot all the time.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenji answers back with monku bakkari iwanaide yo. A complaint is something you say: monku o iu, here in the -naide form (don't...). Okaasan uses the same pair in line 3 (monku itta no) and line 6 (monku itte mo). B is English 'complain' turned into one verb with suru; Japanese doesn't say monku suru. C has the right verb but the wrong noun for this moment: guchi is moaning to let off steam to someone who'll listen, which is what Okaasan does with Yuki and Satou-san (lines 6-7). What she did to Kenji was object to his face about coming home late, and that is monku.

questions.english: You've spent the whole evening at Kenta's going on about your awful week at work. He looks at the clock: "mou juuniji da yo. kyou wa zutto shigoto no hanashi da ne." (It's midnight already. You've talked about work all night.) Apologise for moaning so much.

questions.kana: もうじゅうにじだよ。きょうはずっとしごとのはなしだね。

Don't use monku here: monku o iu is objecting to someone or something, the way Okaasan tells Kenji off in line 3. You weren't objecting to Kenta, just letting off steam about your week. Like monku, guchi is said with iu, not suru.

questions.answer: Say no and ask him to keep it secret with naisho ni suru as a request: dame! yuki ni wa naisho ni shite ne.

questions.explanation: naisho takes ni suru, and naisho ni shite (ne) is the everyday way to say 'keep this between us', exactly as Okaasan says it in line 11 (kenji ni wa naisho ni shite ne). In line 10 she uses it in the past about Yuki (okaasan ni naisho ni shiteta). English 'keep a secret' leads to mamoru, but naisho o mamotte is wrong; mamoru only goes with himitsu (himitsu mamotte ne), and himitsu ni shite works too. The person it's kept from takes ni wa: yuki ni wa.

script.title: A sudden recovery
script.setting: A weekday evening. Kenji has been off school with a cold. Yuki gets home from work and checks on him. He's on the sofa with his game.

choices.english: Kenji's fever has come back, so Yuki takes his game and tells him to lie down until he's better.

Kenji says his cold isn't better so he can skip school. When Yuki says she'll keep his game until it is, he suddenly feels better, so he's going to school tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Kenji's fever came down yesterday (kusuri nondara, sugu sagatta). Line 4: he says his cold isn't better yet (mada naottenai) and asks to skip school again. Lines 8-13: he wasn't sleeping. He was lying down playing games, so of course he's still tired. Line 15: Yuki will keep the game until his cold is better (kaze ga naoru made). In line 16 it's suddenly better (ima naotta!), so in lines 17-18 he agrees to go to school. A is wrong: his fever is down (lines 2 and 5). Yuki only says she'll keep the game until he's better. B is wrong: Yuki never lets him stay home. She uses the gaming to show he isn't really that sick.

questions.english: Yuki says Kenji has been asleep all day. He answers, "nete wa nai yo. zutto yoko ni natteta dake." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは寝ていましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはねていましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nete imashita ka?

choices.english: He wasn't asleep. He'd just been lying down the whole time.
He'd been sleeping on his side all day, so he didn't sleep well.
He'd slept all day and had only just woken up.

questions.explanation: Line 7: Yuki assumes he slept all day (kyou zutto neteta noni?). Line 8: Kenji corrects her with nete wa nai yo (I wasn't asleep) and zutto yoko ni natteta dake (I was just lying down). Yoko ni naru means lying down to rest, not neru (sleeping). Yuki picks up on it in line 9 (yoko ni natte, nani shiteta no?), and it turns out he was lying there playing his game (line 10). B takes yoko to mean 'side', but yoko ni naru just means lying down, whichever way you face. C is what Yuki assumed, and Kenji says it isn't true.

questions.english: You were in bed with a fever yesterday. Yuki looks in and asks, "kyou wa daijoubu? netsu wa?" (You okay today? How's the fever?) It's come down. Tell her.
questions.ja: 今日は大丈夫？熱は？
questions.kana: きょうはだいじょうぶ？ねつは？
questions.romaji: kyou wa daijoubu? netsu wa?
questions.answer: Say your fever has come down, using sagaru in the past: un, netsu sagatta yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, netsu sagatta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、熱下がったよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, my fever's come down.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kusuri nondara, netsu sagatta.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、薬飲んだら、熱下がった。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I took some medicine and my fever went down.

questions.explanation: A fever comes down by itself with sagaru, so netsu takes ga, which casual speech often drops: netsu sagatta. Yuki asks it that way in line 1, and Kenji answers in line 2 (un, sagatta). Don't use oriru or heru here. Netsu o sageru (with o) means someone bringing the fever down. That's why Kenji puts the medicine in a separate clause: kusuri nondara, sugu sagatta. Yuki only said 'netsu wa?', so you have to supply the verb yourself.

questions.english: Kenji remembers you had a cold last week and asks, "sou ieba, kaze dou?" (Oh yeah, how's your cold?) You're completely over it. Tell him.
questions.ja: そういえば、風邪どう？
questions.kana: そういえば、かぜどう？
questions.romaji: sou ieba, kaze dou?
questions.answer: Say it's better now, using naoru in the past with mou: un, mou naotta yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, mou naotta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、もう治ったよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it's all better now.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kaze mou naotta. arigatou.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、風邪もう治った。ありがとう。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm over my cold. Thanks.

questions.explanation: A cold clears up with naoru. Its past form is naotta, and adding mou makes it 'better now'. Kenji says exactly that in line 16 (a, naotta! ima naotta!) once his game is at stake. Mada naottenai (lines 4 and 14) is the 'not yet' answer. Kaze takes ga, which is often dropped. Kaze o naosu (with o) means someone doing the healing, as in hayaku naoshite ne (get well soon).

questions.english: Yuki points out that Kenji's fever is gone. What does Kenji say back?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: But my tiredness hasn't healed yet.
choices.romaji: demo, tsukare ga mada naoranai n da yo.

choices.english: But I still can't shake this tiredness.
choices.romaji: demo, tsukare ga mada torenai n da yo.

choices.english: But my tiredness hasn't gone down yet.
choices.romaji: demo, tsukare ga mada sagaranai n da yo.

questions.explanation: Line 6: tsukare ga mada torenai. Tiredness 'comes off' you (toreru), the way a stain or a button comes off. Yuki repeats it in line 7 and again in line 13 (tsukare mo torenai yo). A is the trap: naoru is for getting over an illness or injury (kaze ga naoru, lines 3 and 16), and tiredness isn't an illness that gets cured. C borrows sagaru from the fever (netsu wa sagatta, line 5). Sagaru is for things that go down on a scale, like a fever, a temperature or a price. Tiredness doesn't go down. It comes off.

questions.explanation: Line 6: Satou-san says he has been taking piano lessons lately. In line 13 Yuki suggests splitting the bill (kyou wa warikan ni shimashou ne), but in line 14 he says he has already paid, when he went to the toilet. B is wrong twice: the piano isn't new, it's the one his children played years ago (line 10), and they don't split the bill. choices.english: How much is a piano?
choices.romaji: piano tte, ikura suru n desu ka?

questions.explanation: Line 9: ichiman en! piano tte, ikura suru n desu ka? A single thing's price takes suru, and Satou-san answers in the same frame: gojuuman en mo shimasu (line 10). B uses the verb for overall spending: kakaru is what Yuki used for the lessons in line 7 (okane kakarimasen ka?), the running cost of doing piano, not what one piano goes for. A is English 'cost' word for word. kosuto is a business word for expenses, and Japanese never uses it as a verb for a price.

questions.english: After tasting the coffee, what does Yuki say about it?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、コーヒーを飲んで、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、コーヒーをのんで、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, koohii o nonde, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It's cheaper than she expected, so she'll come again.
It's a bit pricey, but it's so good she'd come back anyway.
It's good, but too pricey for her to come back.

questions.explanation: Line 5: kore nara, nedan ga chotto takakute mo, mata kitai desu. nedan ga takai means the price is high, and -te mo means 'even if', so the price doesn't put her off. Satou-san had just said nedan wa chotto takai kedo, oishii n desu yo (line 4). A gets the price backwards: the coffee is roppyaku en mo (a whole 600 yen, line 3), and a low price would be yasui. C catches takai but misses -te mo ... mata kitai: she does want to come again.

questions.english: You're at a café with Kenta. While he was in the toilet, you paid the bill. Now he says "Right, shall we head off?" and gets out his wallet. Tell him you've already paid.
questions.ja: じゃあ、そろそろ帰ろうか。
questions.kana: じゃあ、そろそろかえろうか。
questions.romaji: jaa, sorosoro kaerou ka.
questions.answer: Say it's done, with harau in the past: okane wa mou haratta yo. Keep it casual, since it's Kenta.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, okane wa mou haratta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、お金はもう払ったよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, I've already paid.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu, okane wa sakki haratta kara.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫、お金はさっき払ったから。
modelAnswers.english: It's fine, I paid earlier.

questions.explanation: Handing money over is harau, and the past haratta says it's done, just as Satou-san tells Yuki in line 14 (okane wa mou haraimashita yo, sakki, toire ni itta toki ni). Don't say kaeshita: kaesu is paying back money you borrowed. Offering to pay is more often dasu (koko wa watashi ga dasu yo), and treating someone is ogoru.

questions.english: You've had dinner with Kenta. He looks at the bill and says it comes to four thousand yen altogether. Suggest splitting it evenly.
questions.ja: 全部で四千円だって。
questions.kana: ぜんぶでよんせんえんだって。
questions.romaji: zenbu de yonsen en da tte.
questions.answer: Suggest it with warikan ni shiyou, and add each person's share if you like: hitori nisen en ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, warikan ni shiyou. hitori nisen en ne.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、割り勘にしよう。一人二千円ね。
modelAnswers.english: OK, let's split it. Two thousand each.

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa warikan ni shiyou ka.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日は割り勘にしようか。
modelAnswers.english: Shall we split it today?

questions.explanation: Splitting a bill evenly is one noun, warikan, with ni suru, as in Yuki's kyou wa warikan ni shimashou ne (line 13) and tsugi wa zettai, warikan ni shimashou ne! (line 17). English 'split' leads to wakeru, which is for asking staff for separate bills (kaikei wakete moraemasu ka?). Each person paying for their own is betsubetsu.

newWords.english: month (tsuki ni ichiman en = ten thousand yen a month)
when, at the time (toire ni itta toki ni = when I went to the toilet)

script.title: The wrong trousers
script.setting: A Saturday afternoon in a clothes shop. Sora starts a new part-time job at a restaurant next week, and Mai has come along to help him find a pair of black trousers. She pulls a pair off a rail and he takes them into the fitting room, chatting with her through the curtain.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: atarashii baito tte, kuroi zubon o haku n da yo ne?
lines.ja: 新しいバイトって、黒いズボンを履くんだよね？
lines.kana: あたらしいばいとって、くろいずぼんをはくんだよね？
lines.english: So at your new job, you wear black trousers, right?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. ue wa mise no fuku o kiru kedo, zubon wa jibun no o haku n da.
lines.ja: うん。上は店の服を着るけど、ズボンは自分のを履くんだ。
lines.kana: うん。うえはみせのふくをきるけど、ずぼんはじぶんのをはくんだ。
lines.english: Yeah. On top I wear what the restaurant gives us, but the trousers have to be my own.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, kore wa? sora no saizu mo aru yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、これは？ソラのサイズもあるよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、これは？そらのさいずもあるよ。
lines.english: Then how about these? They've got your size, too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii ne. jaa, kore, haite miru.
lines.ja: いいね。じゃあ、これ、履いてみる。
lines.kana: いいね。じゃあ、これ、はいてみる。
lines.english: Nice. OK, I'll try these on.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora, kigaeta? dou?
lines.ja: ソラ、着替えた？どう？
lines.kana: そら、きがえた？どう？
lines.english: Sora, are you changed? How are they?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: mada. are? nanka saizu awanai. hairanai yo.
lines.ja: まだ。あれ？なんかサイズ合わない。入らないよ。
lines.kana: まだ。あれ？なんかさいずあわない。はいらないよ。
lines.english: Not yet. Huh? They're not my size somehow. I can't get them on.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? itsumo no saizu desho? a, gomen! koko, rediisu da.
lines.ja: え？いつものサイズでしょ？あ、ごめん！ここ、レディースだ。
lines.kana: え？いつものさいずでしょ？あ、ごめん！ここ、れでぃーすだ。
lines.english: What? They're your usual size, aren't they? Oh, sorry! This is the women's section.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: rediisu? sore ja, saizu awanai wake da yo.
lines.ja: レディース？それじゃ、サイズ合わないわけだよ。
lines.kana: れでぃーす？それじゃ、さいずあわないわけだよ。
lines.english: Women's? Well, no wonder they don't fit!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: gomen gomen. hai, menzu no zubon motte kita. kore, haite mite.
lines.ja: ごめんごめん。はい、メンズのズボン持ってきた。これ、履いてみて。
lines.kana: ごめんごめん。はい、めんずのずぼんもってきた。これ、はいてみて。
lines.english: Sorry, sorry. Here, I've brought you some men's trousers. Try these on.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, kore wa saizu atteru. dou? niau?
lines.ja: あ、これはサイズ合ってる。どう？似合う？
lines.kana: あ、これはさいずあってる。どう？にあう？
lines.english: Oh, these fit. What do you think? Do they suit me?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, niau niau! sora, sutairu ii kara, nandemo niau ne.
lines.ja: うん、似合う似合う！ソラ、スタイルいいから、何でも似合うね。
lines.kana: うん、にあうにあう！そら、すたいるいいから、なんでもにあうね。
lines.english: Yeah, they really suit you! You've got such a good figure, everything looks good on you.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, kore ni suru. fuku kigaete kuru ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、これにする。服着替えてくるね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、これにする。ふくきがえてくるね。
lines.english: Then I'll get these. I'll go and change back.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. nee, sakki no rediisu no zubon, kawaikatta yo ne.
lines.ja: うん。ねえ、さっきのレディースのズボン、かわいかったよね。
lines.kana: うん。ねえ、さっきのれでぃーすのずぼん、かわいかったよね。
lines.english: OK. Hey, those women's trousers from before were cute, weren't they?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, mai ga haite mitara? mai ni wa zettai niau yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、マイが履いてみたら？マイには絶対似合うよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、まいがはいてみたら？まいにはぜったいにあうよ。
lines.english: So why don't you try them on? They'd definitely suit you.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto? jaa, watashi mo chotto kigaete kuru.
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、私もちょっと着替えてくる。
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、わたしもちょっときがえてくる。
lines.english: Really? OK, I'll go and change too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: mai, dou? hora, niau jan!
lines.ja: マイ、どう？ほら、似合うじゃん！
lines.kana: まい、どう？ほら、にあうじゃん！
lines.english: Mai, how are they? See? They look great on you!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, saizu mo atteru shi, ki ni itta! kore kau.
lines.ja: うん、サイズも合ってるし、気に入った！これ買う。
lines.kana: うん、さいずもあってるし、きにいった！これかう。
lines.english: Yeah, and they're my size, too. I love them! I'm getting these.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, mai mo kau no? boku no zubon o kai ni kita noni.
lines.ja: え、マイも買うの？僕のズボンを買いに来たのに。
lines.kana: え、まいもかうの？ぼくのずぼんをかいにきたのに。
lines.english: Wait, you're buying some too? We came here to buy MY trousers!

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora's usual size was too small, so Mai found him a bigger size, and he bought those.
Mai handed Sora women's trousers by mistake. He took a men's pair that fit, and Mai decided to buy the women's pair.
Mai picked out black trousers for Sora, but he decided to wear the restaurant's trousers instead.

questions.explanation: Line 7: Mai realises they're in the women's section (koko, rediisu da), so the pair she gave Sora was women's, and that's why he couldn't get them on (line 6: saizu awanai, hairanai; line 8: saizu awanai wake da). In line 9 she brings men's trousers, they fit (line 10), and he takes them (line 12: kore ni suru). Then Mai tries on the women's pair and buys it (line 17: kore kau), and Sora jokes that they came to buy his trousers (line 18). A is wrong: the first pair was his usual size, and the problem was that it was women's; Mai brought men's trousers, not a bigger size. A also leaves out Mai buying a pair. C is wrong: in line 2 Sora says the restaurant gives him the top, but the trousers have to be his own.

questions.english: Sora explains what he wears at his new job. What did he say about the trousers?
questions.ja: ソラは、ズボンのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらは、ずぼんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora wa, zubon no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: the trousers, I wear (kiru) my own
choices.romaji: zubon wa jibun no o kiru n da

choices.english: the trousers, I put on (tsukeru) my own
choices.romaji: zubon wa jibun no o tsukeru n da

choices.english: the trousers, I wear (haku) my own
choices.romaji: zubon wa jibun no o haku n da

questions.explanation: Line 2: 'zubon wa jibun no o haku n da'. Trousers take haku, the same verb as shoes, because you step into them. In the same line Sora uses kiru for the top (ue wa mise no fuku o kiru), so you hear the two verbs side by side. Mai uses haku too: 'kuroi zubon o haku' in line 1 and 'haite mite' (try them on) in line 9. A is the English speaker's trap: kiru is for things on the upper body, like shirts and jackets, not trousers. B is wrong: tsukeru is for accessories such as a necklace or a watch, not trousers.

questions.english: Sora comes to pick you up for dinner just as you get home from work, still in your work clothes. He says, "onaka suita! sugu gohan ni ikou yo." Tell him you'll just go and get changed first.
questions.ja: お腹すいた！すぐご飯に行こうよ。
questions.kana: おなかすいた！すぐごはんにいこうよ。
questions.romaji: onaka suita! sugu gohan ni ikou yo.
questions.answer: Say you'll go and change with kigaeru, usually as kigaete kuru (go, get changed and come back). fuku can stay or be dropped, and you can ask him to wait with chotto matte.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto matte. fuku kigaete kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと待って。服着替えてくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Hang on. I'll just go and get changed.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. demo saki ni kigaete kuru kara, chotto mattete.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。でも先に着替えてくるから、ちょっと待ってて。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. But I'll get changed first, so wait a sec.

questions.explanation: Sora says 'fuku kigaete kuru ne' in line 12, and Mai says 'watashi mo chotto kigaete kuru' in line 15: the -te kuru form means you go, do it, and come back. Mai's 'kigaeta?' in line 5 (are you changed?) shows that fuku is often left out, because kigaeru already means changing clothes. Don't say fuku o kaeru: that's about switching to a different outfit, not getting changed. Sora is a friend speaking casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: You're out shopping with Mai. She comes out of the fitting room in a new jacket, turns around and asks, "dou kana, kore?" Tell her it suits her.
questions.ja: どうかな、これ？
questions.kana: どうかな、これ？
questions.romaji: dou kana, kore?
questions.answer: Say it suits her with niau. In casual speech ga drops and so does the noun: niau yo, or yoku niatteru (it really suits you). sugoku adds emphasis.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, sugoku niau yo!
modelAnswers.ja: うん、すごく似合うよ！
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it really suits you!

modelAnswers.romaji: ii ne! yoku niatteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: いいね！よく似合ってるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nice! It looks great on you.

questions.explanation: In line 11 Mai tells Sora 'niau niau!', and in line 16 Sora tells Mai 'hora, niau jan!' when she comes out in the women's trousers. niau is about how something looks on a person. Whether it's the right size is a different phrase, saizu ga au: in line 10 Sora checks both, one after the other (saizu atteru. dou? niau?). A shop assistant, or anyone speaking politely, says 'yoku oniai desu ne'. Mai asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Sora tries on the men's trousers, he says, "a, kore wa saizu atteru." What does he mean?
questions.ja: メンズのズボンは、どうでしたか？
questions.kana: めんずのずぼんは、どうでしたか？
questions.romaji: menzu no zubon wa, dou deshita ka?

choices.english: These are the right size.
These look good on me.
These go well with my top.

questions.explanation: Line 10: 'a, kore wa saizu atteru'. With saizu as the subject, au (here atteru) means the size is right: unlike the women's pair, which wasn't his size and wouldn't go on (line 6: saizu awanai, hairanai), these fit. B is wrong: 'looks good on me' is niau, which Sora asks about straight after, as a separate question (dou? niau?). C is wrong: au can mean 'go with' when one thing matches another, but Sora is talking about the size, not about what the trousers go with.

script.title: Suddenly free
script.setting: A Sunday evening at home. Okaasan has her phone in her hand after messaging Yuki. She turns to Kenji, who is slumped on the sofa, and asks about next weekend.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji, raishuu no doyoubi, jikan aiteru?
lines.ja: ケンジ、来週の土曜日、時間空いてる？
lines.kana: けんじ、らいしゅうのどようび、じかんあいてる？
lines.english: Kenji, are you free next Saturday?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, nani? mata tetsudai?
lines.ja: え、何？また手伝い？
lines.kana: え、なに？またてつだい？
lines.english: Huh, what for? More chores?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ii kara. aiteru no? aitenai no?
lines.ja: いいから。空いてるの？空いてないの？
lines.kana: いいから。あいてるの？あいてないの？
lines.english: Never mind that. Are you free or not?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: doyou wa, chotto yotei aru.
lines.ja: 土曜は、ちょっと予定ある。
lines.kana: どようは、ちょっとよていある。
lines.english: Saturday I've, um, kind of got plans.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou. jaa, nichiyou wa?
lines.ja: そう。じゃあ、日曜は？
lines.kana: そう。じゃあ、にちようは？
lines.english: Oh? What about Sunday, then?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nichiyou mo muri. getsuyou, shiken aru kara.
lines.ja: 日曜も無理。月曜、試験あるから。
lines.kana: にちようもむり。げつよう、しけんあるから。
lines.english: Sunday's no good either. I've got an exam on Monday.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sokka. yuki ga ne, minna ni gohan ogoru tte. yakiniku da tte.
lines.ja: そっか。ユキがね、みんなにご飯おごるって。焼肉だって。
lines.kana: そっか。ゆきがね、みんなにごはんおごるって。やきにくだって。
lines.english: Oh well. Yuki says she's treating us all to dinner. Yakiniku, apparently.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: yakiniku? a, machigaeta. yotei aru no, sono tsugi no doyou datta.
lines.ja: 焼肉？あ、間違えた。予定あるの、その次の土曜だった。
lines.kana: やきにく？あ、まちがえた。よていあるの、そのつぎのどようだった。
lines.english: Yakiniku? Oh, my mistake. My plans are the Saturday after that.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: honto? sakki, yotei aru tte itta ja nai.
lines.ja: ほんと？さっき、予定あるって言ったじゃない。
lines.kana: ほんと？さっき、よていあるっていったじゃない。
lines.english: Really? You just said you had plans.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: honto honto. doyou wa aiteru aiteru.
lines.ja: ほんとほんと。土曜は空いてる空いてる。
lines.kana: ほんとほんと。どようはあいてるあいてる。
lines.english: Really, really. Saturday I'm free. Totally free.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo ne, yuki wa doyou, tsugou warui n da tte. nichiyou no yoru nara tsugou ii tte.
lines.ja: でもね、ユキは土曜、都合悪いんだって。日曜の夜なら都合いいって。
lines.kana: でもね、ゆきはどよう、つごうわるいんだって。にちようのよるならつごういいって。
lines.english: Thing is, Saturday's no good for Yuki. She says Sunday evening works for her.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, nichiyou?
lines.ja: え、日曜？
lines.kana: え、にちよう？
lines.english: Wait, Sunday?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji wa nichiyou, tsugou warui n desho? getsuyou, shiken aru n da kara.
lines.ja: ケンジは日曜、都合悪いんでしょ？月曜、試験あるんだから。
lines.kana: けんじはにちよう、つごうわるいんでしょ？げつよう、しけんあるんだから。
lines.english: But Sunday's no good for you, is it? You've got an exam on Monday.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: daijoubu. benkyou wa hiru ni yaru. yoru nara jikan aku kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。勉強は昼にやる。夜なら時間空くから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。べんきょうはひるにやる。よるならじかんあくから。
lines.english: It's fine. I'll study during the day. I'll be free by the evening.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, yuki ni, minna tsugou ii tte renraku shitoku ne. a, ato, doyou wa aiteru n da yo ne?
lines.ja: じゃあ、ユキに、みんな都合いいって連絡しとくね。あ、あと、土曜は空いてるんだよね？
lines.kana: じゃあ、ゆきに、みんなつごういいってれんらくしとくね。あ、あと、どようはあいてるんだよね？
lines.english: Right, I'll let Yuki know it works for everyone. Oh, and you're free on Saturday, aren't you?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un, aiteru kedo.
lines.ja: うん、空いてるけど。
lines.kana: うん、あいてるけど。
lines.english: Yeah, I'm free, but...

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yokatta. kaimono ni iku kara, tetsudatte ne.
lines.ja: よかった。買い物に行くから、手伝ってね。
lines.kana: よかった。かいものにいくから、てつだってね。
lines.english: Good. I'm going shopping, so you can come and help.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, yappari tetsudai jan!
lines.ja: え、やっぱり手伝いじゃん！
lines.kana: え、やっぱりてつだいじゃん！
lines.english: What? So it IS chores after all!

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji really does have plans on Saturday, so he'll miss Yuki's dinner and stay home to study for his exam.
Yuki can't make Sunday, so the yakiniku dinner moves to Saturday, and Kenji drops his plans to go.
Kenji claims he's busy all weekend, but once he hears Yuki is treating everyone to yakiniku he's suddenly free, and he ends up helping with Saturday's shopping too.

questions.explanation: Kenji suspects a chore (line 2), so he says he has plans on Saturday (line 4) and can't do Sunday because he has an exam on Monday (line 6). When Okaasan mentions that Yuki is treating everyone to yakiniku (line 7), he suddenly says he got the dates mixed up and is free on Saturday after all (lines 8 and 10). Yuki can only do Sunday evening (line 11), and Kenji says he'll be free by then (line 14). Then Okaasan checks that he's free on Saturday and asks him to help with the shopping (lines 15-17), which was what he was afraid of. A is wrong: Kenji takes back his Saturday plans (line 8) and will go to the dinner. B is wrong: it's Saturday that doesn't suit Yuki, not Sunday (line 11), and the dinner is on Sunday evening.

questions.english: Kenji asks you, "nichiyou no hiru, jikan aiteru? shiken no benkyou, tetsudatte hoshii n da kedo." (Are you free on Sunday during the day? I'd like some help studying for my exam.) Say whether you're free, using aiteru, or jikan aku for when you'll come free.
questions.ja: 日曜の昼、時間空いてる？試験の勉強、手伝ってほしいんだけど。
questions.kana: にちようのひる、じかんあいてる？しけんのべんきょう、てつだってほしいんだけど。
questions.romaji: nichiyou no hiru, jikan aiteru? shiken no benkyou, tetsudatte hoshii n da kedo.
questions.answer: Answer with aiteru (I'm free), or say when you'll come free: un, aiteru yo, or jikan aitara renraku suru ne. In casual speech ga drops (jikan aiteru).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, aiteru yo. nanji kara yaru?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、空いてるよ。何時からやる？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm free. What time do you want to start?

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, hiru wa chotto yotei aru n da. jikan aitara renraku suru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、昼はちょっと予定あるんだ。時間空いたら連絡するね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got something on during the day. I'll message you if I get a moment.

questions.explanation: A free slot 'opens up' (aku), so 'are you free?' is jikan aiteru?, as Okaasan asks in line 1, or just aiteru? as in line 3. Kenji answers with aiteru in lines 10 and 16, and in line 14 he uses plain aku for 'come free': yoru nara jikan aku (I'll be free by the evening). Don't use jiyuu (free as in liberty) or tada (free of charge) here. The second model answer uses both halves of the scene's yes/no pair: yotei aru for the part of the day you're busy, and jikan aitara for 'when I get a moment'. Kenji asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Okaasan first asks about Saturday, what does Kenji say?
questions.ja: ケンジは、最初に土曜日のことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじは、さいしょにどようびのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa, saisho ni doyoubi no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Saturday I'm kind of holding plans (word for word from 'have plans').
choices.romaji: doyou wa, chotto yotei o motteru.

choices.english: Saturday I've kind of got plans.
Saturday I've kind of got a scheme (a worked-out plan or project).

questions.explanation: Line 4: 'doyou wa, chotto yotei aru.' Plans exist, so they take aru, and casual speech drops ga. Kenji says it again when he backtracks (line 8: yotei aru no, sono tsugi no doyou datta), and Okaasan throws it back at him (line 9: yotei aru tte itta ja nai). A is wrong: motsu is for holding or owning things, and 'yotei o motteru' copies the English word for word. C is wrong: keikaku is a worked-out scheme, like a project or a trip itinerary, so 'keikaku aru' sounds like he's plotting something, not that he's busy.

questions.english: Okaasan passes on a message from Yuki: "nichiyou no yoru nara tsugou ii tte." What is Yuki saying?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、何と言っていましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なんといっていましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nan to itte imashita ka?

choices.english: Sunday evening suits her: she can make it then.
She'll be feeling better by Sunday evening.
She'd rather do Sunday evening, but Saturday would work too.

questions.explanation: Line 11: tsugou ii means a time suits someone, so Sunday evening is when Yuki can make it. In line 15 Okaasan uses it again: minna tsugou ii (it works for everyone). B is wrong: tsugou is about your schedule, not how you feel. Feeling better would be choushi ga ii or kibun ga ii, and nobody is ill. C is wrong: in the same line Okaasan says Saturday is tsugou warui for Yuki, so Saturday doesn't work at all.

questions.english: Imagine you're a friend of Yuki's, and her mother invites you along: "nichiyou no yoru, minna de yakiniku ni iku n da kedo, issho ni dou?" (We're all going for yakiniku on Sunday evening. Want to come?) Turn her down politely, using tsugou.
questions.ja: 日曜の夜、みんなで焼肉に行くんだけど、一緒にどう？
questions.kana: にちようのよる、みんなでやきにくにいくんだけど、いっしょにどう？
questions.romaji: nichiyou no yoru, minna de yakiniku ni iku n da kedo, issho ni dou?
questions.answer: Say Sunday evening doesn't suit you: tsugou ga warui. She's older than you, so keep ga and add desu, or soften it by trailing off with tsugou ga warukute.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, nichiyou no yoru wa chotto tsugou ga warui n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、日曜の夜はちょっと都合が悪いんです。
modelAnswers.english: I'm sorry, Sunday evening doesn't really work for me.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. demo, nichiyou wa chotto tsugou ga warukute.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、日曜はちょっと都合が悪くて。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. But Sunday's a bit difficult for me, I'm afraid.

questions.explanation: In line 11 Okaasan says Saturday is tsugou warui for Yuki, and in line 13 she teases Kenji that Sunday is tsugou warui for him. That's the tactful way to say a time doesn't suit you. The English word 'inconvenient' leads to fuben, but fuben is for places and tools (a shop that's a pain to get to), not for a day. taimingu warui means bad timing, an unlucky moment, so you can't use it to say no. Kenji tells his mother nichiyou mo muri (line 6), which is fine within the family, but with a friend's mother chotto tsugou ga warui is the polite choice. Leaving it trailing (warukute...) makes it softer still.

newWords.english: help; a chore you're roped into (from tetsudau)
Korean-style barbecue, meat you grill at the table
just as I thought; after all
a plan, a worked-out scheme (a project, an itinerary)

script.title: A belated birthday
script.setting: The morning after a rainy night, Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, leaves a voicemail for Kenta. Kenta walked him home from the station last night, and only once he got home did Satou-san work out whose birthday it was.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, satou desu. kinou no yoru wa, ame no naka, uchi made okutte kurete, arigatou gozaimashita.
lines.ja: もしもし、佐藤です。きのうの夜は、雨の中、うちまで送ってくれて、ありがとうございました。
lines.kana: もしもし、さとうです。きのうのよるは、あめのなか、うちまでおくってくれて、ありがとうございました。
lines.english: Hello, it's Satou. Thank you for seeing me home in the rain last night.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hisashiburi ni mukashi no tomodachi ni atte, osoku natte shimatte.
lines.ja: 久しぶりに昔の友達に会って、遅くなってしまって。
lines.kana: ひさしぶりにむかしのともだちにあって、おそくなってしまって。
lines.english: I'd been out seeing an old friend for the first time in ages, and it got late.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: eki de kenta-san ga, ie made okurimasu yo tte, kasa o sashite kurete.
lines.ja: 駅でケンタさんが、「家まで送りますよ」って、傘をさしてくれて。
lines.kana: えきでけんたさんが、「いえまでおくりますよ」って、かさをさしてくれて。
lines.english: Then at the station you said, "I'll see you home," and held your umbrella over me.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo kenta-san mo, kore kara tomodachi ni au tokoro datta n desu ne.
lines.ja: でもケンタさんも、これから友達に会うところだったんですね。
lines.kana: でもけんたさんも、これからともだちにあうところだったんですね。
lines.english: But you were on your way to meet your friends too, weren't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-san no sumaho kara, tanjoubi omedetou tte, minna no koe ga kikoemashita.
lines.ja: ケンタさんのスマホから、「誕生日おめでとう」って、みんなの声が聞こえました。
lines.kana: けんたさんのすまほから、「たんじょうびおめでとう」って、みんなのこえがきこえました。
lines.english: I could hear everyone on your phone saying "Happy birthday."

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: uchi ni kaette kara, yatto wakarimashita. kinou wa kenta-san no tanjoubi datta n desu ne.
lines.ja: うちに帰ってから、やっとわかりました。きのうは、ケンタさんの誕生日だったんですね。
lines.kana: うちにかえってから、やっとわかりました。きのうは、けんたさんのたんじょうびだったんですね。
lines.english: It only clicked once I got home. Yesterday was your birthday, wasn't it?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: minna de tanjoubi o iwau yotei datta n deshou?
lines.ja: みんなで誕生日を祝う予定だったんでしょう？
lines.kana: みんなでたんじょうびをいわうよていだったんでしょう？
lines.english: You were all going to celebrate it together, weren't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore na noni, watashi o uchi made okutte kurete. hontou ni sumimasen deshita.
lines.ja: それなのに、わたしをうちまで送ってくれて。本当にすみませんでした。
lines.kana: それなのに、わたしをうちまでおくってくれて。ほんとうにすみませんでした。
lines.english: And still you walked me all the way home. I'm truly sorry.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kondo no shuumatsu wa, jikka ni kaeru tte itte imashita ne.
lines.ja: 今度の週末は、実家に帰るって言っていましたね。
lines.kana: こんどのしゅうまつは、じっかにかえるっていっていましたね。
lines.english: You said you're going back to your parents' this weekend, didn't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jikka ni kaeru mae ni, ichido uchi ni kite kuremasen ka?
lines.ja: 実家に帰る前に、一度うちに来てくれませんか？
lines.kana: じっかにかえるまえに、いちどうちにきてくれませんか？
lines.english: Before you head off to your parents', would you come round to my place?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sukoshi osoku narimashita ga, watashi ni mo tanjoubi o iwawasete kudasai.
lines.ja: 少し遅くなりましたが、わたしにも誕生日を祝わせてください。
lines.kana: すこしおそくなりましたが、わたしにもたんじょうびをいわわせてください。
lines.english: It's a little late, but please let me celebrate your birthday too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: mukashi no tomodachi ni au no mo ii desu ga, atarashii tomodachi to nomu osake mo, ii mono desu kara ne.
lines.ja: 昔の友達に会うのもいいですが、新しい友達と飲むお酒も、いいものですからね。
lines.kana: むかしのともだちにあうのもいいですが、あたらしいともだちとのむおさけも、いいものですからね。
lines.english: Seeing old friends is lovely, but a drink with a new friend is lovely too, you know.

questions.english: What is Satou-san's message about?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Satou-san walked Kenta home in the rain, and now asks to come along to Kenta's parents' place this weekend.
Satou-san missed his own birthday because he was out with an old friend, so he invites Kenta over to celebrate it.
Kenta walked Satou-san home on Kenta's own birthday, so Satou-san invites him round to celebrate before Kenta goes to his parents'.

questions.explanation: Lines 1 and 3: Kenta saw Satou-san home from the station in the rain (uchi made okutte kurete; ie made okurimasu yo). Lines 5-7: Satou-san heard 'happy birthday' on Kenta's phone and, once home, realised it had been Kenta's birthday and his friends had a plan to celebrate. Lines 10-11: he asks Kenta round before he goes to his parents' and asks to celebrate his birthday too. A swaps the roles: Kenta did the walking, and Satou-san asks Kenta to come to his place, not to go along to Kenta's parents'. B: the birthday was Kenta's. Satou-san's evening with his old friend (line 2) just ran late.

questions.english: Kenta asks: "Are you free on Saturday? Want to go to a movie?" You're meeting up with a friend that day. Tell him.
questions.ja: 土曜日、ひま？映画に行かない？
questions.kana: どようび、ひま？えいがにいかない？
questions.romaji: doyoubi, hima? eiga ni ikanai?
questions.answer: Say you're seeing a friend with tomodachi ni au, using ni, not o: gomen, doyoubi wa tomodachi ni au n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, doyoubi wa tomodachi ni au n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、土曜日は友達に会うんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'm seeing a friend on Saturday.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, doyoubi wa hisashiburi ni tomodachi ni au yotei na n da. nichiyoubi wa dou?
modelAnswers.ja: あ、土曜日は久しぶりに友達に会う予定なんだ。日曜日はどう？
modelAnswers.english: Oh, on Saturday I'm meeting a friend I haven't seen in ages. How about Sunday?

questions.explanation: The person you meet takes ni: Satou-san says mukashi no tomodachi ni atte (line 2) and kore kara tomodachi ni au tokoro (line 4). English 'meet a friend' pulls toward tomodachi o au, which is wrong, and tomodachi o miru would mean watching your friend, not meeting up. tomodachi to au also works and suggests a meet-up you both arranged.

questions.english: According to Satou-san, what did Kenta say to him at the station?
questions.ja: 駅で、ケンタさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: えきで、けんたさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: eki de, kenta-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I'll take you along home.
I'll see you home.
I'll watch you home.

questions.explanation: Line 3: eki de kenta-san ga, ie made okurimasu yo tte. Satou-san says it back in lines 1 and 8 as uchi made okutte kurete, uchi being his own home. A, tsurete ikimasu, is English 'take you home' word for word, but tsurete iku is leading someone who can't go alone, like a child or a drunk friend. Said to Satou-san, it would treat him as helpless. Seeing someone home as a courtesy is okuru. C is English 'see you home' word for word, but miru only means look or watch, so it says nothing about walking him home.

questions.english: Mai asks what you're doing this weekend. You're going back to your parents' place. Tell her.
questions.ja: 今度の週末、何するの？
questions.kana: こんどのしゅうまつ、なにするの？
questions.romaji: kondo no shuumatsu, nani suru no?
questions.answer: Say you're going back to your parents' with jikka ni kaeru: jikka ni kaeru n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: jikka ni kaeru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 実家に帰るんだ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm going home to my parents'.

modelAnswers.romaji: hisashiburi ni jikka ni kaeru yo. kotoshi hajimete.
modelAnswers.ja: 久しぶりに実家に帰るよ。今年初めて。
modelAnswers.english: I'm going back to my parents' for the first time in a while. First time this year.

questions.explanation: Satou-san says kondo no shuumatsu wa, jikka ni kaeru tte (line 9) and jikka ni kaeru mae ni (line 10). jikka is the home you grew up in, and you kaeru to it because it's a return, even after years away. Plain uchi ni kaeru, as in line 6 when Satou-san gets back to his own place, only means going home. English 'go to my parents' place' leads to oya no uchi ni iku, which sounds like a visit to someone else's house.

questions.english: Near the end, what does Satou-san ask to do?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、何がしたいと言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、なにがしたいといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, nani ga shitai to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Celebrate Kenta's birthday with him at Satou-san's place, a little late.
Go with Kenta to his parents' and celebrate his birthday there.
Have Kenta and his friends round to celebrate the old friend's birthday.

questions.explanation: Line 11: watashi ni mo tanjoubi o iwawasete kudasai, 'please let me celebrate your birthday too'. iwau is celebrate, and -sasete kudasai asks to be allowed to. sukoshi osoku narimashita ga ('it's a little late') because the birthday was yesterday (line 6). The place is his own home: ichido uchi ni kite kuremasen ka (line 10). B: Kenta goes to his parents' on his own; Satou-san wants to see him before that (jikka ni kaeru mae ni). C: the plan in line 7 (minna de tanjoubi o iwau yotei) was Kenta's friends celebrating Kenta, and nobody mentions a birthday for Satou-san's old friend.

newWords.english: once, one time (ichido kite = come over sometime)

script.title: Who's the lightweight?
script.setting: Friday night at a small izakaya. Yuki and her old friend Kenta are out drinking together for the first time. She warns him she can't hold her drink. He says he can hold his, and it never shows on his face. A few glasses of strong sake later, things look rather different.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kanpai! sou ieba, yuki to nomi ni itta koto, nakatta yo ne.
lines.ja: 乾杯！そういえば、ユキと飲みに行ったこと、なかったよね。
lines.kana: かんぱい！そういえば、ゆきとのみにいったこと、なかったよね。
lines.english: Cheers! Come to think of it, we've never been out drinking together before, have we?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. gohan ni wa yoku iku kedo ne. watashi, osake yowai kara.
lines.ja: うん。ご飯にはよく行くけどね。私、お酒弱いから。
lines.kana: うん。ごはんにはよくいくけどね。わたし、おさけよわいから。
lines.english: Right. We go out to eat a lot, though. I'm a lightweight, you see.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sou na n da. boku wa kekkou osake tsuyoi yo. nanbai nonde mo, kao ni denai n da.
lines.ja: そうなんだ。僕はけっこうお酒強いよ。何杯飲んでも、顔に出ないんだ。
lines.kana: そうなんだ。ぼくはけっこうおさけつよいよ。なんばいのんでも、かおにでないんだ。
lines.english: Oh, really? I can hold my drink pretty well. No matter how many I have, it never shows on my face.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii naa. jaa, watashi wa kore ippai dake ni shitoku ne.
lines.ja: いいなあ。じゃあ、私はこれ一杯だけにしとくね。
lines.kana: いいなあ。じゃあ、わたしはこれいっぱいだけにしとくね。
lines.english: Lucky you. Well, I'll stick to just this one glass.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, kore mo nonde mite yo. kono osake, chotto tsuyoi kedo, oishii yo.
lines.ja: え、これも飲んでみてよ。このお酒、ちょっと強いけど、おいしいよ。
lines.kana: え、これものんでみてよ。このおさけ、ちょっとつよいけど、おいしいよ。
lines.english: Oh, come on, try this one too. This sake's a bit strong, but it's really good.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, chotto dake. a, honto da. oishii!
lines.ja: じゃあ、ちょっとだけ。あ、ほんとだ。おいしい！
lines.kana: じゃあ、ちょっとだけ。あ、ほんとだ。おいしい！
lines.english: Okay, just a little. Oh, you're right. It's good!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: desho? jaa, mou ippai tanomou.
lines.ja: でしょ？じゃあ、もう一杯頼もう。
lines.kana: でしょ？じゃあ、もういっぱいたのもう。
lines.english: Told you. Let's order another, then.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenta, mou yonhai mo nonderu yo. kao ni deteru kedo, daijoubu?
lines.ja: ケンタ、もう四杯も飲んでるよ。顔に出てるけど、大丈夫？
lines.kana: けんた、もうよんはいものんでるよ。かおにでてるけど、だいじょうぶ？
lines.english: Kenta, you've had four already. It's showing on your face. Are you okay?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: daijoubu, daijoubu. a, chotto tabako sutte kite mo ii?
lines.ja: 大丈夫、大丈夫。あ、ちょっとタバコ吸ってきてもいい？
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ、だいじょうぶ。あ、ちょっとたばこすってきてもいい？
lines.english: I'm fine, I'm fine. Oh, mind if I pop out for a smoke?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, kenta, tabako suu no? shiranakatta.
lines.ja: え、ケンタ、タバコ吸うの？知らなかった。
lines.kana: え、けんた、たばこすうの？しらなかった。
lines.english: Wait, Kenta, you smoke? I had no idea.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: itsumo wa suwanai yo. demo, osake ga hairu to, tabako suitaku naru n da yo ne.
lines.ja: いつもは吸わないよ。でも、お酒が入ると、タバコ吸いたくなるんだよね。
lines.kana: いつもはすわないよ。でも、おさけがはいると、たばこすいたくなるんだよね。
lines.english: Not usually. But once I've had a few, I start wanting a cigarette.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hee. demo kenta, honto ni osake tsuyoi no? watashi, mou gohai nonderu kedo.
lines.ja: へえ。でもケンタ、ほんとにお酒強いの？私、もう五杯飲んでるけど。
lines.kana: へえ。でもけんた、ほんとにおさけつよいの？わたし、もうごはいのんでるけど。
lines.english: Huh. But Kenta, can you really hold your drink? I've already had five, you know.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e! gohai? osake yowai tte itta jan! uso tsuita no?
lines.ja: え！五杯？お酒弱いって言ったじゃん！嘘ついたの？
lines.kana: え！ごはい？おさけよわいっていったじゃん！うそついたの？
lines.english: What? Five? You said you were a lightweight! Were you lying?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: gomen. shigoto no hito to nomi ni iku to, itsumo osake yowai n desu tte iu n da.
lines.ja: ごめん。仕事の人と飲みに行くと、いつも「お酒弱いんです」って言うんだ。
lines.kana: ごめん。しごとのひととのみにいくと、いつも「おさけよわいんです」っていうんだ。
lines.english: Sorry. Whenever I go drinking with people from work, I always tell them I'm not much of a drinker.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sokka. jaa, kore kara wa issho ni nomi ni ikeru ne!
lines.ja: そっか。じゃあ、これからは一緒に飲みに行けるね！
lines.kana: そっか。じゃあ、これからはいっしょにのみにいけるね！
lines.english: I see. Well then, from now on we can go out drinking together!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenta wa? osake tsuyoi n ja nakatta no?
lines.ja: ケンタは？お酒強いんじゃなかったの？
lines.kana: けんたは？おさけつよいんじゃなかったの？
lines.english: What about you? Weren't you the one who could hold his drink?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku ga yowai n ja nai yo. kono osake ga tsuyoi n da yo.
lines.ja: 僕が弱いんじゃないよ。このお酒が強いんだよ。
lines.kana: ぼくがよわいんじゃないよ。このおさけがつよいんだよ。
lines.english: I'm not the lightweight here. This sake is just strong.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai hai. mizu nonde. kondo wa, gohan ni ikou ne.
lines.ja: はいはい。水飲んで。今度は、ご飯に行こうね。
lines.kana: はいはい。みずのんで。こんどは、ごはんにいこうね。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. Drink some water. Next time, let's go out to eat instead.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki gets drunk on Kenta's strong sake, so Kenta orders her some water, and they agree to just go out to eat next time.
Kenta wants to smoke, but Yuki won't let him, so they leave the bar and go out to eat instead.
Kenta boasts that he can hold his drink, but it soon shows on his face. Yuki, who said she was a lightweight, drinks more than him and is fine.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-3 set it up: Yuki says she's a lightweight (watashi, osake yowai kara), and Kenta boasts that he can hold his drink and it never shows on his face. By line 8 he's had four glasses and it's showing. In line 12 Yuki has had five and is fine. In line 14 she admits that osake yowai n desu is just what she tells people from work, and in line 17 Kenta blames the sake. A gets them the wrong way round: Yuki is the one telling Kenta to drink water (line 18). B: Kenta asks to pop out for a smoke (line 9), but nobody leaves. Going out to eat is only Yuki's idea for next time (line 18).

questions.english: Kenta says: "You free tonight? Let's go somewhere." Suggest going out for drinks.
questions.ja: 今晩ひま？どこか行こうよ。
questions.kana: こんばんひま？どこかいこうよ。
questions.romaji: konban hima? doko ka ikou yo.
questions.answer: Suggest going out for a drink with nomi ni iku: nomi ni ikanai? or nomi ni ikou yo. You don't need to say osake, because nomi already means alcohol.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii ne. jaa, nomi ni ikanai?
modelAnswers.ja: いいね。じゃあ、飲みに行かない？
modelAnswers.english: Sounds good. Want to go for a drink, then?

modelAnswers.romaji: hima da yo. hisashiburi ni, nomi ni ikou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ひまだよ。久しぶりに、飲みに行こうよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm free. Let's go for a drink, it's been ages.

questions.explanation: Kenta uses it in line 1 (yuki to nomi ni itta koto, nakatta yo ne) and line 15 (issho ni nomi ni ikeru ne), and Yuki uses it in line 14 (shigoto no hito to nomi ni iku to). On its own, nomi already means drinking alcohol, so you don't need osake. It's the drinking version of gohan ni iku, which Yuki uses for going out to eat (lines 2 and 18). Friends also invite with plain nomou (kondo nomou yo, let's grab a drink sometime), but nomi ni iku is the clearest way to suggest going out for one.

questions.english: Kenta wants a cigarette. What does he ask Yuki?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、ユキさんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、ゆきさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, yuki-san ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Okay if I go and smoke?
choices.romaji: chotto kitsuen shite kite mo ii?

choices.english: Mind if I pop out for a smoke?
choices.romaji: chotto tabako sutte kite mo ii?

choices.english: Mind if I go have a cigarette?
choices.romaji: chotto tabako nonde kite mo ii?

questions.explanation: Line 9: chotto tabako sutte kite mo ii? Yuki answers with the same verb in line 10 (tabako suu no?), and Kenta uses it again in line 11 (tabako suitaku naru). In Japanese you breathe tobacco in: tabako (o) suu. A, kitsuen suru, is the dictionary word for 'smoke', but it belongs on signs and forms (kitsuen seki, a smoking seat; kin'en, no smoking). Said to a friend over drinks, it sounds like a notice on the wall. C, tabako o nomu, is an old way of saying it that some elderly people still use. Today it sounds dated, and it's an easy slip here because everyone is drinking (nomu). Tobacco takes suu.

questions.english: At a work drinking party, your manager Tanaka-san offers: "How about another one?" Turn it down politely by saying you can't hold your drink.
questions.ja: もう一杯、どうですか？
questions.kana: もういっぱい、どうですか？
questions.romaji: mou ippai, dou desu ka?
questions.answer: Say that you are the weak one: osake yowai n desu. Use the polite form with your manager, and keep yourself as the topic, not the drink.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, osake yowai n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、お酒弱いんです。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'm not much of a drinker.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. demo, osake ga yowai n de, ippai dake ni shitokimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、お酒が弱いんで、一杯だけにしときます。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you, but I can't really hold my drink, so I'll stop at one.

questions.explanation: Yuki says it about herself in line 2 (watashi, osake yowai kara). Line 14 shows it's the polite line she uses with people from work: osake yowai n desu. Saying you're weak with alcohol is the standard, gentle way to turn down another glass, and people usually accept it without fuss. amari nomenai n desu (I can't drink much) is correct but blunter. Keep yourself as the topic. With the drink as the subject, kono osake yowai would mean the drink is weak, just as kono osake ga tsuyoi in line 17 is about the sake, not about Kenta. osake ni yowai is fine too.

questions.english: Late in the evening, Yuki asks Kenta "honto ni osake tsuyoi no?" What is she asking?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、ケンタさんに「ほんとにお酒強いの？」と聞きました。どういう意味ですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、けんたさんに「ほんとにおさけつよいの？」とききました。どういういみですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, kenta-san ni honto ni osake tsuyoi no to kikimashita. dou iu imi desu ka?

choices.english: Whether he can really drink a lot without it getting to him.
Whether the sake he ordered is really as strong as he says.
Whether he really prefers strong drinks.

questions.explanation: When a person is the topic, osake (ga) tsuyoi means that person can hold their drink. Kenta boasts about it in line 3 (boku wa kekkou osake tsuyoi yo). By line 8 he's on his fourth glass and it shows on his face, so in line 12 Yuki, who has had five, doubts him. In line 16 she throws it back at him: osake tsuyoi n ja nakatta no? B is the other tsuyoi: when the drink is the subject, kono osake tsuyoi means the drink itself is strong. Kenta says that in line 5 (kono osake, chotto tsuyoi kedo, oishii yo) and blames it in line 17 (kono osake ga tsuyoi n da yo), but Yuki's question is about him. C: liking something would be suki. tsuyoi here is about how well he handles alcohol, not his taste.

newWords.english: counter for glasses and cups (ippai = one glass, nanbai = how many glasses, yonhai = four, gohai = five)
show on your face (kao ni denai = it doesn't show; kao ni deteru = it's showing)
have had a drink or two (literally, the alcohol is in you)

script.title: Mom's important call
script.setting: Evening at Kenta and Sora's flat. Sora has just got out of the bath. While he was in there, his phone kept ringing on the table.

speakers.name: Sora's mom
speakers.voice: female, 50s, lively and talkative (heard over the phone)

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, sora. sakki, sora no okaasan kara denwa atta yo.
lines.ja: あ、ソラ。さっき、ソラのお母さんから電話あったよ。
lines.kana: あ、そら。さっき、そらのおかあさんからでんわあったよ。
lines.english: Oh, Sora. Your mom called a little while ago.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, honto? ofuro haitteta kara, kikoenakatta.
lines.ja: え、ほんと？お風呂入ってたから、聞こえなかった。
lines.kana: え、ほんと？おふろはいってたから、きこえなかった。
lines.english: Really? I was in the bath, so I didn't hear it.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un, zutto natteta yo. de, boku no denwa ni mo kakatte kita n da.
lines.ja: うん、ずっと鳴ってたよ。で、僕の電話にもかかってきたんだ。
lines.kana: うん、ずっとなってたよ。で、ぼくのでんわにもかかってきたんだ。
lines.english: Yeah, it kept ringing. And then she called my phone too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, kenta ni mo denwa atta no? nande?
lines.ja: え、ケンタにも電話あったの？なんで？
lines.kana: え、けんたにもでんわあったの？なんで？
lines.english: Wait, she called you too? Why?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora ga denwa ni denai kara tte. daiji na hanashi da kara, sugu denwa kakete tte.
lines.ja: ソラが電話に出ないからって。大事な話だから、すぐ電話かけてって。
lines.kana: そらがでんわにでないからって。だいじなはなしだから、すぐでんわかけてって。
lines.english: She said it was because you weren't picking up. It's important, so call her right away.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: daiji na hanashi? nan darou. jaa, kakete miru.
lines.ja: 大事な話？何だろう。じゃあ、かけてみる。
lines.kana: だいじなはなし？なんだろう。じゃあ、かけてみる。
lines.english: Something important? I wonder what. OK, I'll call her.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, mata natteru yo! hayaku dete.
lines.ja: あ、また鳴ってるよ！早く出て。
lines.kana: あ、またなってるよ！はやくでて。
lines.english: Oh, it's ringing again! Quick, answer it.

lines.speaker: sora-mom
lines.romaji: sora? yatto deta! mou, nando mo kaketa noni.
lines.ja: ソラ？やっと出た！もう、何度もかけたのに。
lines.kana: そら？やっとでた！もう、なんどもかけたのに。
lines.english: Sora? Finally, you picked up! Honestly, I called you so many times.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, ofuro haitteta. de, daiji na hanashi tte nani?
lines.ja: ごめん、お風呂入ってた。で、大事な話って何？
lines.kana: ごめん、おふろはいってた。で、だいじなはなしってなに？
lines.english: Sorry, I was in the bath. So what's the important thing?

lines.speaker: sora-mom
lines.romaji: sora, chanto gohan tabeteru?
lines.ja: ソラ、ちゃんとご飯食べてる？
lines.kana: そら、ちゃんとごはんたべてる？
lines.english: Sora, are you eating properly?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, sore dake? tabeteru yo. jaa, kiru ne.
lines.ja: え、それだけ？食べてるよ。じゃあ、切るね。
lines.kana: え、それだけ？たべてるよ。じゃあ、きるね。
lines.english: What, that's it? Yes, I'm eating. OK, I'm hanging up.

lines.speaker: sora-mom
lines.romaji: a, matte, mada kiranaide! ato ne, kinou no koto na n da kedo.
lines.ja: あ、待って、まだ切らないで！あとね、昨日のことなんだけど。
lines.kana: あ、まって、まだきらないで！あとね、きのうのことなんだけど。
lines.english: Oh, wait, don't hang up yet! And another thing, about yesterday...

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, ima isogashii kara. jaa ne!
lines.ja: ごめん、今忙しいから。じゃあね！
lines.kana: ごめん、いまいそがしいから。じゃあね！
lines.english: Sorry, I'm busy right now. Bye!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, denwa kitchatta no? isogashikunai jan.
lines.ja: え、電話切っちゃったの？忙しくないじゃん。
lines.kana: え、でんわきっちゃったの？いそがしくないじゃん。
lines.english: What, you hung up on her? You're not busy.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: datte okaasan, hanashi nagai n da mon. ichijikan wa kirasete kurenai yo.
lines.ja: だってお母さん、話長いんだもん。一時間は切らせてくれないよ。
lines.kana: だっておかあさん、はなしながいんだもん。いちじかんはきらせてくれないよ。
lines.english: Well, Mom goes on forever. She won't let me hang up for at least an hour.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, kondo wa boku no denwa natteru. sora no okaasan da.
lines.ja: あ、今度は僕の電話鳴ってる。ソラのお母さんだ。
lines.kana: あ、こんどはぼくのでんわなってる。そらのおかあさんだ。
lines.english: Oh, now my phone's ringing. It's your mom.

lines.speaker: sora
