lines.romaji: e, mata kenta ni denwa kakatte kita no? denaide!
lines.ja: え、またケンタに電話かかってきたの？出ないで！
lines.kana: え、またけんたにでんわかかってきたの？でないで！
lines.english: What, she's calling you again? Don't answer!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: moshimoshi? hai, sora nara, koko ni imasu yo.
lines.ja: もしもし？はい、ソラなら、ここにいますよ。
lines.kana: もしもし？はい、そらなら、ここにいますよ。
lines.english: Hello? Yes, Sora's right here.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora's mom has important news about yesterday, so Sora calls her back and they talk for an hour.
The important thing Sora's mom calls about is just whether he's eating. Sora hangs up on her, and when she calls Kenta, Kenta tells her Sora is right there.
Sora can't reach his mom, so Kenta calls her for him and tells her Sora is busy.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Kenta passes on that Sora's mom called (okaasan kara denwa atta), and in line 3 she called Kenta's phone too. Line 5: she said it was important. Lines 8-10: when Sora finally picks up, the important thing is only whether he's eating properly (chanto gohan tabeteru?). Lines 11-13: she wants to keep talking (mada kiranaide), but Sora says he's busy and hangs up. Lines 16-18: she calls Kenta's phone again, Sora begs him not to answer (denaide), and Kenta answers and tells her Sora is right here (koko ni imasu yo). A is wrong: the important thing was just about eating, and Sora hangs up as soon as she starts on yesterday (line 12). The hour is how long he says she'd keep him (line 15). C is wrong: Kenta never calls her. She calls him (lines 3 and 16), and Sora is the one who says he's busy (line 13). Kenta says Sora is right there.

questions.english: You and Kenta are waiting for Yuki at a café, and she's late. Kenta says, "yuki, osoi ne. dou shita n darou." Offer to phone her, using denwa o kakeru.
questions.ja: ユキ、遅いね。どうしたんだろう。
questions.kana: ゆき、おそいね。どうしたんだろう。
questions.romaji: yuki, osoi ne. dou shita n darou.
questions.answer: Offer to try calling her: denwa kakete miru (let me try calling), with the person marked by ni if you name her (yuki ni denwa kakete miru). Phoning someone is denwa o kakeru, not yobu (that's calling someone over) and not iu.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto denwa kakete miru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと電話かけてみるね。
modelAnswers.english: Let me try calling her.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, yuki ni denwa kakete miyou ka.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、ユキに電話かけてみようか。
modelAnswers.english: Shall I try calling Yuki, then?

questions.explanation: In line 5 Kenta passes on 'sugu denwa kakete' (call her right away), in line 6 Sora answers 'kakete miru' (I'll try calling her), and in line 8 his mom says 'nando mo kaketa noni' (I called you so many times). kakeru is the one you do: you make the call. When a call comes to you, it's kakaru instead (line 3: kakatte kita). kakete miru, 'try calling', is the everyday way to say it when you don't know whether they'll pick up. Kenta is a friend, so a casual answer fits.

questions.english: When Sora's phone starts ringing again, what does Kenta tell him?
questions.ja: また電話が鳴りました。ケンタは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: またでんわがなりました。けんたはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mata denwa ga narimashita. kenta wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Quick, reply to it.
Quick, pick it up (off the floor).
Quick, answer it.

questions.explanation: Line 7: 'a, mata natteru yo! hayaku dete.' Picking up a phone is denwa ni deru, literally 'come out to the phone', and dete on its own means 'get the phone'. The same verb comes back in line 5 (denwa ni denai, you weren't picking up), line 8 (yatto deta, finally you picked up) and line 17 (denaide, don't answer). A is wrong: kotaeru is for answering a question (shitsumon ni kotaeru), not a phone. B is wrong: hirou is picking something up off the ground. The English 'pick up' doesn't carry over to phones.

questions.english: You've been chatting with Yuki on the phone late at night. She says, "a, mou juuniji da! sorosoro neru ne." Wrap up the call, using denwa o kiru.
questions.ja: あ、もう十二時だ！そろそろ寝るね。
questions.kana: あ、もうじゅうにじだ！そろそろねるね。
questions.romaji: a, mou juuniji da! sorosoro neru ne.
questions.answer: Say you'll hang up: jaa, kiru ne (OK, I'll hang up), then say good night. Ending a call is kiru, 'cut', not kakeru: kakeru starts a call.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, jaa kiru ne. oyasumi!
modelAnswers.ja: うん、じゃあ切るね。おやすみ！
modelAnswers.english: OK, I'll hang up then. Night!

modelAnswers.romaji: sou da ne. jaa, denwa kiru yo. mata ashita ne.
modelAnswers.ja: そうだね。じゃあ、電話切るよ。また明日ね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah. I'll hang up, then. Talk tomorrow.

questions.explanation: In line 11 Sora tries to end the call with exactly this phrase, 'jaa, kiru ne'. In line 12 his mom says 'mada kiranaide' (don't hang up yet), in line 14 Kenta says 'denwa kitchatta no?' (you hung up on her?), and in line 15 Sora says she won't let him hang up for an hour (kirasete kurenai). kakeru 'hang' makes the call, and kiru 'cut' ends it. Don't mix it up with kiru 'wear': hung up is kitta (kitchatta), wore is kita. Yuki is a friend, so stay casual.

questions.english: Kenta says, "a, mata natteru yo!" What has he noticed?
questions.ja: ケンタは、何に気がつきましたか？
questions.kana: けんたは、なににきがつきましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta wa, nani ni ki ga tsukimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora's phone is ringing again.
Someone is ringing the doorbell.
Things are turning out the same way again.

questions.explanation: Line 7: natteru is (denwa ga) natteru, the phone is ringing. Kenta says mata (again) because in line 3 he told Sora it had been ringing the whole time (zutto natteta), and in line 8 Sora's mom is on the line. In line 16 Kenta uses it again for his own phone (boku no denwa natteru). B is wrong: naru does work for a doorbell too, but the next voice is Sora's mom on the phone, not someone at the door. C reads it as naru 'become' (natteru = has become). The two are said with a different pitch, and nothing 'becomes' anything here: it's the phone.

questions.english: Sora went out and left his phone at the flat. While he was gone, Yuki called it. When he gets back, he says, "a, denwa wasureteta. nanka atta?" Tell him Yuki called, using denwa ga aru.
questions.ja: あ、電話忘れてた。なんかあった？
questions.kana: あ、でんわわすれてた。なんかあった？
questions.romaji: a, denwa wasureteta. nanka atta?
questions.answer: Pass on the call: yuki kara denwa atta yo, with the caller marked by kara. Not yuki ga denwa shita (that sounds like she phoned someone else) and not yuki ni denwa atta (that's a call for Yuki).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, yuki kara denwa atta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、ユキから電話あったよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, Yuki called.

modelAnswers.romaji: yuki kara denwa atta yo. ato de kakete hoshii tte.
modelAnswers.ja: ユキから電話あったよ。あとでかけてほしいって。
modelAnswers.english: Yuki called. She wants you to call her back later.

questions.explanation: This is what Kenta does in line 1: 'sakki, sora no okaasan kara denwa atta yo' (your mom called a little while ago). denwa ga aru reports that a call happened, to pass it on, and kara marks who called. In line 4 Sora uses ni instead (kenta ni mo denwa atta no?) because there ni marks the person the call came to. Sora is your flatmate, so a casual answer fits, and ga usually drops (denwa atta).

questions.english: Early on, Kenta tells Sora that his mom got in touch with Kenta as well. What does he say?
questions.ja: ソラのお母さんは、ケンタにも連絡しました。ケンタは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらのおかあさんは、けんたにもれんらくしました。けんたはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora no okaasan wa, kenta ni mo renraku shimashita. kenta wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I called your mom too.
choices.romaji: boku mo okaasan ni denwa kaketa

choices.english: I got called (summoned) too.
She called my phone too.
choices.romaji: boku no denwa ni mo kakatte kita

questions.explanation: Line 3: 'boku no denwa ni mo kakatte kita n da.' For a call coming in to you, the call is the subject with kakaru, and -te kuru shows it coming toward you. In line 17 Sora says it again: 'mata kenta ni denwa kakatte kita no?' (she's calling you again?). A is wrong: kaketa would mean Kenta made the call himself. He never calls her. She calls him. B is wrong: yobu means calling someone over (summoning), so yobareta means 'I was called in', not a phone call.

script.title: Two stops too far
script.setting: Saturday morning. Yuki and Mai have arranged to meet at a station at ten and go shopping. Mai came by bus through heavy traffic and is already there. She calls Yuki, who picks up on the platform of a different station further down the line.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? watashi, mou eki tsuita yo. ima doko?
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？私、もう駅着いたよ。今どこ？
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？わたし、もうえきついたよ。いまどこ？
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? I'm at the station already. Where are you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, gomen! sore ga ne, ima chigau eki ni iru no.
lines.ja: マイ、ごめん！それがね、今違う駅にいるの。
lines.kana: まい、ごめん！それがね、いまちがうえきにいるの。
lines.english: Mai, I'm so sorry! The thing is, I'm at the wrong station.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? chigau eki? nande?
lines.ja: え？違う駅？なんで？
lines.kana: え？ちがうえき？なんで？
lines.english: What? The wrong station? How come?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: densha, saisho wa kekkou kondeta n da kedo, me no mae no seki ga aite ne.
lines.ja: 電車、最初はけっこう混んでたんだけど、目の前の席が空いてね。
lines.kana: でんしゃ、さいしょはけっこうこんでたんだけど、めのまえのせきがあいてね。
lines.english: The train was pretty packed at first, but then the seat right in front of me came free.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: aa, seki aitara suwatchau yo ne. de, nechatta?
lines.ja: ああ、席空いたら座っちゃうよね。で、寝ちゃった？
lines.kana: ああ、せきあいたらすわっちゃうよね。で、ねちゃった？
lines.english: Oh, when a seat comes free you just have to sit, right? And then you fell asleep?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou na no. kimochi yokute, futaeki mo norisugoshichatta.
lines.ja: そうなの。気持ちよくて、二駅も乗り過ごしちゃった。
lines.kana: そうなの。きもちよくて、ふたえきものりすごしちゃった。
lines.english: Yep. It was so comfy that I went two whole stops past mine.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: futaeki mo? demo wakaru. watashi mo kono aida, oriru eki o norisugoshichatta.
lines.ja: 二駅も？でもわかる。私もこの間、降りる駅を乗り過ごしちゃった。
lines.kana: ふたえきも？でもわかる。わたしもこのあいだ、おりるえきをのりすごしちゃった。
lines.english: Two stops? I get it, though. I went past my stop the other day too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai wa? basu, daijoubu datta? doyoubi wa michi komu desho?
lines.ja: マイは？バス、大丈夫だった？土曜日は道混むでしょ？
lines.kana: まいは？ばす、だいじょうぶだった？どようびはみちこむでしょ？
lines.english: What about you? Was the bus OK? The roads always get busy on Saturdays, don't they?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, michi sugoku kondeta. demo hayaku uchi deta kara, maniatta.
lines.ja: うん、道すごく混んでた。でも早くうち出たから、間に合った。
lines.kana: うん、みちすごくこんでた。でもはやくうちでたから、まにあった。
lines.english: Yeah, the traffic was really heavy. But I left home early, so I made it on time.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yokatta. watashi wa densha na noni okurechatte, honto gomen.
lines.ja: よかった。私は電車なのに遅れちゃって、ほんとごめん。
lines.kana: よかった。わたしはでんしゃなのにおくれちゃって、ほんとごめん。
lines.english: Oh, good. And here I am on the train and still late. I'm so sorry.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii yo, ii yo. de, kotchi no eki ni wa nanji ni tsuku?
lines.ja: いいよ、いいよ。で、こっちの駅には何時に着く？
lines.kana: いいよ、いいよ。で、こっちのえきにはなんじにつく？
lines.english: It's fine, really. So what time will you get to the station here?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tsugi no densha de modoru kara, juuji han ni wa tsuku to omou.
lines.ja: 次の電車で戻るから、十時半には着くと思う。
lines.kana: つぎのでんしゃでもどるから、じゅうじはんにはつくとおもう。
lines.english: I'll come back on the next train, so I should be there by half past ten.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. jaa, eki no mae de matteru ne.
lines.ja: うん。じゃあ、駅の前で待ってるね。
lines.kana: うん。じゃあ、えきのまえでまってるね。
lines.english: OK. I'll wait for you out front, then.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, densha kita. suitete, seki mo ippai aiteru yo.
lines.ja: あ、電車来た。空いてて、席もいっぱい空いてるよ。
lines.kana: あ、でんしゃきた。すいてて、せきもいっぱいあいてるよ。
lines.english: Oh, here's the train. It's nearly empty, there are loads of free seats.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: dame dame, suwatcha! mata norisugoshichau yo.
lines.ja: だめだめ、座っちゃ！また乗り過ごしちゃうよ。
lines.kana: だめだめ、すわっちゃ！またのりすごしちゃうよ。
lines.english: No, no, don't sit down! You'll go past your stop again.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakatta, suwaranai. eki tsuitara, sugu renraku suru ne.
lines.ja: わかった、座らない。駅着いたら、すぐ連絡するね。
lines.kana: わかった、すわらない。えきついたら、すぐれんらくするね。
lines.english: OK, I won't sit. I'll let you know as soon as I get to the station.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kaeri wa nete mo ii yo. okoshite ageru kara.
lines.ja: 帰りは寝てもいいよ。起こしてあげるから。
lines.kana: かえりはねてもいいよ。おこしてあげるから。
lines.english: On the way home you can sleep. I'll wake you up.

questions.english: What happened?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai's bus got stuck in traffic, so Yuki is waiting for her at the station.
Yuki missed her train, so she'll take the next one and Mai will meet her at another station.
Yuki fell asleep on the train and went past her stop, so Mai, who came by bus, is the one waiting.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Mai is already at the station (mou eki tsuita yo). Lines 2-6: Yuki is at the wrong station because a seat came free, she sat down, fell asleep and went two stops past hers (futaeki mo norisugoshichatta). A swaps them: the roads were jammed (line 9), but Mai left home early and made it on time, and it's Yuki who is late (line 10). B: Yuki didn't miss a train. She rode past her stop, and she's coming back on the next train (line 12) while Mai waits outside their station (line 13).

questions.english: You're meeting Tanaka-san at the station for a work trip. He calls you: "Hello, it's Tanaka. Where are you now?" You've just got to the station. Tell him.
questions.ja: もしもし、田中です。今どこですか？
questions.kana: もしもし、たなかです。いまどこですか？
questions.romaji: moshimoshi, tanaka desu. ima doko desu ka?
questions.answer: Say you've arrived, using the past of tsuku in the polite form: ima eki ni tsukimashita.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima, eki ni tsukimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: 今、駅に着きました。
modelAnswers.english: I've just got to the station.

modelAnswers.romaji: sakki eki ni tsukimashita. ima, eki no mae ni imasu.
modelAnswers.ja: さっき駅に着きました。今、駅の前にいます。
modelAnswers.english: I got to the station a moment ago. I'm out front now.

questions.explanation: 'I'm here' is the past of tsuku: Mai opens with mou eki tsuita yo (line 1), and Yuki promises eki tsuitara, sugu renraku suru ne (line 16). To your manager, use the -masu form, tsukimashita. eki ni touchaku shimashita is correct but stiff, the language of announcements and work emails. In conversation you arrive with tsuku. Friends drop ni (eki tsuita), but keep it with Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Yuki asks how Mai's bus ride went. What does Mai say about the roads?
questions.ja: マイさんは、道について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、みちについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, michi ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: The roads were really jammed.
The roads were really busy.
The roads were really clear.

questions.explanation: Line 9: un, michi sugoku kondeta, which answers Yuki's doyoubi wa michi komu desho? (line 8). A road full of cars is konderu, the same verb as a packed train (densha ... kondeta, line 4). B, isogashikatta, is English 'busy' word for word, but isogashii is for people and their time, never a road. C, suiteta, is the opposite: clear roads. Mai only made it on time because she left home early (hayaku uchi deta kara, maniatta).

questions.english: Yuki's train back pulls in. What does she tell Mai about it?
questions.ja: 次の電車が来て、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: つぎのでんしゃがきて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tsugi no densha ga kite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It's packed, but the seat right in front of her has just come free.
It's nearly empty, with lots of free seats.
It's packed, so she'll have to stand all the way.

questions.explanation: Line 14: suitete, seki mo ippai aiteru yo. aiteru is about seats: a seat that has come free (seki ga aku). suiteru is about the whole train: it isn't crowded. Together they mean an empty train with plenty of free seats, which is why Mai cries dame dame, suwatcha! (line 15). A mixes this up with line 4, the crowded train on the way there, where one seat (me no mae no seki) came free. C would be konderu, which is how the first train was, not this one.

questions.english: You're meeting Kenta, but you fell asleep on the train and went one stop past your station. When you call him, he says: "What happened? You're late." Tell him what happened.
questions.ja: どうしたの？遅いね。
questions.kana: どうしたの？おそいね。
questions.romaji: dou shita no? osoi ne.
questions.answer: Apologise and say you rode past your stop, with norisugoshita or norisugoshichatta: gomen, nechatte, hitoeki norisugoshichatta.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen! nechatte, hitoeki norisugoshichatta.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん！寝ちゃって、一駅乗り過ごしちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry! I fell asleep and went one stop too far.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen ne. oriru eki o norisugoshichatte, ima modotteru tokoro.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんね。降りる駅を乗り過ごしちゃって、今戻ってるところ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry. I went past my stop, and I'm on my way back now.

questions.explanation: Riding past your stop is norisugosu (noru 'ride' + sugosu 'let go by'), nearly always in the past. Yuki's futaeki mo norisugoshichatta (line 6) counts how far she went in stops, and Mai's oriru eki o norisugoshichatta (line 7) names the stop with o, not the ni of eki ni tsuku. Not eki o nogashita: nogasu is for a train that left without you. misu shita doesn't work for a stop either.

newWords.english: right in front of you (me = eyes)
two stops, two stations (hitoeki = one stop)
(a train, road or shop) is empty, not crowded; the opposite of konderu

script.title: Booked all week
script.setting: Monday morning at the office. Mai comes in to find her manager, Tanaka-san, already at his desk. He wants to take the team out to eat one evening this week.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. tanaka-san, kyou mo asa hayai desu ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます。田中さん、今日も朝早いですね。
lines.kana: おはようございます。たなかさん、きょうもあさはやいですね。
lines.english: Good morning, Tanaka-san. You're in early again today.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. kimura-san, konshuu, minna de gohan ni ikimasen ka? kyou no yoru wa dou desu ka?
lines.ja: おはようございます。木村さん、今週、みんなでごはんに行きませんか？今日の夜はどうですか？
lines.kana: おはようございます。きむらさん、こんしゅう、みんなでごはんにいきませんか？きょうのよるはどうですか？
lines.english: Morning. Kimura-san, how about we all go out to eat this week? How's tonight?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii desu ne! a, demo kyou wa chotto youji ga atte...
lines.ja: いいですね！あ、でも今日はちょっと用事があって…
lines.kana: いいですね！あ、でもきょうはちょっとようじがあって…
lines.english: Sounds great! Oh, but I've got something on today, so...

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. jaa, ashita wa dou desu ka?
lines.ja: そうですか。じゃあ、明日はどうですか？
lines.kana: そうですか。じゃあ、あしたはどうですか？
lines.english: I see. Then how about tomorrow?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ashita wa... suiyoubi no asa ga hayai n desu. rokuji no densha ni noru node.
lines.ja: 明日は…水曜日の朝が早いんです。六時の電車に乗るので。
lines.kana: あしたは…すいようびのあさがはやいんです。ろくじのでんしゃにのるので。
lines.english: Tomorrow's... I've got an early start on Wednesday. I'm catching the six o'clock train.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: rokuji desu ka! jaa, suiyoubi ka mokuyoubi wa?
lines.ja: 六時ですか！じゃあ、水曜日か木曜日は？
lines.kana: ろくじですか！じゃあ、すいようびかもくようびは？
lines.english: Six! Then Wednesday or Thursday?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sumimasen, suiyoubi mo mokuyoubi mo, mou yotei ga haitte iru n desu.
lines.ja: すみません、水曜日も木曜日も、もう予定が入っているんです。
lines.kana: すみません、すいようびももくようびも、もうよていがはいっているんです。
lines.english: Sorry, Wednesday and Thursday are both booked already.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jaa, kin'youbi wa? tsugi no hi wa doyoubi desu kara, asa mo yukkuri dekimasu yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、金曜日は？次の日は土曜日ですから、朝もゆっくりできますよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、きんようびは？つぎのひはどようびですから、あさもゆっくりできますよ。
lines.english: Friday, then? The next day's Saturday, so you can take it easy in the morning.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kin'youbi wa... sumimasen, sen'yaku ga atte...
lines.ja: 金曜日は…すみません、先約があって…
lines.kana: きんようびは…すみません、せんやくがあって…
lines.english: Friday... I'm sorry, I already have plans that day...

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san... watashi to gohan, iya na n desu ka?
lines.ja: 木村さん…私とごはん、嫌なんですか？
lines.kana: きむらさん…わたしとごはん、いやなんですか？
lines.english: Kimura-san... do you just not want to eat with me?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: chigaimasu yo! kyou no youji mo, kin'youbi no sen'yaku mo, honto ni aru n desu!
lines.ja: 違いますよ！今日の用事も、金曜日の先約も、ほんとにあるんです！
lines.kana: ちがいますよ！きょうのようじも、きんようびのせんやくも、ほんとにあるんです！
lines.english: No, that's not it! Today's thing and Friday's plans are both real!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sumimasen, joudan desu yo. sen'yaku ga aru nara, sotchi ga saki desu ne.
lines.ja: すみません、冗談ですよ。先約があるなら、そっちが先ですね。
lines.kana: すみません、じょうだんですよ。せんやくがあるなら、そっちがさきですね。
lines.english: Sorry, I'm only joking. If you made plans first, those come first.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kin'youbi wa, yuki-san to karaoke ni iku n desu. tanaka-san mo issho ni dou desu ka?
lines.ja: 金曜日は、ユキさんとカラオケに行くんです。田中さんも一緒にどうですか？
lines.kana: きんようびは、ゆきさんとからおけにいくんです。たなかさんもいっしょにどうですか？
lines.english: On Friday, Yuki-san and I are going to karaoke. Why don't you come too, Tanaka-san?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: e, ii n desu ka? kin'youbi no yoru wa, mada yotei wa haitte imasen yo.
lines.ja: え、いいんですか？金曜日の夜は、まだ予定は入っていませんよ。
lines.kana: え、いいんですか？きんようびのよるは、まだよていははいっていませんよ。
lines.english: Oh, are you sure? Nothing's booked for my Friday night yet.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yokatta! jaa, yuki-san ni renraku shimasu ne.
lines.ja: よかった！じゃあ、ユキさんに連絡しますね。
lines.kana: よかった！じゃあ、ゆきさんにれんらくしますね。
lines.english: Great! I'll let Yuki-san know, then.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: onegai shimasu. a, demo watashi wa ichijikan dake ni shimasu ne. doyoubi no asa ga hayai node.
lines.ja: お願いします。あ、でも私は一時間だけにしますね。土曜日の朝が早いので。
lines.kana: おねがいします。あ、でもわたしはいちじかんだけにしますね。どようびのあさがはやいので。
lines.english: Please do. Oh, but I'll only stay an hour. I've got an early start on Saturday.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? tsugi no hi wa doyoubi da kara, asa mo yukkuri dekiru tte...
lines.ja: え？次の日は土曜日だから、朝もゆっくりできるって…
lines.kana: え？つぎのひはどようびだから、あさもゆっくりできるって…
lines.english: What? But you said the next day's Saturday, so we could take it easy in the morning...

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sore wa kimura-san no hanashi desu yo. watashi wa mainichi asa ga hayai n desu.
lines.ja: それは木村さんの話ですよ。私は毎日朝が早いんです。
lines.kana: それはきむらさんのはなしですよ。わたしはまいにちあさがはやいんです。
lines.english: That was about you. Me, I'm up early every day.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai doesn't really want to eat with Tanaka-san, so she makes up an excuse for every day he suggests.
Mai is free on Friday, but Tanaka-san has an early start on Saturday, so they put the dinner off.
Mai can't make any evening Tanaka-san suggests, so she invites him along to her Friday karaoke with Yuki.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Tanaka-san wants everyone to go out to eat this week. Mai can't do tonight (line 3: youji ga atte...), tomorrow (line 5: she has an early start on Wednesday), Wednesday or Thursday (line 7: already booked) or Friday (line 9: sen'yaku ga atte...). Line 13: her Friday plan is karaoke with Yuki, and she asks Tanaka-san to come too. In line 14 he says his Friday night is free. A is wrong: Tanaka-san only jokes that she doesn't want to eat with him (line 10), he says it was a joke (line 12), and Mai says her reasons are all real (line 11). B is wrong: Friday is the day Mai already has plans (line 9), and Tanaka-san's early Saturday only means he'll stay an hour at the karaoke (line 16).

questions.english: Yuki asks you, "kyou, shigoto owattara, gohan ikanai?" (Want to grab dinner after work today?) You can't make it. Turn her down the usual vague way, without saying what you're doing.
questions.ja: 今日、仕事終わったら、ごはん行かない？
questions.kana: きょう、しごとおわったら、ごはんいかない？
questions.romaji: kyou, shigoto owattara, gohan ikanai?
questions.answer: Give the vague reason with youji and aru, and let it trail off: gomen, kyou wa chotto youji ga atte...

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou wa chotto youji ga atte...
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日はちょっと用事があって…
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got something on today, so...

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen! kyou wa youji ga aru n da. mata kondo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん！今日は用事があるんだ。また今度ね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry! I've got something to do today. Next time, okay?

questions.explanation: Having something to do takes aru: Mai turns down tonight with kyou wa chotto youji ga atte... (line 3), and later insists kyou no youji mo... honto ni aru n desu (line 11). Don't say youji o motte iru: English 'have' points to motsu, but errands and things on are aru. Stopping after atte... is the polite part: the 'so I can't' is left unsaid, and nobody asks what the youji is. If something has just come up, the verb is dekiru: kyuu ni youji ga dekichatte, not okichatte. Yuki is a friend, so both answers are casual; with Tanaka-san it would be youji ga aru n desu.

questions.english: When Tanaka-san suggests tomorrow evening, why is that no good for Mai?
questions.ja: 木村さんは、明日の夜、どうしてだめなんですか？
questions.kana: きむらさんは、あしたのよる、どうしてだめなんですか？
questions.romaji: kimura-san wa, ashita no yoru, doushite dame na n desu ka?

choices.english: She has to be up early on Wednesday to catch a six o'clock train.
She has to leave work early tomorrow to catch a six o'clock train.
She gets in early every day, like Tanaka-san, so she's too tired in the evenings.

questions.explanation: Line 5: suiyoubi no asa ga hayai n desu. asa ga hayai makes the morning the subject: Wednesday's morning starts early, because she's catching the six o'clock train (rokuji no densha ni noru node). A late dinner on Tuesday night would clash with that. B is wrong: the train is at six in the morning (asa), not six in the evening, and she says nothing about leaving work early. C mixes it up with line 1, where Mai says kyou mo asa hayai desu ne to Tanaka-san: he's the one who is in early every day (line 18: watashi wa mainichi asa ga hayai n desu).

questions.english: When Tanaka-san asks about Wednesday or Thursday, what does Mai say?
questions.ja: 木村さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: きむらさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kimura-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I already have plans on both Wednesday and Thursday (with motsu, 'hold').
choices.romaji: suiyoubi mo mokuyoubi mo, mou yotei o motte iru n desu.

choices.english: Wednesday and Thursday are both booked already.
choices.romaji: suiyoubi mo mokuyoubi mo, mou yotei ga haitte iru n desu.

choices.english: Things came up on both Wednesday and Thursday (with okiru, 'happen').
choices.romaji: suiyoubi mo mokuyoubi mo, yotei ga okite shimatta n desu.

questions.explanation: Line 7: mou yotei ga haitte iru n desu. Plans go into a day (hairu), and haitte iru says the day is already taken. Tanaka-san uses the same verb in line 14 when he finds his Friday free (mada yotei wa haitte imasen). A is 'have plans' word for word: motsu is holding or carrying something, and plans never take motsu. Plain 'I have plans' is yotei ga aru. C uses okiru for 'come up', but okiru is for things that happen, like an accident or an earthquake, so it sounds as if something went wrong. A plan that comes up suddenly is kyuu ni yotei ga haitta.

questions.english: Satou-san, your elderly neighbour, invites you: "nichiyoubi, uchi de ocha demo dou desu ka?" (Would you like to come over for tea on Sunday?) You've already promised Sunday to someone else. Turn him down politely.
questions.ja: 日曜日、うちでお茶でもどうですか？
questions.kana: にちようび、うちでおちゃでもどうですか？
questions.romaji: nichiyoubi, uchi de ocha demo dou desu ka?
questions.answer: Turn it down with sen'yaku ga aru and let it trail off: sumimasen, nichiyoubi wa sen'yaku ga atte...

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, nichiyoubi wa sen'yaku ga atte...
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、日曜日は先約があって…
modelAnswers.english: I'm sorry, I already have plans on Sunday...

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. demo, sono hi wa sen'yaku ga aru n desu. mata kondo, onegai shimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、その日は先約があるんです。また今度、お願いします。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. But I already have plans that day. Another time, please.

questions.explanation: sen'yaku is a plan made earlier, usually with someone else, and like youji it takes aru. Mai uses it to turn down her manager in line 9 (kin'youbi wa... sumimasen, sen'yaku ga atte...), and Tanaka-san accepts it at once in line 12 (sen'yaku ga aru nara, sotchi ga saki desu ne: plans made first come first). That's why it suits an older neighbour: yotei ga aru also works but is vaguer, while sen'yaku tells him the day was promised first. Let it trail after atte..., or soften it with ...n desu; a flat ...kara sounds like an excuse. Never sen'yaku o motte imasu.

newWords.english: day (tsugi no hi = the next day)

script.title: Mum tidies up
script.setting: Saturday morning at Yuki's small flat in the city. Her mum has come to stay for the weekend, and two bags of rubbish are sitting by the front door. Partway through, Yuki heads out to the shops and comes back an hour later.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: okaasan, douzo. gomen ne, heya chirakatteru kedo.
lines.ja: お母さん、どうぞ。ごめんね、部屋散らかってるけど。
lines.kana: おかあさん、どうぞ。ごめんね、へやちらかってるけど。
lines.english: Come on in, Mum. Sorry, the place is a mess.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kono heya, itsu kite mo chirakatteru wa ne. kore, nani? gomi?
lines.ja: この部屋、いつ来ても散らかってるわね。これ、何？ゴミ？
lines.kana: このへや、いつきてもちらかってるわね。これ、なに？ごみ？
lines.english: This room's a mess every time I come. And what's this? Rubbish?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. kinou wa asa ga hayakute, gomi dasu no wasurechatta.
lines.ja: うん。昨日は朝が早くて、ゴミ出すの忘れちゃった。
lines.kana: うん。きのうはあさがはやくて、ごみだすのわすれちゃった。
lines.english: Yeah. I had an early start yesterday and forgot to put the rubbish out.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mou. shigoto ga isogashii no wa wakaru kedo, heya gurai katazukenasai.
lines.ja: もう。仕事が忙しいのはわかるけど、部屋ぐらい片付けなさい。
lines.kana: もう。しごとがいそがしいのはわかるけど、へやぐらいかたづけなさい。
lines.english: Honestly. I know work's busy, but you could at least tidy your room.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakatteru yo. demo, kitanaku wa nai desho? chotto chirakatteru dake.
lines.ja: わかってるよ。でも、汚くはないでしょ？ちょっと散らかってるだけ。
lines.kana: わかってるよ。でも、きたなくはないでしょ？ちょっとちらかってるだけ。
lines.english: I know. But it's not dirty, is it? It's just a bit messy.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: tsukatta mono o moto ni modosanai kara, chirakaru no yo.
lines.ja: 使ったものを元に戻さないから、散らかるのよ。
lines.kana: つかったものをもとにもどさないから、ちらかるのよ。
lines.english: You never put things back after you use them. That's why it gets messy.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai hai. kaimono ni itte kitara, heya katazukeru kara.
lines.ja: はいはい。買い物に行ってきたら、部屋片付けるから。
lines.kana: はいはい。かいものにいってきたら、へやかたづけるから。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. I'll tidy my room when I get back from the shops.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ii wa yo. watashi ga katazuketoku kara, itte kinasai.
lines.ja: いいわよ。私が片付けとくから、行ってきなさい。
lines.kana: いいわよ。わたしがかたづけとくから、いってきなさい。
lines.english: Don't worry, I'll tidy up while you're out. Off you go.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto? jaa, gomi wa sutete ii kedo, hoka no mono wa sutenaide ne. itte kuru!
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、ゴミは捨てていいけど、ほかのものは捨てないでね。行ってくる！
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、ごみはすてていいけど、ほかのものはすてないでね。いってくる！
lines.english: Really? Then you can throw away the rubbish, but don't throw out anything else, OK? See you in a bit!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tadaima! e, sugoi! heya, katazuketa dake ja nakute, souji mo shita no?
lines.ja: ただいま！え、すごい！部屋、片付けただけじゃなくて、掃除もしたの？
lines.kana: ただいま！え、すごい！へや、かたづけただけじゃなくて、そうじもしたの？
lines.english: I'm home! Wow, amazing! You didn't just tidy the room, you cleaned it too?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou yo. gomi wa zenbu sutete, fuku mo hon mo moto ni modoshita wa.
lines.ja: そうよ。ゴミは全部捨てて、服も本も元に戻したわ。
lines.kana: そうよ。ごみはぜんぶすてて、ふくもほんももとにもどしたわ。
lines.english: That's right. I threw all the rubbish away, and put your clothes and books back where they go.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou! are? koko ni atta gomi wa?
lines.ja: ありがとう！あれ？ここにあったゴミは？
lines.kana: ありがとう！あれ？ここにあったごみは？
lines.english: Thank you! Huh? Where's the rubbish that was here?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: aa, ano gomi nara, dashitoita wa yo.
lines.ja: ああ、あのゴミなら、出しといたわよ。
lines.kana: ああ、あのごみなら、だしといたわよ。
lines.english: Oh, that rubbish? I put it out for collection.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, gomi dashichatta no? kyou, doyoubi da yo!
lines.ja: え、ゴミ出しちゃったの？今日、土曜日だよ！
lines.kana: え、ごみだしちゃったの？きょう、どようびだよ！
lines.english: What, you put the rubbish out? It's Saturday today!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e? datte, gomi wa sutete ii tte itta ja nai.
lines.ja: え？だって、ゴミは捨てていいって言ったじゃない。
lines.kana: え？だって、ごみはすてていいっていったじゃない。
lines.english: What? But you said I could throw the rubbish away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore wa heya no gomi no koto! koko wa, gomi wa kayoubi to kin'youbi shika dasenai no.
lines.ja: それは部屋のゴミのこと！ここは、ゴミは火曜日と金曜日しか出せないの。
lines.kana: それはへやのごみのこと！ここは、ごみはかようびときんようびしかだせないの。
lines.english: I meant the rubbish in the room! Round here, rubbish can only go out on Tuesdays and Fridays.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou na no? gomen ne. jaa, sugu totte kuru wa.
lines.ja: そうなの？ごめんね。じゃあ、すぐ取ってくるわ。
lines.kana: そうなの？ごめんね。じゃあ、すぐとってくるわ。
lines.english: Oh, is that so? Sorry. I'll go and get it right away, then.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. dashita mono wa, moto ni modoshite ne.
lines.ja: うん。出したものは、元に戻してね。
lines.kana: うん。だしたものは、もとにもどしてね。
lines.english: Okay. Whatever you take out, put it back where it was!

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mum tidies the flat but throws out some of Yuki's things by mistake, so she has to go and get them back.
Mum tidies the flat and puts the rubbish out, but it isn't a collection day, so she has to go and get it back.
Yuki forgot to put the rubbish out, so Mum puts it out for her on the right day and tidies the flat too.

questions.explanation: In line 8 Mum offers to tidy while Yuki goes shopping, and in line 9 Yuki says she can throw away the rubbish but nothing else. When Yuki gets back (lines 10-11) the room is tidy and clean. But in line 13 Mum says she put the rubbish out (dashitoita), and Yuki points out that it's Saturday (line 14): rubbish only goes out on Tuesdays and Fridays (line 16). In line 17 Mum says she'll go and get it (totte kuru). A is wrong: Mum threw away only the rubbish in the room and put the clothes and books back (line 11). None of Yuki's things were thrown out by mistake. C is wrong: Yuki did forget to put the rubbish out (line 3), but Mum put it out on a Saturday, which is the wrong day.

questions.english: Before she heads out to the shops, Yuki tells Mum what she can do with the rubbish. What did Yuki say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、買い物に行く前に、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、かいものにいくまえに、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, kaimono ni iku mae ni, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: you can put the rubbish out (for collection), but...
you can toss the rubbish (through the air), but...
you can throw the rubbish away, but...

questions.explanation: Line 9: 'gomi wa sutete ii kedo, hoka no mono wa sutenaide ne' (you can throw away the rubbish, but don't throw out anything else). suteru is getting rid of something. Yuki meant the rubbish lying around the room (line 16: sore wa heya no gomi no koto), and Mum quotes her in line 15. A is wrong: gomi o dasu is putting the bags out for collection. If Yuki had said that, Mum would have been right to put the bags out, and Yuki couldn't complain in lines 14-16. B is wrong: nageru is throwing through the air, like a ball. gomi o nageru means throwing rubbish away only in Hokkaido and Tohoku dialect.

questions.english: Yuki asks where the rubbish by the door has gone, and Mum says, "ano gomi nara, dashitoita wa yo." What had Mum done with it?
questions.ja: お母さんは、ゴミをどうしましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、ごみをどうしましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, gomi o dou shimashita ka?

choices.english: She'd put the bags out at the collection point to be picked up.
She'd gone through the bags and taken out anything that wasn't rubbish.
She'd emptied the bags into the bin in the kitchen.

questions.explanation: Line 13: gomi o dasu is putting rubbish out for collection, and -toita (-te oita) means she did it for Yuki ahead of time. That's why Yuki says 'kyou, doyoubi da yo!' (line 14): here rubbish can only go out on Tuesdays and Fridays (line 16). Yuki uses the same phrase in line 3 for what she forgot to do yesterday. B is wrong: dasu on its own can mean 'take something out', but with gomi it's the collection chore, and Yuki's complaint is about the day, not about anything missing. C is wrong: putting rubbish in a bin is gomi o suteru, which is what Mum did with the rubbish in the room (line 11). The bags by the door went out.

questions.english: Mum calls the evening before a visit: "ashita, sotchi ni iku kedo, heya daijoubu?" Tell her you'll tidy your room tonight.
questions.ja: 明日、そっちに行くけど、部屋大丈夫？
questions.kana: あした、そっちにいくけど、へやだいじょうぶ？
questions.romaji: ashita, sotchi ni iku kedo, heya daijoubu?
questions.answer: Say you'll tidy up tonight with katazukeru: heya katazukeru (o drops in casual speech), or katazuketoku to get it done before she arrives. katazukeru is putting things away; souji suru would be cleaning (vacuuming and wiping).

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu. konban, heya katazukeru kara.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫。今晩、部屋片付けるから。
modelAnswers.english: It's fine. I'll tidy my room tonight.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima chotto chirakatteru kedo, konban katazuketoku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 今ちょっと散らかってるけど、今晩片付けとくね。
modelAnswers.english: It's a bit of a mess right now, but I'll tidy up tonight.

questions.explanation: Mum's nag in line 4 is 'heya gurai katazukenasai', and Yuki answers 'heya katazukeru kara' (line 7). In line 8 Mum offers 'watashi ga katazuketoku kara', the -toku form for getting it done ahead. In line 10 Yuki sets katazukeru (putting things away) against souji (cleaning): 'katazuketa dake ja nakute, souji mo shita no?'. A messy room needs katazukeru; souji suru is for a dirty one. You're talking to your mum, so casual is right.

questions.english: Yuki calls you: "ima kara, sotchi ni asobi ni itte mo ii?" Say yes, but warn her that your place is a mess.
questions.ja: 今から、そっちに遊びに行ってもいい？
questions.kana: いまから、そっちにあそびにいってもいい？
questions.romaji: ima kara, sotchi ni asobi ni itte mo ii?
questions.answer: Say yes and warn her with the state form chirakatteru: heya chirakatteru kedo (ga drops in casual speech). Don't say kitanai, which says it's dirty.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo! demo, heya chirakatteru kedo, gomen ne.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ！でも、部屋散らかってるけど、ごめんね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure! My place is a mess, though. Sorry.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kite kite. heya sugoku chirakatteru kedo, ki ni shinaide ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、来て来て。部屋すごく散らかってるけど、気にしないでね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, come over! My place is a real mess, but don't mind it.

questions.explanation: Yuki opens the door to Mum with exactly this host's apology in line 1: 'gomen ne, heya chirakatteru kedo'. Use the -teru form: chirakatteru is the state, with stuff lying everywhere. In line 5 Yuki says her room isn't kitanai (dirty), only chirakatteru (messy). kitanai is blunter and says it's dirty. Yuki asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Mum is staying at your place and takes a book off your shelf: "kono hon, chotto yonde mo ii?" Say yes, and ask her to put it back afterwards.
questions.ja: この本、ちょっと読んでもいい？
questions.kana: このほん、ちょっとよんでもいい？
questions.romaji: kono hon, chotto yonde mo ii?
questions.answer: Say yes and ask her to put it back where it was: moto ni modoshite (ne). The putting-back verb is modosu; modoru is something (or someone) going back by itself.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. yondara, moto ni modoshite ne.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。読んだら、元に戻してね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. Put it back when you're done.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, douzo. demo, ato de chanto moto ni modoshite ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、どうぞ。でも、後でちゃんと元に戻してね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, go ahead. But put it back properly afterwards, OK?

questions.explanation: In line 6 Mum says Yuki's room gets messy because she doesn't put things back: 'tsukatta mono o moto ni modosanai kara'. In line 18 Yuki turns it on her: 'dashita mono wa, moto ni modoshite ne' (whatever you take out, put back), since Mum put the rubbish out. Don't say moto ni modotte, which would tell Mum herself to go back. kaeshite (give it back) is for returning something to its owner; here you want the book back on the shelf.

newWords.english: dirty (kitanaku wa nai: it's not dirty)
cleaning: vacuuming, wiping, dusting (souji suru: clean)
take, pick up (totte kuru: go and get)
at least, if nothing else (heya gurai: at least your room)
do ...! (a parent's firm order: katazukenasai, itte kinasai)

script.title: One more favour
script.setting: Late on a school night at Yuki's flat. Her little brother Kenji turns up at the door without warning, looking glum. Later their mother comes on the phone.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, kenji? nande koko ni iru no? mou konna jikan da yo.
lines.ja: え、ケンジ？なんでここにいるの？もうこんな時間だよ。
lines.kana: え、けんじ？なんでここにいるの？もうこんなじかんだよ。
lines.english: Kenji? What are you doing here? It's so late!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: neechan, gomen. chotto onegai ga aru n da kedo.
lines.ja: 姉ちゃん、ごめん。ちょっとお願いがあるんだけど。
lines.kana: ねえちゃん、ごめん。ちょっとおねがいがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Sorry, sis. There's something I need to ask you.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: dou shita no? nanka genki nai jan.
lines.ja: どうしたの？なんか元気ないじゃん。
lines.kana: どうしたの？なんかげんきないじゃん。
lines.english: What's wrong? You seem kind of down.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shiken, zenbu dame datta. uchi ni kaeritakunakute.
lines.ja: 試験、全部ダメだった。うちに帰りたくなくて。
lines.kana: しけん、ぜんぶだめだった。うちにかえりたくなくて。
lines.english: My exams all went badly. I didn't want to go home.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sokka. de, onegai tte?
lines.ja: そっか。で、お願いって？
lines.kana: そっか。で、おねがいって？
lines.english: I see. So what's the favour?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: neechan ni meiwaku kakeru no wa wakatteru kedo, konban, tomete kurenai?
lines.ja: 姉ちゃんに迷惑かけるのはわかってるけど、今晩、泊めてくれない？
lines.kana: ねえちゃんにめいわくかけるのはわかってるけど、こんばん、とめてくれない？
lines.english: I know I'm putting you out, but can I stay at yours tonight?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii kedo, okaasan ni wa renraku shita no?
lines.ja: いいけど、お母さんには連絡したの？
lines.kana: いいけど、おかあさんにはれんらくしたの？
lines.english: Sure, but did you tell Mom?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shitenai. sumaho, uchi ni wasurechatta.
lines.ja: してない。スマホ、うちに忘れちゃった。
lines.kana: してない。すまほ、うちにわすれちゃった。
lines.english: No. I left my phone at home.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e! okaasan, zettai shinpai shiteru yo.
lines.ja: え！お母さん、絶対心配してるよ。
lines.kana: え！おかあさん、ぜったいしんぱいしてるよ。
lines.english: What? Mom must be worried sick!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: dakara, mou hitotsu onegai ga aru n da. neechan kara denwa kakete kurenai?
lines.ja: だから、もう一つお願いがあるんだ。姉ちゃんから電話かけてくれない？
lines.kana: だから、もうひとつおねがいがあるんだ。ねえちゃんからでんわかけてくれない？
lines.english: That's why I've got one more favour. Could you call her for me?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakatta. moshimoshi, okaasan? kenji, ima watashi no tokoro ni iru yo.
lines.ja: わかった。もしもし、お母さん？ケンジ、今私のところにいるよ。
lines.kana: わかった。もしもし、おかあさん？けんじ、いまわたしのところにいるよ。
lines.english: Okay. Hello, Mom? Kenji's here at my place.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: aa, yokatta. renraku mo nai kara, honto ni shinpai shita no yo.
lines.ja: ああ、よかった。連絡もないから、ほんとに心配したのよ。
lines.kana: ああ、よかった。れんらくもないから、ほんとにしんぱいしたのよ。
lines.english: Oh, thank goodness. Not a word from him, I was so worried.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, okaasan? shinpai kakete gomen. shiken, dame datta n da.
lines.ja: もしもし、お母さん？心配かけてごめん。試験、ダメだったんだ。
lines.kana: もしもし、おかあさん？しんぱいかけてごめん。しけん、だめだったんだ。
lines.english: Hello, Mom? Sorry I worried you. My exams went badly.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shiken no koto wa ii no. tsugi ganbareba ii n da kara, genki dashite.
lines.ja: 試験のことはいいの。次がんばればいいんだから、元気出して。
lines.kana: しけんのことはいいの。つぎがんばればいいんだから、げんきだして。
lines.english: Forget about the exams. You can just try harder next time, so cheer up.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: neechan, meiwaku kakete gomen ne.
lines.ja: 姉ちゃん、迷惑かけてごめんね。
lines.kana: ねえちゃん、めいわくかけてごめんね。
lines.english: Sis, sorry for all the trouble.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii yo. demo, mou okaasan ni shinpai kakecha dame da yo.
lines.ja: いいよ。でも、もうお母さんに心配かけちゃダメだよ。
lines.kana: いいよ。でも、もうおかあさんにしんぱいかけちゃだめだよ。
lines.english: It's fine. But don't make Mom worry like that again.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ato hitotsu dake, onegai ga aru n da kedo. ashita, issho ni uchi ni kaette kurenai?
lines.ja: あと一つだけ、お願いがあるんだけど。明日、一緒にうちに帰ってくれない？
lines.kana: あとひとつだけ、おねがいがあるんだけど。あした、いっしょにうちにかえってくれない？
lines.english: There's just one more thing I need to ask. Will you come home with me tomorrow?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mada aru no? hai hai, sono onegai mo kiite ageru kara, genki dashite.
lines.ja: まだあるの？はいはい、そのお願いも聞いてあげるから、元気出して。
lines.kana: まだあるの？はいはい、そのおねがいもきいてあげるから、げんきだして。
lines.english: There's more? Okay, okay, I'll do that one too, so cheer up.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji missed the last train, so Yuki lets him stay and keeps it from their mother.
Their mother is angry about Kenji's exams, so Yuki phones her to calm her down.
Kenji turns up after bad exams, and Yuki phones their mother, who was only worried.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenji's exams went badly and he didn't want to go home, so in line 6 he asks to stay the night. He left his phone at home (line 8), so in line 10 he asks Yuki to call their mother. Mom is relieved (line 12: aa, yokatta) and tells him to forget about the exams (line 14: shiken no koto wa ii no). A is wrong: nobody mentions the last train. Kenji came because he didn't want to go home, and Yuki phones their mother instead of keeping it from her. B is wrong: Yuki does phone her, but Mom isn't angry. She was worried (line 12) and says never mind the exams (line 14).

questions.english: Near the end, Kenji says, "ato hitotsu dake, onegai ga aru n da kedo." What happens?
questions.ja: 最後に、何がありましたか？
questions.kana: さいごに、なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: saigo ni, nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji asks Yuki to go home with him tomorrow, and she says yes.
Kenji offers to do Yuki a favour tomorrow, to make up for tonight.
Kenji asks Yuki to call their mother again, but she says no.

questions.explanation: Line 17: onegai ga aru opens a request, so Kenji is the one asking: ashita, issho ni uchi ni kaette kurenai? (will you come home with me tomorrow?). In line 18 Yuki says sono onegai mo kiite ageru. onegai o kiku is the other side of it, granting a favour. This is the third time Kenji says onegai ga aru (line 2 led to staying the night, line 10 to phoning Mom), which is why Yuki says mada aru no? (there's more?). B gets the direction backwards: onegai ga aru doesn't mean offering to do someone a favour, and Kenji offers nothing. C is wrong: Yuki already phoned their mother in line 11, and in the end she agrees instead of refusing.

questions.english: After the phone call, how does Kenji apologise to Yuki?
questions.ja: 電話のあと、ケンジはユキに何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: でんわのあと、けんじはゆきになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: denwa no ato, kenji wa yuki ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Sis, sorry for causing trouble (okosu, like English 'cause').
Sis, sorry for all the trouble.
Sis, sorry for being bothered (meiwaku suru).

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'neechan, meiwaku kakete gomen ne.' Trouble you cause someone is put on them with kakeru. Kenji also uses it in line 6 (meiwaku kakeru no wa wakatteru kedo: I know I'm putting you out). A is a calque of English 'cause trouble': okosu works for incidents (mondai o okosu), but meiwaku doesn't take it. C uses meiwaku suru, which describes the person being bothered, so it turns the apology around.

questions.english: Imagine you're Kenji, back home the next day. Okaasan says to you, "kenji, kinou wa honto ni shinpai shita no yo." Apologise for worrying her, using shinpai o kakeru.
questions.ja: ケンジ、昨日はほんとに心配したのよ。
questions.kana: けんじ、きのうはほんとにしんぱいしたのよ。
questions.romaji: kenji, kinou wa honto ni shinpai shita no yo.
questions.answer: Say sorry for making her worry: shinpai kakete gomen (the o drops in casual speech). She was the one who worried (shinpai shita), and you put the worry on her with kakeru.

modelAnswers.romaji: shinpai kakete gomen. kondo kara chanto renraku suru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 心配かけてごめん。今度からちゃんと連絡するよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry I worried you. From now on I'll let you know.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen ne, shinpai kakechatte. sumaho, uchi ni wasurechatta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんね、心配かけちゃって。スマホ、うちに忘れちゃったんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry for making you worry. I'd left my phone at home.

questions.explanation: Kenji says this to Mom on the phone (line 13: shinpai kakete gomen), and Yuki warns him in line 16 (mou okaasan ni shinpai kakecha dame da yo). Notice who does what. Mom says shinpai shita (line 12) and Yuki says okaasan, zettai shinpai shiteru yo (line 9), because Mom is the one worrying. When you're the cause, you put the worry on her with kakeru. 'shinpai shite gomen' would mean you were the one worrying, which makes no sense here. She's your mother, so casual speech fits. With someone like Tanaka-san you'd say shinpai o kakete sumimasen.

questions.english: Imagine you're Yuki. A week later, Kenji mumbles, "neechan, mata shiken dame datta." He's clearly down. Cheer him up using genki o dasu.
questions.ja: 姉ちゃん、また試験ダメだった。
questions.kana: ねえちゃん、またしけんだめだった。
questions.romaji: neechan, mata shiken dame datta.
questions.answer: Tell him to cheer up: genki dashite (the o drops in casual speech). You can soften it with daijoubu da yo, or add that there's always next time. Don't lead with ganbatte, which tells him to keep trying when what he needs is to feel better.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu da yo, genki dashite. tsugi ga aru jan.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫だよ、元気出して。次があるじゃん。
modelAnswers.english: It's okay, cheer up. There's always next time.

modelAnswers.romaji: sokka. maa, genki dashite. nanka oishii mono demo tabe ni iku?
modelAnswers.ja: そっか。まあ、元気出して。なんかおいしいものでも食べに行く？
modelAnswers.english: I see. Well, cheer up. Want to go get something nice to eat?

questions.explanation: Mom (line 14) and Yuki (line 18) both say genki dashite to Kenji while he's down. Line 14 also lets you hear the contrast. tsugi ganbareba ii (you can just try harder next time) is about effort later, while genki dashite is about feeling better now. ganbatte on its own can feel like pressure to someone who's already low, and genki ni natte is what you say to someone who's ill (get well). Kenji is family, so casual speech fits.

newWords.english: big sis (what a younger sibling calls an older sister)
let someone stay the night (tomete kurenai?: can I stay at yours?)
try hard, hang in there (ganbareba: if you try hard)

script.title: He never left the hotel
script.setting: A Sunday afternoon outside their homes. Yuki runs into Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, wheeling a suitcase, and assumes he is just setting off.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, satou-san, konnichiwa. kore kara ryokou ni iku n desu ka?
lines.ja: あ、佐藤さん、こんにちは。これから旅行に行くんですか？
lines.kana: あ、さとうさん、こんにちは。これからりょこうにいくんですか？
lines.english: Oh, hello, Satou-san! Are you off on a trip?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: iie, ima kaette kita n desu yo. mukashi kara no tomodachi to, hokkaidou ni ryokou ni itte kimashita.
lines.ja: いいえ、今帰ってきたんですよ。昔からの友達と、北海道に旅行に行ってきました。
lines.kana: いいえ、いまかえってきたんですよ。むかしからのともだちと、ほっかいどうにりょこうにいってきました。
lines.english: No, I've just got back. I went on a trip to Hokkaido with some friends I've known for years.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hokkaidou! ii desu ne. hikouki de itta n desu ka?
lines.ja: 北海道！いいですね。飛行機で行ったんですか？
lines.kana: ほっかいどう！いいですね。ひこうきでいったんですか？
lines.english: Hokkaido! How lovely. Did you fly?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai, hisashiburi ni hikouki ni norimashita. demo, notte sugu nechatta n desu yo.
lines.ja: はい、久しぶりに飛行機に乗りました。でも、乗ってすぐ寝ちゃったんですよ。
lines.kana: はい、ひさしぶりにひこうきにのりました。でも、のってすぐねちゃったんですよ。
lines.english: Yes, my first time on a plane in ages. But I fell asleep the moment I got on.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakarimasu. watashi mo hikouki ni noru to, sugu nechau n desu.
lines.ja: わかります。私も飛行機に乗ると、すぐ寝ちゃうんです。
lines.kana: わかります。わたしもひこうきにのると、すぐねちゃうんです。
lines.english: I know the feeling. I always nod off as soon as I'm on a plane, too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sorede ne, onsen no aru hoteru ni tomatta n desu. totemo ii hoteru deshita yo.
lines.ja: それでね、温泉のあるホテルに泊まったんです。とてもいいホテルでしたよ。
lines.kana: それでね、おんせんのあるホテルにとまったんです。とてもいいホテルでしたよ。
lines.english: Anyway, we stayed at a hotel with a hot spring. It was a really lovely hotel.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii naa. onsen ni wa nando mo haitta n desu ka?
lines.ja: いいなあ。温泉には何度も入ったんですか？
lines.kana: いいなあ。おんせんにはなんどもはいったんですか？
lines.english: Lucky you. Did you get in the hot spring a lot?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai, asa mo hiru mo yoru mo. kimochi yokatta desu yo.
lines.ja: はい、朝も昼も夜も。気持ちよかったですよ。
lines.kana: はい、あさもひるもよるも。きもちよかったですよ。
lines.english: Oh yes, morning, noon and night. It felt wonderful.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hoka ni wa, doko ni itta n desu ka?
lines.ja: ほかには、どこに行ったんですか？
lines.kana: ほかには、どこにいったんですか？
lines.english: And where else did you go?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore ga ne, hoteru kara ichido mo soto ni denakatta n desu. zutto onsen ni haittemashita.
lines.ja: それがね、ホテルから一度も外に出なかったんです。ずっと温泉に入ってました。
lines.kana: それがね、ホテルからいちどもそとにでなかったんです。ずっとおんせんにはいってました。
lines.english: Well, that's the thing. I never once set foot outside the hotel. I was in the hot spring the whole time.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, ichido mo? jaa, omiyage mo kaenakatta n desu ka?
lines.ja: え、一度も？じゃあ、お土産も買えなかったんですか？
lines.kana: え、いちども？じゃあ、おみやげもかえなかったんですか？
lines.english: What, not once? So you couldn't buy any gifts to bring back either?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: omiyage wa, hoteru no naka de kaimashita yo. hai, kore, yuki-san ni.
lines.ja: お土産は、ホテルの中で買いましたよ。はい、これ、ユキさんに。
lines.kana: おみやげは、ホテルのなかでかいましたよ。はい、これ、ゆきさんに。
lines.english: Oh, I bought the gifts right there in the hotel. Here, this one's for you, Yuki.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, watashi ni desu ka? arigatou gozaimasu!
lines.ja: え、私にですか？ありがとうございます！
lines.kana: え、わたしにですか？ありがとうございます！
lines.english: What, for me? Thank you so much!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yuki-san mo ryokou ni iku nara, ano hoteru ni tomatte mite kudasai.
lines.ja: ユキさんも旅行に行くなら、あのホテルに泊まってみてください。
lines.kana: ゆきさんもりょこうにいくなら、あのホテルにとまってみてください。
lines.english: If you go on a trip yourself, Yuki, do try staying at that hotel.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai, sono hoteru ni tomatte mimasu. kondo wa watashi ga, omiyage katte kimasu ne.
lines.ja: はい、そのホテルに泊まってみます。今度は私が、お土産買ってきますね。
lines.kana: はい、そのホテルにとまってみます。こんどはわたしが、おみやげかってきますね。
lines.english: I will, I'll try that hotel. And next time, I'll be the one bringing you back a gift.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: tanoshimi ni shite imasu ne. demo, yuki-san wa, chanto soto ni mo dete kudasai ne.
lines.ja: 楽しみにしていますね。でも、ユキさんは、ちゃんと外にも出てくださいね。
lines.kana: たのしみにしていますね。でも、ゆきさんは、ちゃんとそとにもでてくださいね。
lines.english: I'll look forward to it. But you, Yuki, make sure you go outside too.

questions.english: How was Satou-san's trip?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんの旅行は、どうでしたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんのりょこうは、どうでしたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san no ryokou wa, dou deshita ka?

choices.english: He went sightseeing all over Hokkaido, so he had no time to buy gifts for anyone.
He flew to Hokkaido, slept through the flight and spent the whole stay in the hotel's hot spring, but he still brought Yuki a gift.
He is just about to fly to Hokkaido, and Yuki tells him about a hotel with a hot spring.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Yuki thinks he is setting off, but he has just got back (ima kaette kita n desu yo). Line 4: he fell asleep as soon as he got on the plane. Lines 6-10: he stayed at a hotel with a hot spring and never once went outside it (ichido mo soto ni denakatta), because he was in the hot spring the whole time. Lines 11-12: he bought gifts inside the hotel, and hands one to Yuki. A is wrong: he never left the hotel (line 10), and he did buy gifts (line 12). C is wrong: the trip is over (line 2), and it is Satou-san who tells Yuki to try the hotel (line 14), not the other way round.

questions.english: Yuki asks you, "ne, kondo no shuumatsu, nani suru no?" (Hey, what are you up to this weekend?) You're going away with some friends. Tell her you're going on a trip.
questions.ja: ね、今度の週末、何するの？
questions.kana: ね、こんどのしゅうまつ、なにするの？
questions.romaji: ne, kondo no shuumatsu, nani suru no?
questions.answer: Say you're going on a trip with ryokou ni iku: tomodachi to ryokou ni iku n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: tomodachi to ryokou ni iku n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 友達と旅行に行くんだ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm going on a trip with some friends.

modelAnswers.romaji: tomodachi to ryokou itte kuru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 友達と旅行行ってくるよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm off on a trip with some friends.

questions.explanation: You go on a trip: ryokou ni iku. Yuki asks Satou-san kore kara ryokou ni iku n desu ka? in line 1, and he answers ryokou ni itte kimashita in line 2, the shape for a trip you're back from. English 'take a trip' points to ryokou o toru, which Japanese doesn't say. In the second model, itte kuru adds 'go and come back', and casual speech drops the ni (ryokou itte kuru).

questions.english: Yuki asks Satou-san whether he flew to Hokkaido. What did he say?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Yes, I booked a flight for the first time in ages.
choices.romaji: hai, hisashiburi ni hikouki o torimashita.

choices.english: Yes, I flew by plane for the first time in ages.
choices.romaji: hai, hisashiburi ni hikouki de tobimashita.

choices.english: Yes, I went on a plane for the first time in ages.
choices.romaji: hai, hisashiburi ni hikouki ni norimashita.

questions.explanation: Line 4: hai, hisashiburi ni hikouki ni norimashita. Being on a plane takes ni noru, like every vehicle (densha ni noru), and Yuki uses it too in line 5 (hikouki ni noru to, sugu nechau). A is 'take a plane' put into Japanese, but hikouki o toru means booking a flight, not being on one. B is English 'fly': tobu is what the plane or a bird does, and people say hikouki ni noru, or hikouki de iku for how they got somewhere, as Yuki asks in line 3 (hikouki de itta n desu ka?).

questions.english: You're about to go on a trip. Satou-san asks, "hoteru wa, mou kimemashita ka?" (Have you decided on a hotel yet?) Tell him you're staying at a hotel near the station.
questions.ja: ホテルは、もう決めましたか？
questions.kana: ホテルは、もうきめましたか？
questions.romaji: hoteru wa, mou kimemashita ka?
questions.answer: Say where you'll sleep with ni tomaru: hai, eki no chikaku no hoteru ni tomarimasu.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, eki no chikaku no hoteru ni tomarimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、駅の近くのホテルに泊まります。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, I'm staying at a hotel near the station.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, eki no chikaku no hoteru ni tomaru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、駅の近くのホテルに泊まるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm staying at a hotel near the station.

questions.explanation: Staying the night somewhere is tomaru: Satou-san says onsen no aru hoteru ni tomatta n desu in line 6 and ano hoteru ni tomatte mite kudasai in line 14. Not hoteru ni iru, which only says where you are right now, and not hoteru ni yoru, which is dropping in on the way. The first model is the polite one for Satou-san; the second is the casual version for a friend like Kenta.

questions.english: When Yuki hears he never left the hotel, she asks if he couldn't buy omiyage either. What did Satou-san do about omiyage?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、お土産をどうしましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、おみやげをどうしましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, omiyage o dou shimashita ka?

choices.english: He bought gifts inside the hotel to bring home, and gives one to Yuki.
He bought one souvenir at the hotel to keep for himself.
He couldn't buy any, so he asks Yuki to pick some up for him.

questions.explanation: Line 11: Yuki asks omiyage mo kaenakatta n desu ka? Line 12: Satou-san bought them inside the hotel (hoteru no naka de kaimashita) and hands one over: hai, kore, yuki-san ni. Omiyage are gifts you bring back for other people, so the one for Yuki is exactly what omiyage are for. B is the English idea of a 'souvenir' for yourself, which is jibun-you or a keepsake (kinenhin), and he gives this one away. C is wrong: he did buy them (kaimashita). Yuki promises to bring him a gift next time (line 15), but he doesn't ask her to buy anything.

questions.english: You and Yuki are staying at an inn with a hot spring. She says, "gohan made mada jikan aru ne. dou suru?" (We've still got time before dinner. What do you want to do?) Say you'll go and soak in the hot spring.
questions.ja: ご飯までまだ時間あるね。どうする？
questions.kana: ごはんまでまだじかんあるね。どうする？
questions.romaji: gohan made mada jikan aru ne. dou suru?
questions.answer: Say you'll get into the hot spring with ni hairu, plus kuru for 'go and come back': jaa, onsen haitte kuru.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, onsen haitte kuru.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、温泉入ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: Then I'll go and have a soak in the hot spring.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, onsen ni haitte kimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、温泉に入ってきます。
modelAnswers.english: Then I'll go and have a dip in the hot spring.

questions.explanation: You get into a hot spring the way you get into a bath, with ni hairu (ofuro ni hairu). Yuki asks onsen ni wa nando mo haitta n desu ka? in line 7, and Satou-san says zutto onsen ni haittemashita in line 10. Not onsen o abiru: abiru is for showers. Onsen ni iku would be heading off to a hot-spring town, but you're already there. Casual speech drops the ni (onsen haitte kuru); the second model is the polite version, for someone like Satou-san.

newWords.english: for the first time in a long while
not even once (with a negative: ichido mo denakatta = never once went out)

script.title: Lunch on points
script.setting: Saturday lunchtime in town. Mai and Sora, who know each other through Yuki and Kenta, have spent the morning shopping together. Sora's hands are full of bags; Mai hasn't bought a thing. They stop outside a small ramen shop Sora likes.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora-kun, ippai katta ne. kyou, kekkou okane tsukatta n ja nai?
lines.ja: ソラくん、いっぱい買ったね。今日、結構お金使ったんじゃない？
lines.kana: そらくん、いっぱいかったね。きょう、けっこうおかねつかったんじゃない？
lines.english: Sora, you bought loads. You've spent quite a bit of money today, haven't you?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, kongetsu mou okane tsukaisugichatta. demo itsumo kaado tsukatte, pointo tameteru kara ii n da.
lines.ja: うん、今月もうお金使いすぎちゃった。でもいつもカード使って、ポイント貯めてるからいいんだ。
lines.kana: うん、こんげつもうおかねつかいすぎちゃった。でもいつもカードつかって、ポイントためてるからいいんだ。
lines.english: Yeah, I've already spent too much this month. But it's fine, because I always pay by card and collect the points.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, sore tte, pointo wa tameteru kedo, okane wa tamete nai jan.
lines.ja: え、それって、ポイントは貯めてるけど、お金は貯めてないじゃん。
lines.kana: え、それって、ポイントはためてるけど、おかねはためてないじゃん。
lines.english: Wait, so you're collecting points, but you're not saving any money.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: datte, kaado da to, okane tsukatteru kanji shinai n da yo ne.
lines.ja: だって、カードだと、お金使ってる感じしないんだよね。
lines.kana: だって、カードだと、おかねつかってるかんじしないんだよね。
lines.english: Well, when it's a card, it doesn't feel like I'm spending money.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sore ga abunai n da yo. watashi wa ima, ryokou no okane tameteru n da.
lines.ja: それが危ないんだよ。私は今、旅行のお金貯めてるんだ。
lines.kana: それがあぶないんだよ。わたしはいま、りょこうのおかねためてるんだ。
lines.english: That's exactly the danger. Me, I'm saving up for a trip right now.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, ryokou? doko ni iku no?
lines.ja: え、旅行？どこに行くの？
lines.kana: え、りょこう？どこにいくの？
lines.english: Oh, a trip? Where are you going?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mada kimete nai kedo, rainen, hitori de ryokou ni ikitai n da.
lines.ja: まだ決めてないけど、来年、一人で旅行に行きたいんだ。
lines.kana: まだきめてないけど、らいねん、ひとりでりょこうにいきたいんだ。
lines.english: I haven't decided yet, but next year I want to go travelling on my own.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: hitori de? sugoi naa. boku mo okane tamenakya.
lines.ja: 一人で？すごいなあ。僕もお金貯めなきゃ。
lines.kana: ひとりで？すごいなあ。ぼくもおかねためなきゃ。
lines.english: On your own? That's amazing. I need to start saving money too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, mou ichiji da. onaka suita ne.
lines.ja: あ、もう一時だ。おなかすいたね。
lines.kana: あ、もういちじだ。おなかすいたね。
lines.english: Oh, it's already one o'clock. I'm hungry, aren't you?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kono mise no raamen, oishii n da yo. a, demo koko, kaado tsukaeru kana?
lines.ja: この店のラーメン、おいしいんだよ。あ、でもここ、カード使えるかな？
lines.kana: このみせのラーメン、おいしいんだよ。あ、でもここ、カードつかえるかな？
lines.english: The ramen here is really good. Oh, but I wonder if I can pay by card here.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, koko wa genkin dake da yo. kono aida kita kedo, kaado tsukaenakatta.
lines.ja: ううん、ここは現金だけだよ。この間来たけど、カード使えなかった。
lines.kana: ううん、ここはげんきんだけだよ。このあいだきたけど、カードつかえなかった。
lines.english: No, it's cash only. I came the other day and couldn't pay by card.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, uso! genkin, sanbyaku en shika nai.
lines.ja: え、うそ！現金、三百円しかない。
lines.kana: え、うそ！げんきん、さんびゃくえんしかない。
lines.english: No way! I've only got three hundred yen in cash.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, asoko no konbini ni shiyou. konbini nara kaado tsukaeru shi.
lines.ja: じゃあ、あそこのコンビニにしよう。コンビニならカード使えるし。
lines.kana: じゃあ、あそこのコンビニにしよう。コンビニならカードつかえるし。
lines.english: Then let's go to that konbini over there instead. You can pay by card at a konbini.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sou da! kyou no gohan wa, boku ga ogoru yo. tameta pointo de.
lines.ja: そうだ！今日のご飯は、僕がおごるよ。貯めたポイントで。
lines.kana: そうだ！きょうのごはんは、ぼくがおごるよ。ためたポイントで。
lines.english: I know! Lunch is on me today. With the points I've collected.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, ii no? pointo, sonna ni aru no?
lines.ja: え、いいの？ポイント、そんなにあるの？
lines.kana: え、いいの？ポイント、そんなにあるの？
lines.english: Really? Have you got that many points?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, sanzen pointo aru yo. hora, pointo tameru no mo daiji desho?
lines.ja: うん、三千ポイントあるよ。ほら、ポイント貯めるのも大事でしょ？
lines.kana: うん、さんぜんポイントあるよ。ほら、ポイントためるのもだいじでしょ？
lines.english: Yep, three thousand. See? Collecting points matters too, right?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai hai, arigatou. demo raigetsu wa, okane mo tamete ne.
lines.ja: はいはい、ありがとう。でも来月は、お金も貯めてね。
lines.kana: はいはい、ありがとう。でもらいげつは、おかねもためてね。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah, thank you. But next month, save some money too, OK?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: wakatta. raigetsu wa kaado tsukawanai yo. tabun.
lines.ja: わかった。来月はカード使わないよ。たぶん。
lines.kana: わかった。らいげつはカードつかわないよ。たぶん。
lines.english: Got it. Next month I won't use my card. Probably.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai lends Sora some of her trip savings so they can eat ramen.
Sora decides to stop paying by card and pays for the ramen in cash.
The ramen shop is cash only, so they go to a konbini, and Sora treats Mai with his points.

questions.explanation: Lines 10-12: Sora wonders if the ramen shop takes cards, Mai says it's cash only, and Sora has just 300 yen on him. Line 13: Mai suggests the konbini, where cards work. Line 14: Sora says lunch is on him, paid with the points he has collected (tameta pointo de). A is wrong because Mai is saving for her trip (line 5) and never lends him anything. B is wrong because Sora only says he won't use his card next month, and adds tabun, 'probably' (line 18); with 300 yen he couldn't pay for ramen anyway.

questions.english: You've spent the day shopping with Yuki and bought far more than you meant to. She says: "Today's shopping was fun! Let's go again." Agree, but say you spent too much money.
questions.ja: 今日の買い物、楽しかったね！また行こうよ。
questions.kana: きょうのかいもの、たのしかったね！またいこうよ。
questions.romaji: kyou no kaimono, tanoshikatta ne! mata ikou yo.
questions.answer: Say you overspent with okane o tsukau plus -sugiru: tanoshikatta kedo, okane tsukaisugichatta. Not sugosu, which is only for time.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, tanoshikatta! demo, okane tsukaisugichatta.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、楽しかった！でも、お金使いすぎちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it was fun! But I spent way too much money.

modelAnswers.romaji: tanoshikatta kedo, kongetsu wa mou okane tsukaenai yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 楽しかったけど、今月はもうお金使えないよ。
modelAnswers.english: It was fun, but I can't spend any more money this month.

questions.explanation: Spending money is tsukau, 'use': Mai asks kyou, kekkou okane tsukatta n ja nai? (line 1), and Sora admits kongetsu mou okane tsukaisugichatta (line 2). The dictionary words for 'spend' don't fit here: sugosu is only for time (shuumatsu o sugosu, spend the weekend), and tsuiyasu sounds like a written report. -sugichatta adds 'too much, oops'.

questions.english: Outside the ramen shop, what does Sora wonder?
questions.ja: 店の前で、ソラくんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: みせのまえで、そらくんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mise no mae de, sora-kun wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Do they take cards here, I wonder?
I wonder if I can pay by card here.
I wonder if they accept cards here.

questions.explanation: Line 10: a, demo koko, kaado tsukaeru kana? Asking whether a place takes cards uses tsukau in its can-form: 'can I use a card here?'. Mai answers the same way: kaado tsukaenakatta (line 11) and konbini nara kaado tsukaeru shi (line 13). A is 'take' word for word, but toru means picking something up or taking it away, not accepting a payment. C is 'accept' word for word; ukeru is for things like taking an exam or a phone call, and kaado ukeru doesn't ask about paying.

questions.english: Kenta has noticed you keep skipping nights out and asks: "You never come out drinking lately. Are you busy?" Tell him you're saving up money right now.
questions.ja: 最近、飲みに来ないね。忙しいの？
questions.kana: さいきん、のみにこないね。いそがしいの？
questions.romaji: saikin, nomi ni konai ne. isogashii no?
questions.answer: Say you're saving up with tameru in the -teru form: uun, ima okane tameteru n da. Not hozon suru, which is saving a file.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, ima okane tameteru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、今お金貯めてるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm saving up money right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: isogashiku nai kedo, ima ryokou no okane tameteru kara, gomen ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 忙しくないけど、今旅行のお金貯めてるから、ごめんね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm not busy, but I'm saving up for a trip right now, so sorry.

questions.explanation: Saving up is tameru, 'let it pile up', usually as tameteru while you're still at it: Mai says ima, ryokou no okane tameteru n da (line 5), and Sora says boku mo okane tamenakya (line 8). English 'save' leads elsewhere: hozon suru is saving a file, tasukeru is saving a person, and setsuyaku is cutting back. chokin shiteru also works.

questions.english: Sora says he always pays by card and collects the points. What does Mai point out about that?
questions.ja: マイさんはソラくんのポイントについて、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはそらくんのポイントについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa sora-kun no pointo ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: His points are piling up, but he isn't saving any money.
He's using up his points as fast as his money.
He's saving money by paying with points instead of cash.

questions.explanation: Line 3: pointo wa tameteru kedo, okane wa tamete nai jan. The same verb tameru does both jobs: collecting points (pointo tameteru, line 2) and saving money (okane tameteru, line 5), and Mai's wa ... wa sets the two against each other: one is piling up, the other isn't. B mixes tameru up with tsukau, spending. C turns it around: Sora pays by card, and only spends his points at the very end, at the konbini (tameta pointo de, line 14).

newWords.english: too much (tsukaisugichatta = I spent too much)

script.title: The wrong number
script.setting: Evening at home. Kenji is slumped on the sofa with his phone when his mother sits down next to him, excited: she has made a friend at her piano lessons and got her number. She still calls every message on her phone a meeru.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji, chotto kiite. okaasan, piano naratteru desho? soko de tomodachi ga dekita no.
lines.ja: ケンジ、ちょっと聞いて。お母さん、ピアノ習ってるでしょ？そこで友達ができたの。
lines.kana: けんじ、ちょっときいて。おかあさん、ピアノならってるでしょ？そこでともだちができたの。
lines.english: Kenji, listen to this. You know I've been taking piano lessons? I made a friend there.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: hee. yokatta jan.
lines.ja: へえ。よかったじゃん。
lines.kana: へえ。よかったじゃん。
lines.english: Huh. Good for you.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kyou ne, bangou oshiete tte ittara, sugu oshiete kureta no.
lines.ja: 今日ね、「番号教えて」って言ったら、すぐ教えてくれたの。
lines.kana: きょうね、「ばんごうおしえて」っていったら、すぐおしえてくれたの。
lines.english: Today I asked for her number, and she gave it to me straight away.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: okaasan, yaru jan.
lines.ja: お母さん、やるじゃん。
lines.kana: おかあさん、やるじゃん。
lines.english: Look at you, Mom.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, hiru ni sugu meeru okutta no. demo, mada kaeshite kurenai no.
lines.ja: で、昼にすぐメール送ったの。でも、まだ返してくれないの。
lines.kana: で、ひるにすぐメールおくったの。でも、まだかえしてくれないの。
lines.english: So I emailed her right away, at lunchtime. But she still hasn't replied.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: isogashii n desho. boku nanka, okaasan ni meeru kaesu no, mikka mo kakaru shi.
lines.ja: 忙しいんでしょ。僕なんか、お母さんにメール返すの、三日もかかるし。
lines.kana: いそがしいんでしょ。ぼくなんか、おかあさんにメールかえすの、みっかもかかるし。
lines.english: She's probably busy. I mean, it takes me three whole days to answer your emails.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji to issho ni shinaide. demo, nande meeru konai n darou.
lines.ja: ケンジと一緒にしないで。でも、なんでメール来ないんだろう。
lines.kana: けんじといっしょにしないで。でも、なんでメールこないんだろう。
lines.english: Don't lump her in with you. But why haven't I got an email back?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, sumaho natta yo. meeru kita n ja nai?
lines.ja: あ、スマホ鳴ったよ。メール来たんじゃない？
lines.kana: あ、スマホなったよ。メールきたんじゃない？
lines.english: Oh, your phone just went off. Isn't that an email?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: honto da, meeru kita! e, dare desu ka tte.
lines.ja: ほんとだ、メール来た！え、「誰ですか」って。
lines.kana: ほんとだ、メールきた！え、「だれですか」って。
lines.english: It is, an email! Wait, it says: 'Who is this?'

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sore, chigau bangou ni meeru okutta n ja nai?
lines.ja: それ、違う番号にメール送ったんじゃない？
lines.kana: それ、ちがうばんごうにメールおくったんじゃない？
lines.english: Sounds like you sent your email to the wrong number.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e, demo chanto bangou oshiete moratta yo. a, shichi to ichi, machigaeta kamo!
lines.ja: え、でもちゃんと番号教えてもらったよ。あ、「しち」と「いち」、間違えたかも！
lines.kana: え、でもちゃんとばんごうおしえてもらったよ。あ、「しち」と「いち」、まちがえたかも！
lines.english: What? But she gave me her number, properly. Oh! I might have mixed up 'shichi' and 'ichi'!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: aa, sore yoku aru. dakara nana tte iu n da yo.
lines.ja: ああ、それよくある。だから「なな」って言うんだよ。
lines.kana: ああ、それよくある。だから「なな」っていうんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, that happens a lot. That's why people say 'nana' for seven.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dou shiyou. shiranai hito ni meeru okutchatta. hazukashii!
lines.ja: どうしよう。知らない人にメール送っちゃった。恥ずかしい！
lines.kana: どうしよう。しらないひとにメールおくっちゃった。はずかしい！
lines.english: Oh no. I've sent an email to a total stranger. How embarrassing!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: raishuu mata au n desho? jaa, okaasan no bangou mo oshietara?
lines.ja: 来週また会うんでしょ？じゃあ、お母さんの番号も教えたら？
lines.kana: らいしゅうまたあうんでしょ？じゃあ、おかあさんのばんごうもおしえたら？
lines.english: You're seeing her again next week, right? Why not give her your number too, then?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou suru. a, sono mae ni, kono hito ni meeru kaesanakya.
lines.ja: そうする。あ、その前に、この人にメール返さなきゃ。
lines.kana: そうする。あ、そのまえに、このひとにメールかえさなきゃ。
lines.english: I will. Oh, but first I'd better reply to this person.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. sugu kaeshite agete.
lines.ja: うん。すぐ返してあげて。
lines.kana: うん。すぐかえしてあげて。
lines.english: Yeah. Write back to them right away.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji ni iwaretakunai. kesa okutta meeru mo, mada kaeshitenai desho.
lines.ja: ケンジに言われたくない。今朝送ったメールも、まだ返してないでしょ。
lines.kana: けんじにいわれたくない。けさおくったメールも、まだかえしてないでしょ。
lines.english: That's rich, coming from you. You still haven't answered the email I sent you this morning, have you?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. ashita kaesu.
lines.ja: うん。明日返す。
lines.kana: うん。あしたかえす。
lines.english: Nope. I'll answer it tomorrow.

questions.english: What happened to Mom's email to her new friend?
questions.ja: お母さんのメールは、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんのメールは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan no meeru wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: Her friend from piano finally wrote back, but had forgotten who she was.
She sent it to Kenji by mistake, which is why her friend never answered.
She got one digit of her friend's number wrong, so it went to a stranger.

questions.explanation: Lines 3-5: Mom got her new friend's number and emailed her at lunchtime, but no reply came (line 7). When an email finally comes, it says 'Who is this?' (line 9). Kenji guesses she sent it to the wrong number (line 10), and she realises she mixed up shichi (seven) and ichi (one) when her friend told her the number (line 11), so she has emailed a stranger (line 13). A is wrong because the 'Who is this?' comes from the stranger, not her friend. B mixes in a different email: the one Kenji hasn't answered is the one she sent him this morning (line 17).

questions.english: At the end of a party, Sora says: "Today was fun. Let's hang out again." Ask him for his number.
questions.ja: 今日、楽しかったね。また遊ぼうよ。
questions.kana: きょう、たのしかったね。またあそぼうよ。
questions.romaji: kyou, tanoshikatta ne. mata asobou yo.
questions.answer: Ask with oshieru ('tell'), not kudasai: bangou oshiete. Soften it with kureru: bangou oshiete kurenai?

modelAnswers.romaji: un! jaa, bangou oshiete.
modelAnswers.ja: うん！じゃあ、番号教えて。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah! Give me your number, then.

modelAnswers.romaji: yokattara, bangou oshiete kurenai?
modelAnswers.ja: よかったら、番号教えてくれない？
modelAnswers.english: If you don't mind, could I get your number?

questions.explanation: Asking for someone's number is bangou oshiete, literally 'tell me your number', which is just what Mom said to her friend in line 3 (bangou oshiete tte ittara, sugu oshiete kureta). Giving your own uses the same verb: Kenji's okaasan no bangou mo oshietara? (line 14). English 'give' pulls toward kudasai, but bangou o kudasai sounds stiff, like a form being filled in.
