questions.english: Why does Mom say she's embarrassed?
questions.ja: お母さんは、なんで「恥ずかしい」と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、なんで「はずかしい」といいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, nande hazukashii to iimashita ka?

choices.english: She had sent a friendly email to someone she doesn't know.
A stranger had emailed her, and she couldn't remember who they were.
She had told Kenji all about her new friend before even getting a reply.

questions.explanation: Line 13: shiranai hito ni meeru okutchatta. meeru o okuru is her sending the email, with the person it went to marked by ni (shiranai hito ni, 'to someone I don't know'), and -chatta adds 'oops'. B turns the direction around: an email did come to her (meeru kita, line 9), but it was the stranger's answer to hers, and it was the stranger who didn't know her. C: she did tell Kenji about her friend, but that isn't what embarrasses her.

questions.english: When Mom's phone goes off, what does Kenji say?
questions.ja: スマホが鳴って、ケンジは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: スマホがなって、けんじはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sumaho ga natte, kenji wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Aren't you going to send an email?
Isn't that an email?
Didn't you receive an email?

questions.explanation: Line 8: a, sumaho natta yo. meeru kita n ja nai? In Japanese the email is the one that comes: meeru (ga) kita, 'an email came', and Mom answers honto da, meeru kita! A, okuru, is the other direction, sending, which makes no sense when her phone has just gone off; Kenji uses okuru only for her email going out to the wrong number (line 10). C, uketoru, is English 'receive' word for word, but it sounds stiff and is for parcels and documents, not emails.

questions.english: At work, Tanaka-san asks: "Did you see the email I sent yesterday?" You read it but forgot to answer. Apologise and say you'll reply right away.
questions.ja: 昨日送ったメール、見ましたか？
questions.kana: きのうおくったメール、みましたか？
questions.romaji: kinou okutta meeru, mimashita ka?
questions.answer: Say you forgot to reply, using kaesu ('send back'): sumimasen, meeru o kaesu no o wasuretemashita. sugu kaeshimasu.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, meeru o kaesu no o wasuretemashita. sugu kaeshimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、メールを返すのを忘れてました。すぐ返します。
modelAnswers.english: I'm sorry, I forgot to reply. I'll get back to you right away.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, mimashita. sumimasen, ima sugu meeru kaeshimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、見ました。すみません、今すぐメール返します。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, yes, I saw it. Sorry, I'll reply right now.

questions.explanation: Replying to an email is meeru o kaesu, 'send the email back': Kenji's okaasan ni meeru kaesu no, mikka mo kakaru (line 6) and Mom's kesa okutta meeru mo, mada kaeshitenai desho (line 17). Not meeru ni kotaeru: kotaeru is for answering questions (shitsumon ni kotaeru). And keep the s: kaeshimasu is 'I'll reply', but kaerimasu would be 'I'll go home'.

script.title: Satou-san's miso soup
script.setting: Saturday lunchtime in Satou-san's kitchen. The elderly neighbour's wife is away this week, so he is cooking for himself for the first time, and he has asked Kenta, who likes cooking, to come over and taste his miso soup. Kenta speaks politely to him, with the odd plain-form reaction when he tastes something.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: satou-san, konnichiwa. waa, ii nioi ga shimasu ne!
lines.ja: 佐藤さん、こんにちは。わあ、いいにおいがしますね！
lines.kana: さとうさん、こんにちは。わあ、いいにおいがしますね！
lines.english: Hello, Satou-san. Oh, something smells good!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kite kurete arigatou gozaimasu. tsuma ga konshuu inai node, jibun de gohan o tsukutte iru n desu.
lines.ja: 来てくれてありがとうございます。妻が今週いないので、自分でご飯を作っているんです。
lines.kana: きてくれてありがとうございます。つまがこんしゅういないので、じぶんでごはんをつくっているんです。
lines.english: Thank you for coming. My wife's away this week, so I'm doing my own cooking.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hee, sugoi desu ne. nani o tsukutta n desu ka?
lines.ja: へえ、すごいですね。何を作ったんですか？
lines.kana: へえ、すごいですね。なにをつくったんですか？
lines.english: Oh, good for you. What did you make?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: misoshiru desu. chotto aji o mite moraemasu ka?
lines.ja: みそ汁です。ちょっと味を見てもらえますか？
lines.kana: みそしるです。ちょっとあじをみてもらえますか？
lines.english: Miso soup. Could you taste it for me?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ii desu yo. uun, chotto aji ga usui kamo shiremasen.
lines.ja: いいですよ。うーん、ちょっと味が薄いかもしれません。
lines.kana: いいですよ。うーん、ちょっとあじがうすいかもしれません。
lines.english: Sure. Hmm, it might be a little bland.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou desu ka, aji ga usui desu ka. jaa, shio o sukoshi iremasu ne.
lines.ja: そうですか、味が薄いですか。じゃあ、塩を少し入れますね。
lines.kana: そうですか、あじがうすいですか。じゃあ、しおをすこしいれますね。
lines.english: I see, it's bland, is it? Then I'll add a little salt.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: are? nanka amai aji ga suru. satou-san, sore, shio desu ka?
lines.ja: あれ？なんか甘い味がする。佐藤さん、それ、塩ですか？
lines.kana: あれ？なんかあまいあじがする。さとうさん、それ、しおですか？
lines.english: Huh? It tastes kind of sweet. Satou-san, is that salt?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ee, shio desu yo. dore dore. a, tashika ni amai aji ga shimasu ne.
lines.ja: ええ、塩ですよ。どれどれ。あ、確かに甘い味がしますね。
lines.kana: ええ、しおですよ。どれどれ。あ、たしかにあまいあじがしますね。
lines.english: Yes, it's salt. Let me see. Oh, it does taste sweet.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: satou-san, sore, shio ja nakute satou desu yo!
lines.ja: 佐藤さん、それ、塩じゃなくて砂糖ですよ！
lines.kana: さとうさん、それ、しおじゃなくてさとうですよ！
lines.english: Satou-san, that's not salt, it's sugar!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: oya. haha, satou ga satou o irete shimaimashita.
lines.ja: おや。はは、佐藤が砂糖を入れてしまいました。
lines.kana: おや。はは、さとうがさとうをいれてしまいました。
lines.english: Oh dear. Ha, Satou went and put in the satou.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: haha. demo, amai dake de, mada aji ga usui desu ne.
lines.ja: はは。でも、甘いだけで、まだ味が薄いですね。
lines.kana: はは。でも、あまいだけで、まだあじがうすいですね。
lines.english: Ha ha. But it's only sweet. It's still bland.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, kondo wa chanto shio o. watashi wa aji ga koi hou ga suki na node, takusan iremashou.
lines.ja: じゃあ、今度はちゃんと塩を。私は味が濃いほうが好きなので、たくさん入れましょう。
lines.kana: じゃあ、こんどはちゃんとしおを。わたしはあじがこいほうがすきなので、たくさんいれましょう。
lines.english: Then this time, real salt. I like my food on the strong side, so I'll put in plenty.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, sonna ni? uwa, kondo wa aji ga koi.
lines.ja: えっ、そんなに？うわ、今度は味が濃い。
lines.kana: えっ、そんなに？うわ、こんどはあじがこい。
lines.english: Wait, that much? Whoa, now it's way too strong.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: dore. aa, hontou da. kore wa aji ga koi desu ne.
lines.ja: どれ。ああ、本当だ。これは味が濃いですね。
lines.kana: どれ。ああ、ほんとうだ。これはあじがこいですね。
lines.english: Let me try. Ah, you're right. This is much too strong.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: omizu o sukoshi iremashou ka?
lines.ja: お水を少し入れましょうか？
lines.kana: おみずをすこしいれましょうか？
lines.english: Shall we add a little water?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo, omizu o iretara, mata aji ga usuku narimasen ka?
lines.ja: でも、お水を入れたら、また味が薄くなりませんか？
lines.kana: でも、おみずをいれたら、またあじがうすくなりませんか？
lines.english: But if we add water, won't it go bland again?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sukoshi dake nara daijoubu desu yo. a, oishii! chanto misoshiru no aji ga shimasu.
lines.ja: 少しだけなら大丈夫ですよ。あ、おいしい！ちゃんとみそ汁の味がします。
lines.kana: すこしだけならだいじょうぶですよ。あ、おいしい！ちゃんとみそしるのあじがします。
lines.english: Just a little will be fine. Oh, that's good! Now it tastes like proper miso soup.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yokatta. kenta-san, satou no koto wa, tsuma ni wa naisho ni shite kudasai ne.
lines.ja: よかった。ケンタさん、砂糖のことは、妻には内緒にしてくださいね。
lines.kana: よかった。けんたさん、さとうのことは、つまにはないしょにしてくださいね。
lines.english: Thank goodness. Kenta, please don't tell my wife about the sugar.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenta cooks miso soup for Satou-san but mixes up the salt and the sugar, so they start again from scratch.
Satou-san's miso soup is bland; he adds sugar by mistake, then too much salt, and a little water fixes it.
Satou-san's miso soup is too salty, so Kenta has him add sugar and water until it tastes right.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-4: Satou-san's wife is away, so he is cooking for himself and asks Kenta to taste his miso soup. Kenta finds it bland (line 5). The 'salt' Satou-san adds makes it taste sweet (lines 7-8), because it is sugar (line 9). He then pours in plenty of real salt and it is far too strong (lines 12-14), and a little water makes it taste like proper miso soup (lines 15-17). A is wrong because Satou-san is the cook and Kenta only tastes, and they fix the soup rather than start again. C gets the order backwards: the soup was bland at first and too salty only near the end, and the sugar went in by accident, not as Kenta's fix.

questions.english: Sora, who works at a café, hands you a drink he has made and says: "I tried making a new one. Have a sip. What does it taste like?" It tastes of coffee. Tell him.
questions.ja: 新しいの作ってみたんだ。飲んでみて。どんな味？
questions.kana: あたらしいのつくってみたんだ。のんでみて。どんなあじ？
questions.romaji: atarashii no tsukutte mita n da. nonde mite. donna aji?
questions.answer: Say what it tastes of with aji ga suru, putting the flavour in front with no: koohii no aji ga suru (casually, koohii no aji suru).

modelAnswers.romaji: nanka, koohii no aji suru.
modelAnswers.ja: なんか、コーヒーの味する。
modelAnswers.english: It kind of tastes of coffee.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, koohii no aji ga suru ne. oishii!
modelAnswers.ja: うん、コーヒーの味がするね。おいしい！
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it tastes of coffee. It's good!

questions.explanation: A taste you notice 'does': aji ga suru. Kenta says nanka amai aji ga suru (line 7), Satou-san agrees with amai aji ga shimasu ne (line 8), and at the end Kenta says chanto misoshiru no aji ga shimasu (line 17). For 'tastes of X', put X no in front: koohii no aji ga suru. Don't say koohii no aji ga aru, the English 'it has a taste' word for word, which sounds off. And aji o miru, what Satou-san asks Kenta to do in line 4, is tasting something on purpose, not saying what it tastes like.

questions.english: Kenta has cooked dinner for you and asks: "First time I've made this. How is it?" It's good, but it needs more salt. Tell him, gently.
questions.ja: これ、初めて作ったんだ。どう？
questions.kana: これ、はじめてつくったんだ。どう？
questions.romaji: kore, hajimete tsukutta n da. dou?
questions.answer: Say it's a little bland with aji ga usui, softened with chotto: oishii kedo, chotto aji usui kamo.

modelAnswers.romaji: oishii kedo, chotto aji usui kamo.
modelAnswers.ja: おいしいけど、ちょっと味薄いかも。
modelAnswers.english: It's good, but it might be a bit bland.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, oishii yo. demo, chotto aji ga usui ne. shio aru?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、おいしいよ。でも、ちょっと味が薄いね。塩ある？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it's good. But it's a bit bland. Got any salt?

questions.explanation: Food that needs more salt is aji ga usui (thin): Kenta tells Satou-san chotto aji ga usui kamo shiremasen (line 5), and even after the sugar it is mada aji ga usui (line 11). Not aji ga yowai: yowai goes with drink (osake ga yowai, can't hold your drink), not with seasoning. With a friend you can drop ga (aji usui), and chotto and kamo soften it, the way Kenta softens it for Satou-san.

questions.english: After Satou-san puts in a lot of real salt, what does Kenta say when he tastes the soup?
questions.ja: 塩をたくさん入れたあと、ケンタさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: しおをたくさんいれたあと、けんたさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: shio o takusan ireta ato, kenta-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Now the taste is strong (sharp, pungent).
Now it's bland.
Now it's too heavily seasoned.

questions.explanation: Line 13: e, sonna ni? uwa, kondo wa aji ga koi. All that salt has made the soup heavily seasoned, which is koi (dense), the same word as strong coffee; Satou-san agrees in line 14 (kore wa aji ga koi desu ne), even though he had just said he likes his food aji ga koi (line 12). A, aji ga tsuyoi, is 'strong flavour' word for word, but tsuyoi is for a sharp, distinctive taste, or for wind and for someone who can hold their drink (osake ga tsuyoi), not for heavy seasoning. B, aji ga usui, is the opposite: what Kenta said before any salt went in (line 5), and what Satou-san fears the water will do (line 16).

newWords.english: sugar (sounds just like the name Satou)

script.title: Three days off
script.setting: A weekday afternoon. Sora gets back to the flat he shares with Kenta after a morning shift at the café and is surprised to find Kenta at home in the middle of the working week.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: are? kenta, kyou shigoto yasunda no? kaze?
lines.ja: あれ？ケンタ、今日仕事休んだの？風邪？
lines.kana: あれ？けんた、きょうしごとやすんだの？かぜ？
lines.english: Huh? Kenta, did you take today off work? Have you got a cold?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: uun, kaze ja nai yo. kyou kara mikka, yasumi totta n da.
lines.ja: ううん、風邪じゃないよ。今日から三日、休み取ったんだ。
lines.kana: ううん、かぜじゃないよ。きょうからみっか、やすみとったんだ。
lines.english: No, it's not a cold. I've taken three days off, starting today.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, mikka mo? kenta ga yasumi toru no, hajimete ja nai? dou shita no?
lines.ja: え、三日も？ケンタが休み取るの、初めてじゃない？どうしたの？
lines.kana: え、みっかも？けんたがやすみとるの、はじめてじゃない？どうしたの？
lines.english: What, three whole days? Isn't this the first time you've ever taken time off? What's going on?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: saikin shigoto ga sugoku isogashikute, hiru no kyuukei mo torenakatta n da.
lines.ja: 最近仕事がすごく忙しくて、昼の休憩も取れなかったんだ。
lines.kana: さいきんしごとがすごくいそがしくて、ひるのきゅうけいもとれなかったんだ。
lines.english: Work's been really busy lately. I couldn't even take my lunch break.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kyuukei mo? boku nanka, baito de ichijikan ni ikkai wa kyuukei totteru yo.
lines.ja: 休憩も？僕なんか、バイトで一時間に一回は休憩取ってるよ。
lines.kana: きゅうけいも？ぼくなんか、ばいとでいちじかんにいっかいはきゅうけいとってるよ。
lines.english: Not even a break? Me, I take a break at least once an hour at my job.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora wa torisugi. de, sengetsu, mae no seki no hito ga kaisha yameta n da.
lines.ja: ソラは取りすぎ。で、先月、前の席の人が会社辞めたんだ。
lines.kana: そらはとりすぎ。で、せんげつ、まえのせきのひとがかいしゃやめたんだ。
lines.english: You take way too many. Anyway, last month the person who sits in front of me quit.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: aa, sore de isogashii n da.
lines.ja: ああ、それで忙しいんだ。
lines.kana: ああ、それでいそがしいんだ。
lines.english: Oh, so that's why you're so busy.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un. sono hito no shigoto mo, zenbu boku ga yatteru n da.
lines.ja: うん。その人の仕事も、全部僕がやってるんだ。
lines.kana: うん。そのひとのしごとも、ぜんぶぼくがやってるんだ。
lines.english: Yeah. I'm doing all their work as well.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uwa, taihen jan. sore wa kenta mo kaisha yametaku naru yo ne.
lines.ja: うわ、大変じゃん。それはケンタも会社辞めたくなるよね。
lines.kana: うわ、たいへんじゃん。それはけんたもかいしゃやめたくなるよね。
lines.english: Ugh, that's rough. No wonder you'd want to quit too.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: maa, chotto dake kangaeta.
lines.ja: まあ、ちょっとだけ考えた。
lines.kana: まあ、ちょっとだけかんがえた。
lines.english: Well, I did think about it. A little.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, dame dame! kenta ga kaisha yametara, kono heya dou suru no?
lines.ja: え、だめだめ！ケンタが会社辞めたら、この部屋どうするの？
lines.kana: え、だめだめ！けんたがかいしゃやめたら、このへやどうするの？
lines.english: What? No, no, no! If you quit your job, what happens to this flat?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: soko? daijoubu, kaisha wa yamenai yo. dakara yasumi totta n da.
lines.ja: そこ？大丈夫、会社は辞めないよ。だから休み取ったんだ。
lines.kana: そこ？だいじょうぶ、かいしゃはやめないよ。だからやすみとったんだ。
lines.english: That's what you're worried about? Relax, I'm not quitting. That's why I took the time off.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: yokatta. jaa, mikka mo shigoto yasunde, nani suru no?
lines.ja: よかった。じゃあ、三日も仕事休んで、何するの？
lines.kana: よかった。じゃあ、みっかもしごとやすんで、なにするの？
lines.english: Phew. So what are you going to do with three whole days off work?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gohan tsukutte, sakkaa mite, yukkuri neru.
lines.ja: ご飯作って、サッカー見て、ゆっくり寝る。
lines.kana: ごはんつくって、さっかーみて、ゆっくりねる。
lines.english: Cook, watch football, and get a good long sleep.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii naa. boku mo ashita, shigoto yasumou kana.
lines.ja: いいなあ。僕も明日、仕事休もうかな。
lines.kana: いいなあ。ぼくもあした、しごとやすもうかな。
lines.english: Lucky you. Maybe I'll take tomorrow off work too.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: dame. sora wa mainichi kyuukei torisugi desho.
lines.ja: だめ。ソラは毎日休憩取りすぎでしょ。
lines.kana: だめ。そらはまいにちきゅうけいとりすぎでしょ。
lines.english: No way. You take far too many breaks every day as it is.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kyuukei to yasumi wa chigau yo!
lines.ja: 休憩と休みは違うよ！
lines.kana: きゅうけいとやすみはちがうよ！
lines.english: A break and a day off aren't the same thing!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hai hai. jaa ashita chanto shigoto ittara, oishii gohan tsukuttoku yo.
lines.ja: はいはい。じゃあ明日ちゃんと仕事行ったら、おいしいご飯作っとくよ。
lines.kana: はいはい。じゃああしたちゃんとしごといったら、おいしいごはんつくっとくよ。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. Tell you what: if you actually go to work tomorrow, I'll have a nice dinner waiting.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenta has caught a cold and is off work, so Sora decides to stay home tomorrow and look after him.
Kenta has quit his job because a coworker left, and Sora is worried about who will pay for the flat.
Kenta has booked three days off because work got too much; he thought about quitting, but he's staying.

questions.explanation: Line 2: it isn't a cold; Kenta has booked three days off starting today (kyou kara mikka, yasumi totta n da). Lines 4-8: work has been so busy he couldn't even take a lunch break, because the colleague in front of him quit and Kenta is doing that person's work too. Line 10: he admits he thought about quitting a little, but in line 12 he says kaisha wa yamenai yo, dakara yasumi totta n da: he's not quitting, and that's why he took the time off. A is wrong: Kenta says kaze ja nai (line 2), and Sora's idea of skipping work tomorrow (line 15) is turned down. B is wrong: the one who quit is the colleague (line 6); Sora only panics about the flat in line 11, after Kenta says he thought about it.

questions.english: You've got a cold and stayed home from work today. Kenta calls: "Want to go out to eat tonight?" Tell him you took today off work with a cold.
questions.ja: 今日の夜、ご飯行かない？
questions.kana: きょうのよる、ごはんいかない？
questions.romaji: kyou no yoru, gohan ikanai?
questions.answer: Say you missed work with shigoto o yasumu in the past: kyou kaze de shigoto yasunda n da. Work is the object (shigoto o, or just shigoto), not shigoto kara.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou kaze de shigoto yasunda n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日風邪で仕事休んだんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I took today off work with a cold.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen ne. kaze hiite, kyou wa shigoto yasunda n da. mata kondo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんね。風邪ひいて、今日は仕事休んだんだ。また今度ね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry. I've caught a cold and stayed off work today. Another time, OK?

questions.explanation: Staying away from work, sick or not, is shigoto o yasumu, with work as the object: Sora asks kyou shigoto yasunda no? kaze? (line 1), mikka mo shigoto yasunde (line 13) and shigoto yasumou kana (line 15). 'Off work' tempts shigoto kara yasumu, but kara is wrong here. A sudden sick day is yasumu rather than yasumi o toru, which is for days off you arrange. And careful with the sound-alike: shigoto yameta would mean you quit your job.

questions.english: You work on Fridays. Yuki says: "Hey, want to go on a trip together, starting next Friday?" Say yes, and that you'll take Friday off.
questions.ja: ねえ、来週の金曜日から、一緒に旅行行かない？
questions.kana: ねえ、らいしゅうのきんようびから、いっしょにりょこういかない？
questions.romaji: nee, raishuu no kin'youbi kara, issho ni ryokou ikanai?
questions.answer: Say you'll book the day off with yasumi o toru: jaa, kin'youbi wa yasumi toru yo. Not kyuukei, which is a short break during the working day.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii ne! jaa, kin'youbi wa yasumi toru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: いいね！じゃあ、金曜日は休み取るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sounds great! I'll take Friday off, then.

modelAnswers.romaji: iku iku! kin'youbi, yasumi toreru ka kaisha ni kiite miru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 行く行く！金曜日、休み取れるか会社に聞いてみるね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm in! I'll ask work if I can get Friday off.

questions.explanation: Days off that you arrange with work are yasumi o toru, as Kenta says in line 2 (kyou kara mikka, yasumi totta n da) and line 12 (dakara yasumi totta n da), and Sora in line 3 (kenta ga yasumi toru no, hajimete ja nai?). The o is usually dropped in casual speech. kyuukei o toru would be a few minutes' break inside a working day, like Kenta's lunch break in line 4. Taking time off is not yameru: kaisha yameru means quitting the job for good.

questions.english: Sora says he might take tomorrow off work too. Why does Kenta say no?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、どうして「だめ」と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、どうして「だめ」といいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, doushite dame to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora already takes far too many short breaks at work every day.
Sora has already had too many days off from the café this month.
The café is too busy for Sora to stay home tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Line 16: sora wa mainichi kyuukei torisugi desho. kyuukei o toru is taking a short break during the working day, and in line 5 Sora boasted that he takes one at least once an hour (ichijikan ni ikkai wa kyuukei totteru). B mixes kyuukei up with yasumi: days off would be yasumi o toru, and that difference is exactly Sora's comeback in line 17 (kyuukei to yasumi wa chigau yo!). C: nobody says the café is busy; the busy workplace is Kenta's (lines 4 and 7).

questions.english: When Kenta admits he thought about quitting, Sora panics. What does he say?
questions.ja: ソラさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: If you head out of the office, what happens to this flat?
choices.romaji: kenta ga kaisha detara, kono heya dou suru no?

choices.english: If you quit your job, what happens to this flat?
choices.romaji: kenta ga kaisha yametara, kono heya dou suru no?

choices.english: If you take time off work, what happens to this flat?
choices.romaji: kenta ga kaisha yasundara, kono heya dou suru no?

questions.explanation: Line 11: kenta ga kaisha yametara, kono heya dou suru no? Leaving a job for good is kaisha o yameru, the same verb Kenta uses for his colleague in line 6 (kaisha yameta n da) and for himself in line 12 (kaisha wa yamenai yo). A is the 'leave the company' calque: kaisha o deru means walking out of the office building, to go home or out to lunch, not leaving the job. C, yasumu, sounds close to yameru but means staying off work for a while, which is what Kenta has actually done (yasumi totta, lines 2 and 12) and is no threat to the flat.

script.title: The café with no queue
script.setting: A Saturday afternoon on a busy shopping street. Yuki and her coworker and friend Mai have been out shopping, and Mai has stocked up on cat food. They'd planned to finish the day at a pancake place they'd been talking about.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, daijoubu? nimotsu, hitotsu motou ka?
lines.ja: マイ、大丈夫？荷物、一つ持とうか？
lines.kana: まい、だいじょうぶ？にもつ、ひとつもとうか？
lines.english: Mai, you okay? Want me to carry one of your bags?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii no? arigatou. neko no gohan takusan katchatte, nimotsu sugoku omoi n da.
lines.ja: いいの？ありがとう。猫のごはんたくさん買っちゃって、荷物すごく重いんだ。
lines.kana: いいの？ありがとう。ねこのごはんたくさんかっちゃって、にもつすごくおもいんだ。
lines.english: Are you sure? Thanks. I went and bought loads of cat food, so my bags are really heavy.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uwa, honto da. nanka kyou, hito ooi ne.
lines.ja: うわ、ほんとだ。なんか今日、人多いね。
lines.kana: うわ、ほんとだ。なんかきょう、ひとおおいね。
lines.english: Whoa, they really are. It's kind of crowded today, isn't it?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: doyoubi da kara ne. a, hora, ano pankeeki no omise, metcha naranderu.
lines.ja: 土曜日だからね。あ、ほら、あのパンケーキのお店、めっちゃ並んでる。
lines.kana: どようびだからね。あ、ほら、あのぱんけーきのおみせ、めっちゃならんでる。
lines.english: Well, it is Saturday. Oh, look, there's a huge line at that pancake place.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, are, ikou tte itteta omise ja nai?
lines.ja: え、あれ、行こうって言ってたお店じゃない？
lines.kana: え、あれ、いこうっていってたおみせじゃない？
lines.english: Wait, isn't that the place we said we'd go to?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou. saikin, sugoku ninki aru n da tte.
lines.ja: そう。最近、すごく人気あるんだって。
lines.kana: そう。さいきん、すごくにんきあるんだって。
lines.english: Yeah. Apparently it's really popular right now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: demo kore, ichijikan wa matsu yo. nimotsu omoi shi, kyou wa yameyou ka.
lines.ja: でもこれ、一時間は待つよ。荷物重いし、今日はやめようか。
lines.kana: でもこれ、いちじかんはまつよ。にもつおもいし、きょうはやめようか。
lines.english: But that's an hour's wait at least, and our bags are heavy. Shall we give it a miss today?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. jaa, kono chikaku no kafe, ikanai? soko, hyouban ii n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。じゃあ、この近くのカフェ、行かない？そこ、評判いいんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。じゃあ、このちかくのかふぇ、いかない？そこ、ひょうばんいいんだよ。
lines.english: Okay. Then how about a café near here? It's got a really good reputation.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hee. demo, ninki aru nara, soko mo hito ooi n ja nai?
lines.ja: へえ。でも、人気あるなら、そこも人多いんじゃない？
lines.kana: へえ。でも、にんきあるなら、そこもひとおおいんじゃない？
lines.english: Oh yeah? But if it's popular, won't it be crowded there too?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, ninki aru tte iu yori, hyouban no ii omise na no.
lines.ja: ううん、人気あるっていうより、評判のいいお店なの。
lines.kana: ううん、にんきあるっていうより、ひょうばんのいいおみせなの。
lines.english: No, it's not so much popular as well thought of.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: dou chigau no?
lines.ja: どう違うの？
lines.kana: どうちがうの？
lines.english: What's the difference?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: itta hito wa minna yokatta tte iu kedo, omise wa sonna ni konde nai n da tte.
lines.ja: 行った人はみんなよかったって言うけど、お店はそんなに混んでないんだって。
lines.kana: いったひとはみんなよかったっていうけど、おみせはそんなにこんでないんだって。
lines.english: Everyone who's been says it was great, but apparently it doesn't get that packed.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sokka. jaa, sotchi itte miyou.
lines.ja: そっか。じゃあ、そっち行ってみよう。
lines.kana: そっか。じゃあ、そっちいってみよう。
lines.english: I see. Let's try that one, then.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: koko da yo. ii fun'iki desho?
lines.ja: ここだよ。いい雰囲気でしょ？
lines.kana: ここだよ。いいふんいきでしょ？
lines.english: Here it is. Nice vibe, right?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, sugoku ii. a, mite, pankeeki mo aru!
lines.ja: うん、すごくいい。あ、見て、パンケーキもある！
lines.kana: うん、すごくいい。あ、みて、ぱんけーきもある！
lines.english: Yeah, really nice. Oh, look, they've got pancakes too!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto da. narabanakute yokatta ne.
lines.ja: ほんとだ。並ばなくてよかったね。
lines.kana: ほんとだ。ならばなくてよかったね。
lines.english: Oh, they do. Good thing we didn't queue.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: oishii! fun'iki mo ii shi, hyouban ii no, wakaru naa.
lines.ja: おいしい！雰囲気もいいし、評判いいの、わかるなあ。
lines.kana: おいしい！ふんいきもいいし、ひょうばんいいの、わかるなあ。
lines.english: So good! And it's got a lovely feel. I can see why people rave about it.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: desho? demo, minna ni wa naisho ni shite ne. koko mo hito ooku nattara, iya da kara.
lines.ja: でしょ？でも、みんなには内緒にしてね。ここも人多くなったら、嫌だから。
lines.kana: でしょ？でも、みんなにはないしょにしてね。ここもひとおおくなったら、いやだから。
lines.english: Right? But keep it to yourself, okay? I don't want this place getting crowded too.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai takes Yuki to a café everyone is talking about, but it's packed as well, so they head home with their bags.
They queue for an hour at the popular pancake place, then decide a quieter café nearby would have been better.
They skip the long line at the popular pancake place and go to a quieter, well-reviewed café, which has pancakes too.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Mai points out the huge line at the pancake place they'd planned to visit, and line 6 says it's really popular right now. Line 7: Yuki says it's at least an hour's wait and their bags are heavy, so they give it a miss. Line 8: Mai suggests a café nearby with a good reputation, and line 12 says it doesn't get that packed. In lines 15-16 they find it has pancakes too and are glad they didn't queue. A is wrong: Yuki worries the café will be crowded (line 9), but Mai says it isn't (line 12), and they stay and eat there (line 17). B is wrong: they never join the queue. Yuki suggests skipping it in line 7, and Mai agrees in line 8.

questions.english: Your friend Kenta asks you, "nee, doyoubi ni ano pankeeki no omise, ikanai?" Say Saturdays are crowded and suggest another time, using hito ga ooi.
questions.ja: ねえ、土曜日にあのパンケーキのお店、行かない？
questions.kana: ねえ、どようびにあのぱんけーきのおみせ、いかない？
questions.romaji: nee, doyoubi ni ano pankeeki no omise, ikanai?
questions.answer: Say Saturdays are crowded with hito ga ooi (in casual speech, hito ooi), give it as your reason with kara, and suggest another time.

modelAnswers.romaji: doyoubi wa hito ooi kara, kin'youbi no yoru ni shinai?
modelAnswers.ja: 土曜日は人多いから、金曜日の夜にしない？
modelAnswers.english: Saturdays are crowded, so why don't we go Friday night instead?

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. demo doyoubi wa hito ga ooi kara, asa hayaku ikou.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。でも土曜日は人が多いから、朝早く行こう。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. But it's crowded on Saturdays, so let's go early in the morning.

questions.explanation: In line 3 Yuki says 'nanka kyou, hito ooi ne' (it's crowded today), and Mai answers that it's Saturday (doyoubi da kara ne). In line 9 Yuki asks 'soko mo hito ooi n ja nai?' (won't it be crowded there too?), and in line 18 Mai says 'hito ooku nattara' (if it gets crowded). The people are the subject and ooi comes after them, so don't say 'ooi hito ga iru' for 'there are lots of people'. Before a noun it's takusan no hito. Don't call a place isogashii (busy) either: crowded is hito ga ooi or konderu, as in line 12 (konde nai). Kenta is a friend, so a casual answer fits.

questions.english: You walk past the pancake place with your little brother Kenji, and he asks, "nee, nande ano mise, anna ni naranderu no?" Tell him why, using ninki ga aru.
questions.ja: ねえ、なんであの店、あんなに並んでるの？
questions.kana: ねえ、なんであのみせ、あんなにならんでるの？
questions.romaji: nee, nande ano mise, anna ni naranderu no?
questions.answer: Say the place is popular: ninki ga aru, with ga dropped in casual speech (ninki aru). Add n da tte if it's something you've heard, or n da yo if you're telling him.

modelAnswers.romaji: saikin, sugoku ninki aru n da tte.
modelAnswers.ja: 最近、すごく人気あるんだって。
modelAnswers.english: Apparently it's really popular right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: ano mise, ima sugoku ninki ga aru n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あの店、今すごく人気があるんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: That place is really popular at the moment.

questions.explanation: Mai says the first model answer word for word in line 6, about the same long line. A queue like that means lots of people like the place and go there, which is ninki ga aru. Line 10 sets it against hyouban ga ii (people speak well of it), which doesn't need a crowd. Don't say popyuraa: in Japanese it's for things that are widely known or standard, not a shop people flock to. Kenji is your little brother, so answer casually.

questions.english: When they get to the café, what does Mai say about it?
questions.ja: マイさんは、カフェのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、かふぇのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, kafe no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Nice fresh air, right?
Nice vibe, right?
It's popular, right?

questions.explanation: Line 14: 'koko da yo. ii fun'iki desho?' fun'iki is the feel of a place, so ii fun'iki is a nice vibe. In line 17 Yuki says it with the noun first, 'fun'iki mo ii shi', which is just as natural. A is wrong: ii kuuki means fresh air. kuuki is only a mood in set phrases like kuuki o yomu (read the room) and kuuki ga omoi (an awkward mood). C is wrong: in line 10 Mai says the café isn't so much popular (ninki aru tte iu yori) as well thought of, and in line 12 that it doesn't get packed. ninki aru is what she said about the pancake place (line 6).

questions.english: Mai says the café is "ninki aru tte iu yori, hyouban no ii omise." What kind of place is it?
questions.ja: そのカフェは、どんなお店ですか？
questions.kana: そのかふぇは、どんなおみせですか？
questions.romaji: sono kafe wa, donna omise desu ka?

choices.english: People who've been there speak well of it, but it doesn't get crowded.
So many people go there that it's always packed.
Everyone has heard of it, but people say it isn't very good.

questions.explanation: Line 10 sets the two apart: not so much ninki aru (popular) as hyouban no ii omise (a place people speak well of). Line 12 explains: everyone who's been says it was good (itta hito wa minna yokatta tte iu), but it doesn't get that packed. That's hyouban ga ii: it's about what people say. Before a noun ga becomes no, as in hyouban no ii omise. Mai first says it in line 8 (hyouban ii n da yo), and Yuki agrees in line 17. B is ninki ga aru, what Mai says about the pancake place (line 6) and what Yuki wrongly expects of the café in line 9. C is wrong: that would be hyouban ga warui, the opposite. And being widely known is yuumei (famous), which nobody says here.

questions.english: You meet Mai in the street with two big shopping bags, and she sighs, "neko no gohan, mata takusan katchatta." Offer to help, using nimotsu ga omoi.
questions.ja: 猫のごはん、またたくさん買っちゃった。
questions.kana: ねこのごはん、またたくさんかっちゃった。
questions.romaji: neko no gohan, mata takusan katchatta.
questions.answer: Say her bags must be heavy with nimotsu ga omoi (in casual speech, nimotsu omoi desho?), then offer to carry one: hitotsu motou ka?

modelAnswers.romaji: nimotsu omoi desho? hitotsu motou ka?
modelAnswers.ja: 荷物重いでしょ？一つ持とうか？
modelAnswers.english: Your bags must be heavy. Want me to take one?

modelAnswers.romaji: uwa, nimotsu omosou. hitotsu motsu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うわ、荷物重そう。一つ持つよ。
modelAnswers.english: Whoa, those bags look heavy. Let me take one.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Yuki offers to carry one of Mai's bags (nimotsu, hitotsu motou ka?), and in line 2 Mai says 'nimotsu sugoku omoi n da' (my bags are really heavy). In line 7 Yuki uses 'nimotsu omoi shi' as a reason to skip the queue. The bags are the subject, nimotsu ga omoi, and ga usually drops in casual speech. Before a noun it's omoi nimotsu. omosou means 'looks heavy'. Mai is a friend, so answer casually.

newWords.english: line up, queue (naranderu: there's a line)

script.title: The thank-you dinner
script.setting: A small izakaya on a Friday evening. Mai (Kimura-san at work) has invited her manager Tanaka-san out to thank him for last month, when her cat was sick and she had to take a week off work. She means to pay.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: tanaka-san, kyou wa oisogashii tokoro, arigatou gozaimasu.
lines.ja: 田中さん、今日はお忙しいところ、ありがとうございます。
lines.kana: たなかさん、きょうはおいそがしいところ、ありがとうございます。
lines.english: Tanaka-san, thank you for coming tonight when you're so busy.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: iie. de, kyuu ni dou shita n desu ka?
lines.ja: いいえ。で、急にどうしたんですか？
lines.kana: いいえ。で、きゅうにどうしたんですか？
lines.english: Not at all. So what's all this, out of the blue?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sengetsu wa, neko ga byouki de isshuukan mo shigoto o yasunde, hontou ni osewa ni narimashita. dakara, chanto orei o iitakute.
lines.ja: 先月は、猫が病気で一週間も仕事を休んで、本当にお世話になりました。だから、ちゃんとお礼を言いたくて。
lines.kana: せんげつは、ねこがびょうきでいっしゅうかんもしごとをやすんで、ほんとうにおせわになりました。だから、ちゃんとおれいをいいたくて。
lines.english: Last month my cat was sick and I took a whole week off work, and you really looked after me. So I wanted to thank you properly.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sorede gohan desu ka. sonna ni ki o tsukawanakute ii noni.
lines.ja: それでご飯ですか。そんなに気を遣わなくていいのに。
lines.kana: それでごはんですか。そんなにきをつかわなくていいのに。
lines.english: So that's what dinner is for. You didn't need to go to all that trouble.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: iie! kyou no gohan wa, watashi ni ogorasete kudasai.
lines.ja: いいえ！今日のご飯は、私におごらせてください。
lines.kana: いいえ！きょうのごはんは、わたしにおごらせてください。
lines.english: No, no! Please let me treat you to dinner tonight.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. jaa, kyou wa gochisou ni narimasu.
lines.ja: そうですか。じゃあ、今日はごちそうになります。
lines.kana: そうですか。じゃあ、きょうはごちそうになります。
lines.english: Is that so? Well then, tonight I'll let you treat me.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, biiru, mou nai desu ne. tsugi, nani nomimasu ka? watashi, tanomimasu ne.
lines.ja: あ、ビール、もうないですね。次、何飲みますか？私、頼みますね。
lines.kana: あ、ビール、もうないですね。つぎ、なにのみますか？わたし、たのみますね。
lines.english: Oh, your beer's finished. What would you like next? I'll order it.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san, sakki kara ki o tsukatte bakari desu ne. kyou wa shigoto ja nai n desu kara, keigo mo tsukawanakute ii desu yo.
lines.ja: 木村さん、さっきから気を遣ってばかりですね。今日は仕事じゃないんですから、敬語も使わなくていいですよ。
lines.kana: きむらさん、さっきからきをつかってばかりですね。きょうはしごとじゃないんですから、けいごもつかわなくていいですよ。
lines.english: Kimura-san, you've done nothing but fuss over me all evening. We're not at work tonight, so you don't need to be formal with me, either.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, demo, tanaka-san mo keigo tsukattemasu yo.
lines.ja: え、でも、田中さんも敬語使ってますよ。
lines.kana: え、でも、たなかさんもけいごつかってますよ。
lines.english: Huh? But you're being formal too, Tanaka-san.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: a, hontou da. jaa, kimura-san, tsugi, nani nomu?
lines.ja: あ、本当だ。じゃあ、木村さん、次、何飲む？
lines.kana: あ、ほんとうだ。じゃあ、きむらさん、つぎ、なにのむ？
lines.english: Oh, you're right. Okay then... Kimura-san, what're you drinking next?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: muri desu! tanaka-san ni wa, keigo tsukawasete kudasai.
lines.ja: 無理です！田中さんには、敬語使わせてください。
lines.kana: むりです！たなかさんには、けいごつかわせてください。
lines.english: I can't! Please let me keep being polite with you.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: wakarimashita. jaa, ki wa tsukawanaide kudasai ne.
lines.ja: わかりました。じゃあ、気は遣わないでくださいね。
lines.kana: わかりました。じゃあ、きはつかわないでくださいね。
lines.english: All right. But no more fussing over me, then.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sorosoro kaerimashou ka. watashi, haratte kimasu ne.
lines.ja: そろそろ帰りましょうか。私、払ってきますね。
lines.kana: そろそろかえりましょうか。わたし、はらってきますね。
lines.english: Shall we call it a night? I'll go and pay.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: aa, sore nara, mou harattemasu yo.
lines.ja: ああ、それなら、もう払ってますよ。
lines.kana: ああ、それなら、もうはらってますよ。
lines.english: Oh, that? I've already paid.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e! gochisou ni narimasu tte itta ja nai desu ka!
lines.ja: え！「ごちそうになります」って言ったじゃないですか！
lines.kana: え！「ごちそうになります」っていったじゃないですか！
lines.english: What? But you said you'd let me treat you!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: orei nara, mou chanto itte moraimashita kara. minna no mendou o miru no wa, watashi no shigoto desu yo.
lines.ja: お礼なら、もうちゃんと言ってもらいましたから。みんなの面倒を見るのは、私の仕事ですよ。
lines.kana: おれいなら、もうちゃんといってもらいましたから。みんなのめんどうをみるのは、わたしのしごとですよ。
lines.english: You've already thanked me properly, and that's plenty. Looking after everyone is my job.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: itsumo osewa ni natte bakari desu ne. gochisou ni narimashita. ashita, mata chanto orei o iwasete kudasai ne.
lines.ja: いつもお世話になってばかりですね。ごちそうになりました。明日、またちゃんとお礼を言わせてくださいね。
lines.kana: いつもおせわになってばかりですね。ごちそうになりました。あした、またちゃんとおれいをいわせてくださいね。
lines.english: I'm always the one being looked after. Thank you for dinner. Let me thank you properly again tomorrow.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sore jaa, itsu made mo owarimasen yo. ki o tsukete kaette kudasai ne.
lines.ja: それじゃあ、いつまでも終わりませんよ。気をつけて帰ってくださいね。
lines.kana: それじゃあ、いつまでもおわりませんよ。きをつけてかえってくださいね。
lines.english: At that rate, it'll never end. Get home safely, okay?

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Tanaka-san takes Mai out to thank her for her hard work, and in the end she pays.
Mai takes Tanaka-san out to thank him and means to pay, but he has already paid the bill.
Mai takes Tanaka-san out to thank him, and they agree to split the bill.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Mai has invited Tanaka-san out because he looked after her last month, and she wants to thank him properly (chanto orei o iitakute). In line 5 she asks to pay (watashi ni ogorasete kudasai) and in line 6 he seems to agree (gochisou ni narimasu). But when she goes to pay, he has already done it (mou harattemasu yo, line 14), and she protests in line 15. A swaps their roles: Mai is the one saying thanks, and she never gets to pay. C: nobody suggests splitting the bill; Tanaka-san pays all of it.

questions.english: Your friend Yuki tells you: "Tanaka-san helped me with all of yesterday's work." Ask whether she thanked him properly, or remind her that she should.
questions.ja: 昨日の仕事、田中さんが全部手伝ってくれたんだ。
questions.kana: きのうのしごと、たなかさんがぜんぶてつだってくれたんだ。
questions.romaji: kinou no shigoto, tanaka-san ga zenbu tetsudatte kureta n da.
questions.answer: Talk about the thanking with orei o iu: chanto orei itta? (did you thank him properly?) or ato de orei iwanakya ne (you'll have to thank him later).

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, chanto orei itta?
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、ちゃんとお礼言った？
modelAnswers.english: So did you thank him properly?

modelAnswers.romaji: yokatta ne. ato de chanto orei iwanakya ne.
modelAnswers.ja: よかったね。後でちゃんとお礼言わなきゃね。
modelAnswers.english: That's great. You'll need to thank him properly later.

questions.explanation: Saying thanks, as opposed to just feeling it, is orei o iu. Mai says chanto orei o iitakute (line 3) and ashita, mata chanto orei o iwasete kudasai ne (line 17), and Tanaka-san answers orei nara, mou chanto itte moraimashita (line 16). English 'thank' points to kansha suru, but kansha shita? asks whether she felt grateful, not whether she said it. orei o suru would mean giving something back, like the dinner Mai planned.

questions.english: Kenta's flatmate Sora meets you for the first time and is very formal with you. You're about the same age. Tell him he doesn't need to be formal.
questions.ja: はじめまして、ソラです。よろしくお願いします。
questions.kana: はじめまして、そらです。よろしくおねがいします。
questions.romaji: hajimemashite, sora desu. yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
questions.answer: Drop the formality with keigo o tsukau in the negative: keigo tsukawanakute ii yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: keigo tsukawanakute ii yo. yoroshiku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 敬語使わなくていいよ。よろしくね。
modelAnswers.english: No need to be formal with me. Nice to meet you.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, keigo wa tsukawanakute ii desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、敬語は使わなくていいですよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, you don't need to speak formally with me.

questions.explanation: The everyday verb with keigo is tsukau: Tanaka-san says keigo mo tsukawanakute ii desu yo (line 8), Mai answers tanaka-san mo keigo tsukattemasu yo (line 9) and then asks keigo tsukawasete kudasai (line 11). keigo o hanasu, built like nihongo o hanasu, is the English speaker's version. Don't swap in ki: ki o tsukawanakute ii means 'don't go to any trouble'. Tanaka-san says both in the same breath in line 8.

questions.english: When Mai says she wanted to thank him properly, what does Tanaka-san say?
questions.ja: 「お礼を言いたくて」と聞いて、田中さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: 「おれいをいいたくて」ときいて、たなかさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: orei o iitakute to kiite, tanaka-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: You didn't need to be so careful.
choices.romaji: sonna ni ki o tsukenakute ii noni.

choices.english: You didn't need to be so formal.
choices.romaji: sonna ni keigo o tsukawanakute ii noni.

choices.english: You didn't need to go to all that trouble.
choices.romaji: sonna ni ki o tsukawanakute ii noni.

questions.explanation: Line 4: sorede gohan desu ka. sonna ni ki o tsukawanakute ii noni. A thank-you dinner is more trouble than he thinks she needed to go to, and ki o tsukau is going to trouble for someone. A, ki o tsukenakute, is ki o tsukeru (be careful), the phrase in Tanaka-san's last line, ki o tsukete kaette kudasai ne (get home safely). B shares tsukau too, but Tanaka-san only brings up keigo later in the evening (line 8), not here.

questions.english: At the start, Mai tells Tanaka-san "hontou ni osewa ni narimashita" about last month. What does she mean?
questions.ja: 木村さんの「本当にお世話になりました」は、どういう意味ですか？
questions.kana: きむらさんの「ほんとうにおせわになりました」は、どういういみですか？
questions.romaji: kimura-san no hontou ni osewa ni narimashita wa, dou iu imi desu ka?

choices.english: She's thanking him for all his help when she had to take a week off for her sick cat.
She's reminding him that she covered his work for a week while he was away.
She's thanking him for looking after her cat while it was sick.

questions.explanation: Line 3: neko ga byouki de isshuukan mo shigoto o yasunde, hontou ni osewa ni narimashita. With ni naru, Mai is on the receiving end: she was the one looked after, through the week she was off work. She says it again at the end, itsumo osewa ni natte bakari desu ne (line 17). B turns it around; the one who does the looking after says mendou o miru, as Tanaka-san does in line 16 (minna no mendou o miru no wa, watashi no shigoto desu yo). C reads osewa as literal pet care, but nothing in the scene says Tanaka-san minded the cat; Mai stayed home with it.

questions.english: Tanaka-san takes you out to lunch and says: "Today's on me, so order whatever you like." Accept his offer politely.
questions.ja: 今日は私がおごりますから、好きなもの頼んでくださいね。
questions.kana: きょうはわたしがおごりますから、すきなものたのんでくださいね。
questions.romaji: kyou wa watashi ga ogorimasu kara, suki na mono tanonde kudasai ne.
questions.answer: Accept the treat with gochisou ni narimasu: jaa, gochisou ni narimasu.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. jaa, gochisou ni narimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。じゃあ、ごちそうになります。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. Then I'll gladly let you treat me.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii n desu ka? jaa, kyou wa gochisou ni narimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: いいんですか？じゃあ、今日はごちそうになります。
modelAnswers.english: Are you sure? Then I'll let you treat me today.

questions.explanation: With ni naru you are the one being treated. That's how Tanaka-san accepts Mai's offer in line 6 (jaa, kyou wa gochisou ni narimasu), and Mai uses the past, gochisou ni narimashita, to thank him afterwards (line 17). The payer's verbs are ogoru and gochisou suru, like Mai's watashi ni ogorasete kudasai (line 5), so gochisou shimasu here would mean you're paying. The passive gochisou saremasu is heard but much less usual.

newWords.english: a week (isshuukan mo = a whole week)

script.title: Why Kenji did the dishes
script.setting: Okaasan leaves a voice message for her daughter Yuki about Yuki's little brother Kenji, who was suddenly very helpful in the kitchen last night.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? okaasan da kedo. kinou no kenji, sugokatta no yo.
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？お母さんだけど。昨日のケンジ、すごかったのよ。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？おかあさんだけど。きのうのけんじ、すごかったのよ。
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? It's Mum. You should have seen Kenji last night.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: gochisousama tte ittara, sugu osara arattoku yo tte. tanonde nai noni.
lines.ja: ごちそうさまって言ったら、すぐ「お皿洗っとくよ」って。頼んでないのに。
lines.kana: ごちそうさまっていったら、すぐ「おさらあらっとくよ」って。たのんでないのに。
lines.english: The moment we'd said thanks for the meal, he goes, 'I'll do the dishes.' I hadn't even asked!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: osara zenbu aratte, teeburu mo chanto fuite kureta no.
lines.ja: お皿全部洗って、テーブルもちゃんと拭いてくれたの。
lines.kana: おさらぜんぶあらって、テーブルもちゃんとふいてくれたの。
lines.english: He washed every single plate, and gave the table a proper wipe too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sorekara oyu wakasu kedo, nanka nomu? tte. ocha made motte kite kureta no.
lines.ja: それから「お湯沸かすけど、なんか飲む？」って。お茶まで持ってきてくれたの。
lines.kana: それから「おゆわかすけど、なんかのむ？」って。おちゃまでもってきてくれたの。
lines.english: Then he says, 'I'm putting the kettle on, want anything?' He even brought me a cup of tea.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mae wa oyu mo wakasenakatta noni ne. yatto otona ni natta naa tte omotta no.
lines.ja: 前はお湯も沸かせなかったのにね。やっと大人になったなあって思ったの。
lines.kana: まえはおゆもわかせなかったのにね。やっとおとなになったなあっておもったの。
lines.english: This from a boy who couldn't even boil water! I thought, he's finally grown up.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo ne, kesa gomi o dasou to shitara, naka ni wareta osara ga haitteta no.
lines.ja: でもね、今朝ゴミを出そうとしたら、中に割れたお皿が入ってたの。
lines.kana: でもね、けさごみをだそうとしたら、なかにわれたおさらがはいってたの。
lines.english: But this morning, when I went to take the rubbish out, there was a broken plate in it.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: okaasan no daiji na osara. kinou, kenji ga watchatta no ne.
lines.ja: お母さんの大事なお皿。昨日、ケンジが割っちゃったのね。
lines.kana: おかあさんのだいじなおさら。きのう、けんじがわっちゃったのね。
lines.english: My favourite plate. Kenji must have broken it yesterday.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dakara kyuu ni, osara arattari, teeburu fuitari shite kureta no ne.
lines.ja: だから急に、お皿洗ったり、テーブル拭いたりしてくれたのね。
lines.kana: だからきゅうに、おさらあらったり、テーブルふいたりしてくれたのね。
lines.english: So that's why he was suddenly washing the dishes and wiping the table for me.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: okottenai yo. kesa mo, mou oyu wakashite kureteta shi ne.
lines.ja: 怒ってないよ。今朝も、もうお湯沸かしてくれてたしね。
lines.kana: おこってないよ。けさも、もうおゆわかしてくれてたしね。
lines.english: I'm not angry. He even had the kettle on for me again this morning.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo, okaasan ga shitteru koto, kenji ni wa naisho ni shite ne. mou chotto tetsudatte hoshii kara.
lines.ja: でも、お母さんが知ってること、ケンジには内緒にしてね。もうちょっと手伝ってほしいから。
lines.kana: でも、おかあさんがしってること、けんじにはないしょにしてね。もうちょっとてつだってほしいから。
lines.english: But don't tell Kenji I know, OK? I want a bit more help out of him first.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa ne. yuki mo kondo kaette kitara, teeburu kurai fuite ne.
lines.ja: じゃあね。ユキも今度帰ってきたら、テーブルくらい拭いてね。
lines.kana: じゃあね。ゆきもこんどかえってきたら、テーブルくらいふいてね。
lines.english: Bye now. And next time you're home, you could at least wipe the table too.

questions.english: What is Mum's message about?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji broke Mum's favourite plate, and she's angry and wants Yuki to have a word with him.
Kenji suddenly started helping because he wants something from Mum, and she wants Yuki to find out what.
Kenji was suddenly helpful in the kitchen because he'd broken Mum's favourite plate; she isn't angry, but wants Yuki to keep quiet so he keeps helping.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-4: without being asked, Kenji washed the dishes, wiped the table and put the kettle on, and in line 5 Mum thought he'd finally grown up. Lines 6-8: taking the rubbish out this morning, she found her favourite plate broken in it and worked out why he'd been so helpful (dakara kyuu ni ... shite kureta no ne). Lines 9-10: she isn't angry (okottenai yo), and asks Yuki not to tell Kenji she knows, because she wants a bit more help out of him. A is wrong because she says she isn't angry and wants it kept secret, not a talking-to. B is wrong because Mum already knows the reason; she asks Yuki to keep a secret, not to find anything out.

questions.english: You've just eaten a dinner Kenta cooked for you at his flat. He asks: "So? Are you full?" Thank him and offer to do the dishes.
questions.ja: どう？おなかいっぱいになった？
questions.kana: どう？おなかいっぱいになった？
questions.romaji: dou? onaka ippai ni natta?
questions.answer: Thank him and offer to wash up with osara (o) arau: un, gochisousama! osara wa watashi ga arau ne. Not osara o suru.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, gochisousama! osara wa watashi ga arau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、ごちそうさま！お皿は私が洗うね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, thanks, that was lovely! I'll do the dishes.

modelAnswers.romaji: onaka ippai! tsukutte kureta kara, osara arattoku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: おなかいっぱい！作ってくれたから、お皿洗っとくね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm stuffed! You cooked, so I'll wash up.

questions.explanation: Washing up is osara (o) arau, the same offer Kenji makes in line 2 (osara arattoku yo), and in line 3 he does it (osara zenbu aratte). English 'do the dishes' tempts osara o suru, but suru doesn't go with osara. If you want suru, put it on the chore noun instead: sara-arai suru or araimono suru (araimono shitoku ne). Saying osara wa watashi ga arau ne ('the dishes, I'll do') makes it an offer.

questions.english: Mum quotes what Kenji asked her after he'd washed up. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンジくんは、お母さんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんは、おかあさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-kun wa, okaasan ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: I'm simmering some water, want anything?
I'm putting the kettle on, want anything?
I'm boiling up some water, want anything?

questions.explanation: Line 4: Mum quotes Kenji, oyu wakasu kedo, nanka nomu?, and in line 9 he had the water on again this morning (oyu wakashite kureteta). Water is heated with wakasu, and it's already called oyu (hot water) before it boils. A uses niru, where English 'boil' often points, but niru is simmering food (vegetables, fish) in a broth, never water on its own. C uses yuderu, which is boiling food in water (eggs, pasta, noodles): you yuderu the egg, not the water. Line 5 uses the same verb as the right answer: oyu mo wakasenakatta, 'couldn't even boil water'.

questions.english: You're cooking dinner at your parents' place, and it's nearly ready. Your mum comes in and asks: "Want me to help with anything?" Ask her to give the table a wipe.
questions.ja: なんか手伝おうか？
questions.kana: なんかてつだおうか？
questions.romaji: nanka tetsudaou ka?
questions.answer: Ask for a wipe with teeburu (o) fuku as a casual request: jaa, teeburu fuite kureru? A table gets wiped with a cloth (fuku), not washed (arau).

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, teeburu fuite kureru?
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、テーブル拭いてくれる？
modelAnswers.english: Then could you give the table a wipe?

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. mou sugu dekiru kara, teeburu fuitoite.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。もうすぐできるから、テーブル拭いといて。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. It's nearly ready, so could you wipe the table?

questions.explanation: Wiping with a cloth is fuku: Kenji gave the table a wipe (teeburu mo chanto fuite kureta, line 3; teeburu fuitari, line 8), and Mum's parting shot in line 11, teeburu kurai fuite ne, is the same request you're making. Don't say teeburu o arau: arau is washing with water, which is what happened to the dishes in the same breath (osara zenbu aratte, teeburu mo ... fuite). And souji suru is for cleaning a room or the whole house; a table just gets a wipe. -te kureru? or -toite (fuite oite, 'get it done') turns it into a casual request.

newWords.english: break, get broken (wareta osara = a broken plate)
at least, even just (teeburu kurai = at least the table)

script.title: One more match
script.setting: A Saturday evening at home. Kenji, Yuki's little brother, is slumped on the sofa playing a football video game when Yuki comes in with some news.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji, mata sono geemu shiteru no? kinou mo osoku made shiteta desho.
lines.ja: ケンジ、またそのゲームしてるの？昨日も遅くまでしてたでしょ。
lines.kana: けんじ、またそのげーむしてるの？きのうもおそくまでしてたでしょ。
lines.english: Kenji, playing that game again? You were on it till late last night too, weren't you?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. saikin, kono geemu ni metcha hamatteru n da.
lines.ja: うん。最近、このゲームにめっちゃハマってるんだ。
lines.kana: うん。さいきん、このげーむにめっちゃはまってるんだ。
lines.english: Yeah. I'm totally hooked on this game lately.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sakkaa no geemu ka. de, tsuyoi no?
lines.ja: サッカーのゲームか。で、強いの？
lines.kana: さっかーのげーむか。で、つよいの？
lines.english: A football game, huh. So, are you any good?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: uun. kyou no shiai, zenbu maketa.
lines.ja: ううん。今日の試合、全部負けた。
lines.kana: ううん。きょうのしあい、ぜんぶまけた。
lines.english: Nah. I lost every match today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: zenbu? dakara kigen warui n da.
lines.ja: 全部？だから機嫌悪いんだ。
lines.kana: ぜんぶ？だからきげんわるいんだ。
lines.english: Every one? No wonder you're in a mood.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: warukunai yo. nani, sono kao?
lines.ja: 悪くないよ。何、その顔？
lines.kana: わるくないよ。なに、そのかお？
lines.english: I'm not in a mood. What's with that face?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nee, kiite! raishuu no nihon to kankoku no shiai, chiketto toreta no!
lines.ja: ねえ、聞いて！来週の日本と韓国の試合、チケット取れたの！
lines.kana: ねえ、きいて！らいしゅうのにほんとかんこくのしあい、ちけっととれたの！
lines.english: Hey, listen! I got tickets for next week's Japan–Korea match!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, uso! sore, chiketto zettai torenai tte, minna itteta yo. dare ni moratta no?
lines.ja: え、うそ！それ、チケット絶対取れないって、みんな言ってたよ。誰にもらったの？
lines.kana: え、うそ！それ、ちけっとぜったいとれないって、みんないってたよ。だれにもらったの？
lines.english: What, no way! Everyone said you'd never get tickets for that. Who gave them to you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: moratta n ja nai yo. jibun de totta no! juuji kara ichijikan, zutto sumaho mitete.
lines.ja: もらったんじゃないよ。自分で取ったの！10時から1時間、ずっとスマホ見てて。
lines.kana: もらったんじゃないよ。じぶんでとったの！じゅうじからいちじかん、ずっとすまほみてて。
lines.english: Nobody gave them to me. I got them myself! I was glued to my phone for an hour from ten o'clock.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sugoi. ii naa. dare to iku no?
lines.ja: すごい。いいなあ。誰と行くの？
lines.kana: すごい。いいなあ。だれといくの？
lines.english: Wow. Lucky you. Who are you going with?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji to da yo. ichimai wa kenji no.
lines.ja: ケンジとだよ。一枚はケンジの。
lines.kana: けんじとだよ。いちまいはけんじの。
lines.english: With you! One of them's yours.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: honto ni? yatta! kono mae no shiai wa maketa kedo, kondo wa zettai katsu yo.
lines.ja: ほんとに？やった！この前の試合は負けたけど、今度は絶対勝つよ。
lines.kana: ほんとに？やった！このまえのしあいはまけたけど、こんどはぜったいかつよ。
lines.english: Seriously? Yes! We lost last time, but this time we're definitely winning.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, sou da. sono geemu de mo, nihon to kankoku no shiai, dekiru?
lines.ja: あ、そうだ。そのゲームでも、日本と韓国の試合、できる？
lines.kana: あ、そうだ。そのげーむでも、にほんとかんこくのしあい、できる？
lines.english: Oh, I know. Can you play Japan against Korea in that game too?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: dekiru yo. yatte miru? kekkou muzukashii kedo.
lines.ja: できるよ。やってみる？けっこう難しいけど。
lines.kana: できるよ。やってみる？けっこうむずかしいけど。
lines.english: Yeah. Want to try? It's pretty hard, though.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yatta! katta! kankoku ni katta yo!
lines.ja: やった！勝った！韓国に勝ったよ！
lines.kana: やった！かった！かんこくにかったよ！
lines.english: Yes! I won! I beat Korea!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, hajimete no shiai ni katta no? kotchi wa kyou, zenbu maketa noni.
lines.ja: え、初めての試合に勝ったの？こっちは今日、全部負けたのに。
lines.kana: え、はじめてのしあいにかったの？こっちはきょう、ぜんぶまけたのに。
lines.english: What, you won your very first match? I lost every single one today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un! kenji ga kono geemu ni hamaru no, wakaru. mou ikkai!
lines.ja: うん！ケンジがこのゲームにハマるの、わかる。もう一回！
lines.kana: うん！けんじがこのげーむにはまるの、わかる。もういっかい！
lines.english: Yep! I totally get why you're hooked on this game. One more!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sakki made monku itteta noni. mou hamatteru jan.
lines.ja: さっきまで文句言ってたのに。もうハマってるじゃん。
lines.kana: さっきまでもんくいってたのに。もうはまってるじゃん。
lines.english: A minute ago you were complaining about it. Now you're hooked yourself.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: A friend gave Yuki tickets to the Japan–Korea match, and she says Kenji can only come if he stops playing his game.
Yuki got tickets to the Japan–Korea match for herself and Kenji, then tried his game, won, and got hooked on it herself.
Yuki got tickets to the Japan–Korea match, but she won't take Kenji because he lost every match in his game.

questions.explanation: Line 7: Yuki got tickets (chiketto toreta) for next week's Japan–Korea match, and in line 9 she says she got them herself. Line 11: one of the two is Kenji's (ichimai wa kenji no). Lines 13-15: she plays Japan against Korea in his game and wins. Lines 17-18: she wants another go, and Kenji points out she's hooked now (mou hamatteru jan). A is wrong: nobody gave her the tickets (line 9: moratta n ja nai yo), and she never sets a condition. C is wrong: Kenji does lose every match today (line 4), but Yuki is taking him (line 11).

questions.english: Yuki asks what you've been doing at weekends lately. Tell her you're hooked on a game right now, using hamaru.
questions.ja: 最近、週末は何してるの？
questions.kana: さいきん、しゅうまつはなにしてるの？
questions.romaji: saikin, shuumatsu wa nani shiteru no?
questions.answer: Say what you're into right now with ni and hamatteru (am hooked): saikin, geemu ni hamatteru n da. Keep ni, never o. To explain why it eats your weekends, geemu ni hamatchatte (I've got hooked, so...) works well.

modelAnswers.romaji: saikin, sakkaa no geemu ni hamatteru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 最近、サッカーのゲームにハマってるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Lately I'm hooked on a football game.

modelAnswers.romaji: geemu ni hamatchatte, shuumatsu wa zutto uchi ni iru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ゲームにハマっちゃって、週末はずっとうちにいるよ。
modelAnswers.english: I've got hooked on a game, so I'm home all weekend.

questions.explanation: Kenji says 'saikin, kono geemu ni metcha hamatteru n da' in line 2, and Yuki uses the same pair in line 17 (kono geemu ni hamaru no, wakaru). The game takes ni, not o. 'geemu ga suki' would only say you like games in general; hamatteru says you're into one right now. Yuki is a friend asking casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Yuki plays her first match in Kenji's game. What does she shout at the end of it?
questions.ja: ユキは、ゲームの試合のあとで、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきは、げーむのしあいのあとで、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki wa, geemu no shiai no ato de, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I beat Korea! (with o, as in English)
I lost to Korea!
I beat Korea!

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'yatta! katta! kankoku ni katta yo!' The team you beat takes ni, just like the match itself: Kenji answers 'hajimete no shiai ni katta no?' (line 16). A follows English 'beat Korea' with o, but katsu never takes o, and o katta sounds like the past of kau (buy), so it comes out as 'I bought Korea!'. B is the opposite result: maketa means lost, but Yuki shouts yatta! and Kenji can't believe she won her very first match.

questions.english: Yuki asks Kenji if he's any good at his football game, and he says, "kyou no shiai, zenbu maketa." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンジは、今日どうでしたか？
questions.kana: けんじは、きょうどうでしたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa, kyou dou deshita ka?

choices.english: He lost every match he played in the game today.
All his saved games got wiped today.
He missed all of today's matches on TV.

questions.explanation: Line 4: makeru is losing a contest, and these are the matches Kenji plays in his football game (Yuki has just asked if he's any good at it, line 3). He says it again in line 16 (kotchi wa kyou, zenbu maketa noni) when Yuki wins her first match. B mixes makeru up with losing a thing, which is nakusu in Japanese, never makeru. C is missing a match, not losing one, and nobody mentions TV.

questions.english: You've got tickets for a sold-out football match. Kenta can't believe it and asks you this. Tell him nobody gave them to you: you got them yourself.
questions.ja: え、あの試合のチケット？誰にもらったの？
questions.kana: え、あのしあいのちけっと？だれにもらったの？
questions.romaji: e, ano shiai no chiketto? dare ni moratta no?
questions.answer: Say you got them yourself with toru: jibun de totta (or yatto toreta, finally managed to get them). moratta is what Kenta is asking about (someone gave them to you), so you can set the two against each other: moratta n ja nai yo, jibun de totta n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: moratta n ja nai yo. jibun de totta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: もらったんじゃないよ。自分で取ったんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Nobody gave them to me. I got them myself.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, jibun de totta yo. ichijikan kakatta kedo, yatto toreta.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、自分で取ったよ。1時間かかったけど、やっと取れた。
modelAnswers.english: No, I got them myself. It took an hour, but I finally got them.

questions.explanation: In line 9 Yuki answers Kenji's 'dare ni moratta no?' the same way: 'moratta n ja nai yo. jibun de totta no!' Tickets you get hold of yourself are chiketto o toru, and 'I got them!' is toreta (line 7: chiketto toreta no!; line 8: chiketto zettai torenai, there's no way to get any). moratta means someone gave them to you, which is exactly what you're denying. katta (bought) isn't wrong, but it doesn't say you managed to get hold of them. Kenta is a friend, so answer casually.

script.title: Left at the second corner
script.setting: A Saturday morning outside their building. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, has to go to a new hospital by the station next week and is worried about getting lost: last week he turned at the wrong corner and ended up an hour late. Yuki offers to go with him, and he reminds her of the day she got lost at that same station when she was five.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, satou-san, ohayou gozaimasu. dou shita n desu ka? komatta kao shitemasu ne.
lines.ja: あ、佐藤さん、おはようございます。どうしたんですか？困った顔してますね。
lines.kana: あ、さとうさん、おはようございます。どうしたんですか？こまったかおしてますね。
lines.english: Oh, Satou-san, good morning. Is something wrong? You look worried.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: aa, yuki-san, ohayou gozaimasu. raishuu, eki no chikaku no atarashii byouin ni iku n desu ga, michi ni mayowanai ka shinpai de.
lines.ja: ああ、ユキさん、おはようございます。来週、駅の近くの新しい病院に行くんですが、道に迷わないか心配で。
lines.kana: ああ、ゆきさん、おはようございます。らいしゅう、えきのちかくのあたらしいびょういんにいくんですが、みちにまよわないかしんぱいで。
lines.english: Ah, Yuki-san, good morning. I'm going to the new hospital near the station next week, and I'm worried I'll get lost.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, ano byouin nara kantan desu yo. eki o dete, futatsume no kado o hidari ni magaru dake desu.
lines.ja: ああ、あの病院なら簡単ですよ。駅を出て、二つ目の角を左に曲がるだけです。
lines.kana: ああ、あのびょういんならかんたんですよ。えきをでて、ふたつめのかどをひだりにまがるだけです。
lines.english: Oh, that hospital's easy. You come out of the station and just turn left at the second corner.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore ga desu ne, senshuu ichido itta n desu ga, michi o machigaete shimatte.
lines.ja: それがですね、先週一度行ったんですが、道を間違えてしまって。
lines.kana: それがですね、せんしゅういちどいったんですが、みちをまちがえてしまって。
lines.english: Well, you see, I went once last week, but I went the wrong way.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, doko de machigaeta n desu ka?
lines.ja: え、どこで間違えたんですか？
lines.kana: え、どこでまちがえたんですか？
lines.english: Oh no, where did you go wrong?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hitotsume no kado o, hidari ni magatte shimatta n desu. futatsume da to wa shiranakute.
lines.ja: 一つ目の角を、左に曲がってしまったんです。二つ目だとは知らなくて。
lines.kana: ひとつめのかどを、ひだりにまがってしまったんです。ふたつめだとはしらなくて。
lines.english: I turned left at the first corner. I didn't know it was the second one.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, eki no mae wa kado ga ippai arimasu kara ne. sore wa michi ni mayoimasu yo ne.
lines.ja: ああ、駅の前は角がいっぱいありますからね。それは道に迷いますよね。
lines.kana: ああ、えきのまえはかどがいっぱいありますからね。それはみちにまよいますよね。
lines.english: Ah, there are so many corners outside the station. No wonder you got lost.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore kara wa, doko ni iru no ka mo wakaranakute. nanajuugo ni mo natte, maigo ni naru to wa omoimasen deshita yo.
lines.ja: それからは、どこにいるのかもわからなくて。七十五にもなって、迷子になるとは思いませんでしたよ。
lines.kana: それからは、どこにいるのかもわからなくて。ななじゅうごにもなって、まいごになるとはおもいませんでしたよ。
lines.english: After that I didn't even know where I was. I never thought I'd end up a lost child at seventy-five.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, raishuu wa watashi mo issho ni ikimasu yo. futari nara, michi ni mayoimasen kara.
lines.ja: じゃあ、来週は私も一緒に行きますよ。二人なら、道に迷いませんから。
lines.kana: じゃあ、らいしゅうはわたしもいっしょにいきますよ。ふたりなら、みちにまよいませんから。
lines.english: Then I'll come with you next week. With two of us, we won't get lost.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. demo yuki-san, oboete imasu ka? mukashi, ano eki de maigo ni natta koto.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。でもユキさん、覚えていますか？昔、あの駅で迷子になったこと。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。でもゆきさん、おぼえていますか？むかし、あのえきでまいごになったこと。
lines.english: Thank you. But Yuki-san, do you remember? The time you got lost at that station, years ago.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, watashi ga maigo ni natta n desu ka? oboete nai desu.
lines.ja: え、私が迷子になったんですか？覚えてないです。
lines.kana: え、わたしがまいごになったんですか？おぼえてないです。
lines.english: What, I got lost? I don't remember that.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: gosai gurai deshita ka ne. eki no mae de hitori de, okaasan o sagashite imashita yo.
lines.ja: 五歳ぐらいでしたかね。駅の前で一人で、お母さんを探していましたよ。
lines.kana: ごさいぐらいでしたかね。えきのまえでひとりで、おかあさんをさがしていましたよ。
lines.english: You must have been about five. You were outside the station all alone, looking for your mother.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore de, dou natta n desu ka?
lines.ja: それで、どうなったんですか？
lines.kana: それで、どうなったんですか？
lines.english: So what happened?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: watashi ga uchi made okutta n desu ga, yuki-san ga kotchi! hidari ni magaru no! tte itte kikanakute.
lines.ja: 私がうちまで送ったんですが、ユキさんが「こっち！左に曲がるの！」って言って聞かなくて。
lines.kana: わたしがうちまでおくったんですが、ゆきさんが「こっち！ひだりにまがるの！」っていってきかなくて。
lines.english: I walked you home, but you kept insisting, 'This way! We turn left!' and wouldn't listen.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, demo uchi wa, eki kara migi desu yo ne?
lines.ja: え、でもうちは、駅から右ですよね？
lines.kana: え、でもうちは、えきからみぎですよね？
lines.english: Wait, but home is to the right from the station, isn't it?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ee. futari de michi o machigaete, ichijikan mo kakarimashita yo.
lines.ja: ええ。二人で道を間違えて、一時間もかかりましたよ。
lines.kana: ええ。ふたりでみちをまちがえて、いちじかんもかかりましたよ。
lines.english: Yes. We went the wrong way together, and it took us a whole hour.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sumimasen deshita! raishuu wa chanto, futatsume no kado o hidari ni magarimasu kara.
lines.ja: すみませんでした！来週はちゃんと、二つ目の角を左に曲がりますから。
lines.kana: すみませんでした！らいしゅうはちゃんと、ふたつめのかどをひだりにまがりますから。
lines.english: I'm so sorry! Next week I'll turn left at the second corner, properly. I promise.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai. kondo wa, michi o machigaenaide kudasai ne.
lines.ja: はい。今度は、道を間違えないでくださいね。
lines.kana: はい。こんどは、みちをまちがえないでくださいね。
lines.english: Yes. This time, please don't take us the wrong way.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Satou-san got lost on his way to the hospital last week, so Yuki offers to drive him there, and he tells her how he once got lost as a boy.
Satou-san is worried about getting lost on the way to a new hospital. Yuki offers to go with him, and he reminds her of the time she got lost as a little girl and led them both the wrong way.
Yuki got lost on her way to the new hospital last week, and Satou-san explains that you turn left at the second corner.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Satou-san is going to the new hospital next week and is worried he'll get lost (michi ni mayowanai ka shinpai de). Line 9: Yuki says she'll go with him. In lines 10-16 he reminds her that she got lost at the station when she was about five (maigo ni natta), and that when he walked her home she insisted on turning left, so the two of them went the wrong way. A gets the memory backwards: Yuki was the lost child, not Satou-san, and she offers to go with him (issho ni ikimasu), not to drive. C swaps their roles: Satou-san is the one who went wrong last week (lines 4-6), and Yuki gives the directions (line 3).

questions.english: Tanaka-san is giving you a lift home after work. Near your place he asks: "Which way next?" Ask him to turn left at the next corner.
questions.ja: 次はどっちですか？
questions.kana: つぎはどっちですか？
questions.romaji: tsugi wa dotchi desu ka?
questions.answer: Ask politely for a left turn with hidari ni magaru, the side marked with ni: tsugi no kado o hidari ni magatte kudasai.

modelAnswers.romaji: tsugi no kado o hidari ni magatte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: 次の角を左に曲がってください。
modelAnswers.english: Please turn left at the next corner.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, tsugi, hidari ni magatte moraemasu ka?
modelAnswers.ja: あ、次、左に曲がってもらえますか？
modelAnswers.english: Oh, could you turn left next?

questions.explanation: Turning is magaru and the side takes ni: Yuki's directions are futatsume no kado o hidari ni magaru (line 3), and little Yuki's insistence was hidari ni magaru no! (line 14). Not hidari ni mawaru: mawaru is spinning or going round something. If you name the corner, it takes o (or de): tsugi no kado o hidari ni. In a taxi the verb often drops: tsugi, hidari de onegai shimasu.

questions.english: How does Yuki first explain the way to the hospital?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、病院までどう行くと言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、びょういんまでどういくといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, byouin made dou iku to iimashita ka?

choices.english: You just turn left at the second corner.
choices.romaji: futatsume no kado o hidari ni magaru dake desu.

choices.english: You just turn left into the second corner.
choices.romaji: futatsume no kado ni hidari ni magaru dake desu.

choices.english: You just go round to the left at the second corner.
choices.romaji: futatsume no kado o hidari ni mawaru dake desu.

questions.explanation: Line 3: eki o dete, futatsume no kado o hidari ni magaru dake desu, and she promises the same in line 17. The corner takes o because you go round it, and the side takes ni, so one sentence holds both: kado o hidari ni magaru. B puts ni on the corner, as English 'turn into the corner' suggests, but ni already marks the side, so kado ni hidari ni sounds broken. C uses mawaru, which is spinning or going round something; a turn at a corner with a side named is magaru.

questions.english: You're walking to meet friends in a part of town you don't know, and you have no idea where you are. Kenta calls: "Hello? Where are you? Everyone's already here." Tell him you've got lost.
questions.ja: もしもし、今どこ？もうみんな来てるよ。
questions.kana: もしもし、いまどこ？もうみんなきてるよ。
questions.romaji: moshimoshi, ima doko? mou minna kiteru yo.
questions.answer: Say you're lost with michi ni mayou, usually as mayotta or mayotchatta: gomen, michi ni mayotchatta.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, michi ni mayotchatta. chotto okureru.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、道に迷っちゃった。ちょっと遅れる。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got lost. I'll be a bit late.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, ima michi ni mayottete, doko ni iru ka wakannai.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今道に迷ってて、どこにいるかわかんない。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'm lost right now. I don't know where I am.

questions.explanation: Being lost, with no idea where you are, is michi ni mayou: Satou-san worries michi ni mayowanai ka (line 2), and Yuki says sore wa michi ni mayoimasu yo ne (line 7). Not michi o nakusu: nakusu is for losing things like keys. michi machigaeta would only say you took a wrong road, and maigo ni natta would make you sound like a child who has lost their parents.

questions.english: Satou-san says he went the wrong way last week. What had he done?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは先週、どこで道を間違えましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんはせんしゅう、どこでみちをまちがえましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa senshuu, doko de michi o machigaemashita ka?

choices.english: He got off the train at the wrong station.
He turned right at the second corner instead of left.
He turned left at the first corner instead of the second.

questions.explanation: Line 4: michi o machigaete shimatte, and line 6 says where: hitotsume no kado o, hidari ni magatte shimatta n desu. futatsume da to wa shiranakute. michi o machigaeru is taking the wrong road on a route; what came after, not knowing where he was (line 8), is michi ni mayou. A: his mistake came after he left the station; a wrong stop would be eki o machigaeta. B: he did turn left, as he should have; it was the corner he got wrong.

questions.english: You and Sora are at a packed fireworks festival. He says: "Wow, so many people. I'm just popping to the toilet." Tell him, half joking, not to get lost.
questions.ja: うわ、すごい人。ちょっとトイレ行ってくるね。
questions.kana: うわ、すごいひと。ちょっとトイレいってくるね。
questions.romaji: uwa, sugoi hito. chotto toire itte kuru ne.
questions.answer: Tell him not to wander off with maigo ni naru in the -naide form: maigo ni naranaide ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: un. hito ooi kara, maigo ni naranaide ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん。人多いから、迷子にならないでね。
modelAnswers.english: Okay. There are loads of people, so don't get lost.

modelAnswers.romaji: wakatta. maigo ni nattara, denwa shite ne.
modelAnswers.ja: わかった。迷子になったら、電話してね。
modelAnswers.english: Got it. If you get lost, give me a call.

questions.explanation: maigo is a noun, 'lost child', so you become one: maigo ni naru, never maigo suru. It is for getting separated in a crowd, like five-year-old Yuki outside the station looking for her mother (lines 10-12), and adults use it of themselves half-jokingly, as Satou-san does in line 8. Being lost on the road with nobody to be separated from is michi ni mayou.

newWords.english: the first, the second (counting along: futatsume no kado = the second corner)
two people; the two of us (futari de = together)

script.title: The last problem
script.setting: Monday evening at the café where Sora works part-time. Mai drops in on her way home from work and finds Sora on his break, frowning over a sheet of maths homework.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, sora-kun. kyuukei totteru no? sore, nani?
lines.ja: あ、ソラくん。休憩取ってるの？それ、何？
lines.kana: あ、そらくん。きゅうけいとってるの？それ、なに？
lines.english: Oh, Sora. Are you on your break? What's that?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, mai-san. kore? suugaku no shukudai.
lines.ja: あ、マイさん。これ？数学の宿題。
lines.kana: あ、まいさん。これ？すうがくのしゅくだい。
lines.english: Oh, hi Mai. This? Maths homework.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? sora-kun ga shukudai shiteru no?
lines.ja: え？ソラくんが宿題してるの？
lines.kana: え？そらくんがしゅくだいしてるの？
lines.english: Huh? You're doing homework?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: chigau chigau, kenji-kun no da yo. yuki-san ni tanomarete, kayoubi to kin'youbi ni benkyou oshieteru n da.
lines.ja: 違う違う、ケンジくんのだよ。ユキさんに頼まれて、火曜日と金曜日に勉強教えてるんだ。
lines.kana: ちがうちがう、けんじくんのだよ。ゆきさんにたのまれて、かようびときんようびにべんきょうおしえてるんだ。
lines.english: No, no, it's Kenji's. Yuki asked me to help him study, so I tutor him on Tuesdays and Fridays.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: aa, kenji-kun ne. jibun de shukudai shinai no?
lines.ja: ああ、ケンジくんね。自分で宿題しないの？
lines.kana: ああ、けんじくんね。じぶんでしゅくだいしないの？
lines.english: Oh, Kenji. Doesn't he do his homework on his own?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: shukudai wa chanto suru n da yo. demo, dasu no o wasurechau n da.
lines.ja: 宿題はちゃんとするんだよ。でも、出すのを忘れちゃうんだ。
lines.kana: しゅくだいはちゃんとするんだよ。でも、だすのをわすれちゃうんだ。
lines.english: Oh, he does his homework all right. He just forgets to hand it in.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, shukudai shita noni, dasanai no?
lines.ja: え、宿題したのに、出さないの？
lines.kana: え、しゅくだいしたのに、ださないの？
lines.english: What, he does the homework and then doesn't hand it in?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sou na n da yo. dakara seiseki ga yokunakute, yuki-san ga shinpai shiteru n da.
lines.ja: そうなんだよ。だから成績がよくなくて、ユキさんが心配してるんだ。
lines.kana: そうなんだよ。だからせいせきがよくなくて、ゆきさんがしんぱいしてるんだ。
lines.english: I know. So his grades aren't good, and Yuki's worried about him.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, ashita, shukudai chanto dashita ka, kiite mitara?
lines.ja: じゃあ、明日、宿題ちゃんと出したか、聞いてみたら？
lines.kana: じゃあ、あした、しゅくだいちゃんとだしたか、きいてみたら？
lines.english: Then why not ask him tomorrow whether he actually handed it in?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, sou suru. de, ashita no mondai o saki ni toitoku n da kedo, saigo no ga tokenai n da yo.
lines.ja: うん、そうする。で、明日の問題を先に解いとくんだけど、最後のが解けないんだよ。
lines.kana: うん、そうする。で、あしたのもんだいをさきにといとくんだけど、さいごのがとけないんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, I will. Anyway, I'm working through tomorrow's problems ahead of time, but I can't get the last one.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: chotto misete. aa, kore, kou yatte toku n ja nai kana. jishin nai kedo.
lines.ja: ちょっと見せて。ああ、これ、こうやって解くんじゃないかな。自信ないけど。
lines.kana: ちょっとみせて。ああ、これ、こうやってとくんじゃないかな。じしんないけど。
lines.english: Let me see. Oh, I think maybe you solve it like this? I'm not sure, though.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e? a, honto da, toketa! mai-san, zettai seiseki yokatta desho?
