lines.ja: え？あ、ほんとだ、解けた！マイさん、絶対成績よかったでしょ？
lines.kana: え？あ、ほんとだ、とけた！まいさん、ぜったいせいせきよかったでしょ？
lines.english: Huh? Oh, you're right, I've got it! Mai, I bet you had great grades.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, suugaku dake da yo. hoka wa zenbu dame datta.
lines.ja: ううん、数学だけだよ。ほかは全部ダメだった。
lines.kana: ううん、すうがくだけだよ。ほかはぜんぶだめだった。
lines.english: No, only in maths. I was hopeless at everything else.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, kondo kenji-kun ni mo oshiete yo. mai-san ga oshietara, kitto seiseki yoku naru yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、今度ケンジくんにも教えてよ。マイさんが教えたら、きっと成績よくなるよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、こんどけんじくんにもおしえてよ。まいさんがおしえたら、きっとせいせきよくなるよ。
lines.english: Then come and teach Kenji too sometime. If you taught him, I bet his grades would go up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, muri muri. watashi, oshieru no nigate da shi.
lines.ja: え、無理無理。私、教えるの苦手だし。
lines.kana: え、むりむり。わたし、おしえるのにがてだし。
lines.english: Oh, no way. I'm no good at teaching.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, hitotsu dake onegai. boku ga kono mondai tokenakatta koto, kenji-kun ni wa naisho ni shite ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、一つだけお願い。僕がこの問題解けなかったこと、ケンジくんには内緒にしてね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ひとつだけおねがい。ぼくがこのもんだいとけなかったこと、けんじくんにはないしょにしてね。
lines.english: Then just one favour. Don't tell Kenji I couldn't solve this one, OK?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, naisho ni shite ageru. demo, koohii ogotte ne.
lines.ja: うん、内緒にしてあげる。でも、コーヒーおごってね。
lines.kana: うん、ないしょにしてあげる。でも、こーひーおごってね。
lines.english: Sure, your secret's safe. But you're buying me a coffee.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai agrees to come and teach Kenji maths, because her grades were always good.
Sora finds out Kenji never does his homework, so Mai offers to check it for him tomorrow.
Sora is stuck on one of Kenji's maths problems; Mai works it out, and Sora asks her to keep that from Kenji.

questions.explanation: Line 10: Sora is working through Kenji's problems ahead of time but can't get the last one (saigo no ga tokenai). Line 11: Mai shows him how (kou yatte toku), and in line 12 he gets it (toketa). Line 16: he asks her not to tell Kenji he couldn't solve it (naisho ni shite ne), and in line 17 she agrees, for a coffee. A is wrong: Sora does ask her to teach Kenji (line 14), but she says no way, she's bad at teaching (line 15), and her grades were only good in maths (line 13). B is wrong: Kenji does do his homework (line 6, chanto suru); he just forgets to hand it in. And it's Sora who will ask him about it tomorrow (lines 9-10), not Mai.

questions.english: You're taking an evening Japanese class. Sora asks you, "konban hima? issho ni geemu shinai?" Answer that you've got to do your homework, or do it first.
questions.ja: 今晩ひま？一緒にゲームしない？
questions.kana: こんばんひま？いっしょにげーむしない？
questions.romaji: konban hima? issho ni geemu shinai?
questions.answer: Say you've got to do your homework with shukudai and suru: shukudai shinakya (I've got to do my homework), or say yes but do it first: saki ni shukudai shichau (I'll get my homework done first). In casual speech the o drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, konban wa shukudai shinakya.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今晩は宿題しなきゃ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got to do my homework tonight.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, demo saki ni shukudai shichau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、でも先に宿題しちゃうね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure, but let me get my homework done first.

questions.explanation: Doing homework is shukudai o suru, and in casual talk the o drops: Mai asks "sora-kun ga shukudai shiteru no?" in line 3 and "jibun de shukudai shinai no?" in line 5, and Sora says Kenji does do it in line 6 (shukudai wa chanto suru). Don't reach for dasu here: that's handing it in, which is a different step (lines 6-7). Sora is a friend asking casually, so a casual answer fits; yaru also works (shukudai yaranakya).

questions.english: What does Sora say is Kenji's problem with homework?
questions.ja: ソラくんは、ケンジくんの宿題のことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらくんは、けんじくんのしゅくだいのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-kun wa, kenji-kun no shukudai no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: he forgets to do it
choices.romaji: suru no o wasurechau n da

choices.english: he forgets to hand it in
choices.romaji: dasu no o wasurechau n da

choices.english: he forgets to pass it over (to someone)
choices.romaji: watasu no o wasurechau n da

questions.explanation: Line 6: "shukudai wa chanto suru n da yo. demo, dasu no o wasurechau n da." Handing in homework is dasu (put it out). Mai picks it up in line 7 (shukudai shita noni, dasanai no?) and line 9 (shukudai chanto dashita ka). A is the partner phrase, and Sora says the opposite: Kenji does do it (chanto suru). Doing it and handing it in are two steps, and Kenji only manages the first. C, watasu, is handing something over to a person; turning in schoolwork is dasu.

questions.english: Sora says, "saigo no ga tokenai n da yo." What's he stuck on?
questions.ja: ソラくんは、何に困っていましたか？
questions.kana: そらくんは、なににこまっていましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-kun wa, nani ni komatte imashita ka?

choices.english: He can't work out the last maths problem.
He can't answer the last question Kenji asked him.
He can't get the last of the homework finished before his break ends.

questions.explanation: Line 10: tokenai is the can't-form of toku, and a maths or test problem is something you toku (untie): mondai o toku. He's working out tomorrow's problems ahead of time (saki ni toitoku). Mai shows him how in line 11 (kou yatte toku), he gets it in line 12 (toketa), and in line 16 he asks her not to tell Kenji he couldn't (tokenakatta). B mixes it up with shitsumon ni kotaeru (answer a question someone asks); Kenji isn't there and hasn't asked anything. C: his break comes up in line 1, but nobody mentions it ending, and toku is about solving, not finishing.

questions.english: After Mai answers, Sora turns to you: "sotchi wa? seiseki yokatta?" Tell him about your own grades at school, and play it down the way Mai does.
questions.ja: そっちは？成績よかった？
questions.kana: そっちは？せいせきよかった？
questions.romaji: sotchi wa? seiseki yokatta?
questions.answer: Use seiseki with ii in the past: yokatta (were good) or yokunakatta (weren't good). It's about you, so keep it modest: say they weren't that good, or name just one subject.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, seiseki wa sonna ni yokunakatta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、成績はそんなによくなかったよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nah, my grades weren't all that good.

modelAnswers.romaji: eigo dake wa seiseki yokatta kedo, hoka wa dame datta.
modelAnswers.ja: 英語だけは成績よかったけど、ほかはダメだった。
modelAnswers.english: My grades were good in English, but the rest were hopeless.

questions.explanation: The grades are the subject and ii describes them: seiseki ga yokunakute (line 8), seiseki yokatta (line 12), seiseki yoku naru (line 14). ii takes its forms from yoi, so it's yokatta and yokunakatta, never iikatta. Don't calque 'get good grades' as ii seiseki o morau. Saying your own grades were good sounds like bragging, which is why Mai plays it down in line 13 (suugaku dake da yo).

script.title: The wrong sunrise
script.setting: A Saturday in autumn, around five in the afternoon. Kenji, Yuki's little brother, gamed through the night and slept all day. He shuffles into the living room, where his mother is, as the low sun shines in through the window.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ohayou. a, yabai! mou hi ga nobotteru! okureru!
lines.ja: おはよう。あ、やばい！もう日が昇ってる！遅れる！
lines.kana: おはよう。あ、やばい！もうひがのぼってる！おくれる！
lines.english: Morning. Oh no! The sun's already up! I'm going to be late!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: nani itteru no. ima goji da yo. mou sugu hi ga kureru yo.
lines.ja: 何言ってるの。今五時だよ。もうすぐ日が暮れるよ。
lines.kana: なにいってるの。いまごじだよ。もうすぐひがくれるよ。
lines.english: What are you on about? It's five o'clock. It'll be dark soon.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, goji? jaa, hi ga nobotteru n ja nakute, shizundeku tokoro?
lines.ja: え、五時？じゃあ、日が昇ってるんじゃなくて、沈んでくところ？
lines.kana: え、ごじ？じゃあ、ひがのぼってるんじゃなくて、しずんでくところ？
lines.english: Huh, five? So the sun isn't up, it's on its way down?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou yo. mata asa made geemu shiteta n desho.
lines.ja: そうよ。また朝までゲームしてたんでしょ。
lines.kana: そうよ。またあさまでゲームしてたんでしょ。
lines.english: That's right. You were gaming till morning again, weren't you?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. chotto dake tte omotta n da kedo, ki ga tsuitara hi ga nobotteta.
lines.ja: うん。ちょっとだけって思ったんだけど、気がついたら日が昇ってた。
lines.kana: うん。ちょっとだけっておもったんだけど、きがついたらひがのぼってた。
lines.english: Yeah. I only meant to play for a bit, but next thing I knew, the sun was up.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mou. saikin wa hi ga kureru no ga hayai n da kara, sonna ni netetara ichinichi sugu owatchau yo.
lines.ja: もう。最近は日が暮れるのが早いんだから、そんなに寝てたら一日すぐ終わっちゃうよ。
lines.kana: もう。さいきんはひがくれるのがはやいんだから、そんなにねてたらいちにちすぐおわっちゃうよ。
lines.english: Honestly. It gets dark so early these days. Sleep that long and the day's gone in no time.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ii jan, doyoubi da shi. a, hi ga shizunjatta.
lines.ja: いいじゃん、土曜日だし。あ、日が沈んじゃった。
lines.kana: いいじゃん、どようびだし。あ、ひがしずんじゃった。
lines.english: So what, it's Saturday. Oh, the sun's gone down.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hora, hi ga kurete kita. denki tsukete.
lines.ja: ほら、日が暮れてきた。電気つけて。
lines.kana: ほら、ひがくれてきた。でんきつけて。
lines.english: See, it's getting dark. Turn the light on.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: hai hai. a, mite. atchi, tsuki ga deteru.
lines.ja: はいはい。あ、見て。あっち、月が出てる。
lines.kana: はいはい。あ、みて。あっち、つきがでてる。
lines.english: Okay, okay. Oh, look. Over there, the moon's out.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: honto da. kirei ne. kyou wa mangetsu da tte.
lines.ja: ほんとだ。きれいね。今日は満月だって。
lines.kana: ほんとだ。きれいね。きょうはまんげつだって。
lines.english: Oh, so it is. Isn't it lovely? Apparently it's a full moon tonight.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: hi ga shizunde, tsuki ga dete. kyou, nani mo shitenai.
lines.ja: 日が沈んで、月が出て。今日、何もしてない。
lines.kana: ひがしずんで、つきがでて。きょう、なにもしてない。
lines.english: The sun's gone down, the moon's come out, and I haven't done a thing today.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dakara itta desho. konban wa, hi ga noboru made geemu shinaide ne.
lines.ja: だから言ったでしょ。今晩は、日が昇るまでゲームしないでね。
lines.kana: だからいったでしょ。こんばんは、ひがのぼるまでゲームしないでね。
lines.english: See, I told you. Tonight, no gaming till the sun comes up, okay?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: wakatta. jaa, tsuki ga deteru aida dake ni suru.
lines.ja: わかった。じゃあ、月が出てる間だけにする。
lines.kana: わかった。じゃあ、つきがでてるあいだだけにする。
lines.english: Fine. Then I'll only play while the moon's out.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mangetsu da yo? sore, asa made desho!
lines.ja: 満月だよ？それ、朝まででしょ！
lines.kana: まんげつだよ？それ、あさまででしょ！
lines.english: It's a full moon, remember? That's till morning!

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji gets up early to watch the sunrise, but he's too late and misses it.
Kenji wakes up at five in the evening after gaming all night, and at first thinks the setting sun is the sunrise.
Kenji oversleeps on a school day, and his mother tells him he'll be late for school.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-3: Kenji wakes up, sees the low sun and says mou hi ga nobotteru! okureru!, thinking it's morning. His mother tells him it's five and mou sugu hi ga kureru (it'll be dark soon), and he realises the sun isn't coming up but going down (shizundeku tokoro). Lines 4-5: he gamed until the sun came up (ki ga tsuitara hi ga nobotteta) and then slept all day. A is wrong: he never meant to watch a sunrise; the 'sunrise' he saw was the sunset. C is wrong: okureru! was only his sleepy panic. It's Saturday (line 7) and five in the afternoon.

questions.english: On an autumn afternoon you run into Satou-san, your elderly neighbour, outside. He says: "It's only five, but it's already like night out here." Agree, and say how early it gets dark these days.
questions.ja: まだ五時なのに、外はもう夜ですね。
questions.kana: まだごじなのに、そとはもうよるですね。
questions.romaji: mada goji na noni, soto wa mou yoru desu ne.
questions.answer: Agree politely (he's your elderly neighbour) and use hi ga kureru: sou desu ne, hi ga kureru no ga hayaku narimashita ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: sou desu ne. hi ga kureru no ga hayaku narimashita ne.
modelAnswers.ja: そうですね。日が暮れるのが早くなりましたね。
modelAnswers.english: It's true. It gets dark so much earlier now, doesn't it?

modelAnswers.romaji: hontou desu ne. saikin wa hi ga kureru no ga hayai desu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 本当ですね。最近は日が暮れるのが早いですね。
modelAnswers.english: You're right. It gets dark early these days, doesn't it?

questions.explanation: The evenings drawing in is hi ga kureru, the classic autumn remark: Okaasan says saikin wa hi ga kureru no ga hayai (line 6) and mou sugu hi ga kureru yo (line 2). Kureru here is the day closing, not kureru 'give me'. Kuraku naru no ga hayaku narimashita ne (it gets dark earlier) says the same thing, and people also say hi ga ochiru no ga hayai. Hi ga shizumu is the sun itself going down at a given moment (line 7: a, hi ga shizunjatta), not the evening coming on. Use -masu forms with Satou-san.

questions.english: When Kenji first wakes up and sees the sun through the window, what does he say?
questions.ja: ケンジは最初に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはさいしょになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa saisho ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: The sun's already gone up!
The sun's already awake!
The sun's already up!

questions.explanation: Line 1: mou hi ga nobotteru! He says it again in line 5 (ki ga tsuitara hi ga nobotteta), and his mother uses it in line 12 (hi ga noboru made). Nobotteru means the sun is up now, not that it is in the middle of rising. A: agaru is the everyday 'go up' (stairs, prices), and English 'rise' points to it, but it isn't the usual verb for the sun: the sun noboru. B: okiteru is 'up' as in awake. People and pets okiru; the sun doesn't.

questions.english: On a hot summer evening, Kenta asks if you want to head out for your walk now: "Man, it's hot. Shall we go for our walk now?" Suggest waiting until the sun has gone down.
questions.ja: 暑いね。散歩、今から行く？
questions.kana: あついね。さんぽ、いまからいく？
questions.romaji: atsui ne. sanpo, ima kara iku?
questions.answer: Suggest going once the sun is down, with hi ga shizumu in the -tara or -te kara form: hi ga shizundara ikou.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, hi ga shizundara ikou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、日が沈んだら行こうよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nah, let's go once the sun's down.

modelAnswers.romaji: mada atsui kara, hi ga shizunde kara ni shiyou.
modelAnswers.ja: まだ暑いから、日が沈んでからにしよう。
modelAnswers.english: It's still hot, so let's wait until the sun's gone down.

questions.explanation: The sun going below the horizon is hi ga shizumu, the same verb as a ship sinking: Kenji says a, hi ga shizunjatta (line 7) and hi ga shizunde, tsuki ga dete (line 11). Not hi ga oriru or hi ga sagaru: English 'go down' points there, but the sun sinks. Hi ga ochiru is also natural in chat. Hi ga kuretara ikou would also be fine Japanese, but it means after dark, a little later: in lines 7-8 the sun goes down first (shizunjatta) and only then does it get dark (hi ga kurete kita).

questions.english: At the end, what does Kenji say he'll do tonight?
questions.ja: ケンジは今晩、どうすると言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはこんばん、どうするといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa konban, dou suru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Game only while the moon is out, which on a full-moon night means until morning.
Stop gaming as soon as the moon comes out.
Go outside to look at the full moon instead of gaming.

questions.explanation: Line 13: tsuki ga deteru aida dake ni suru. Deteru means the moon is out, a state that lasts, not the moment it appears, so 'only while the moon's out'. Kenji first spots it in line 9 (atchi, tsuki ga deteru), just after sunset, and line 10 says it's a full moon (mangetsu). A full moon is up from sunset until morning, which is why his mother says sore, asa made desho! (line 14). B reads deteru as 'comes out'. That would be tsuki ga detara yameru, and the moon was already out. C: nobody suggests going outside.

newWords.english: while, during (tsuki ga deteru aida = while the moon's out)

script.title: Breakfast next door
script.setting: Seven in the morning. Satou-san, the elderly man next door, leaves a voicemail for Kenta, who told him yesterday that he never eats breakfast. Yesterday Satou-san also baked his first ever loaf of bread, and it came out far too big for one person.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, kenta-kun? tonari no satou desu. asa hayaku ni sumimasen ne.
lines.ja: もしもし、ケンタくん？隣の佐藤です。朝早くにすみませんね。
lines.kana: もしもし、けんたくん？となりのさとうです。あさはやくにすみませんね。
lines.english: Hello, Kenta? It's Satou from next door. Sorry to call so early.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kinou, kenta-kun, asagohan wa itsumo nuiteru tte ittemashita yo ne.
lines.ja: 昨日、ケンタくん、朝ご飯はいつも抜いてるって言ってましたよね。
lines.kana: きのう、けんたくん、あさごはんはいつもぬいてるっていってましたよね。
lines.english: Yesterday you told me you always skip breakfast, didn't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jitsu wa watashi, kinou hajimete pan o yaite mita n desu.
lines.ja: 実は私、昨日初めてパンを焼いてみたんです。
lines.kana: じつはわたし、きのうはじめてパンをやいてみたんです。
lines.english: Well, actually, yesterday I tried baking bread for the first time.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore ga ne, sugoku ookii no ga dekichatte. hitori ja zenbu wa taberarenai n desu yo.
lines.ja: それがね、すごく大きいのができちゃって。一人じゃ全部は食べられないんですよ。
lines.kana: それがね、すごくおおきいのができちゃって。ひとりじゃぜんぶはたべられないんですよ。
lines.english: The thing is, it came out enormous. I can't eat it all by myself.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: dakara, shigoto ni iku mae ni, uchi ni yotte ikimasen ka? asagohan o nuku no wa, karada ni yokunai desu kara ne.
lines.ja: だから、仕事に行く前に、うちに寄っていきませんか？朝ご飯を抜くのは、体によくないですからね。
lines.kana: だから、しごとにいくまえに、うちによっていきませんか？あさごはんをぬくのは、からだによくないですからね。
lines.english: So why not drop by my place before you go to work? Skipping breakfast isn't good for you, you know.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-kun ga kitara, sugu sono pan o yaite, ocha mo iremasu yo.
lines.ja: ケンタくんが来たら、すぐそのパンを焼いて、お茶も入れますよ。
lines.kana: けんたくんがきたら、すぐそのパンをやいて、おちゃもいれますよ。
lines.english: As soon as you get here, I'll toast some of that bread and make tea, too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, sou ieba, kenta-kun wa koohii ni osatou o mittsu mo iremasu yo ne.
lines.ja: あ、そういえば、ケンタくんはコーヒーにお砂糖を三つも入れますよね。
lines.kana: あ、そういえば、けんたくんはコーヒーにおさとうをみっつもいれますよね。
lines.english: Oh, come to think of it, you put three sugars in your coffee, don't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: zannen desu kedo, uchi ni wa koohii ga nai n desu. sono kawari, oishii ocha o iremasu kara.
lines.ja: 残念ですけど、うちにはコーヒーがないんです。その代わり、おいしいお茶を入れますから。
lines.kana: ざんねんですけど、うちにはコーヒーがないんです。そのかわり、おいしいおちゃをいれますから。
lines.english: I'm sorry to say I don't have any coffee. But I'll make you a nice cup of green tea instead.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo, ocha ni wa osatou, irenaide kudasai ne.
lines.ja: でも、お茶にはお砂糖、入れないでくださいね。
lines.kana: でも、おちゃにはおさとう、いれないでくださいね。
lines.english: Just don't put sugar in the tea, all right?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, oyu o wakashite mattemasu ne. kyou wa asagohan, nuicha dame desu yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、お湯を沸かして待ってますね。今日は朝ご飯、抜いちゃだめですよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、おゆをわかしてまってますね。きょうはあさごはん、ぬいちゃだめですよ。
lines.english: Well then, I'll put the kettle on and wait for you. No skipping breakfast today!

questions.english: Why does Satou-san call Kenta?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、どうしてケンタくんに電話したんですか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、どうしてけんたくんにでんわしたんですか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, doushite kenta-kun ni denwa shita n desu ka?

choices.english: He has run out of coffee, and he asks Kenta to bring some over before work.
His first loaf of bread is too big to finish alone, so he invites Kenta, who usually skips breakfast, to come and eat before work.
His first loaf of bread went wrong, so he asks Kenta, who's good at cooking, to come and show him how.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Kenta said yesterday that he always skips breakfast (itsumo nuiteru). Lines 3-4: Satou-san baked bread for the first time and it came out huge, too much to eat alone. Line 5: so he invites Kenta to drop by before work (shigoto ni iku mae ni, uchi ni yotte ikimasen ka?). A: he does say he has no coffee (line 8), but he offers tea instead; he doesn't ask Kenta for anything. C: the bread didn't go wrong, it just came out too big (sugoku ookii no ga dekichatte), and Satou-san is the one doing the cooking.

questions.english: Tanaka-san comes back into the office from outside and says: "Brr, that was cold. It's windy out there." Offer to make him a hot cup of tea.
questions.ja: ああ、寒かった。外は風が強いですね。
questions.kana: ああ、さむかった。そとはかぜがつよいですね。
questions.romaji: aa, samukatta. soto wa kaze ga tsuyoi desu ne.
questions.answer: Offer tea with ocha o ireru, politely, since he's your manager. iremashou ka? means 'shall I make some?': atsui ocha, iremashou ka? Not ocha o tsukurimashou ka.

modelAnswers.romaji: otsukaresama desu. atsui ocha, iremashou ka?
modelAnswers.ja: お疲れさまです。熱いお茶、入れましょうか？
modelAnswers.english: Welcome back. Shall I make you a hot cup of tea?

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, ocha iremasu ne. chotto matte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、お茶入れますね。ちょっと待ってください。
modelAnswers.english: I'll make you some tea, then. Just a moment.

questions.explanation: Satou-san offers tea the same way: ocha mo iremasu yo (line 6) and oishii ocha o iremasu kara (line 8). For a cup or a pot of tea or coffee the verb is ireru, which here means brewing it by pouring on hot water. English 'make' leads to ocha o tsukuru, but tsukuru is for a big jug made in advance, like a pitcher of cold barley tea. Handing the cup to a guest afterwards is ocha o dasu; ireru is the making.

questions.english: Mai, your coworker and friend, has made you a coffee and says: "I made coffee. Is black OK?" You like it sweet. Ask her to put some sugar in.
questions.ja: コーヒー入れたよ。ブラックでいい？
questions.kana: コーヒーいれたよ。ブラックでいい？
questions.romaji: koohii ireta yo. burakku de ii?
questions.answer: Ask for sugar with satou o ireru; Japanese has no 'take' here: satou irete kureru?

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. demo, satou irete kureru?
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。でも、砂糖入れてくれる？
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. Could you put some sugar in, though?

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen. satou futatsu irete moraeru?
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん。砂糖二つ入れてもらえる？
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry. Could I get two sugars in it?

questions.explanation: Sugar going into a drink is ireru in its plain 'put in' sense: Satou-san says koohii ni osatou o mittsu mo iremasu yo ne (line 7) and ocha ni wa osatou, irenaide kudasai ne (line 9). English 'I take sugar' has no match: satou o toru means picking the sugar up (satou totte = pass me the sugar), not having it in your coffee. Mai's koohii ireta is the other ireru, brewing the cup. With a friend plain satou is fine; Satou-san says osatou because he's speaking politely. (satou, sugar, has the same sounds as his name, only the pitch differs; the o- is politeness, but it also keeps the two apart.) If you do want it black: burakku de ii yo.

questions.english: What did Satou-san do with bread yesterday, and what will he do with it when Kenta arrives?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、昨日パンをどうしましたか？ケンタくんが来たら、どうしますか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、きのうパンをどうしましたか？けんたくんがきたら、どうしますか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, kinou pan o dou shimashita ka? kenta-kun ga kitara, dou shimasu ka?

choices.english: Yesterday he made toast for the first time, and when Kenta comes he'll make more toast.
Yesterday he baked bread for the first time, and when Kenta comes he'll bake a fresh loaf.
Yesterday he baked bread for the first time, and when Kenta comes he'll toast some of it.

questions.explanation: yaku covers bake, toast and grill, so the moment decides the English. Line 3, hajimete pan o yaite mita, is baking: line 4 says it came out huge (sugoku ookii no ga dekichatte), a whole loaf. Line 6, kitara sugu sono pan o yaite, is toasting: sono pan is the loaf he already has, done the moment Kenta walks in. A misses the loaf; an enormous result only makes sense for baking. B misses sono pan: he already has more bread than he can eat, and a loaf can't be baked sugu.

questions.english: What does Satou-san say at the very end of his message?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは最後に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんはさいごになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa saigo ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: No skipping breakfast today!

questions.explanation: Line 10: kyou wa asagohan, nuicha dame desu yo. nuicha is from nuku (pull out, leave out), and he used it twice before: itsumo nuiteru (line 2) and asagohan o nuku no wa, karada ni yokunai (line 5). B, tobasu, is where English 'skip' leads, but it's for skipping pages, questions or steps, not meals. C, yasumu, is taking time off from something you go to (shigoto o yasumu, gakkou o yasumu); a meal isn't something you take a day off from.

script.title: Whose washing is it?
script.setting: Saturday, late morning, at the flat Kenta shares with Sora. Yuki has come round so they can go to a movie together, but Kenta is still in the middle of the housework.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenta, kita yo. mou ikeru?
lines.ja: ケンタ、来たよ。もう行ける？
lines.kana: けんた、きたよ。もういける？
lines.english: Kenta, I'm here. Ready to go?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gomen, mada. asa kara zutto kaji shiteru n da. sora, kyou shigoto da kara.
lines.ja: ごめん、まだ。朝からずっと家事してるんだ。ソラ、今日仕事だから。
lines.kana: ごめん、まだ。あさからずっとかじしてるんだ。そら、きょうしごとだから。
lines.english: Sorry, not yet. I've been doing housework all morning. Sora's at work today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sokka, taihen da ne. jaa, tetsudau yo. ato nani yaru no?
lines.ja: そっか、大変だね。じゃあ、手伝うよ。あと何やるの？
lines.kana: そっか、たいへんだね。じゃあ、てつだうよ。あとなにやるの？
lines.english: Oh, that's a lot. I'll help, then. What's left?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: honto? sentakumono wa mou hoshita kara, ato wa soujiki kakeru dake.
lines.ja: ほんと？洗濯物はもう干したから、あとは掃除機かけるだけ。
lines.kana: ほんと？せんたくものはもうほしたから、あとはそうじきかけるだけ。
lines.english: Really? I've already hung the washing out, so it's just the vacuuming now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyou wa tenki ii kara, sentakumono sugu kawaku yo.
lines.ja: 今日は天気いいから、洗濯物すぐ乾くよ。
lines.kana: きょうはてんきいいから、せんたくものすぐかわくよ。
lines.english: The weather's nice today, so the washing will dry in no time.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un. jaa, soujiki kakechau ne. ato de, fuku tatamu no tetsudatte.
lines.ja: うん。じゃあ、掃除機かけちゃうね。あとで、服畳むの手伝って。
lines.kana: うん。じゃあ、そうじきかけちゃうね。あとで、ふくたたむのてつだって。
lines.english: Yeah. Right, I'll get the vacuuming done. Help me fold the clothes after, okay?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: are? kyuu ni ame futte kita! kenta!
lines.ja: あれ？急に雨降ってきた！ケンタ！
lines.kana: あれ？きゅうにあめふってきた！けんた！
lines.english: Huh? It's suddenly started raining! Kenta!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? nani? kikoenai!
lines.ja: え？何？聞こえない！
lines.kana: え？なに？きこえない！
lines.english: What? I can't hear you!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: soujiki tomete! ame da yo! sentakumono, hayaku naka ni irenakya!
lines.ja: 掃除機止めて！雨だよ！洗濯物、早く中に入れなきゃ！
lines.kana: そうじきとめて！あめだよ！せんたくもの、はやくなかにいれなきゃ！
lines.english: Turn the vacuum off! It's raining! We need to get the washing in, quick!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yokatta, maniatta. demo sentakumono, mada kawaitenai no mo aru na.
lines.ja: よかった、間に合った。でも洗濯物、まだ乾いてないのもあるな。
lines.kana: よかった、まにあった。でもせんたくもの、まだかわいてないのもあるな。
lines.english: Phew, we made it. But some of the washing still isn't dry.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, kawaitenai sentakumono wa heya ni hoshite. watashi wa fuku tatamu ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、乾いてない洗濯物は部屋に干して。私は服畳むね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、かわいてないせんたくものはへやにほして。わたしはふくたたむね。
lines.english: Then hang the damp washing up indoors. I'll fold the clothes.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: arigatou. a, sora no fuku wa tatamanakute ii yo. douse heya chirakatteru shi.
lines.ja: ありがとう。あ、ソラの服は畳まなくていいよ。どうせ部屋散らかってるし。
lines.kana: ありがとう。あ、そらのふくはたたまなくていいよ。どうせへやちらかってるし。
lines.english: Thanks. Oh, don't bother folding Sora's clothes. His room's a mess anyway.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sora no fuku? nee, kore, zenbu kenta no ja nai?
lines.ja: ソラの服？ねえ、これ、全部ケンタのじゃない？
lines.kana: そらのふく？ねえ、これ、ぜんぶけんたのじゃない？
lines.english: Sora's clothes? Hey, aren't these all yours?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? a, honto da. sou ieba sora, jibun no wa jibun de aratteru n datta.
lines.ja: え？あ、ほんとだ。そういえばソラ、自分のは自分で洗ってるんだった。
lines.kana: え？あ、ほんとだ。そういえばそら、じぶんのはじぶんであらってるんだった。
lines.english: Huh? Oh, you're right. Come to think of it, Sora washes his own stuff himself.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nan da. sora mo chanto kaji shiteru jan.
lines.ja: なんだ。ソラもちゃんと家事してるじゃん。
lines.kana: なんだ。そらもちゃんとかじしてるじゃん。
lines.english: Well then. So Sora does do his share of the housework.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sou da na. zenbu hitori de kaji shiteru to omotteta.
lines.ja: そうだな。全部一人で家事してると思ってた。
lines.kana: そうだな。ぜんぶひとりでかじしてるとおもってた。
lines.english: Yeah, fair enough. I thought I was doing all the housework on my own.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hora, hayaku soujiki kakete. eiga, hajimatchau yo.
lines.ja: ほら、早く掃除機かけて。映画、始まっちゃうよ。
lines.kana: ほら、はやくそうじきかけて。えいが、はじまっちゃうよ。
lines.english: Come on, hurry up and vacuum. The movie's going to start without us.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: The rain soaks the washing before they can get it in, so they call off the movie.
Yuki folds Sora's clothes for him, and Kenta says Sora never does any housework.
Kenta thought he was doing all the housework, but the washing is all his own: Sora washes his own clothes.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Kenta says he's been doing housework all morning because Sora is at work. Line 12: he tells Yuki not to bother folding Sora's clothes, but in line 13 she points out that everything is his (zenbu kenta no ja nai?). Line 14: he remembers that Sora washes his own clothes himself, and in lines 15-16 Yuki teases him and he admits he thought he was doing all the housework alone. A is wrong: the rain does start (line 7), but they get the washing in in time (line 10: yokatta, maniatta), and in line 17 Yuki is still hurrying him so they don't miss the movie. B is wrong: there are no clothes of Sora's to fold (line 13), and the scene ends with Kenta finding out that Sora does do his own share (lines 14-16).

questions.english: On Monday, Mai asks you about your weekend: "shuumatsu, nani shiteta no?" Say you spent it doing housework.
questions.ja: 週末、何してたの？
questions.kana: しゅうまつ、なにしてたの？
questions.romaji: shuumatsu, nani shiteta no?
questions.answer: Say you were doing the housework: kaji (o) suru, in the -teta form for 'was doing' (kaji shiteta). You can add when or how long: doyoubi wa (on Saturday), ichinichi (all day), zutto uchi de (at home the whole time).

modelAnswers.romaji: doyoubi wa ichinichi kaji shiteta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 土曜日は一日家事してたよ。
modelAnswers.english: I spent all of Saturday doing housework.

modelAnswers.romaji: zutto uchi de kaji shiteta. tsukareta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ずっとうちで家事してた。疲れたよ。
modelAnswers.english: I was home doing housework the whole time. I'm worn out.

questions.explanation: Lines 2, 15 and 16: kaji covers all the housework (cooking, cleaning, laundry), and it takes suru, like souji or sentaku. Kenta says asa kara zutto kaji shiteru (I've been doing housework all morning), and later admits he thought he was doing it all alone (hitori de kaji shiteru to omotteta). Don't translate 'housework' word for word as uchi no shigoto: say kaji. Mai is a friend asking casually, so drop o (kaji shiteta); kaji yatteta is just as natural.

questions.english: Yuki asks what's left to do, and Kenta tells her about the washing. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは洗濯物について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんはせんたくものについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa sentakumono ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I've already hung the washing up on hangers, so all that's left is vacuuming.
choices.romaji: sentakumono wa mou kaketa kara, ato wa soujiki kakeru dake.

choices.english: I've already hung the washing out to dry, so all that's left is vacuuming.
choices.romaji: sentakumono wa mou hoshita kara, ato wa soujiki kakeru dake.

choices.english: The washing's already dry, so all that's left is vacuuming.
choices.romaji: sentakumono wa mou kawaita kara, ato wa soujiki kakeru dake.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenta says sentakumono wa mou hoshita: hosu is putting the washing out to dry, and he had done that already. A is English 'hang' carried over: kakeru hangs a coat on a hook or a shirt on a hanger, but washing put out to dry is always hosu. C swaps in the partner verb: kawaku is the washing drying by itself, and it wasn't dry yet. In line 5 Yuki says it will dry soon (sugu kawaku yo), and in line 10 some of it still isn't (mada kawaitenai).

questions.english: After they rush the washing inside, Kenta says, "demo sentakumono, mada kawaitenai no mo aru na." What's the problem?
questions.ja: 洗濯物は、どうでしたか？
questions.kana: せんたくものは、どうでしたか？
questions.romaji: sentakumono wa, dou deshita ka?

choices.english: Some of it still wasn't dry.
Some of it had got soaked in the rain.
Some of it hadn't been hung out yet.

questions.explanation: Line 10: kawaitenai is kawaku (the washing drying by itself) in the negative -teru form, and mada makes it 'still not dry'. Yuki had expected it to dry quickly in the sun (line 5: sugu kawaku yo), but the sudden rain brought it in early, so in line 11 she says to hang the damp things up indoors. B is wrong: Kenta's yokatta, maniatta (phew, we made it) means they got it in before the rain reached it; still damp from the wash is not the same as soaked by rain. C mixes kawaku up with hosu: hanging it out is hosu, and Kenta had done that already (line 4: mou hoshita).

questions.english: Kenta has brought in the dry washing and asks, "sentakumono, zenbu kawaita yo. chotto tetsudatte kureru?" Say you'll fold the clothes.
questions.ja: 洗濯物、全部乾いたよ。ちょっと手伝ってくれる？
questions.kana: せんたくもの、ぜんぶかわいたよ。ちょっとてつだってくれる？
questions.romaji: sentakumono, zenbu kawaita yo. chotto tetsudatte kureru?
questions.answer: Offer to fold the clothes: fuku (o) tatamu. Casually, watashi ga fuku tatamu ne (I'll fold the clothes), or fuku tatamu no tetsudau yo (I'll help fold them).

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. jaa, watashi ga fuku tatamu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。じゃあ、私が服畳むね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. I'll fold the clothes, then.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, fuku tatamu no tetsudau yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、服畳むの手伝うよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll help fold the clothes.

questions.explanation: Lines 6, 11 and 12: folding clothes is tatamu. Kenta asks for help with it (fuku tatamu no tetsudatte), Yuki takes it on (watashi wa fuku tatamu ne), and Kenta says she needn't fold Sora's (tatamanakute ii yo). Don't use oru for 'fold' here: oru is folding paper, as in origami, or snapping something (hone o oru, break a bone), so fuku o oru sounds wrong. Futons and umbrellas are tatamu too. Kenta is a friend, so drop o and keep it casual.

questions.english: Kenta says, "ato de minna kuru n da kedo, heya, chotto kirei ni shitoite kureru?" Offer to vacuum.
questions.ja: あとでみんな来るんだけど、部屋、ちょっときれいにしといてくれる？
questions.kana: あとでみんなくるんだけど、へや、ちょっときれいにしといてくれる？
questions.romaji: ato de minna kuru n da kedo, heya, chotto kirei ni shitoite kureru?
questions.answer: Offer to run the vacuum: soujiki (o) kakeru. The -toku form fits, since people are coming and you're doing it ahead: soujiki kaketoku ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. jaa, soujiki kaketoku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。じゃあ、掃除機かけとくね。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. I'll run the vacuum round before they get here.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, ima soujiki kakeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、今掃除機かけるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Okay, I'll vacuum now.

questions.explanation: Lines 4, 6 and 17: Kenta still has to vacuum (soujiki kakeru dake), says he'll get it done (soujiki kakechau ne), and Yuki hurries him at the end (hayaku soujiki kakete). English 'vacuum' is a verb, but Japanese has no verb for it: you run the machine with kakeru, the same kakeru as mezamashi o kakeru (set an alarm). Casual soujiki suru is also heard; souji suru is cleaning in general, and soujiki o tsukau (use the vacuum) is correct but not how people usually say it. The -toku in kaketoku means doing it ahead, before everyone arrives.

script.title: Where the sound went
script.setting: A weekday evening in the flat Kenta and Sora share. Sora gets home with a dead phone and plugs it in. Kenta has been calling him all afternoon about something that has gone missing.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, sora! yatto kaette kita. nande denwa denakatta no? nando mo shita noni.
lines.ja: あ、ソラ！やっと帰ってきた。なんで電話出なかったの？何度もしたのに。
lines.kana: あ、そら！やっとかえってきた。なんででんわでなかったの？なんどもしたのに。
lines.english: Sora! Finally, you're back. Why didn't you pick up? I called you over and over.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen! sumaho, hiru gurai ni juuden kirechatta n da.
lines.ja: ごめん！スマホ、昼ぐらいに充電切れちゃったんだ。
lines.kana: ごめん！スマホ、ひるぐらいにじゅうでんきれちゃったんだ。
lines.english: Sorry! My phone died around lunchtime.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, sou na no? dengen kitteru n da to omotta.
lines.ja: え、そうなの？電源切ってるんだと思った。
lines.kana: え、そうなの？でんげんきってるんだとおもった。
lines.english: Oh, really? I thought you'd switched it off.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: dengen nanka kittenai yo. honto ni juuden kireta n da tte.
lines.ja: 電源なんか切ってないよ。ほんとに充電切れたんだって。
lines.kana: でんげんなんかきってないよ。ほんとにじゅうでんきれたんだって。
lines.english: I didn't switch it off! It really did die, I'm telling you.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sokka. ne, boku no supiikaa shiranai? sore de denwa shita n da kedo.
lines.ja: そっか。ね、僕のスピーカー知らない？それで電話したんだけど。
lines.kana: そっか。ね、ぼくのスピーカーしらない？それででんわしたんだけど。
lines.english: Okay. Hey, have you seen my speaker? That's why I was calling.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: supiikaa? uun, shiranai. a, chotto juuden shita kara, dengen irete miru ne.
lines.ja: スピーカー？ううん、知らない。あ、ちょっと充電したから、電源入れてみるね。
lines.kana: スピーカー？ううん、しらない。あ、ちょっとじゅうでんしたから、でんげんいれてみるね。
lines.english: Your speaker? No, no idea. Oh, it's charged a bit, so I'll try turning it on.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: dou? tsuita?
lines.ja: どう？ついた？
lines.kana: どう？ついた？
lines.english: Well? Is it on?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, tsuita. jaa, ongaku kakete miyou.
lines.ja: うん、ついた。じゃあ、音楽かけてみよう。
lines.kana: うん、ついた。じゃあ、おんがくかけてみよう。
lines.english: Yep, it's on. Okay, let's try putting some music on.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: are? oto detenai yo.
lines.ja: あれ？音出てないよ。
lines.kana: あれ？おとでてないよ。
lines.english: Huh? There's no sound coming out.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: honto da. oto denai. nande?
lines.ja: ほんとだ。音出ない。なんで？
lines.kana: ほんとだ。おとでない。なんで？
lines.english: You're right. No sound. Why?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ikkai dengen kitte mitara? sore de naoru koto aru yo.
lines.ja: 一回電源切ってみたら？それで直ることあるよ。
lines.kana: いっかいでんげんきってみたら？それでなおることあるよ。
lines.english: Why not try switching it off for a sec? Sometimes that fixes it.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: wakatta. dengen kitte, mou ikkai dengen irete. kore de dou?
lines.ja: わかった。電源切って、もう一回電源入れて。これでどう？
lines.kana: わかった。でんげんきって、もういっかいでんげんいれて。これでどう？
lines.english: Okay. Off, and back on again. How about now?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: dame da. yappari oto denai ne.
lines.ja: だめだ。やっぱり音出ないね。
lines.kana: だめだ。やっぱりおとでないね。
lines.english: Nope. Still no sound.

lines.ja: うそ！充電切れたときに、壊れちゃったのかな。
lines.kana: うそ！じゅうでんきれたときに、こわれちゃったのかな。
lines.english: No way! Maybe it broke when the battery died.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: chotto matte. nanka, sora no kaban kara oto ga suru n da kedo.
lines.ja: ちょっと待って。なんか、ソラのカバンから音がするんだけど。
lines.kana: ちょっとまって。なんか、そらのカバンからおとがするんだけど。
lines.english: Hang on. I can hear something coming from your bag.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e? a! kenta no supiikaa da! oto, koko kara deteta n da!
lines.ja: え？あ！ケンタのスピーカーだ！音、ここから出てたんだ！
lines.kana: え？あ！けんたのスピーカーだ！おと、ここからでてたんだ！
lines.english: Huh? Oh! It's your speaker! So that's where the sound was coming out!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku no supiikaa! sora, kesa katte ni tsukatta desho. dengen mo ireta mama da shi.
lines.ja: 僕のスピーカー！ソラ、今朝勝手に使ったでしょ。電源も入れたままだし。
lines.kana: ぼくのスピーカー！そら、けさかってにつかったでしょ。でんげんもいれたままだし。
lines.english: My speaker! You took it this morning without asking, didn't you? And you left it switched on, too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, sou datta. gomen gomen. demo, supiikaa no juuden, kiretenakute yokatta ne!
lines.ja: あ、そうだった。ごめんごめん。でも、スピーカーの充電、切れてなくてよかったね！
lines.kana: あ、そうだった。ごめんごめん。でも、スピーカーのじゅうでん、きれてなくてよかったね！
lines.english: Oh, right, I did. Sorry, sorry! But hey, lucky the speaker's battery didn't die!

questions.english: What happens in this scene?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora had switched his phone off, and when he turned it back on the sound didn't work, so Kenta lent him his speaker.
Sora's phone broke when its battery died, so from now on he'll play his music through Kenta's speaker.
Sora's phone made no sound because it was playing through Kenta's missing speaker, left switched on in Sora's bag.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Kenta called Sora over and over, and line 5 says why: to ask about his missing speaker. Lines 2 and 4: Sora's phone died (juuden kireta). Lines 6-13: once it is charged and on, Sora puts music on, but no sound comes out of the phone (oto detenai / oto denai), even after switching it off and on. Lines 15-16: the sound is coming from Sora's bag, where Kenta's speaker is playing the music. Line 17: Sora took it this morning and left it switched on. A is wrong: Sora didn't switch his phone off (line 4: dengen nanka kittenai yo), and nobody lent him the speaker; he took it without asking (line 17). B is wrong: the phone only seemed broken (line 14: kowarechatta no kana); the sound was going to the speaker (line 16).

questions.english: When the phone gives no sound, what does Kenta suggest?
questions.ja: ケンタは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Why not try turning the phone off (kesu) for a sec?
Why not try switching it off for a sec?
Why not try letting the power go off (kireru) for a sec?

questions.explanation: Line 11: ikkai dengen kitte mitara? Switching a device off yourself is dengen o kiru, with transitive kiru, and Sora does it in line 12 (dengen kitte). A is the English speaker's guess: kesu is for lights and the TV (denki o kesu), and sumaho kesu can sound like turning only the screen off. C uses kireru, the intransitive partner: power or a battery cuts out by itself (juuden kireta, line 2), so it isn't something you can try doing. Sora draws the same line in line 4: dengen nanka kittenai yo (I didn't switch it off), honto ni juuden kireta (it really died).

questions.english: Your phone died at Sora's place and he put it on charge for you. Now he says, "ne, sumaho no juuden, owatta yo." (Hey, your phone's done charging.) Say you'll try turning it on, or ask him to turn it on.
questions.ja: ね、スマホの充電、終わったよ。
questions.kana: ね、スマホのじゅうでん、おわったよ。
questions.romaji: ne, sumaho no juuden, owatta yo.
questions.answer: Use dengen with ireru, dropping o in casual speech: dengen irete miru (I'll try turning it on), or dengen irete kureru? to ask him to do it.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. jaa, dengen irete miru.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。じゃあ、電源入れてみる。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. I'll try turning it on, then.

modelAnswers.romaji: honto? jaa, dengen irete kureru?
modelAnswers.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、電源入れてくれる？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah? Could you switch it on for me, then?

questions.explanation: The power goes on with ireru ('put in'), as Sora says in line 6 (dengen irete miru ne) and line 12 (mou ikkai dengen irete). English 'turn on' pulls toward tsukeru, but that's the verb for lights and the TV; for a phone's power, ireru is the usual one. tsuita? (is it on?) in line 7 is what the phone does once you've switched it on. Sora is talking to you casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Yuki tried to call you last night and asks, "kinou no yoru, nande denwa denakatta no?" (Why didn't you pick up last night?) Your phone had died. Tell her.
questions.ja: 昨日の夜、なんで電話出なかったの？
questions.kana: きのうのよる、なんででんわでなかったの？
questions.romaji: kinou no yoru, nande denwa denakatta no?
questions.answer: Say your phone died, with juuden and kireru in the past: gomen, juuden kirechatta n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, sumaho no juuden kirechatta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、スマホの充電切れちゃったんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, my phone died.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen. juuden ga kireteta n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん。充電が切れてたんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry. My phone was dead.

questions.explanation: A dead phone is juuden kireta, 'the charge ran out', as Sora tells Kenta in lines 2 and 4. Don't say sumaho shinda (slang) or dengen kitta: that means you switched it off yourself, which is exactly what Sora denies in line 4 (dengen nanka kittenai yo). kirechatta adds 'unfortunately'; kireteta is 'it was dead at the time'. Yuki is a friend, so casual is right.

questions.english: When Sora finds the speaker in his bag, he says "oto, koko kara deteta n da!" What does he realise?
questions.ja: ソラは何がわかりましたか？
questions.kana: そらはなにがわかりましたか？
questions.romaji: sora wa nani ga wakarimashita ka?

choices.english: The music from his phone had been coming out of the speaker the whole time.
The speaker in his bag had been making a strange noise all day.
His phone's sound had just started working again.

questions.explanation: Line 16: oto ga deru is sound coming out of a device, and deteta n da means 'so that's where it was coming out'. The phone was playing through Kenta's speaker, which is why no sound came out of the phone itself in lines 9-13 (oto detenai, oto denai). B mixes it up with oto ga suru, Kenta's line 15 (kaban kara oto ga suru = I can hear something from your bag): that's hearing a noise, and the speaker was playing Sora's music, which he only put on in line 8. C is wrong: the phone still had no sound of its own; the music was going to the speaker.

script.title: Foggy glasses at lunch
script.setting: Lunchtime at a small café near the office. Mai has a cold and turns up in a mask, and every breath fogs up her glasses. She sits down across from Yuki while they wait for their food.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, kotchi kotchi! are, masuku shiteru. kaze hiita no?
lines.ja: マイ、こっちこっち！あれ、マスクしてる。風邪ひいたの？
lines.kana: まい、こっちこっち！あれ、マスクしてる。かぜひいたの？
lines.english: Mai, over here! Oh, you're wearing a mask. Have you caught a cold?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, chotto nodo ga itakute. demo masuku suru to, megane ga sugu kumoru n da yo ne.
lines.ja: うん、ちょっと喉が痛くて。でもマスクすると、眼鏡がすぐ曇るんだよね。
lines.kana: うん、ちょっとのどがいたくて。でもマスクすると、めがねがすぐくもるんだよね。
lines.english: Yeah, my throat's a bit sore. But whenever I wear a mask, my glasses fog up right away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, sore, megane kaketeru hito wa minna iu yo ne.
lines.ja: ああ、それ、眼鏡かけてる人はみんな言うよね。
lines.kana: ああ、それ、めがねかけてるひとはみんないうよね。
lines.english: Oh, everyone who wears glasses says that.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hora, ima mo. mae ga zenzen mienai.
lines.ja: ほら、今も。前が全然見えない。
lines.kana: ほら、いまも。まえがぜんぜんみえない。
lines.english: See, it's happening right now. I can't see a thing.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, masuku hazushitara? koko, hito sukunai shi.
lines.ja: じゃあ、マスク外したら？ここ、人少ないし。
lines.kana: じゃあ、マスクはずしたら？ここ、ひとすくないし。
lines.english: Then why not take your mask off? There aren't many people in here.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, yuki ni kaze utsuttara iya da kara, masuku wa shitoku.
lines.ja: ううん、ユキに風邪うつったら嫌だから、マスクはしとく。
lines.kana: ううん、ゆきにかぜうつったらいやだから、マスクはしとく。
lines.english: No, I'd hate for you to catch my cold, so I'll keep it on.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, megane no hou o hazushitara?
lines.ja: じゃあ、眼鏡のほうを外したら？
lines.kana: じゃあ、めがねのほうをはずしたら？
lines.english: Then how about taking your glasses off instead?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: megane hazusu to nanimo mienai n da kedo, maa, ii ka. hazushitoku.
lines.ja: 眼鏡外すと何も見えないんだけど、まあ、いいか。外しとく。
lines.kana: めがねはずすとなにもみえないんだけど、まあ、いいか。はずしとく。
lines.english: I can't see a thing without my glasses, but oh well. I'll take them off for now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sonna ni mienai no?
lines.ja: そんなに見えないの？
lines.kana: そんなにみえないの？
lines.english: Is it really that bad?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, zenzen. a, asoko, tanaka-san ja nai? tanaka-san, otsukaresama desu!
lines.ja: うん、全然。あ、あそこ、田中さんじゃない？田中さん、お疲れさまです！
lines.kana: うん、ぜんぜん。あ、あそこ、たなかさんじゃない？たなかさん、おつかれさまです！
lines.english: Yeah, totally. Oh, isn't that Tanaka-san over there? Hi, Tanaka-san!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: chotto, mai! hayaku megane kakete! ano hito, tanaka-san ja nai yo.
lines.ja: ちょっと、マイ！早く眼鏡かけて！あの人、田中さんじゃないよ。
lines.kana: ちょっと、まい！はやくめがねかけて！あのひと、たなかさんじゃないよ。
lines.english: Mai, wait! Put your glasses on, quick! That's not Tanaka-san.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, uso! megane, megane. a, honto da. zenzen chigau hito da.
lines.ja: え、うそ！眼鏡、眼鏡。あ、ほんとだ。全然違う人だ。
lines.kana: え、うそ！めがね、めがね。あ、ほんとだ。ぜんぜんちがうひとだ。
lines.english: What, no way! Glasses, where are my glasses? Oh, you're right. That's someone else entirely.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ano hito, metcha bikkuri shiteta yo. mou megane hazushicha dame.
lines.ja: あの人、めっちゃびっくりしてたよ。もう眼鏡外しちゃだめ。
lines.kana: あのひと、めっちゃびっくりしてたよ。もうめがねはずしちゃだめ。
lines.english: He looked so startled. No more taking your glasses off.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hazukashii. demo, masuku shitetara, mata kumoru yo.
lines.ja: 恥ずかしい。でも、マスクしてたら、また曇るよ。
lines.kana: はずかしい。でも、マスクしてたら、またくもるよ。
lines.english: So embarrassing. But as long as I've got the mask on, they'll just fog up again.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, gohan kita yo. hora, masuku hazushite.
lines.ja: あ、ご飯来たよ。ほら、マスク外して。
lines.kana: あ、ごはんきたよ。ほら、マスクはずして。
lines.english: Oh, the food's here. Come on, take your mask off.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou da ne. masuku hazushitara, megane kakete mo kumoranai. yatto yuki no kao ga mieta!
lines.ja: そうだね。マスク外したら、眼鏡かけても曇らない。やっとユキの顔が見えた！
lines.kana: そうだね。マスクはずしたら、めがねかけてもくもらない。やっとゆきのかおがみえた！
lines.english: True. With the mask off, my glasses don't fog up. At last I can see your face!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yokatta. kono hanashi, ato de tanaka-san ni hanasou kana.
lines.ja: よかった。この話、あとで田中さんに話そうかな。
lines.kana: よかった。このはなし、あとでたなかさんにはなそうかな。
lines.english: Good. Maybe I'll tell Tanaka-san this story later.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yamete! zettai dame!
lines.ja: やめて！絶対だめ！
lines.kana: やめて！ぜったいだめ！
lines.english: Don't you dare! Absolutely not!

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai takes her mask off so her glasses stop fogging up, and then Tanaka-san walks in and sees her.
Yuki doesn't recognise Mai at first, because Mai is wearing a mask and glasses.
Mai takes off her fogged-up glasses, and without them she greets a stranger, thinking he's Tanaka-san.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-8: Mai's mask keeps fogging up her glasses. She won't take the mask off in case Yuki catches her cold (line 6), so she takes her glasses off instead. In line 10 she calls out to 'Tanaka-san', and in lines 11-12 Yuki makes her put her glasses back on: it's someone else entirely. A is wrong because Mai only takes the mask off when the food arrives (lines 15-16), and the real Tanaka-san never turns up. B is wrong because Yuki spots Mai straight away and calls her over (line 1).

questions.english: When Yuki first suggests taking the mask off, what does Mai say she'll do with it?
questions.ja: マイさんは、マスクをどうすると言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、マスクをどうするといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, masuku o dou suru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I'll keep wearing the mask (with kiru, as for a shirt).
I'll keep the mask on.
I'll hang on to the mask (keep it with me).

questions.explanation: Line 6: Mai says masuku wa shitoku (shite oku, leave it on), and Yuki noticed it in line 1 with masuku shiteru. Small things you wear, like a mask or a watch, take suru. A, kiru, is where English 'wear' points, but kiru is for clothes you put your body into, like a shirt or jacket (fuku o kiru), not a mask. C, motte oku, means keeping the mask with you, in your hand or your bag, not on your face.

questions.english: Yuki holds up her phone and says: "OK, I'm taking the photo. Look this way!" You've still got your mask on. Ask her to wait while you take it off.
questions.ja: じゃあ、写真撮るよ。こっち見て！
questions.kana: じゃあ、しゃしんとるよ。こっちみて！
questions.romaji: jaa, shashin toru yo. kotchi mite!
questions.answer: Ask her to wait while you take your mask off, using hazusu: chotto matte, masuku hazusu kara.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, chotto matte. masuku hazusu kara.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ちょっと待って。マスク外すから。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, hang on. Let me take my mask off.

modelAnswers.romaji: matte, masuku hazushite mo ii?
modelAnswers.ja: 待って、マスク外してもいい？
modelAnswers.english: Wait, is it OK if I take my mask off?

questions.explanation: A mask comes off with hazusu, as in Yuki's masuku hazushitara? (line 5) and masuku hazushite (line 15). Don't say nugu: that's for clothes and shoes. Casual toru works too (masuku toru kara), but masuku totte on its own can sound like 'pass me a mask'. Putting it back on afterwards is suru again: mata masuku suru.

questions.english: Mai complains that her mask fogs up her glasses. Yuki says a certain kind of person always says that. Who does she mean?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、どんな人がみんなそう言うと言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、どんなひとがみんなそういうといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, donna hito ga minna sou iu to iimashita ka?

choices.english: People who wear glasses.
People who are just putting their glasses on.
People who keep their glasses hooked on their shirt.

questions.explanation: Line 3: megane kaketeru hito. kakeru is the verb for glasses, and kaketeru describes a state, so this simply means people who wear glasses. It's a way of describing someone. B reads -teru as an action happening right now, but Yuki means glasses-wearers in general, who all complain about masks fogging their lenses. C: kakeru does literally mean 'hang', which is why it goes with glasses (they hang on your ears), but megane kaketeru means they're on your face, not hooked on your clothes.

questions.english: You're having ramen with Kenta. The steam hits his face and he groans: "Ugh, my glasses have fogged up and I can't see a thing." Suggest he take them off while he eats.
questions.ja: ああ、眼鏡曇って、全然見えない。
questions.kana: ああ、めがねくもって、ぜんぜんみえない。
questions.romaji: aa, megane kumotte, zenzen mienai.
questions.answer: Suggest he take them off with hazusu, the same verb as for a mask: jaa, megane hazushitara?

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, megane hazushitara?
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、眼鏡外したら？
modelAnswers.english: Then why don't you take your glasses off?

modelAnswers.romaji: taberu toki wa, megane hazushita hou ga ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 食べる時は、眼鏡外したほうがいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: You'd better take your glasses off while you eat.

questions.explanation: Yuki does exactly this in line 7 (megane no hou o hazushitara?), and Mai answers megane hazusu to nanimo mienai (line 8). Glasses and masks share hazusu for taking off, but not for putting on: a mask takes suru, glasses take kakeru (line 16, megane kakete mo kumoranai). Not megane o nugu: nugu is for things you're dressed in, like clothes and shoes.

newWords.english: fog up, mist over (glasses); also cloud over (the sky)
can see, be visible (mienai = can't see, mieta = could see)

script.title: Results at noon
script.setting: Just before noon at the office. Last month Mai (Kimura-san at work) sat a bookkeeping exam, and the results go up online at twelve today. Her manager, Tanaka-san, stops by her desk to ask how she's feeling.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san, sengetsu, boki no shiken o ukemashita yo ne. kekka wa mou demashita ka?
lines.ja: 木村さん、先月、簿記の試験を受けましたよね。結果はもう出ましたか？
lines.kana: きむらさん、せんげつ、ぼきのしけんをうけましたよね。けっかはもうでましたか？
lines.english: Kimura-san, you took the bookkeeping exam last month, didn't you? Are the results out yet?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: mada desu. kyou no juuniji ni, kekka ga deru n desu.
lines.ja: まだです。今日の十二時に、結果が出るんです。
lines.kana: まだです。きょうのじゅうにじに、けっかがでるんです。
lines.english: Not yet. They come out today at twelve.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: mou sugu desu ne. jishin wa arimasu ka?
lines.ja: もうすぐですね。自信はありますか？
lines.kana: もうすぐですね。じしんはありますか？
lines.english: That's any minute now. Are you feeling confident?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: iie, zenzen. saigo no mondai ga, hotondo tokenakatta n desu.
lines.ja: いいえ、全然。最後の問題が、ほとんど解けなかったんです。
lines.kana: いいえ、ぜんぜん。さいごのもんだいが、ほとんどとけなかったんです。
lines.english: No, not at all. I barely got anywhere with the last question.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: daijoubu desu yo. ano shiken wa, nanajutten toreba ukarimasu kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫ですよ。あの試験は、七十点取れば受かりますから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶですよ。あのしけんは、ななじゅってんとればうかりますから。
lines.english: You'll be fine. On that exam, you pass if you get seventy.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: demo, nanajutten mo toretenai kamo shiremasen. shiken ni ochitara, dou shiyou.
lines.ja: でも、七十点も取れてないかもしれません。試験に落ちたら、どうしよう。
lines.kana: でも、ななじゅってんもとれてないかもしれません。しけんにおちたら、どうしよう。
lines.english: But I might not even have got seventy. What'll I do if I've failed?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jitsu wa watashi mo, mukashi ano shiken ni nikai ochita n desu yo.
lines.ja: 実は私も、昔あの試験に二回落ちたんですよ。
lines.kana: じつはわたしも、むかしあのしけんににかいおちたんですよ。
lines.english: Actually, I failed that exam twice myself, years ago.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, tanaka-san ga desu ka?
lines.ja: え、田中さんがですか？
lines.kana: え、たなかさんがですか？
lines.english: What, you did?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: hai. shiken o sankai ukete, yatto ukatta n desu.
lines.ja: はい。試験を三回受けて、やっと受かったんです。
lines.kana: はい。しけんをさんかいうけて、やっとうかったんです。
lines.english: Yes. I took it three times before I finally passed.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou na n desu ka. jaa, moshi shiken ni ochite mo, mata ukereba ii n desu ne.
lines.ja: そうなんですか。じゃあ、もし試験に落ちても、また受ければいいんですね。
lines.kana: そうなんですか。じゃあ、もししけんにおちても、またうければいいんですね。
lines.english: Really? So even if I fail, I can just take it again.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou desu. hora, mou juuniji desu yo.
lines.ja: そうです。ほら、もう十二時ですよ。
lines.kana: そうです。ほら、もうじゅうにじですよ。
lines.english: Exactly. Look, it's twelve already.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, kekka demashita! nanajuuniten toremashita!
lines.ja: あ、結果出ました！七十二点取れました！
lines.kana: あ、けっかでました！ななじゅうにてんとれました！
lines.english: Oh, the results are up! I got seventy-two!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: omedetou gozaimasu! ikkai de shiken ni ukatta n desu kara, sugoi desu yo.
lines.ja: おめでとうございます！一回で試験に受かったんですから、すごいですよ。
lines.kana: おめでとうございます！いっかいでしけんにうかったんですから、すごいですよ。
lines.english: Congratulations! You passed on your first try. That's impressive.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu! tanaka-san wa, ukatta toki, nanten totta n desu ka?
lines.ja: ありがとうございます！田中さんは、受かったとき、何点取ったんですか？
lines.kana: ありがとうございます！たなかさんは、うかったとき、なんてんとったんですか？
lines.english: Thank you! What did you get when you passed?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kyuujuuhachiten desu. onaji shiken o sankai mo ukereba, mondai mo oboechaimasu yo.
lines.ja: 九十八点です。同じ試験を三回も受ければ、問題も覚えちゃいますよ。
lines.kana: きゅうじゅうはちてんです。おなじしけんをさんかいもうければ、もんだいもおぼえちゃいますよ。
lines.english: Ninety-eight. Take the same exam three times and you end up knowing the questions.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, kyuujuuhachiten! jaa, rainen wa motto muzukashii shiken o ukete mimasu.
lines.ja: え、九十八点！じゃあ、来年はもっと難しい試験を受けてみます。
lines.kana: え、きゅうじゅうはちてん！じゃあ、らいねんはもっとむずかしいしけんをうけてみます。
lines.english: Ninety-eight! Then next year I'll try a harder exam.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ii desu ne. moshi ochite mo, sankai made wa daijoubu desu yo.
lines.ja: いいですね。もし落ちても、三回までは大丈夫ですよ。
lines.kana: いいですね。もしおちても、さんかいまではだいじょうぶですよ。
lines.english: Good idea. And if you fail, you're fine up to three tries.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai finds out she failed by two points, and Tanaka-san tells her she can just take it again.
Mai is worried she's failed, but when the results come out at twelve, she has passed on her first try.
Tanaka-san got ninety-eight on his first try, so he gives Mai tips before her exam.

questions.explanation: Lines 3-6: Mai has no confidence and fears she didn't get the seventy points she needs to pass. Line 12: the results come out and she got 72, and in line 13 Tanaka-san congratulates her on passing first time (ikkai de). A is wrong: 72 is two points over the pass mark, not under, and the 'just take it again' idea (line 10) comes before the results. C is wrong: Tanaka-san failed twice (line 7) and passed on his third try (line 9); the 98 was that third time (lines 14-15). Mai's exam was last month (line 1), so it's already over.

questions.english: At the start, how does Tanaka-san bring up the exam Mai sat last month?
questions.ja: 田中さんは、先月の試験のことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんは、せんげつのしけんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa, sengetsu no shiken no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: You passed the bookkeeping exam last month, didn't you?
choices.romaji: sengetsu, boki no shiken ni ukarimashita yo ne.

choices.english: You 'took' the bookkeeping exam last month (toru, like English 'take'), didn't you?
choices.romaji: sengetsu, boki no shiken o torimashita yo ne.

choices.english: You took (sat) the bookkeeping exam last month, didn't you?
choices.romaji: sengetsu, boki no shiken o ukemashita yo ne.

questions.explanation: Line 1: 'boki no shiken o ukemashita yo ne'. You sit an exam with ukeru and o, and Tanaka-san says it again in line 9 (shiken o sankai ukete) and line 15 (onaji shiken o sankai mo ukereba). B follows English 'take', but toru goes with the score, not the exam: nanajutten toreba (line 5), nanajuuniten toremashita (line 12). A sounds very close, but ukaru (with ni) means pass, and at this point nobody knows the result yet. He asks whether the results are out in the same line, and Mai only finds out she passed in lines 12-13.

questions.english: Sora asks how your Japanese test went: "nihongo no shiken, nanten datta?" You got 85. Tell him your score.
questions.ja: 日本語の試験、何点だった？
questions.kana: にほんごのしけん、なんてんだった？
questions.romaji: nihongo no shiken, nanten datta?
questions.answer: Give the number with ten fused on, then toru: hachijuugoten totta. Casual speech drops o. Don't use morau (that's a mark someone hands you), and never say shiken o totta: the exam is ukeru, the score is toru.

modelAnswers.romaji: hachijuugoten totta yo!
modelAnswers.ja: 八十五点取ったよ！
modelAnswers.english: I got eighty-five!

modelAnswers.romaji: hachijuugoten. kekkou ii ten toreta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 八十五点。けっこういい点取れたよ。
modelAnswers.english: Eighty-five. I managed a pretty good score.

questions.explanation: Score + toru is how Tanaka-san and Mai talk about marks: nanajutten toreba (line 5), nanajuuniten toremashita (line 12), nanten totta n desu ka (line 14). The toreta / toremashita form adds 'managed to get', as in Mai's line 12. hachijuugoten moratta would sound like a teacher just gave you the mark, and shiken o totta mixes up the exam (ukeru) with the score (toru). Sora asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: Mai tells Tanaka-san, "kyou no juuniji ni, kekka ga deru n desu." What happens at twelve?
questions.ja: 十二時に、何がありますか？
questions.kana: じゅうにじに、なにがありますか？
questions.romaji: juuniji ni, nani ga arimasu ka?

choices.english: Her exam results are announced.
She has to go out to collect her results.
Her exam finishes.

questions.explanation: Line 2: kekka ga deru means the results come out, with the results as the subject, not Mai. At twelve (lines 11-12) she checks and says kekka demashita: they're up, and she got 72. B takes deru in its 'go out, leave' sense, but it's the results that come out, and Mai never leaves her desk. C is wrong because she sat the exam last month (line 1); only the results were still to come.

questions.english: Tanaka-san asks about an exam you took last month. You checked this morning: you passed. Tell him.
questions.ja: 先月の試験の結果は、もう出ましたか？
questions.kana: せんげつのしけんのけっかは、もうでましたか？
questions.romaji: sengetsu no shiken no kekka wa, mou demashita ka?
questions.answer: Say the results are out and you passed: shiken ni ukarimashita. The exam takes ni, and the verb is ukaru (ukarimashita), not ukeru (ukemashita), which would only say you sat it. goukaku shimashita also works.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, demashita. shiken ni ukarimashita!
modelAnswers.ja: はい、出ました。試験に受かりました！
modelAnswers.english: Yes, they're out. I passed!

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, kesa demashita. ikkai de shiken ni ukarimashita!
modelAnswers.ja: はい、今朝出ました。一回で試験に受かりました！
modelAnswers.english: Yes, they came out this morning. I passed on my first try!

questions.explanation: Tanaka-san says it this way in line 13 (ikkai de shiken ni ukatta) and line 9 (yatto ukatta). ukaru and ukeru are one sound apart, and line 9 has both: shiken o sankai ukete, yatto ukatta (took it three times, finally passed). shiken o ukarimashita is wrong: the exam takes ni. Tanaka-san asks politely, so answer with -masu.

questions.english: You've just found out you failed an exam you took last month. Kenta sees you looking down and asks what's wrong. Tell him.
questions.ja: どうしたの？なんか元気ないね。
questions.kana: どうしたの？なんかげんきないね。
questions.romaji: dou shita no? nanka genki nai ne.
questions.answer: Say you failed with shiken ni ochiru, casually shiken ochichatta (-chatta adds 'sadly'). English 'fail' tempts shippai shita, but that means you messed something up; for a pass/fail result you 'fall': ochita.

modelAnswers.romaji: jitsu wa, shiken ochichatta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 実は、試験落ちちゃったんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Actually, I failed my exam.

modelAnswers.romaji: sengetsu no shiken, ochichatta. demo, mata ukeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 先月の試験、落ちちゃった。でも、また受けるよ。
modelAnswers.english: I failed last month's exam. But I'll take it again.

questions.explanation: Mai and Tanaka-san use ochiru with ni for failing: shiken ni ochitara (line 6), ano shiken ni nikai ochita (line 7), shiken ni ochite mo (line 10). With a friend, ni usually drops and -chatta adds 'unfortunately'. shiken ni shippai shita means you blew it, which isn't the same as the result. Like Mai in line 10, you can add that you'll just take it again (mata ukeru), with ukeru, not ukaru.

newWords.english: times (counter): nikai twice, sankai three times; ikkai de on the first try

script.title: Two minutes late
script.setting: Saturday, late afternoon. It's Kenji's birthday, and Okaasan has gone out to buy his cake at the family's usual cake shop, which only takes cash. Yuki doesn't pick up, so Okaasan leaves her three voicemails: one from the queue at the bank by the station, one once she has her cash, and one outside the cake shop.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki? okaasan da kedo. ima ne, eki no mae no ginkou ni, okane oroshi ni kiteru no.
lines.ja: ユキ？お母さんだけど。今ね、駅の前の銀行に、お金下ろしに来てるの。
lines.kana: ゆき？おかあさんだけど。いまね、えきのまえのぎんこうに、おかねおろしにきてるの。
lines.english: Yuki? It's Mum. I'm at the bank by the station, getting some cash out.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji no tanjoubi no keeki, itsumo no mise de kau n da kedo, asoko, kaado tsukaenai no yo.
lines.ja: ケンジの誕生日のケーキ、いつもの店で買うんだけど、あそこ、カード使えないのよ。
lines.kana: けんじのたんじょうびのけーき、いつものみせでかうんだけど、あそこ、かーどつかえないのよ。
lines.english: I'm getting Kenji's birthday cake at the usual place, but they don't take cards.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo, doyoubi da kara ka, hito ga ookute ne. mou nijuppun mo junban matteru no.
lines.ja: でも、土曜日だからか、人が多くてね。もう二十分も順番待ってるの。
lines.kana: でも、どようびだからか、ひとがおおくてね。もうにじゅっぷんもじゅんばんまってるの。
lines.english: But it's packed, maybe because it's Saturday. I've already been waiting my turn for twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: maa, mise wa rokuji made aiteru kara, shimaru mae ni wa ikeru to omou kedo.
lines.ja: まあ、店は六時まで開いてるから、閉まる前には行けると思うけど。
lines.kana: まあ、みせはろくじまであいてるから、しまるまえにはいけるとおもうけど。
lines.english: Well, the shop's open till six, so I should get there before it closes.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki, mata okaasan. yatto okane oroseta wa. kekkyoku sanjuppun yo.
lines.ja: ユキ、またお母さん。やっとお金下ろせたわ。結局三十分よ。
lines.kana: ゆき、またおかあさん。やっとおかねおろせたわ。けっきょくさんじゅっぷんよ。
lines.english: Yuki, Mum again. I finally got the cash out. Thirty minutes, in the end!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mae no chiisai kodomo ga ne, zutto mada? mada? tte ittete.
lines.ja: 前の小さい子どもがね、ずっと「まだ？まだ？」って言ってて。
lines.kana: まえのちいさいこどもがね、ずっと「まだ？まだ？」っていってて。
lines.english: The little kid in front of me kept going, 'Is it our turn yet? Is it our turn yet?'

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: chanto junban matte ne tte iwareteta wa. kenji mo mukashi wa sou datta wa ne.
lines.ja: 「ちゃんと順番待ってね」って言われてたわ。ケンジも昔はそうだったわね。
lines.kana: 「ちゃんとじゅんばんまってね」っていわれてたわ。けんじもむかしはそうだったわね。
lines.english: He kept getting told, 'Wait your turn nicely, OK?' Kenji was just like that when he was little.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: a, mou rokuji juppun mae! hayaku ikanai to, mise shimatchau. jaa ne.
lines.ja: あ、もう六時十分前！早く行かないと、店閉まっちゃう。じゃあね。
lines.kana: あ、もうろくじじゅっぷんまえ！はやくいかないと、みせしまっちゃう。じゃあね。
lines.english: Oh, it's already ten to six! If I don't hurry, the shop'll close. Bye!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: yuki, nando mo gomen ne. mise, mou shimatteta no.
lines.ja: ユキ、何度もごめんね。店、もう閉まってたの。
lines.kana: ゆき、なんどもごめんね。みせ、もうしまってたの。
lines.english: Yuki, sorry for all the calls. The shop was already closed.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: nifun osokatta no yo. sekkaku okane oroshita noni.
lines.ja: 二分遅かったのよ。せっかくお金下ろしたのに。
lines.kana: にふんおそかったのよ。せっかくおかねおろしたのに。
lines.english: I was two minutes too late. And after all that trouble getting the cash out, too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sore de onegai na n da kedo, kaeri ni keeki katte kite kurenai? jikan aitetara de ii kara.
lines.ja: それでお願いなんだけど、帰りにケーキ買ってきてくれない？時間空いてたらでいいから。
lines.kana: それでおねがいなんだけど、かえりにけーきかってきてくれない？じかんあいてたらでいいから。
lines.english: So, a favour: could you pick up a cake on your way home? Only if you've got time.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: eki no naka no mise nara, hachiji made aiteru kara. okane wa ato de ageru ne.
lines.ja: 駅の中の店なら、八時まで開いてるから。お金はあとであげるね。
lines.kana: えきのなかのみせなら、はちじまであいてるから。おかねはあとであげるね。
lines.english: The shop inside the station is open till eight. I'll give you the money later.

questions.english: What happened in Okaasan's messages?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: The bank queue was so long that she gave up on getting cash, so she wants Yuki to pay for the cake by card.
She got her cash, but the cake shop had closed by the time she got there, so she's asking Yuki to pick up a cake on the way home.
She bought the cake in time, but now she's out of cash, so she's asking Yuki to stop at the bank on the way home.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-3: Okaasan is at the bank getting cash for Kenji's birthday cake, because the usual shop doesn't take cards, and she has been waiting her turn for twenty minutes. Line 5: she finally gets the cash, and in line 8 she hurries off before the shop closes. Lines 9-10: it was already closed, and she was two minutes late. Lines 11-12: she asks Yuki to buy a cake on her way home at the shop inside the station, which is open till eight. A is wrong because she did get the cash (line 5), and the cake shop doesn't take cards anyway (line 2). C is wrong because she never got the cake (line 9). She has the cash, and the favour is buying the cake.

questions.english: You're out for dinner with Kenta. When it's time to pay, he says: "Apparently this place doesn't take cards." You have no cash on you, and there's a konbini right by. Tell him you'll go and get some cash.
questions.ja: この店、カード使えないって。
questions.kana: このみせ、かーどつかえないって。
questions.romaji: kono mise, kaado tsukaenai tte.
questions.answer: Say you'll go and get cash with okane o orosu plus -te kuru (go, do it, come back): chotto okane oroshite kuru ne. Not okane o toru.

modelAnswers.romaji: e, honto? jaa, chotto okane oroshite kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: え、ほんと？じゃあ、ちょっとお金下ろしてくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Really? Then I'll just go and grab some cash.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, konbini de okane oroshite kuru kara, chotto mattete.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、コンビニでお金下ろしてくるから、ちょっと待ってて。
modelAnswers.english: Then I'll go get some cash at the konbini. Wait here a sec.

questions.explanation: Getting cash from a machine is orosu ('bring down'). Okaasan went to the bank okane oroshi ni (line 1), finally okane oroseta (line 5), and complains sekkaku okane oroshita noni (line 10). Adding -te kuru makes it 'go and do it, then come back', which is what you say as you head off. okane o toru, the word-for-word 'take money', sounds like taking someone's money. Casual okane dasu also works. Kenta's cue is the same problem Okaasan has in line 2 (kaado tsukaenai).

questions.english: In her last message, Okaasan says the shop inside the station is "hachiji made aiteru". What does she mean?
questions.ja: お母さんは、駅の中の店について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、えきのなかのみせについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, eki no naka no mise ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It opens at eight, so Yuki would have to wait around.
Yuki is free until eight, so she has time to go.
It's open until eight, so Yuki can still get there in time.

questions.explanation: Line 12: eki no naka no mise nara, hachiji made aiteru kara. A shop that aiteru is open, and made says until when, so it's open till eight. Okaasan said the same about the cake shop in line 4 (rokuji made aiteru). A would be hachiji ni aku, because plain aku is the moment a shop opens. B mixes it up with the other aiteru, one line earlier: jikan aitetara de ii kara (line 11) means 'only if you're free'. That one is about Yuki's time, not the shop.

questions.english: It's ten at night. Kenta says he's heading out to the shop by the station and asks if you want anything. You know that shop closes at nine. Tell him it's already closed.
questions.ja: 今から駅の前の店に買い物に行くけど、何か欲しいものある？
questions.kana: いまからえきのまえのみせにかいものにいくけど、なにかほしいものある？
questions.romaji: ima kara eki no mae no mise ni kaimono ni iku kedo, nanika hoshii mono aru?
questions.answer: Tell him it's shut with shimatteru (is closed): ano mise, mou shimatteru yo. For the closing time, use plain shimaru: kuji ni shimaru.

modelAnswers.romaji: e, ano mise, mou shimatteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: え、あの店、もう閉まってるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Huh? That shop's already closed.

modelAnswers.romaji: ano mise, kuji ni shimaru kara, mou shimatteru n ja nai?
modelAnswers.ja: あの店、九時に閉まるから、もう閉まってるんじゃない？
modelAnswers.english: That shop closes at nine, so it's probably shut by now, isn't it?

questions.explanation: A shop closing is shimaru. Okaasan says shimaru mae ni (before it closes, line 4), mise shimatchau (the shop'll close, line 8) and mise, mou shimatteta (it was already closed, line 9). For how the shop is right now, use shimatteru. shimeru is what the staff do when they close up, so it fits when you ask them (nanji ni shimemasu ka?). Casual owaru also works: mou owatteru yo.

questions.english: The little kid in front of Okaasan kept asking "mada?". What was he told?
questions.ja: 前の子どもは、何と言われていましたか？
questions.kana: まえのこどもは、なんといわれていましたか？
questions.romaji: mae no kodomo wa, nan to iwarete imashita ka?

choices.english: Wait your turn nicely, OK?
Wait for your (anata no) turn nicely, OK?
choices.romaji: chanto anata no ban o matte ne.

choices.english: Don't get the order mixed up, OK?

questions.explanation: Line 7: chanto junban matte ne. Waiting your turn is junban o matsu, and in casual speech the o drops. Okaasan uses it about herself in line 3 (mou nijuppun mo junban matteru). Standing in the queue itself would be narabu. B is English 'wait for your turn' word for word: Japanese leaves out 'your' here, and anata sounds cold from a parent to a small child. C sounds close (junban, machi-) but means 'don't get the order wrong'. The kid was impatient, not muddled.

script.title: A lighter for Dad
script.setting: Saturday afternoon at the family home. Yuki is back for the weekend and their dad's birthday is tomorrow. Kenji, half awake on the sofa, shows her the present he has bought.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nee, mite. otousan no tanjoubi purezento, kore ni shita.
lines.ja: ねえ、見て。お父さんの誕生日プレゼント、これにした。
lines.kana: ねえ、みて。おとうさんのたんじょうびぷれぜんと、これにした。
lines.english: Hey, look. This is what I got Dad for his birthday.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, raitaa? kenji, shiranai no? otousan, sengetsu yameta n da yo.
lines.ja: え、ライター？ケンジ、知らないの？お父さん、先月やめたんだよ。
lines.kana: え、らいたー？けんじ、しらないの？おとうさん、せんげつやめたんだよ。
lines.english: Huh, a lighter? Kenji, didn't you know? Dad quit last month.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: yameta? e, kaisha yameta no?
lines.ja: やめた？え、会社やめたの？
lines.kana: やめた？え、かいしゃやめたの？
lines.english: Quit? Wait, he quit his job?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: chigau yo! tabako. tabako yameta no.
lines.ja: 違うよ！タバコ。タバコやめたの。
lines.kana: ちがうよ！たばこ。たばこやめたの。
lines.english: No! Smoking. He quit smoking.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: maji de? anna ni tabako sutteta noni. nande?
lines.ja: マジで？あんなにタバコ吸ってたのに。なんで？
lines.kana: まじで？あんなにたばこすってたのに。なんで？
lines.english: Seriously? After all that smoking? How come?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou toshi totta kara na tte. saikin, karada ni ii koto bakkari shiteru yo.
lines.ja: もう年取ったからなって。最近、体にいいことばっかりしてるよ。
lines.kana: もうとしとったからなって。さいきん、からだにいいことばっかりしてるよ。
lines.english: He says it's because he's getting old. Lately he's all about stuff that's good for him.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: aa, dakara asa, koohii ja nakute ocha nonderu n da.
lines.ja: ああ、だから朝、コーヒーじゃなくてお茶飲んでるんだ。
lines.kana: ああ、だからあさ、こーひーじゃなくておちゃのんでるんだ。
lines.english: Oh, so that's why he has tea in the morning now, not coffee.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou. ocha wa karada ni ii kara tte.
lines.ja: そう。お茶は体にいいからって。
lines.kana: そう。おちゃはからだにいいからって。
lines.english: Yep. He says tea's good for you.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: tabako yameta n nara, kore, mou tsukawanai yo ne. dou shiyou.
lines.ja: タバコやめたんなら、これ、もう使わないよね。どうしよう。
lines.kana: たばこやめたんなら、これ、もうつかわないよね。どうしよう。
lines.english: If he's quit smoking, he won't be using this anymore, will he? What do I do?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: karada ni ii mono ni shitara? toshi o toru to, sou iu no ga ureshii rashii yo.
lines.ja: 体にいいものにしたら？年を取ると、そういうのがうれしいらしいよ。
lines.kana: からだにいいものにしたら？としをとると、そういうのがうれしいらしいよ。
lines.english: Why not something that's good for him? Apparently that's what you like getting as you get older.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jaa, soba wa? ii soba toka.
lines.ja: じゃあ、そばは？いいそばとか。
lines.kana: じゃあ、そばは？いいそばとか。
lines.english: Then how about soba? Some really good soba or something.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: soba wa dame. otousan, soba arerugii aru jan.
lines.ja: そばはダメ。お父さん、そばアレルギーあるじゃん。
lines.kana: そばはだめ。おとうさん、そばあれるぎーあるじゃん。
lines.english: Not soba. Dad's allergic to soba, remember?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, arerugii aru no? shiranakatta.
lines.ja: え、アレルギーあるの？知らなかった。
