lines.kana: え、あれるぎーあるの？しらなかった。
lines.english: Wait, he has an allergy? I didn't know that.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou, kenji wa otousan no koto, nanimo shiranai n da kara. tabako yameta no mo shiranakatta shi.
lines.ja: もう、ケンジはお父さんのこと、何も知らないんだから。タバコやめたのも知らなかったし。
lines.kana: もう、けんじはおとうさんのこと、なにもしらないんだから。たばこやめたのもしらなかったし。
lines.english: Honestly, Kenji, you don't know a thing about Dad. You didn't even know he'd quit smoking.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: gomen tte. jaa, ocha wa? ocha nara, arerugii nai yo ne?
lines.ja: ごめんって。じゃあ、お茶は？お茶なら、アレルギーないよね？
lines.kana: ごめんって。じゃあ、おちゃは？おちゃなら、あれるぎーないよね？
lines.english: All right, sorry! So what about tea? He's not allergic to tea, is he?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, nai. ii ne, sore. kondo wa chanto kangaeta jan.
lines.ja: うん、ない。いいね、それ。今度はちゃんと考えたじゃん。
lines.kana: うん、ない。いいね、それ。こんどはちゃんとかんがえたじゃん。
lines.english: Nope, he isn't. That's a good one. You actually thought it through this time.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: aa, kangaetara tsukareta. toshi totta kana.
lines.ja: ああ、考えたら疲れた。年取ったかな。
lines.kana: ああ、かんがえたらつかれた。としとったかな。
lines.english: Ugh, all that thinking wore me out. Must be getting old.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: juunana de nani itten no. kinou osoku made okiteta dake desho.
lines.ja: 十七で何言ってんの。昨日遅くまで起きてただけでしょ。
lines.kana: じゅうななでなにいってんの。きのうおそくまでおきてただけでしょ。
lines.english: You're seventeen, what are you on about? You just stayed up too late last night.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji finds out his dad has quit his job, so they pick tea to cheer him up.
Kenji's lighter is no good as a present because his dad has quit smoking, so he picks tea instead.
Kenji wants to give his dad some good soba, and Yuki agrees because soba is good for you.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Kenji has bought his dad a lighter for his birthday. Lines 2-4: Yuki tells him their dad quit smoking last month (tabako yameta), and in line 9 Kenji sees the lighter is no use now. Soba is out because of an allergy (line 12), and in lines 15-16 they settle on tea. A is wrong: in line 3 Kenji thinks his dad quit his job (kaisha yameta), but Yuki corrects him straight away in line 4: it's smoking. C is wrong: Kenji does suggest soba (line 11), but Yuki says no, because their dad is allergic to it (line 12).

questions.english: You always drink tea, never coffee. Kenji asks you, "nande itsumo ocha na no? koohii no hou ga oishii jan." Tell him tea is good for you, using karada ni ii.
questions.ja: なんでいつもお茶なの？コーヒーのほうがおいしいじゃん。
questions.kana: なんでいつもおちゃなの？こーひーのほうがおいしいじゃん。
questions.romaji: nande itsumo ocha na no? koohii no hou ga oishii jan.
questions.answer: Say tea is good for you: ocha wa karada ni ii kara, keeping the ni even in casual speech. You could add that tea is better for you than coffee (ocha no hou ga karada ni ii).

modelAnswers.romaji: datte, ocha wa karada ni ii kara.
modelAnswers.ja: だって、お茶は体にいいから。
modelAnswers.english: Because tea's good for you.

modelAnswers.romaji: koohii mo suki da kedo, ocha no hou ga karada ni ii n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: コーヒーも好きだけど、お茶のほうが体にいいんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: I like coffee too, but tea's better for you.

questions.explanation: In line 8 Yuki explains why their dad drinks tea now: ocha wa karada ni ii kara tte (because tea's good for you, he says), and lines 6 and 10 use karada ni ii for healthy habits and presents. It's said of food, drinks and habits, and ni stays even in casual talk. Don't say ocha wa kenkou desu: kenkou is a person's health, not something that's good for you. Kenji asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: At the end, Kenji says all that thinking has worn him out. What does he say next?
questions.ja: ケンジは最後に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはさいごになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa saigo ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: have I gone old and worn? (said of things)
am I the older one?
must be getting old

questions.explanation: Line 17: toshi totta kana. People take on years, toshi o toru, and 'I'm getting old' comes out in the past (toshi totta), with o dropped in casual talk. Their dad's excuse in line 6 is the same phrase (mou toshi totta kara na), and Yuki uses the general form in line 10 (toshi o toru to, as you get older). A is wrong: furuku naru is for things wearing out, like old shoes, not people. B is wrong: toshi ga ue means older than someone, and Kenji isn't comparing himself with anyone.

questions.english: Kenji says, "tabako yameta n nara, kore, mou tsukawanai yo ne." What does he mean?
questions.ja: ケンジは何が言いたかったんですか？
questions.kana: けんじはなにがいいたかったんですか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa nani ga iitakatta n desu ka?

choices.english: His dad has given up smoking, so he won't have any use for the lighter now.
His dad smokes less these days, so he'll only use the lighter now and then.
His dad has left his job, so he won't need anything for the office.

questions.explanation: Line 9: tabako yameta means he has quit smoking. Yameru is giving up a habit for good, so Kenji adds mou tsukawanai (he won't use it anymore), meaning the lighter is no use as a present. B is wrong: yameta means he stopped completely, not that he cut down. C mixes it up with kaisha o yameru (quit your job), the same-sounding yameru Kenji wrongly jumped to in line 3. Yuki corrects him in line 4 (chigau yo! tabako).

questions.english: Like Kenji's dad, you're allergic to soba. Yuki asks you, "nee, ohiru, soba ni shinai?" Say you can't have it because of your allergy.
questions.ja: ねえ、お昼、そばにしない？
questions.kana: ねえ、おひる、そばにしない？
questions.romaji: nee, ohiru, soba ni shinai?
questions.answer: Say you have a soba allergy: soba arerugii aru (ga drops in casual talk), or soba no arerugii ga aru. Put the cause in front of arerugii, then suggest something else.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen. soba arerugii aru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん。そばアレルギーあるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry. I'm allergic to soba.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, watashi, soba no arerugii ga aru kara, hoka no ni shinai?
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、私、そばのアレルギーがあるから、ほかのにしない？
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've got a soba allergy, so can we have something else?

questions.explanation: An allergy is something you have, so it takes aru: Yuki says otousan, soba arerugii aru jan (line 12), Kenji echoes arerugii aru no? (line 13), and in line 15 he uses the negative, arerugii nai. The cause goes in front: soba arerugii, or soba no arerugii. Say it a-re-ru-gii, not like English 'allergy'. Yuki asks casually, so answer casually.

script.title: Persimmons from next door
script.setting: Saturday morning outside a small apartment building. Yuki has come down to the mailboxes in her sweatpants, her washing still sitting in the machine upstairs. Next door, Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, is hanging out his laundry beside a basket of persimmons he has just picked from his tree.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu, yuki-san. kyou wa sentakumono ga yoku kawakisou desu ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます、ユキさん。今日は洗濯物がよく乾きそうですね。
lines.kana: おはようございます、ゆきさん。きょうはせんたくものがよくかわきそうですね。
lines.english: Good morning, Yuki. Looks like a good day for drying laundry.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. sou desu ne. demo kyou wa nanka, yaruki ga nai n desu yo ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます。そうですね。でも今日はなんか、やる気がないんですよね。
lines.kana: おはようございます。そうですね。でもきょうはなんか、やるきがないんですよね。
lines.english: Good morning. It does. But today I just can't be bothered.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: dou shita n desu ka? shigoto ga isogashikatta n desu ka?
lines.ja: どうしたんですか？仕事が忙しかったんですか？
lines.kana: どうしたんですか？しごとがいそがしかったんですか？
lines.english: What's the matter? Has work been busy?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai. konshuu wa zutto isogashikute, sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu.
lines.ja: はい。今週はずっと忙しくて、ストレスが溜まってるんです。
lines.kana: はい。こんしゅうはずっといそがしくて、すとれすがたまってるんです。
lines.english: Yes. It's been non-stop all week, and the stress has really piled up.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore wa taihen deshita ne. sutoresu ga tamaru to, yaruki mo naku narimasu yo ne.
lines.ja: それは大変でしたね。ストレスが溜まると、やる気もなくなりますよね。
lines.kana: それはたいへんでしたね。すとれすがたまると、やるきもなくなりますよね。
lines.english: That must have been hard. When stress piles up, your motivation goes too, doesn't it?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyou wa kaji o shiyou to omotteta n desu kedo, zenzen yaruki ga denakute.
lines.ja: 今日は家事をしようと思ってたんですけど、全然やる気が出なくて。
lines.kana: きょうはかじをしようとおもってたんですけど、ぜんぜんやるきがでなくて。
lines.english: I meant to do the housework today, but I just can't get myself going.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yaruki wa ne, hajimetara dete kuru mono desu yo. mazu wa chotto dake, yatte mitara dou desu ka?
lines.ja: やる気はね、始めたら出てくるものですよ。まずはちょっとだけ、やってみたらどうですか？
lines.kana: やるきはね、はじめたらでてくるものですよ。まずはちょっとだけ、やってみたらどうですか？
lines.english: Motivation, you know, comes once you've started. Why not try doing just a little first?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hajimetara, desu ka. demo, sono hajimeru yaruki ga nai n desu yo.
lines.ja: 始めたら、ですか。でも、その始めるやる気がないんですよ。
lines.kana: はじめたら、ですか。でも、そのはじめるやるきがないんですよ。
lines.english: Once I've started, huh? But I don't even have the motivation to start.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, uchi no kaki, douzo. tabete, genki dashite kudasai.
lines.ja: じゃあ、うちの柿、どうぞ。食べて、元気出してください。
lines.kana: じゃあ、うちのかき、どうぞ。たべて、げんきだしてください。
lines.english: Well then, have some persimmons from my tree. Eat them and cheer up.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, kaki! daisuki na n desu. uwaa, tenshon agarimasu!
lines.ja: え、柿！大好きなんです。うわあ、テンション上がります！
lines.kana: え、かき！だいすきなんです。うわあ、てんしょんあがります！
lines.english: Oh, persimmons! I love them. Wow, I'm getting all excited!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: tenshon ga agaru, desu ka. omoshiroi iikata desu ne.
lines.ja: テンションが上がる、ですか。面白い言い方ですね。
lines.kana: てんしょんがあがる、ですか。おもしろいいいかたですね。
lines.english: "Tenshon ga agaru," is it? What a fun way to put it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. nanka mou, genki ga demashita.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。なんかもう、元気が出ました。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。なんかもう、げんきがでました。
lines.english: Thank you. I feel better already.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore wa yokatta. sutoresu ga tamatta toki wa, oishii mono ga ichiban desu yo.
lines.ja: それはよかった。ストレスが溜まった時は、おいしいものが一番ですよ。
lines.kana: それはよかった。すとれすがたまったときは、おいしいものがいちばんですよ。
lines.english: I'm glad. When stress builds up, something tasty is the best cure.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, yaruki mo chotto dete kimashita. mazu sentakumono, hoshite kimasu!
lines.ja: あ、やる気もちょっと出てきました。まず洗濯物、干してきます！
lines.kana: あ、やるきもちょっとでてきました。まずせんたくもの、ほしてきます！
lines.english: Oh, I'm even getting a bit motivated. I'll go and hang out my laundry first!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ii desu ne. yuki-san ga genki da to, watashi mo genki ga demasu yo.
lines.ja: いいですね。ユキさんが元気だと、私も元気が出ますよ。
lines.kana: いいですね。ゆきさんがげんきだと、わたしもげんきがでますよ。
lines.english: Good for you. When you're cheerful, it gives me a lift too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, jaa satou-san mo, tenshon agarimashita?
lines.ja: え、じゃあ佐藤さんも、テンション上がりました？
lines.kana: え、じゃあさとうさんも、てんしょんあがりました？
lines.english: Oh, so you're all hyped up too, Satou-san?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ee, tenshon agarimashita yo. hajimete tsukaimashita.
lines.ja: ええ、テンション上がりましたよ。初めて使いました。
lines.kana: ええ、てんしょんあがりましたよ。はじめてつかいました。
lines.english: Yes, very hyped. That's the first time I've ever said it.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Satou-san offers to hang out Yuki's laundry for her, since she's worn out from work.
Yuki decides to skip the housework and rest today, as Satou-san suggests.
Yuki can't face the housework, but Satou-san's persimmons cheer her up and she goes off to hang out her laundry.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-8: after a stressful week, Yuki has no motivation (yaruki ga nai) and can't get going on the housework (yaruki ga denakute). In line 9 Satou-san gives her persimmons from his tree; she gets excited (line 10), feels better (line 12), and in line 14 goes off to hang out her laundry. A is wrong: Satou-san never offers to do her laundry; he tells her to try doing a little herself (line 7). B is wrong: he says motivation comes once you start, not that she should rest, and she doesn't take the day off: she starts with the laundry (line 14).

questions.english: It's Sunday and you just want to lie around. Kenta asks you, "nee, kyou nani suru? dokka ikanai?" Tell him you just don't feel like it today, using yaruki ga nai.
questions.ja: ねえ、今日何する？どっか行かない？
questions.kana: ねえ、きょうなにする？どっかいかない？
questions.romaji: nee, kyou nani suru? dokka ikanai?
questions.answer: Say you can't be bothered today: kyou wa nanka yaruki nai. With a friend ga can drop, and gomen softens it.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou wa nanka yaruki nai. uchi ni iru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日はなんかやる気ない。うちにいるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I just can't be bothered today. I'm staying in.

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa yaruki ga nai n da. mata kondo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はやる気がないんだ。また今度ね。
modelAnswers.english: I've got no motivation today. Another time, OK?

questions.explanation: In line 2 Yuki tells Satou-san kyou wa nanka, yaruki ga nai n desu yo ne (today I just can't be bothered), and in line 8 she says she doesn't even have the motivation to start (sono hajimeru yaruki ga nai n desu yo). About yourself, yaruki nai is a flat 'I don't feel like it'; about someone else (ano hito yaruki nai) it's a criticism. Avoid yaruki ga arimasen: it sounds stiff, and even politely people say yaruki ga nai n desu, as Yuki does. Kenta is a friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: Satou-san tells Yuki how motivation works. When does he say it comes?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、やる気はいつ出ると言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、やるきはいつでるといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, yaruki wa itsu deru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: After a proper rest, so she should take the morning off first.
Once she gets started, so she should try doing just a little first.
When she eats something tasty, like his persimmons.

questions.explanation: In line 7 Satou-san says yaruki wa ne, hajimetara dete kuru mono desu yo: motivation comes out (deru) once you start, so try a little first. Yuki uses the negative in line 6 (zenzen yaruki ga denakute, I just can't get going), and in line 14 it finally comes: yaruki mo chotto dete kimashita. A is wrong: he never tells her to rest; his advice is to start. C mixes up yaruki with genki: the persimmons are to lift her mood (genki dashite, line 9), and good food is his cure for stress (line 13), not where motivation comes from.

questions.english: You've had an awful day at work. Mai hands you a hot coffee and says, "hai, kore. muri shinaide ne." Thank her and tell her it's cheered you up, using genki ga deru.
questions.ja: はい、これ。無理しないでね。
questions.kana: はい、これ。むりしないでね。
questions.romaji: hai, kore. muri shinaide ne.
questions.answer: Thank her and say it gave you a lift, in the past: arigatou, genki deta. It's about you, so it's deta; genki dashite is what you say to cheer someone else up.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. nanka genki deta.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。なんか元気出た。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. That's cheered me up.

modelAnswers.romaji: uwaa, ureshii. arigatou, sugoku genki deta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うわあ、うれしい。ありがとう、すごく元気出たよ。
modelAnswers.english: Aw, that's so nice. Thanks, it's really cheered me up.

questions.explanation: In line 9 Satou-san hands Yuki persimmons and says tabete, genki dashite kudasai (eat them and cheer up): genki dashite is what you say to someone else. In line 12 Yuki answers about herself: nanka mou, genki ga demashita (I feel better already), and in line 15 Satou-san says her cheerfulness gives him a lift too (watashi mo genki ga demasu yo). For 'that cheered me up', use the past genki deta. Don't answer genki dashite, which would tell Mai to cheer up, and genki ni natta usually means you've got over an illness. Mai is a friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Yuki sees the persimmons, what does she say?
questions.ja: 柿を見て、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: かきをみて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kaki o mite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I'm getting so excited!
I'm getting all worked up!
What a downer!

questions.explanation: In line 10 Yuki sees the persimmons and says uwaa, tenshon agarimasu! (wow, I'm getting all excited!). Satou-san repeats it in line 11 as a fun, young-sounding expression and tries it himself in lines 16-17. B is the English speaker's trap: koufun shimasu sounds agitated or even sexual, not happily excited. C is the opposite, tenshon sagaru (get bummed out), which doesn't fit someone who loves persimmons. And tenshon is mood or hype, not 'tension' (that's kinchou).

questions.english: You've been working late every night. Your manager, Tanaka-san, asks you, "saikin, tsukaretemasen ka? daijoubu desu ka?" Tell him honestly that stress has been piling up, using sutoresu ga tamaru.
questions.ja: 最近、疲れてませんか？大丈夫ですか？
questions.kana: さいきん、つかれてませんか？だいじょうぶですか？
questions.romaji: saikin, tsukaretemasen ka? daijoubu desu ka?
questions.answer: Tell him stress has built up, politely since he's your manager: sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu. Stress piles up (tamaru); it isn't a verb you do.

modelAnswers.romaji: jitsu wa, saikin chotto sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: 実は、最近ちょっとストレスが溜まってるんです。
modelAnswers.english: To be honest, the stress has been piling up a bit lately.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu desu. demo, chotto sutoresu ga tamatte kimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫です。でも、ちょっとストレスが溜まってきました。
modelAnswers.english: I'm OK. But the stress is starting to build up a bit.

questions.explanation: In line 4 Yuki tells Satou-san that after a busy week, sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu (the stress has piled up); he picks it up in line 5 (sutoresu ga tamaru to, when stress piles up) and again in line 13. Use tamatteru for how you are now. Don't say sutoresu shiteru: stress isn't something you do in Japanese, it's something that piles up. Hear the contrast in the scene: stress piles up (tamaru), while Yuki's mood goes up (tenshon agaru, line 10). Tanaka-san is your manager, so answer politely.

script.title: Yesterday's bento
script.setting: Sunday lunchtime at Kenta and Sora's flat. Last night Kenta made hot pot for Yuki and Mai. Mai drops by to pick up the glasses she left behind, just as Sora, barely awake, is about to heat up a bento he bought yesterday.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora, kinou nando mo renraku shita n da yo.
lines.ja: ソラ、昨日何度も連絡したんだよ。
lines.kana: そら、きのうなんどもれんらくしたんだよ。
lines.english: Sora, I messaged you loads of times last night.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, juuden kireteta. dou shita no?
lines.ja: ごめん、充電切れてた。どうしたの？
lines.kana: ごめん、じゅうでんきれてた。どうしたの？
lines.english: Sorry, my battery was dead. What's up?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: megane, koko ni nai? kinou, nabe no toki hazushite, wasurechatta.
lines.ja: メガネ、ここにない？昨日、鍋のとき外して、忘れちゃった。
lines.kana: めがね、ここにない？きのう、なべのときはずして、わすれちゃった。
lines.english: Are my glasses here? I took them off while we were having hot pot and left them behind.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: aa, are mai no ka. hora, kore.
lines.ja: ああ、あれマイのか。ほら、これ。
lines.kana: ああ、あれまいのか。ほら、これ。
lines.english: Oh, so those were yours. Here you go.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yokatta, arigatou. are, ima kara ohiru?
lines.ja: よかった、ありがとう。あれ、今からお昼？
lines.kana: よかった、ありがとう。あれ、いまからおひる？
lines.english: Phew, thanks. Oh, are you just having lunch?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. kinou katta obentou, renji de atatameru tokoro.
lines.ja: うん。昨日買ったお弁当、レンジで温めるところ。
lines.kana: うん。きのうかったおべんとう、れんじであたためるところ。
lines.english: Yeah. I'm about to microwave the bento I bought yesterday.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kinou? sore, reizouko ni ireta?
lines.ja: 昨日？それ、冷蔵庫に入れた？
lines.kana: きのう？それ、れいぞうこにいれた？
lines.english: Yesterday? Did you put it in the fridge?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uun, zutto koko ni atta. nabe tabete, wasureteta.
lines.ja: ううん、ずっとここにあった。鍋食べて、忘れてた。
lines.kana: ううん、ずっとここにあった。なべたべて、わすれてた。
lines.english: Nope, it's been sitting here the whole time. We had hot pot and I forgot all about it.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, kore, kigen kireteru yo. kinou no yoru juuji made.
lines.ja: あ、これ、期限切れてるよ。昨日の夜十時まで。
lines.kana: あ、これ、きげんきれてるよ。きのうのよるじゅうじまで。
lines.english: Oh, this is past its date. It was only good till ten last night.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: demo, kigen chotto kireta dake desho? obentou wa atatamereba daijoubu da yo.
lines.ja: でも、期限ちょっと切れただけでしょ？お弁当は温めれば大丈夫だよ。
lines.kana: でも、きげんちょっときれただけでしょ？おべんとうはあたためればだいじょうぶだよ。
lines.english: But it's only just past, right? A bento's fine if you heat it up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: dame da yo. reizouko ni iretenakatta shi, kigen mo kireteru n da kara.
lines.ja: だめだよ。冷蔵庫に入れてなかったし、期限も切れてるんだから。
lines.kana: だめだよ。れいぞうこにいれてなかったし、きげんもきれてるんだから。
lines.english: No way. It wasn't in the fridge, and it's past its date as well.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: aa, obentou atatamete taberu tsumori datta noni.
lines.ja: ああ、お弁当温めて食べるつもりだったのに。
lines.kana: ああ、おべんとうあたためてたべるつもりだったのに。
lines.english: Aw, and I was going to heat it up and have it for lunch.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kinou no nabe, mada aru n ja nai?
lines.ja: 昨日の鍋、まだあるんじゃない？
lines.kana: きのうのなべ、まだあるんじゃない？
lines.english: Isn't there still some hot pot left from last night?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, sou da. kenta ga futa shite, reizouko ni iretoite kureta n da.
lines.ja: あ、そうだ。ケンタが蓋して、冷蔵庫に入れといてくれたんだ。
lines.kana: あ、そうだ。けんたがふたして、れいぞうこにいれといてくれたんだ。
lines.english: Oh, right. Kenta put the lid on and stuck it in the fridge for us.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto da, mada ippai aru. sasuga kenta.
lines.ja: ほんとだ、まだいっぱいある。さすがケンタ。
lines.kana: ほんとだ、まだいっぱいある。さすがけんた。
lines.english: So there is, and loads of it. Good old Kenta.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, futa shite, gofun gurai atatameyou.
lines.ja: じゃあ、蓋して、五分ぐらい温めよう。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ふたして、ごふんぐらいあたためよう。
lines.english: Right, lid on, and we'll heat it for about five minutes.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. kondo kara, obentou wa sugu reizouko ni iretoite ne.
lines.ja: うん。今度から、お弁当はすぐ冷蔵庫に入れといてね。
lines.kana: うん。こんどから、おべんとうはすぐれいぞうこにいれといてね。
lines.english: OK. And from now on, put your bento straight in the fridge, alright?

questions.english: What happened with Sora's lunch?
questions.ja: ソラのお昼は、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: そらのおひるは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: sora no ohiru wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: The microwave wasn't working, so they heated his bento up in a pot instead.
His bento had been left out all night and was past its date, so they heated up the leftover hot pot instead.
Kenta had already finished the leftover hot pot, so Sora heated up his bento after all.

questions.explanation: Sora bought the bento yesterday and it sat out all night (lines 6-8). Mai finds its date ran out at ten last night (line 9) and won't let him eat it, even heated (lines 10-11). So they heat up the hot pot Kenta put in the fridge (lines 13-16). A is wrong: the microwave is never a problem, the bento itself is. C is wrong: the hot pot is still there, and plenty of it (line 15).

questions.english: Sora came over for hot pot at your place, and there's a lot left. He asks, "nabe, mada ippai aru ne. dou suru?" Say you'll put it in the fridge, using reizouko ni ireru.
questions.ja: 鍋、まだいっぱいあるね。どうする？
questions.kana: なべ、まだいっぱいあるね。どうする？
questions.romaji: nabe, mada ippai aru ne. dou suru?
questions.answer: Say it goes in the fridge: reizouko ni ireru, with ni for where the food goes. With -toku it means putting it in there for later: reizouko ni iretoku ne (I'll put it in the fridge).

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, reizouko ni iretoku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、冷蔵庫に入れとくね。
modelAnswers.english: I'll put it in the fridge, then.

modelAnswers.romaji: futa shite, reizouko ni irete okou. ashita mo taberareru shi.
modelAnswers.ja: 蓋して、冷蔵庫に入れておこう。明日も食べられるし。
modelAnswers.english: Let's put the lid on and put it in the fridge. We can have it tomorrow too.

questions.explanation: Mai asks 'reizouko ni ireta?' (did you put it in the fridge?) in line 7, Sora says Kenta 'reizouko ni iretoite kureta' (put it in the fridge for us) in line 14, and Mai ends with 'reizouko ni iretoite ne' in line 17. The verb is ireru, put inside; oku, the English 'put', is setting something down on a surface. Keep ni: it marks where the food goes, unlike satou o ireru, where o marks what goes in.

questions.english: Mai tells Sora his bento is past its date. What does Sora say about it?
questions.ja: ソラは、お弁当について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらは、おべんとうについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora wa, obentou ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It would be fine if he put it in the fridge for a while first.
It tastes fine cold, so there's no need to heat it.
It would be fine to eat as long as he heated it up.

questions.explanation: Line 10: 'obentou wa atatamereba daijoubu da yo' (a bento's fine if you heat it up). atatameru is heating food up, and -ba makes it 'if you heat it'. A is wrong: he says nothing about the fridge, and the bento had never been in it, which is Mai's point in line 11. B is wrong: he wants it hot. In line 6 he was about to heat it in the microwave ('renji de atatameru tokoro'), and in line 12 he says he'd planned to heat it up and eat it.

questions.english: There's still plenty of hot pot left. What does Sora say as they heat it up?
questions.ja: 鍋を温めるとき、ソラは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: なべをあたためるとき、そらはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: nabe o atatameru toki, sora wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: lid on, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa shite, gofun gurai atatameyou.

choices.english: set the lid down, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa oite, gofun gurai atatameyou.

choices.english: lid off, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa totte, gofun gurai atatameyou.

questions.explanation: Line 16: 'futa shite' (put the lid on). A lid goes on with suru, the same suru as masuku o suru, and Kenta did the same before the pot went in the fridge (line 14: 'futa shite, reizouko ni iretoite kureta'). B is the English 'put the lid on' turned word for word into futa o oku, which means setting the lid down somewhere, so the pot would heat uncovered. C, futa o toru, takes the lid off: the opposite of what Sora does after Mai has looked inside.

questions.english: Sora offers you a bento from yesterday. You check the label: its date ran out last night. He asks, "kore, kinou no obentou da kedo, taberu?" Tell him it's past its date, using kigen ga kireru.
questions.ja: これ、昨日のお弁当だけど、食べる？
questions.kana: これ、きのうのおべんとうだけど、たべる？
questions.romaji: kore, kinou no obentou da kedo, taberu?
questions.answer: Say it's past its date: kigen kireteru (ga often drops in casual talk), with kireru, the verb for something running out. Then turn it down.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, sore kigen kireteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、それ期限切れてるよ。
modelAnswers.english: No, that's past its date.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, kigen ga kireteru kara, yametoku.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、期限が切れてるから、やめとく。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, it's past its date, so I'll pass.

questions.explanation: Mai says 'kigen kireteru yo' in line 9 and 'kigen mo kireteru' in line 11, and Sora's 'kigen chotto kireta dake desho?' in line 10 is the past form. 'Expire' needs no special verb: a date runs out with kireru, just as Sora's phone battery did in line 2 ('juuden kireteta'). Don't mix it up with kigen ga warui, 'in a bad mood', which is a different kigen.

script.title: Glasses Off
script.setting: Late afternoon at home. Kenji, a high-school boy, comes in from school without his glasses, and his mother notices straight away.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: are? kenji, megane kaketenai ja nai. dou shita no?
lines.ja: あれ？ケンジ、メガネかけてないじゃない。どうしたの？
lines.kana: あれ？けんじ、めがねかけてないじゃない。どうしたの？
lines.english: Huh? Kenji, you're not wearing your glasses. What happened?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: kyou, gakkou de zutto megane hazushiteta.
lines.ja: 今日、学校でずっとメガネ外してた。
lines.kana: きょう、がっこうでずっとめがねはずしてた。
lines.english: I had them off all day at school today.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e, nande? megane nai to, nanimo mienai desho?
lines.ja: え、なんで？メガネないと、何も見えないでしょ？
lines.kana: え、なんで？めがねないと、なにもみえないでしょ？
lines.english: What, why? You can't see a thing without them, can you?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: betsu ni. megane nai hou ga, ii kana tte.
lines.ja: 別に。メガネないほうが、いいかなって。
lines.kana: べつに。めがねないほうが、いいかなって。
lines.english: No reason. I just thought I might look better without them.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: a, wakatta. kakko tsuketakatta n desho. suki na ko demo iru no?
lines.ja: あ、わかった。かっこつけたかったんでしょ。好きな子でもいるの？
lines.kana: あ、わかった。かっこつけたかったんでしょ。すきなこでもいるの？
lines.english: Oh, I get it. You wanted to look cool, didn't you? Is there a girl you like or something?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: chigau tte. sore yori, kyou wa minna no mae de haji o kaita n da yo.
lines.ja: ちがうって。それより、今日はみんなの前で恥をかいたんだよ。
lines.kana: ちがうって。それより、きょうはみんなのまえではじをかいたんだよ。
lines.english: I said no. Anyway, I made a fool of myself in front of everyone today.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e, nani ga atta no?
lines.ja: え、何があったの？
lines.kana: え、なにがあったの？
lines.english: Oh no, what happened?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: asa, ano ko da to omotte, kakko tsukete koe kaketa n da.
lines.ja: 朝、あの子だと思って、かっこつけて声かけたんだ。
lines.kana: あさ、あのこだとおもって、かっこつけてこえかけたんだ。
lines.english: This morning I thought I saw her, so I played it cool and said hi.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ano ko? yappari iru n ja nai. sore de?
lines.ja: あの子？やっぱりいるんじゃない。それで？
lines.kana: あのこ？やっぱりいるんじゃない。それで？
lines.english: Her? So there is someone! And then?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sore ga, sensei datta. tomodachi ni metcha baka ni sareta.
lines.ja: それが、先生だった。友だちにめっちゃバカにされた。
lines.kana: それが、せんせいだった。ともだちにめっちゃばかにされた。
lines.english: It was a teacher. My friends totally made fun of me.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e, sensei ni? sore wa omoshiroi ne.
lines.ja: え、先生に？それはおもしろいね。
lines.kana: え、せんせいに？それはおもしろいね。
lines.english: What, to a teacher? Well, that's funny.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: okaasan made baka ni shinaide yo.
lines.ja: お母さんまでバカにしないでよ。
lines.kana: おかあさんまでばかにしないでよ。
lines.english: Don't you make fun of me too, Mom.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: gomen gomen, baka ni shitenai yo. hazukashikatta ne.
lines.ja: ごめんごめん、バカにしてないよ。恥ずかしかったね。
lines.kana: ごめんごめん、ばかにしてないよ。はずかしかったね。
lines.english: Sorry, sorry, I'm not making fun of you. That must have been embarrassing.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. anna ni haji o kaita no, hajimete da yo.
lines.ja: うん。あんなに恥をかいたの、初めてだよ。
lines.kana: うん。あんなにはじをかいたの、はじめてだよ。
lines.english: Yeah. I've never made such a fool of myself.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dakara, kakko tsukenakute ii no yo. megane kaketete mo, kenji wa kakkoii n da kara.
lines.ja: だから、かっこつけなくていいのよ。メガネかけてても、ケンジはかっこいいんだから。
lines.kana: だから、かっこつけなくていいのよ。めがねかけてても、けんじはかっこいいんだから。
lines.english: That's why you don't need to act cool. You're cool with your glasses on too, you know.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sore, ato de ano ko ni mo iwareta. megane kaketeru hou ga, kakkoii tte.
lines.ja: それ、あとであの子にも言われた。メガネかけてるほうが、かっこいいって。
lines.kana: それ、あとであのこにもいわれた。めがねかけてるほうが、かっこいいって。
lines.english: She said that too, later. That I look cooler with my glasses on.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hora ne. jaa, ashita wa chanto megane kakete ikinasai.
lines.ja: ほらね。じゃあ、明日はちゃんとメガネかけて行きなさい。
lines.kana: ほらね。じゃあ、あしたはちゃんとめがねかけていきなさい。
lines.english: See? Then tomorrow, you wear your glasses to school.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. mou haji wa kakitakunai shi.
lines.ja: うん。もう恥はかきたくないし。
lines.kana: うん。もうはじはかきたくないし。
lines.english: Yeah. I don't want to make a fool of myself again anyway.

questions.english: What happened?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji's friends made fun of his glasses, so he's going to stop wearing them to school.
Kenji took his glasses off to look cool, mistook a teacher for the girl he likes, and will wear them again tomorrow.
Kenji played it cool with the girl he likes, but she told him he looks better without glasses.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-5: Kenji kept his glasses off all day at school, and his mother guesses he wanted to look cool for a girl. Lines 8-10: he called out to someone he took for the girl, but it was a teacher, and his friends made fun of him. Lines 16-18: the girl later told him he looks cooler with his glasses on, so he'll wear them tomorrow. A is wrong: his friends made fun of him for greeting a teacher, not for his glasses, and he's going back to wearing them (lines 17-18). C is wrong: the person he greeted was a teacher, not the girl (line 10), and the girl said he looks cooler with glasses, not without (line 16).

questions.english: You tell Kenji you don't know how to send a photo from your new phone. He smirks and says, "e, sore mo shiranai no? uso desho?" Tell him not to make fun of you, using baka ni suru.
questions.ja: え、それも知らないの？うそでしょ？
questions.kana: え、それもしらないの？うそでしょ？
questions.romaji: e, sore mo shiranai no? uso desho?
questions.answer: Protest with baka ni shinaide (yo), 'don't make fun of me', the way Kenji says it to his mother. Or call him out with baka ni shiteru desho (you're making fun of me, aren't you).

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto, baka ni shinaide yo. shiranai mono wa shiranai n da kara.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと、バカにしないでよ。知らないものは知らないんだから。
modelAnswers.english: Hey, don't make fun of me. I just don't know, all right?

modelAnswers.romaji: baka ni shiteru desho. jaa, kenji ga oshiete yo.
modelAnswers.ja: バカにしてるでしょ。じゃあ、ケンジが教えてよ。
modelAnswers.english: You're making fun of me, aren't you? Fine, then you show me.

questions.explanation: After his friends made fun of him (tomodachi ni metcha baka ni sareta, line 10), Kenji tells his mother okaasan made baka ni shinaide yo when she finds the story funny (line 12), and she answers baka ni shitenai yo (line 13). baka ni suru is mocking someone or treating them as stupid, which is what Kenji's smirk does here. karakau (tease) is lighter, for playful teasing, and warau only means laugh, so warawanaide is 'don't laugh', not 'don't make fun of me'. Keep the ni: baka ni suru, literally 'treat as a fool'.

questions.english: At a meeting today you called a new coworker by the wrong name in front of everyone. When you get home, your mother asks, "dou shita no? genki nai ne." Tell her what happened, using haji o kaku.
questions.ja: どうしたの？元気ないね。
questions.kana: どうしたの？げんきないね。
questions.romaji: dou shita no? genki nai ne.
questions.answer: Say you made a fool of yourself in front of everyone: minna no mae de haji o kaita (or haji o kaichatta). To say how it felt, add hazukashikatta.

modelAnswers.romaji: un. kyou, kaigi de haji o kaichatta. metcha hazukashikatta.
modelAnswers.ja: うん。今日、会議で恥をかいちゃった。めっちゃ恥ずかしかった。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah. I made a fool of myself in a meeting today. It was so embarrassing.

modelAnswers.romaji: minna no mae de haji kaita no. atarashii hito no namae, machigaechatta.
modelAnswers.ja: みんなの前で恥かいたの。新しい人の名前、間違えちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: I embarrassed myself in front of everyone. I got the new person's name wrong.

questions.explanation: Kenji uses haji o kaku three times about his mix-up: minna no mae de haji o kaita (line 6), anna ni haji o kaita no, hajimete (line 14) and mou haji wa kakitakunai (line 18). haji o kaku is the incident; how it felt is hazukashii, which his mother says in line 13 (hazukashikatta ne). 'I embarrassed myself' word for word, jibun o hazukashiku shita, isn't said in Japanese. This kaku is the one in ase o kaku (break out in sweat), not kaku 'write'. In casual speech the o can drop (haji kaita), and -chatta adds that it went wrong.

questions.english: When Kenji says he kept his glasses off all day, his mother says, "kakko tsuketakatta n desho." What does she mean?
questions.ja: お母さんは、ケンジのことをどう思いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、けんじのことをどうおもいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, kenji no koto o dou omoimashita ka?

choices.english: She thinks he was bragging to his friends about something.
She's telling him he looks cool without his glasses.
She thinks he was trying to look cool, maybe for a girl.

questions.explanation: Line 5: kakko tsukeru is putting on a cool act, trying to look good, and she follows it with suki na ko demo iru no? (is there a girl you like?). Kenji does it again in line 8 (kakko tsukete koe kaketa: played it cool and said hi), and in line 15 she tells him kakko tsukenakute ii (you don't need to act cool). A is jiman suru, boasting in words about what you have or did, and nobody brags here. B mixes it up with kakkoii, actually being cool: in line 15 she says he's cool with his glasses on (megane kaketete mo, kenji wa kakkoii), not without them.

newWords.english: can see, be visible (mienai: can't see)
kid; here, a girl (suki na ko: a girl you like; ano ko: that girl, her)
cool, good-looking (being cool, as opposed to kakko tsukeru, acting cool)

script.title: Rained Off
script.setting: A Sunday evening. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, leaves a voicemail for Kenta, who lent him a tent for a camping trip with some old friends. Rain spoiled part of their plan, and Satou-san has an idea for next Saturday.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, kenta-kun? satou desu. tento, kashite kurete arigatou gozaimashita.
lines.ja: もしもし、ケンタくん？佐藤です。テント、貸してくれてありがとうございました。
lines.kana: もしもし、けんたくん？さとうです。てんと、かしてくれてありがとうございました。
lines.english: Hello, Kenta? It's Satou. Thank you for lending me your tent.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kinou kara, mukashi no tomodachi to kyanpu ni itteta n desu. sakki kaette kimashita.
lines.ja: 昨日から、昔の友達とキャンプに行ってたんです。さっき帰ってきました。
lines.kana: きのうから、むかしのともだちときゃんぷにいってたんです。さっきかえってきました。
lines.english: I've been away camping with some old friends since yesterday. I just got back.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hontou wa, kinou minna de yama ni noboru tsumori datta n desu kedo, ame de dame deshita.
lines.ja: 本当は、昨日みんなで山に登るつもりだったんですけど、雨でだめでした。
lines.kana: ほんとうは、きのうみんなでやまにのぼるつもりだったんですけど、あめでだめでした。
lines.english: We'd actually planned to climb a mountain together yesterday, but the rain put a stop to that.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sorede, kawari ni tsuri ni itta n desu. maa, nanimo tsuremasen deshita kedo ne.
lines.ja: それで、代わりに釣りに行ったんです。まあ、何も釣れませんでしたけどね。
lines.kana: それで、かわりにつりにいったんです。まあ、なにもつれませんでしたけどね。
lines.english: So we went fishing instead. Not that we caught a thing.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo, minna de zutto hanashitete, ii kibun tenkan ni narimashita yo.
lines.ja: でも、みんなでずっと話してて、いい気分転換になりましたよ。
lines.kana: でも、みんなでずっとはなしてて、いいきぶんてんかんになりましたよ。
lines.english: But we chatted the whole time, and it made a really nice change of pace.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou ieba kenta-kun, mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai tte, ittemashita yo ne.
lines.ja: そういえばケンタくん、もう三年もキャンプに行ってないって、言ってましたよね。
lines.kana: そういえばけんたくん、もうさんねんもきゃんぷにいってないって、いってましたよね。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Kenta, you told me you hadn't been camping in three whole years.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: saikin wa shigoto bakkari de, zenzen karada o ugokashitenai tte.
lines.ja: 最近は仕事ばっかりで、全然体を動かしてないって。
lines.kana: さいきんはしごとばっかりで、ぜんぜんからだをうごかしてないって。
lines.english: And that lately it's been all work, and you haven't been moving your body at all.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: raishuu no doyoubi, minna de mou ichido, ano yama ni noboru n desu. kenta-kun mo issho ni dou desu ka?
lines.ja: 来週の土曜日、みんなでもう一度、あの山に登るんです。ケンタくんも一緒にどうですか？
lines.kana: らいしゅうのどようび、みんなでもういちど、あのやまにのぼるんです。けんたくんもいっしょにどうですか？
lines.english: Next Saturday we're all having another go at that mountain. Why don't you come along?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: chiisai yama desu kara, toshi o totta watashi demo noboremasu. demo, chanto karada o ugokasemasu yo.
lines.ja: 小さい山ですから、年をとった私でも登れます。でも、ちゃんと体を動かせますよ。
lines.kana: ちいさいやまですから、としをとったわたしでものぼれます。でも、ちゃんとからだをうごかせますよ。
lines.english: It's a small one, so even an old man like me can climb it. But you'll still get some proper exercise.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: shigoto de sutoresu mo tamatteru deshou? tama ni wa kibun tenkan shinai to.
lines.ja: 仕事でストレスもたまってるでしょう？たまには気分転換しないと。
lines.kana: しごとですとれすもたまってるでしょう？たまにはきぶんてんかんしないと。
lines.english: Work must be getting you stressed, too. You need a change of pace now and then.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yama ni nobotte kara, mata tsuri ni iku tsumori desu. sore mo ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
lines.ja: 山に登ってから、また釣りに行くつもりです。それもいい気分転換になりますよ。
lines.kana: やまにのぼってから、またつりにいくつもりです。それもいいきぶんてんかんになりますよ。
lines.english: After the climb, we're planning to go fishing again. That'll do you good, too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, doyoubi wa asa yoji ni demasu kara ne. jaa, renraku mattemasu.
lines.ja: あ、土曜日は朝四時に出ますからね。じゃあ、連絡待ってます。
lines.kana: あ、どようびはあさよじにでますからね。じゃあ、れんらくまってます。
lines.english: Oh, and on Saturday we leave at four in the morning. Well, let me know.

questions.english: Why does Satou-san call Kenta?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、どうしてケンタくんに電話しましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、どうしてけんたくんにでんわしましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, doushite kenta-kun ni denwa shimashita ka?

choices.english: To say the rain spoiled the whole trip, so he's bringing the tent back and staying home next weekend.
To thank him for the tent and invite him to climb the mountain with them next Saturday, after rain stopped them this time.
To tell him they caught lots of fish, and ask him to come fishing with them early tomorrow morning.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Satou-san thanks Kenta for lending him the tent. Lines 3-4: rain stopped them climbing the mountain, so they went fishing instead. Line 8: they're all having another go at that mountain next Saturday, and he asks Kenta to come, since Kenta said he hadn't been getting any exercise (line 7). A is wrong: the rain only stopped the climb, the trip was still a nice change of pace (line 5), and he's going out again next Saturday and wants Kenta along. C is wrong: they didn't catch a thing (line 4), and the outing is next Saturday, leaving at four in the morning (line 12), not tomorrow.

questions.english: Your friend Sora has spent all Sunday indoors. In the evening he stretches and groans, "kyou mo zutto uchi de geemu shiteta. nanka karada ga darui naa." Tell him he needs to get some exercise now and then, using karada o ugokasu.
questions.ja: 今日もずっとうちでゲームしてた。なんか体がだるいなあ。
questions.kana: きょうもずっとうちでげーむしてた。なんかからだがだるいなあ。
questions.romaji: kyou mo zutto uchi de geemu shiteta. nanka karada ga darui naa.
questions.answer: Tell him to get moving: tama ni wa karada (o) ugokasanakya (you've got to get some exercise now and then), or suggest doing it together with karada o ugokasou. It's ugokasu, with o.

modelAnswers.romaji: zutto uchi ni iru kara da yo. tama ni wa karada ugokasanakya.
modelAnswers.ja: ずっとうちにいるからだよ。たまには体動かさなきゃ。
modelAnswers.english: That's because you've been stuck indoors all day. You've got to get some exercise now and then.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita, issho ni soto de karada o ugokasou yo. sukoshi demo zenzen chigau kara.
modelAnswers.ja: 明日、一緒に外で体を動かそうよ。少しでも全然違うから。
modelAnswers.english: Let's go out and get some exercise together tomorrow. Even a little makes a big difference.

questions.explanation: Satou-san reminds Kenta he said he hadn't been moving his body at all (zenzen karada o ugokashitenai, line 7), and promises the small mountain still gives a proper workout (chanto karada o ugokasemasu, line 9). karada o ugokasu is the everyday way to talk about getting exercise, anything from a walk to a climb, and casual speech often drops the o (karada ugokasanakya). ugokasu means move something, so it takes o; ugoku is move by itself, so karada o ugoku is wrong, and karada ga ugokanai means you physically can't move. undou suru (exercise) works too, but it leans towards sport and the gym.

questions.english: Your manager Tanaka-san looks worn out on Friday afternoon and says, "saikin isogashikute, shuumatsu mo shigoto no koto bakari kangaete shimau n desu yo." Suggest something for the weekend and tell him it'll do him good, using kibun tenkan ni naru.
questions.ja: 最近忙しくて、週末も仕事のことばかり考えてしまうんですよ。
questions.kana: さいきんいそがしくて、しゅうまつもしごとのことばかりかんがえてしまうんですよ。
questions.romaji: saikin isogashikute, shuumatsu mo shigoto no koto bakari kangaete shimau n desu yo.
questions.answer: Suggest an outing (tsuri ni itte mitara dou desu ka?) and add ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo (it'd be a nice change of pace). Keep it polite with Tanaka-san: narimasu, not naru.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, shuumatsu wa tsuri ni itte mitara dou desu ka? ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、週末は釣りに行ってみたらどうですか？いい気分転換になりますよ。
modelAnswers.english: Then why not try going fishing this weekend? It'd be a nice change of pace.

modelAnswers.romaji: tama ni wa yama ni nobotte mitara dou desu ka? kitto ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: たまには山に登ってみたらどうですか？きっといい気分転換になりますよ。
modelAnswers.english: How about climbing a mountain for once? I'm sure it'd do you good.

questions.explanation: Satou-san says the rained-off trip still made ii kibun tenkan ni narimashita (a nice change of pace, line 5), and that fishing after the climb will be ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu too (line 11). kibun tenkan ni naru, usually with ii, says something does you good as a break, which makes it the natural phrase for encouraging someone. kibun tenkan suru is taking the break yourself: in line 10 Satou-san tells Kenta tama ni wa kibun tenkan shinai to (you need to take a break now and then). kibarashi ni naru works the same way, but leans towards taking your mind off something bad.

questions.english: On Monday your friend Yuki says, "shuumatsu, nani shiteta no? zutto renraku nakatta kedo." You didn't answer because you were climbing a mountain with friends on Saturday. Tell her, using yama ni noboru.
questions.ja: 週末、何してたの？ずっと連絡なかったけど。
questions.kana: しゅうまつ、なにしてたの？ずっとれんらくなかったけど。
questions.romaji: shuumatsu, nani shiteta no? zutto renraku nakatta kedo.
questions.answer: Say you were up a mountain with friends: tomodachi to yama ni nobotteta (n da), or yama ni nobotta. Keep the ni.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen gomen, tomodachi to yama ni nobotteta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんごめん、友達と山に登ってたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, sorry! I was off climbing a mountain with some friends.

modelAnswers.romaji: doyoubi ni, tomodachi to yama ni nobotta n da. ue made sanjikan mo kakatta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 土曜日に、友達と山に登ったんだ。上まで三時間もかかったよ。
modelAnswers.english: I climbed a mountain with friends on Saturday. It took three whole hours to reach the top.

questions.explanation: Satou-san had planned yama ni noboru tsumori (line 3), says they'll climb ano yama ni noboru next Saturday (line 8), and plans to go fishing again yama ni nobotte kara (after the climb, line 11). English 'climb a mountain' pulls you towards yama o noboru, which is also heard when the way up is the point (a steep path), but for having been up a mountain ni is about three times as common. noboremasu in line 9 is the can-do form: toshi o totta watashi demo noboremasu, even an old man like me can climb it. nobotteta is 'was climbing', a natural excuse for not answering.

questions.english: When rain stopped the climb, what did Satou-san and his friends do instead?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんたちは、代わりに何をしましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんたちは、かわりになにをしましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san-tachi wa, kawari ni nani o shimashita ka?

choices.english: They climbed a smaller mountain nearby.
They went fishing and caught enough for dinner.
They went fishing, but nobody caught anything.

questions.explanation: Line 4: sorede, kawari ni tsuri ni itta n desu (so we went fishing instead), then nanimo tsuremasen deshita (we didn't catch a thing). tsuri ni iku puts the activity straight before ni iku, and tsureru is a fish getting caught on the line, so the negative means nothing bit. B misses that negative. A: nobody climbed anything; rain called off the climb (line 3), and they'll try the same mountain next Saturday (line 8), with fishing again afterwards (mata tsuri ni iku tsumori, line 11).

questions.english: What did Satou-san say Kenta hadn't done for three years?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、ケンタくんのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、けんたくんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, kenta-kun no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He hasn't been camping in three whole years.
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai

choices.english: He hasn't gone 'camping' in three whole years (the English -ing word).
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo kyanpingu ni ittenai

choices.english: He hasn't been fishing in three whole years.
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo tsuri ni ittenai

questions.explanation: Line 6: sou ieba kenta-kun, mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai tte, ittemashita yo ne. ittenai is itte (i)nai, haven't gone, and Satou-san says the same of his own trip in line 2: kyanpu ni itteta n desu (I was away camping). B copies the English '-ing': the activity is kyanpu, and kyanpingu turns up mostly in compounds like kyanpingu kaa (camper van). C: fishing is what Satou-san did on his trip and plans for next Saturday; what Kenta hadn't done in three years was camp, which is why his tent was free to lend.

newWords.english: (of a fish) be caught, bite: nanimo tsuremasen deshita = we didn't catch a thing
name suffix for a younger man or boy (kenta-kun)

script.title: No signal at the bus stop
script.setting: A Saturday afternoon in the countryside. Yuki and Kenta have just hiked down a mountain to a small bus stop at the bottom, and they want to know when the next bus back to town comes.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: haa, yatto basutei made kita. tsugi no basu, nanji kana?
lines.ja: はあ、やっとバス停まで来た。次のバス、何時かな？
lines.kana: はあ、やっとばすていまできた。つぎのばす、なんじかな？
lines.english: Phew, we made it to the bus stop at last. What time's the next bus, I wonder?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: chotto matte. netto de shirabete miru.
lines.ja: ちょっと待って。ネットで調べてみる。
lines.kana: ちょっとまって。ねっとでしらべてみる。
lines.english: Hang on, I'll look it up online.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: arigatou. sumaho, juuden kirechatte sa.
lines.ja: ありがとう。スマホ、充電切れちゃってさ。
lines.kana: ありがとう。すまほ、じゅうでんきれちゃってさ。
lines.english: Thanks. My phone's battery died, see.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: are? nanka netto tsunagaranai n da kedo.
lines.ja: あれ？なんかネットつながらないんだけど。
lines.kana: あれ？なんかねっとつながらないんだけど。
lines.english: Huh? The internet's not working for some reason.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yama no naka da kara ne. koko, denpa warui n ja nai?
lines.ja: 山の中だからね。ここ、電波悪いんじゃない？
lines.kana: やまのなかだからね。ここ、でんぱわるいんじゃない？
lines.english: Well, we're out in the mountains. The signal's probably bad here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto da. denpa warukute, nanimo mirenai.
lines.ja: ほんとだ。電波悪くて、何も見れない。
lines.kana: ほんとだ。でんぱわるくて、なにもみれない。
lines.english: You're right. The signal's so bad I can't load anything.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jaa, basu no jikan ga wakaru apuri toka, irete nai no?
lines.ja: じゃあ、バスの時間がわかるアプリとか、入れてないの？
lines.kana: じゃあ、ばすのじかんがわかるあぷりとか、いれてないの？
lines.english: Then haven't you got an app or something that tells you the bus times?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: irete nai. sore ni, apuri mo netto tsunagaranai to tsukaenai yo.
lines.ja: 入れてない。それに、アプリもネットつながらないと使えないよ。
lines.kana: いれてない。それに、あぷりもねっとつながらないとつかえないよ。
lines.english: Nope. Besides, apps don't work either if the internet's down.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sokka. jaa, ikkai dengen kitte, mata irete mitara?
lines.ja: そっか。じゃあ、一回電源切って、また入れてみたら？
lines.kana: そっか。じゃあ、いっかいでんげんきって、またいれてみたら？
lines.english: Oh, right. Then why not try switching it off and on again?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: dame. dengen irete mo, yappari denpa warui.
lines.ja: だめ。電源入れても、やっぱり電波悪い。
lines.kana: だめ。でんげんいれても、やっぱりでんぱわるい。
lines.english: No good. Even after turning it back on, the signal's still bad.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nee, yuki.
lines.ja: ねえ、ユキ。
lines.kana: ねえ、ゆき。
lines.english: Hey, Yuki.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: matte. mou ikkai netto de shirabete miru kara.
lines.ja: 待って。もう一回ネットで調べてみるから。
lines.kana: まって。もういっかいねっとでしらべてみるから。
lines.english: Wait. I'm going to try looking it up online one more time.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: iya, netto de shirabenakute mo ii kamo. hora, ushiro.
lines.ja: いや、ネットで調べなくてもいいかも。ほら、後ろ。
lines.kana: いや、ねっとでしらべなくてもいいかも。ほら、うしろ。
lines.english: No, I don't think you need to look it up online. Look, behind you.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e? a, jikokuhyou! zutto koko ni atta n da.
lines.ja: え？あ、時刻表！ずっとここにあったんだ。
lines.kana: え？あ、じこくひょう！ずっとここにあったんだ。
lines.english: Huh? Oh, the timetable! It was right here the whole time.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: tsugi wa sanji yonjuppun da tte. ato juppun da yo.
lines.ja: 次は3時40分だって。あと10分だよ。
lines.kana: つぎはさんじよんじゅっぷんだって。あとじゅっぷんだよ。
lines.english: The next one's at 3:40, it says. That's ten minutes from now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yokatta. demo ichiou, apuri iretoku.
lines.ja: よかった。でも一応、アプリ入れとく。
lines.kana: よかった。でもいちおう、あぷりいれとく。
lines.english: Phew. I'll still get the app, though, just in case.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: netto ga tsunagattara ne.
lines.ja: ネットがつながったらね。
lines.kana: ねっとがつながったらね。
lines.english: Once the internet's working, that is.

questions.english: What happens at the bus stop?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki's phone works again after she switches it off and on, so she finds the bus time online.
Kenta's phone has died, so they miss the bus and have to wait another hour.
They can't get online to check the bus times, then Kenta spots the timetable right there at the stop.

questions.explanation: In line 2 Yuki offers to look up the next bus online (netto de shirabete miru). In line 4 the internet won't connect (netto tsunagaranai), and in lines 5-6 they put it down to the bad signal in the mountains (denpa warui). In lines 9-10 switching the phone off and on doesn't help. In line 13 Kenta says she doesn't need to look it up online and points behind her, and in line 14 Yuki sees that the timetable was there all along. A is wrong: in line 10 the signal is still bad after she turns the phone back on, and they get the time from the timetable, not the internet. B is wrong: Kenta's phone has died (line 3), but they don't miss the bus. The next one comes in ten minutes (line 15).

questions.english: You and Kenta want to see a film tonight. He asks, "nee, kono eiga, nanji kara da kke?" You don't know. Offer to look it up online.
questions.ja: ねえ、この映画、何時からだっけ？
questions.kana: ねえ、このえいが、なんじからだっけ？
questions.romaji: nee, kono eiga, nanji kara da kke?
questions.answer: Say you'll look it up online: netto de shirabete miru (let me look it up online), or netto de shiraberu ne. Keep de, because the internet is the tool you look things up with.

modelAnswers.romaji: wakannai. chotto netto de shirabete miru.
modelAnswers.ja: わかんない。ちょっとネットで調べてみる。
modelAnswers.english: No idea. Let me look it up online.

modelAnswers.romaji: nanji da kke. chotto matte, netto de shiraberu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 何時だっけ。ちょっと待って、ネットで調べるね。
modelAnswers.english: What time was it again? Hang on, I'll look it up online.

questions.explanation: When Kenta wonders about the bus, Yuki says 'chotto matte. netto de shirabete miru' (line 2) and says it again in line 12. In line 13 Kenta tells her 'netto de shirabenakute mo ii kamo' (no need to look it up online). de marks the internet as the means, the same way as sumaho de or jisho de. The thing you check takes o (eiga no jikan o netto de shiraberu). shiraberu is for checking facts like times and meanings. For finding a place such as a shop, use sagasu (netto de sagasu). Kenta asks casually, so answer casually. Adding -te miru makes it a friendly offer.

questions.english: When Yuki tries to look up the bus on her phone, something goes wrong. What does she say?
questions.ja: スマホを見て、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: すまほをみて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sumaho o mite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: The internet won't connect for some reason.
choices.romaji: nanka netto tsunagaranai n da kedo

choices.english: The internet isn't working (hataraku: work, as a person does a job).
choices.romaji: nanka netto hatarakanai n da kedo

choices.english: The internet won't move (ugoku, as for a frozen app).
choices.romaji: nanka netto ugokanai n da kedo

questions.explanation: In line 4 Yuki says 'are? nanka netto tsunagaranai n da kedo.' When Wi-Fi or mobile data fails, Japanese says the internet doesn't connect (tsunagaranai). Yuki says it again in line 8 (netto tsunagaranai to tsukaenai), and Kenta uses it in line 17 (netto ga tsunagattara ne). B is wrong: hataraku is 'work' in the sense of a person doing a job, so this copies English 'isn't working' word for word. C is wrong: ugokanai (won't move) is for a frozen app or device, not for a connection that won't come up.

questions.english: You're out in the countryside when Kenta calls. The line keeps breaking up, and he says, "moshimoshi? kikoeru? nanka, yoku kikoenai n da kedo." Tell him it's the signal.
questions.ja: もしもし？聞こえる？なんか、よく聞こえないんだけど。
questions.kana: もしもし？きこえる？なんか、よくきこえないんだけど。
questions.romaji: moshimoshi? kikoeru? nanka, yoku kikoenai n da kedo.
questions.answer: Apologise and blame the signal with denpa ga warui. In casual speech ga drops: gomen, koko denpa warui n da. To give the bad signal as the reason for something, use the -kute form: denpa warukute.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, koko denpa warui n da. ato de mata kakeru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、ここ電波悪いんだ。後でまたかけるね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, the signal's bad here. I'll call you back later.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, denpa warukute, kotchi mo yoku kikoenai.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、電波悪くて、こっちもよく聞こえない。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, the signal's bad. I can't hear you well either.

questions.explanation: Kenta says 'koko, denpa warui n ja nai?' in line 5. Yuki says 'denpa warukute, nanimo mirenai' in line 6 and 'yappari denpa warui' in line 10. Phone signal is denpa ('radio waves'). Don't say shingou, which means a traffic light, or the loanword shigunaru. warui covers both broken-up calls and pages that won't load. If there's no signal at all, say denpa hairanai. Kenta is a friend, so drop ga and answer casually.

questions.english: Once they've found the timetable, Yuki says, "demo ichiou, apuri iretoku." What is she going to do?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、何をしますか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なにをしますか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: Turn her phone back on and try the internet again.
Get the bus-times app on her phone anyway, just in case.
Put her phone away in her bag, since they don't need it now.

questions.explanation: Line 16: apuri iretoku is apuri o ireru (get an app, literally 'put it in') plus -toku (do it ahead of time). It's the kind of app Kenta asked about in line 7 (basu no jikan ga wakaru apuri toka, irete nai no?), and in line 8 she said she didn't have it (irete nai). That's why Kenta jokes in line 17 that she'll have to wait until the internet works. A is wrong: turning the phone on is dengen o ireru, which she already tried in line 10, and here the thing she 'puts in' is the app, not the power. C is wrong: ireru can mean putting something into a bag, but she said apuri, and nobody mentions a bag. Note that English 'get the app' is not apuri o morau, which would sound as if someone handed it to you.

script.title: Camping at home
script.setting: Friday evening in the flat Kenta and Sora share. Kenta has spent a month planning a weekend camping trip for the two of them, and Sora, who dropped out last time when work came up, has sworn he's coming. Then a typhoon turns up in the news.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora, ashita no kyanpu, honto ni daijoubu? kondo wa chanto yakusoku mamotte yo.
lines.ja: ソラ、明日のキャンプ、ほんとに大丈夫？今度はちゃんと約束守ってよ。
lines.kana: そら、あしたのきゃんぷ、ほんとにだいじょうぶ？こんどはちゃんとやくそくまもってよ。
lines.english: Sora, are you really OK for tomorrow's camping? Keep your promise this time, properly.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: daijoubu da tte. mae wa kyuu ni shigoto haitchatta dake da yo. yakusoku wa mamoru yo.
lines.ja: 大丈夫だって。前は急に仕事入っちゃっただけだよ。約束は守るよ。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶだって。まえはきゅうにしごとはいっちゃっただけだよ。やくそくはまもるよ。
lines.english: I told you, it's fine. Last time work just came up out of nowhere. I'll keep my promise.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nara ii kedo. sengetsu kara keikaku tateteta n da kara ne.
lines.ja: ならいいけど。先月から計画立ててたんだからね。
lines.kana: ならいいけど。せんげつからけいかくたててたんだからね。
lines.english: Good, then. I've been planning this since last month, you know.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: shitteru yo. a, chotto kore mite. ashita, taifuu kuru tte.
lines.ja: 知ってるよ。あ、ちょっとこれ見て。明日、台風来るって。
lines.kana: しってるよ。あ、ちょっとこれみて。あした、たいふうくるって。
lines.english: I know. Oh, look at this. They say a typhoon's coming tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, uso. demo, mada wakannai yo ne. toriaezu ashita no asa made yousu miyou.
lines.ja: え、うそ。でも、まだわかんないよね。とりあえず明日の朝まで様子見よう。
lines.kana: え、うそ。でも、まだわかんないよね。とりあえずあしたのあさまでようすみよう。
lines.english: What, no way. But we can't tell yet, right? Let's just wait and see till tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. a, mite. nichiyoubi no sakkaa no shiai, mou chuushi ni natta tte.
lines.ja: うん。あ、見て。日曜日のサッカーの試合、もう中止になったって。
lines.kana: うん。あ、みて。にちようびのさっかーのしあい、もうちゅうしになったって。
lines.english: Yeah. Oh, look. Sunday's football match has already been called off.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: maji de? a, kyanpujou kara meeru da.
lines.ja: マジで？あ、キャンプ場からメールだ。
lines.kana: まじで？あ、きゃんぷじょうからめーるだ。
lines.english: Seriously? Oh, there's an email from the campsite.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, nante?
lines.ja: え、なんて？
lines.kana: え、なんて？
lines.english: Oh, what's it say?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: dame da. taifuu de, kyanpu chuushi ni natta. yoyaku mo kyanseru shinakya.
lines.ja: だめだ。台風で、キャンプ中止になった。予約もキャンセルしなきゃ。
lines.kana: だめだ。たいふうで、きゃんぷちゅうしになった。よやくもきゃんせるしなきゃ。
lines.english: No good. The camping's been called off because of the typhoon. I'll have to cancel the booking too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: zannen. ashita made yousu miru hitsuyou mo nakatta ne.
lines.ja: 残念。明日まで様子見る必要もなかったね。
lines.kana: ざんねん。あしたまでようすみるひつようもなかったね。
lines.english: Too bad. Guess we didn't even need to wait and see till tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: haa, sekkaku keikaku tateta noni naa.
lines.ja: はあ、せっかく計画立てたのになあ。
lines.kana: はあ、せっかくけいかくたてたのになあ。
lines.english: Sigh. After all the trouble I went to planning it.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa sa, uchi de kyanpu shiyou yo. yakusoku wa mamoru tte itta desho?
lines.ja: じゃあさ、うちでキャンプしようよ。約束は守るって言ったでしょ？
lines.kana: じゃあさ、うちできゃんぷしようよ。やくそくはまもるっていったでしょ？
lines.english: Then let's camp at home. I said I'd keep my promise, didn't I?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: uchi de? ii kedo, keikaku wa?
lines.ja: うちで？いいけど、計画は？
lines.kana: うちで？いいけど、けいかくは？
lines.english: At home? Sure, but what's the plan?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: keikaku wa boku ga tateru. tento wa heya no naka. de, gohan wa kenta ga tsukuru.
lines.ja: 計画は僕が立てる。テントは部屋の中。で、ご飯はケンタが作る。
lines.kana: けいかくはぼくがたてる。てんとはへやのなか。で、ごはんはけんたがつくる。
lines.english: I'll work out the plan. The tent goes indoors. And you do the cooking.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora ga keikaku tateru to, kekkyoku boku ga gohan tsukuru n da.
lines.ja: ソラが計画立てると、結局僕がご飯作るんだ。
lines.kana: そらがけいかくたてると、けっきょくぼくがごはんつくるんだ。
lines.english: So when Sora makes the plans, I end up doing the cooking anyway.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii jan. kenta no gohan, oishii shi.
lines.ja: いいじゃん。ケンタのご飯、おいしいし。
lines.kana: いいじゃん。けんたのごはん、おいしいし。
lines.english: So what? Your cooking's good.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: wakatta, wakatta. jaa, taifuu ga kite mo, uchi no kyanpu wa chuushi ni naranai ne.
lines.ja: わかった、わかった。じゃあ、台風が来ても、うちのキャンプは中止にならないね。
lines.kana: わかった、わかった。じゃあ、たいふうがきても、うちのきゃんぷはちゅうしにならないね。
lines.english: Okay, okay. Well, at least our home camp won't get called off, even if the typhoon comes.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Work comes up for Sora again, so Kenta calls off the camping trip and decides to cook at home instead.
A typhoon gets their camping trip called off, so Sora, who promised to come this time, suggests camping at home instead.
They hear a typhoon is coming, so they decide to wait until the morning before deciding whether to go camping.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenta reminds Sora to keep his promise this time, and Sora swears he will. Line 4: a typhoon is coming. Line 9: an email from the campsite settles it, kyanpu chuushi ni natta. Line 12: Sora suggests uchi de kyanpu shiyou yo and reminds Kenta he said he'd keep his promise. A: work came up for Sora last time (line 2), not now, and Kenta isn't the one who calls it off. C: Kenta does suggest waiting until the morning (line 5), but the email arrives that same evening, so there's nothing left to wait for (line 10).

questions.english: Kenta says: "I think I might be getting a cold. Should I take tomorrow off work?" Tell him to wait and see how he feels for now before deciding.
questions.ja: なんか風邪ひいたかも。明日、仕事休んだほうがいいかな？
questions.kana: なんかかぜひいたかも。あした、しごとやすんだほうがいいかな？
questions.romaji: nanka kaze hiita kamo. ashita, shigoto yasunda hou ga ii kana?
questions.answer: Tell him to hold off and see how it goes with yousu o miru, not plain matsu: toriaezu konban wa yousu mitara?

modelAnswers.romaji: toriaezu konban wa yousu mitara?
modelAnswers.ja: とりあえず今晩は様子見たら？
modelAnswers.english: Why not just see how you feel tonight for now?

modelAnswers.romaji: mada wakannai yo. ashita no asa made yousu mite kara kimetara?
modelAnswers.ja: まだわかんないよ。明日の朝まで様子見てから決めたら？
modelAnswers.english: You can't tell yet. Why not wait and see till tomorrow morning, then decide?

questions.explanation: Holding off to see how something develops is yousu o miru, literally 'look at how things are'. Kenta says toriaezu ashita no asa made yousu miyou about the typhoon (line 5), and once the camp is off Sora says ashita made yousu miru hitsuyou mo nakatta ne (line 10). Plain matsu ('wait') says nothing about watching how things go. For a cold, friends and doctors alike say yousu o miru.

questions.english: What did Sora say about Sunday's football match?
questions.ja: ソラさんは日曜日のサッカーの試合について、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんはにちようびのさっかーのしあいについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa nichiyoubi no sakkaa no shiai ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Apparently it's already been postponed.
Apparently they've already cancelled it.
Apparently it's already been called off.

questions.explanation: Line 6: nichiyoubi no sakkaa no shiai, mou chuushi ni natta tte. A match, a festival or any other event that gets called off is chuushi ni naru, and the camping trip gets the same phrase in line 9. B, kyanseru sareta, is English 'cancelled' word for word. kyanseru is for bookings and your own arrangements, as in Kenta's yoyaku mo kyanseru shinakya (line 9), not for an event that gets called off. A, enki ni natta, is the same frame with a different outcome: put off to a later date, not called off.

questions.english: Yuki says: "You're really coming tomorrow at ten, right? Don't be late like last time." Tell her not to worry: this time you'll keep your promise.
questions.ja: 明日の十時、ほんとに来てくれる？前みたいに遅れないでね。
questions.kana: あしたのじゅうじ、ほんとにきてくれる？まえみたいにおくれないでね。
questions.romaji: ashita no juuji, honto ni kite kureru? mae mitai ni okurenaide ne.
questions.answer: Promise with yakusoku o mamoru, not motsu: daijoubu, kondo wa chanto yakusoku mamoru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu, kondo wa chanto yakusoku mamoru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫、今度はちゃんと約束守るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Don't worry, this time I'll keep my promise properly.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, yakusoku wa mamoru kara. juuji ni iku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、約束は守るから。十時に行くね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll keep my word. I'll be there at ten.

questions.explanation: Keeping a promise is yakusoku o mamoru, literally 'protect the promise'. Kenta reminds Sora with kondo wa chanto yakusoku mamotte yo (line 1), and Sora pledges yakusoku wa mamoru yo (line 2), then holds him to it: yakusoku wa mamoru tte itta desho? (line 12). English 'keep' points to motsu, but Japanese doesn't say that about promises. Since Yuki is worried about lateness, being on time takes the same verb: jikan o mamoru.

questions.english: For the camp at home, what does Sora say he'll do himself?
questions.ja: うちでキャンプするとき、ソラさんは何をすると言いましたか？
questions.kana: うちできゃんぷするとき、そらさんはなにをするといいましたか？
questions.romaji: uchi de kyanpu suru toki, sora-san wa nani o suru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Work out the plan for it.
Put the tent up in the room.
Do the cooking.

questions.explanation: Line 14: keikaku wa boku ga tateru. Plans are 'stood up' in Japanese: keikaku o tateru is working out a plan, as Kenta says about his month of planning (sengetsu kara keikaku tateteta, line 3; sekkaku keikaku tateta noni, line 11). B: tateru literally means 'stand something up', and the tent comes up next (tento wa heya no naka), but Sora only says where it goes. The thing he's standing up is the plan. C: the cooking goes to Kenta (gohan wa kenta ga tsukuru), and Kenta notices: sora ga keikaku tateru to, kekkyoku boku ga gohan tsukuru n da (line 15). You tsukuru a meal but tateru a plan.

newWords.english: cancel (a booking, an order, your own plans)

script.title: Tanaka-san dresses up
script.setting: A hot weekday morning at the office. Mai tells Yuki that their manager, Tanaka-san, has come in unusually dressed up, and the two of them try to work out why, until he walks over.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: nee, yuki. kesa no tanaka-san, mita?
lines.ja: ねえ、ユキ。今朝の田中さん、見た？
lines.kana: ねえ、ゆき。けさのたなかさん、みた？
lines.english: Hey, Yuki. Did you see Tanaka-san this morning?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uun, mada. dou shita no?
lines.ja: ううん、まだ。どうしたの？
lines.kana: ううん、まだ。どうしたの？
lines.english: No, not yet. Why, what's up with him?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: boushi kabutte kita no. hajimete mita yo.
lines.ja: 帽子かぶってきたの。初めて見たよ。
lines.kana: ぼうしかぶってきたの。はじめてみたよ。
lines.english: He came in wearing a hat. I've never seen that before.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, tanaka-san tte boushi kaburu n da.
lines.ja: え、田中さんって帽子かぶるんだ。
lines.kana: え、たなかさんってぼうしかぶるんだ。
lines.english: Huh, I didn't know Tanaka-san wore hats.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sore ni, nekutai mo shiteru no. itsumo wa shitenai noni.
lines.ja: それに、ネクタイもしてるの。いつもはしてないのに。
lines.kana: それに、ねくたいもしてるの。いつもはしてないのに。
lines.english: And he's got a tie on, too. He never wears one usually.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, konna ni atsui noni? nanika aru no kana.
lines.ja: え、こんなに暑いのに？何かあるのかな。
lines.kana: え、こんなにあついのに？なにかあるのかな。
lines.english: What, in this heat? I wonder if something's going on.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ato ne, kousui mo tsuketeta. sugoku ii nioi shita yo.
lines.ja: あとね、香水もつけてた。すごくいい匂いしたよ。
lines.kana: あとね、こうすいもつけてた。すごくいいにおいしたよ。
lines.english: Oh, and he had perfume on, too. He smelled really nice.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tanaka-san ga kousui tsukeru nante! moshikashite, deeto?
lines.ja: 田中さんが香水つけるなんて！もしかして、デート？
lines.kana: たなかさんがこうすいつけるなんて！もしかして、でーと？
lines.english: Tanaka-san wearing perfume! Don't tell me he's got a date?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: demo tanaka-san, kekkon shiteru yo.
lines.ja: でも田中さん、結婚してるよ。
lines.kana: でもたなかさん、けっこんしてるよ。
lines.english: But Tanaka-san's married.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, sou datta. demo yubiwa shiteru no, mita koto nai kamo.
lines.ja: あ、そうだった。でも指輪してるの、見たことないかも。
lines.kana: あ、そうだった。でもゆびわしてるの、みたことないかも。
lines.english: Oh, right. But I don't think I've ever seen him wear a ring.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sore ga ne, kyou wa yubiwa mo shiteru no.
lines.ja: それがね、今日は指輪もしてるの。
lines.kana: それがね、きょうはゆびわもしてるの。
lines.english: Well, that's the thing. Today he's wearing his ring, too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: boushi kabutte, nekutai shite, kousui tsukete, yubiwa made? zettai nanika aru yo!
lines.ja: 帽子かぶって、ネクタイして、香水つけて、指輪まで？絶対何かあるよ！
lines.kana: ぼうしかぶって、ねくたいして、こうすいつけて、ゆびわまで？ぜったいなにかあるよ！
lines.english: A hat, a tie, perfume, and his ring as well? Something's definitely going on!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. nanika atta n desu ka?
lines.ja: おはようございます。何かあったんですか？
lines.kana: おはようございます。なにかあったんですか？
lines.english: Good morning. Has something happened?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, ohayou gozaimasu! ano, kyou wa nekutai shiteru n desu ne.
lines.ja: あ、おはようございます！あの、今日はネクタイしてるんですね。
lines.kana: あ、おはようございます！あの、きょうはねくたいしてるんですね。
lines.english: Oh, good morning! Um, I see you're wearing a tie today.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: aa, kore desu ka. jitsu wa kyou de, kekkon shite juu nen na n desu.
lines.ja: ああ、これですか。実は今日で、結婚して十年なんです。
lines.kana: ああ、これですか。じつはきょうで、けっこんしてじゅうねんなんです。
lines.english: Ah, this? Actually, today it's ten years since I got married.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: omedetou gozaimasu! dakara yubiwa mo shite kita n desu ne.
lines.ja: おめでとうございます！だから指輪もしてきたんですね。
lines.kana: おめでとうございます！だからゆびわもしてきたんですね。
lines.english: Congratulations! So that's why you've got your ring on, too.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee. konban wa tsuma to deeto na node, chotto kakko tsukete mimashita.
lines.ja: ええ。今晩は妻とデートなので、ちょっとかっこつけてみました。
lines.kana: ええ。こんばんはつまとでーとなので、ちょっとかっこつけてみました。
lines.english: Yes. I've got a date with my wife tonight, so I thought I'd try to look sharp.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yappari deeto datta n da! nanka watashi made tenshon agatte kita.
lines.ja: やっぱりデートだったんだ！なんか私までテンション上がってきた。
lines.kana: やっぱりでーとだったんだ！なんかわたしまでてんしょんあがってきた。
lines.english: I knew it was a date! Now I'm all excited too.

questions.english: Why has Tanaka-san come in dressed up today?
questions.ja: 田中さんは今日、何があるんですか？
questions.kana: たなかさんはきょう、なにがあるんですか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa kyou, nani ga aru n desu ka?

choices.english: He's going to a friend's wedding after work.
He's meeting an important client at the office today.
It's ten years since he got married, and he has a date with his wife tonight.

questions.explanation: Line 15: kyou de kekkon shite juu nen (today makes ten years since he married), and line 17: konban wa tsuma to deeto (a date with his wife tonight), so he dressed up a little (chotto kakko tsukete mimashita). Yuki's guess of a date was right, just not the way she meant it. A: kekkon is his own marriage, not a friend's wedding. B: nobody mentions a client or a meeting.

questions.english: Mai tells Yuki what Tanaka-san came in wearing this morning. What did she say?
questions.ja: マイさんは、今朝の田中さんについて何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、けさのたなかさんについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, kesa no tanaka-san ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He came in wearing a hat (kiru, the clothes verb).
He came in with a hat on (kaburu).
He came in with a hat put on (tsukeru).

questions.explanation: Line 3: 'boushi kabutte kita no', and Yuki echoes it in line 4: boushi kaburu n da. Anything pulled over the head (a hat, a cap, a helmet) takes kaburu. A: kiru is for clothes on the body, like a shirt or a coat, so boushi o kiru is the English 'wear' carried over. C: tsukeru is for things put onto the body, like the perfume he also had on (kousui tsuketeta), not for a hat.

questions.english: Yuki says she's never seen Tanaka-san wear a ring. What does Mai tell her?
questions.ja: マイさんは、田中さんの指輪について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、たなかさんのゆびわについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, tanaka-san no yubiwa ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Today he's wearing his ring, too.
He's bought a ring to give his wife tonight.
He's left his ring at home again today.

questions.explanation: Line 11: 'sore ga ne, kyou wa yubiwa mo shiteru no': today he has his ring on as well as the hat, tie and perfume. yubiwa shiteru means the ring is on his finger; nothing is said about buying one (B) or leaving it at home (C). Mai says it to him in line 16 too: dakara yubiwa mo shite kita n desu ne (so that's why you came in wearing your ring).

questions.english: A few days later Tanaka-san is back in his usual open-necked shirt. He has to meet someone important tomorrow, and he asks you, "ashita, daiji na hito ni au n desu kedo, kore de daijoubu deshou ka?" Suggest, politely, that he wear a tie.
questions.ja: 明日、大事な人に会うんですけど、これで大丈夫でしょうか？
questions.kana: あした、だいじなひとにあうんですけど、これでだいじょうぶでしょうか？
questions.romaji: ashita, daiji na hito ni au n desu kedo, kore de daijoubu deshou ka?
questions.answer: Suggest a tie with nekutai o suru, politely since he's your manager: nekutai o shite itta hou ga ii to omoimasu, or more softly, nekutai shite itta hou ga ii kamo shiremasen ne. Skip -tara dou desu ka with a manager, as it can sound pushy. A tie takes suru, never kiru.

modelAnswers.romaji: ichiou, nekutai o shite itta hou ga ii to omoimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 一応、ネクタイをして行ったほうがいいと思います。
modelAnswers.english: I think you'd better wear a tie, just in case.

modelAnswers.romaji: kono aida mitai ni, nekutai shite itta hou ga ii kamo shiremasen ne.
modelAnswers.ja: この間みたいに、ネクタイして行ったほうがいいかもしれませんね。
modelAnswers.english: Maybe wear a tie, like you did the other day.

questions.explanation: A tie, like a ring or a watch, takes suru: nekutai shite iku is 'go wearing a tie', nekutai shite kuru 'come in wearing one'. In the scene: nekutai mo shiteru no (line 5) and kyou wa nekutai shiteru n desu ne (line 14). nekutai o kiru is the English 'wear' carried over; kiru is only for clothes on the body.

questions.english: You've just got to the office. Mai leans over and says, "are, nanka ii nioi suru ne." Tell her you've got perfume on.
questions.ja: あれ、なんかいい匂いするね。
questions.kana: あれ、なんかいいにおいするね。
questions.romaji: are, nanka ii nioi suru ne.
questions.answer: Say you're wearing perfume with kousui o tsukeru: kousui tsuketeru (it's on) or kousui tsukete kita (I put some on before I came). Not kousui o kiru.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, kousui tsuketeru kara kamo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、香水つけてるからかも。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, maybe it's my perfume.

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa chotto kousui tsukete kita n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はちょっと香水つけてきたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: I put on a bit of perfume today.

questions.explanation: Perfume takes tsukeru, the verb for anything put onto the body, and tsuketeru means it's on, not that you're putting it on now. In the scene: kousui mo tsuketeta (line 7) and kousui tsukeru nante (line 8). kiru is only for clothes.

script.title: A job close to home
script.setting: Lunchtime at the office in late March. Mai (Kimura-san at work) is about to heat up her packed lunch in the kitchenette microwave when her manager, Tanaka-san, comes in with news about his son, who has spent the past year job hunting.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, tanaka-san, otsukaresama desu. saki ni obentou o atatamete mo ii desu ka?
