lines.ja: あ、田中さん、お疲れさまです。先にお弁当を温めてもいいですか？
lines.kana: あ、たなかさん、おつかれさまです。さきにおべんとうをあたためてもいいですか？
lines.english: Oh, hi, Tanaka-san. Mind if I heat up my lunch first?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: douzo. a, kimura-san, uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo.
lines.ja: どうぞ。あ、木村さん、うちの息子、やっと仕事が見つかったんですよ。
lines.kana: どうぞ。あ、きむらさん、うちのむすこ、やっとしごとがみつかったんですよ。
lines.english: Go ahead. Oh, Kimura-san, guess what: my son's finally found a job!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: waa, omedetou gozaimasu! kyonen kara zutto shigoto o sagashiteta n desu yo ne.
lines.ja: わあ、おめでとうございます！去年からずっと仕事を探してたんですよね。
lines.kana: わあ、おめでとうございます！きょねんからずっとしごとをさがしてたんですよね。
lines.english: Oh, congratulations! He'd been looking for a job since last year, hadn't he?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee. ichinen mo shigoto sagashite, nakanaka mitsukaranakatta n desu.
lines.ja: ええ。一年も仕事探して、なかなか見つからなかったんです。
lines.kana: ええ。いちねんもしごとさがして、なかなかみつからなかったんです。
lines.english: Yes. A whole year of job hunting, and nothing would turn up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: shigoto ga mitsukatte, honto ni yokatta desu ne. doko no kaisha ni hairu n desu ka?
lines.ja: 仕事が見つかって、ほんとによかったですね。どこの会社に入るんですか？
lines.kana: しごとがみつかって、ほんとによかったですね。どこのかいしゃにはいるんですか？
lines.english: I'm so glad he's found one. Which company is he joining?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sore ga, raigetsu kara, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu.
lines.ja: それが、来月から、うちの会社に入るんです。
lines.kana: それが、らいげつから、うちのかいしゃにはいるんです。
lines.english: Well, that's the thing. Next month he's joining our company.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, kono kaisha ni desu ka? zenzen shirimasen deshita.
lines.ja: え、この会社にですか？全然知りませんでした。
lines.kana: え、このかいしゃにですか？ぜんぜんしりませんでした。
lines.english: What, this company? I had no idea.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: watashi mo kinou made shiranakatta n desu yo. musuko ga jibun de shigoto o sagashite, watashi ni wa nanimo iwanakatta n desu.
lines.ja: 私も昨日まで知らなかったんですよ。息子が自分で仕事を探して、私には何も言わなかったんです。
lines.kana: わたしもきのうまでしらなかったんですよ。むすこがじぶんでしごとをさがして、わたしにはなにもいわなかったんです。
lines.english: Neither did I, until yesterday. He looked for work all on his own and never said a word to me.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sugoi desu ne. musuko-san ga daigaku ni haitta no, kono aida ja nakatta desu ka?
lines.ja: すごいですね。息子さんが大学に入ったの、この間じゃなかったですか？
lines.kana: すごいですね。むすこさんがだいがくにはいったの、このあいだじゃなかったですか？
lines.english: Good for him. Didn't he only just start university the other day?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee, hayai desu ne. demo, daigaku ni haitte kara benkyou bakkari de, shigoto no keiken ga zenzen nai n desu.
lines.ja: ええ、早いですね。でも、大学に入ってから勉強ばっかりで、仕事の経験が全然ないんです。
lines.kana: ええ、はやいですね。でも、だいがくにはいってからべんきょうばっかりで、しごとのけいけんがぜんぜんないんです。
lines.english: Yes, time flies. But since he started university it's been nothing but studying, so he's got no work experience at all.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: daijoubu desu yo. saisho kara keiken ga aru hito wa, hotondo imasen kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫ですよ。最初から経験がある人は、ほとんどいませんから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶですよ。さいしょからけいけんがあるひとは、ほとんどいませんから。
lines.english: He'll be fine. Hardly anyone has experience at the start.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou deshou ka. kimura-san mo, saisho wa keiken ga nakatta n desu ka?
lines.ja: そうでしょうか。木村さんも、最初は経験がなかったんですか？
lines.kana: そうでしょうか。きむらさんも、さいしょはけいけんがなかったんですか？
lines.english: You think so? So you had no experience at first either, Kimura-san?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai. kono kaisha ni haitta toki wa, nanimo dekinakute, mainichi haji o kaite imashita.
lines.ja: はい。この会社に入ったときは、何もできなくて、毎日恥をかいていました。
lines.kana: はい。このかいしゃにはいったときは、なにもできなくて、まいにちはじをかいていました。
lines.english: That's right. When I joined this company I couldn't do a thing, and I was making a fool of myself every day.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou deshita ka? demo ima wa, minna, wakaranai koto wa kimura-san ni kiite imasu yo.
lines.ja: そうでしたか？でも今は、みんな、わからないことは木村さんに聞いていますよ。
lines.kana: そうでしたか？でもいまは、みんな、わからないことはきむらさんにきいていますよ。
lines.english: Were you? Well, these days everyone comes to you when they don't know something.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sonna koto nai desu yo. musuko-san ga komatte itara, watashi mo iroiro oshiemasu ne.
lines.ja: そんなことないですよ。息子さんが困っていたら、私もいろいろ教えますね。
lines.kana: そんなことないですよ。むすこさんがこまっていたら、わたしもいろいろおしえますね。
lines.english: Oh, not really. If your son ever gets stuck, I'll help him out too.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. a, demo, watashi no musuko da tte koto wa, mada minna ni iwanaide kudasai ne.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。あ、でも、私の息子だってことは、まだみんなに言わないでくださいね。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。あ、でも、わたしのむすこだってことは、まだみんなにいわないでくださいね。
lines.english: Thank you. Oh, but please don't tell anyone yet that he's my son.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, nande desu ka?
lines.ja: え、なんでですか？
lines.kana: え、なんでですか？
lines.english: Oh? Why not?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jibun de haitta kaisha da kara iwanaide tte, musuko ni iwareta n desu.
lines.ja: 自分で入った会社だから言わないでって、息子に言われたんです。
lines.kana: じぶんではいったかいしゃだからいわないでって、むすこにいわれたんです。
lines.english: My son told me not to. He got into this company on his own, he says.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Tanaka-san's son is still looking for work after a year, so Tanaka-san asks Mai whether their company might take him on.
Tanaka-san's son has just got into university, and Mai offers to help him get some work experience before he starts.
Tanaka-san's son has finally found a job, at their own company, and Tanaka-san asks Mai to keep quiet for now that he's his son.

questions.explanation: Line 2: uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo. Line 6: the job is at their own company, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu. Lines 16-18: Tanaka-san asks Mai not to tell anyone yet that he's his son, because his son wants it known he got in on his own. A: the son did spend a year looking (line 4), but the search is over. B: university only comes up as Mai remembering when he started (line 9); he's finishing now, and the experience talk is Tanaka-san worrying that he has none (line 10).

questions.english: At Yuki's birthday party, her manager Tanaka-san makes small talk: "What kind of work are you doing at the moment?" Tell him that, actually, you're looking for a job right now.
questions.ja: 今、どんなお仕事をしているんですか？
questions.kana: いま、どんなおしごとをしているんですか？
questions.romaji: ima, donna oshigoto o shite iru n desu ka?
questions.answer: Say you're job hunting with shigoto o sagasu in the -te iru form, politely: jitsu wa, ima shigoto o sagashite iru n desu.

modelAnswers.romaji: jitsu wa, ima shigoto o sagashite iru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: 実は、今仕事を探しているんです。
modelAnswers.english: Actually, I'm looking for a job right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima wa, atarashii shigoto o sagashite imasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 今は、新しい仕事を探しています。
modelAnswers.english: At the moment I'm looking for a new job.

questions.explanation: Looking for work is shigoto o sagasu, and an ongoing search takes -te iru: sagashite iru, or sagashiteru in casual speech. Mai uses it about Tanaka-san's son, kyonen kara zutto shigoto o sagashiteta n desu yo ne (line 3), Tanaka-san adds ichinen mo shigoto sagashite (line 4), and his son found the job jibun de shigoto o sagashite, looking on his own (line 8). Sagasu is only the looking: once the search is over, the job takes ga, shigoto ga mitsukaru.

questions.english: Mai asks you: "Oh yeah, how's the job thing going? Are you still looking?" Tell her no, you've finally found a job.
questions.ja: そういえば、仕事どう？まだ探してるの？
questions.kana: そういえば、しごとどう？まださがしてるの？
questions.romaji: sou ieba, shigoto dou? mada sagashiteru no?
questions.answer: Say the search is over with shigoto ga mitsukaru in the past: uun, yatto shigoto mitsukatta n da!

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, yatto shigoto mitsukatta n da!
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、やっと仕事見つかったんだ！
modelAnswers.english: No, I finally found a job!

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, sengetsu atarashii shigoto ga mitsukatta n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、先月新しい仕事が見つかったんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I found a new job last month.

questions.explanation: Finding work is shigoto ga mitsukaru: the job is what turns up, so it takes ga, not the o of sagasu. Tanaka-san's news is uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo (line 2), and Mai answers shigoto ga mitsukatte, honto ni yokatta desu ne (line 5). Mai's question uses sagasu for the looking; your answer switches both the verb and the particle. Casual speech can drop ga, as in the first model answer.

questions.english: Mai remembers when Tanaka-san's son started university. What did she say?
questions.ja: マイさんは、息子さんについて何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、むすこさんについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, musuko-san ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: that he started university (got in)
that he began university (English 'start' word for word)
that he entered university (with o, like English 'enter')

questions.explanation: Mai says musuko-san ga daigaku ni haitta no, kono aida ja nakatta desu ka? (line 9), and Tanaka-san picks it up: daigaku ni haitte kara benkyou bakkari (line 10). You go into a school, so starting university is daigaku ni hairu, with ni for the place you go into, the same ni hairu as kaisha ni hairu. B puts English 'start university' into Japanese word for word, and nobody says it. C copies English 'enter university' with o, but hairu takes ni for what you join: daigaku o haitta is a common learner slip.

questions.english: Tanaka-san's news is that his son will uchi no kaisha ni hairu from next month. What does that mean?
questions.ja: 田中さんの息子さんは、来月から何をしますか？
questions.kana: たなかさんのむすこさんは、らいげつからなにをしますか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san no musuko-san wa, raigetsu kara nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: He'll come into the office with his dad now and then to see what the work is like.
He'll join their company and start working there as a new employee.
He'll take part in a short work-experience event that their company runs.

questions.explanation: Line 6: sore ga, raigetsu kara, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu. Kaisha ni hairu is joining a company as a member of staff: Mai uses it for her own start, kono kaisha ni haitta toki (line 13), and the son wants it known he got in on his own, jibun de haitta kaisha (line 18). Going in to the office is kaisha ni iku or kuru (A), and taking part in an event is sanka suru (C), the word English 'join' tempts you into.

questions.english: Tanaka-san, your manager, asks: "Could I ask you to take on this job? It's a little tricky." Tell him it's fine, because you have experience with this kind of work.
questions.ja: この仕事、お願いしてもいいですか？ちょっと難しいんですけど。
questions.kana: このしごと、おねがいしてもいいですか？ちょっとむずかしいんですけど。
questions.romaji: kono shigoto, onegai shite mo ii desu ka? chotto muzukashii n desu kedo.
questions.answer: Say you have the background with keiken ga aru, politely keiken ga arimasu, not keiken o motte imasu: kou iu shigoto no keiken wa arimasu kara, daijoubu desu.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, kou iu shigoto no keiken wa arimasu kara, daijoubu desu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、こういう仕事の経験はありますから、大丈夫です。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. I've done this kind of work before, so it's fine.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu desu. mae ni mo onaji shigoto o shita keiken ga arimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫です。前にも同じ仕事をした経験があります。
modelAnswers.english: No problem. I've done the same work before.

questions.explanation: Experience is something that exists, so it takes ga aru: keiken ga aru, or keiken ga arimasu to your manager. Tanaka-san worries his son has none, shigoto no keiken ga zenzen nai n desu (line 10); Mai answers saisho kara keiken ga aru hito wa, hotondo imasen (line 11); and Tanaka-san asks her, saisho wa keiken ga nakatta n desu ka? (line 12). Keiken o motte imasu is English 'have experience' word for word and sounds like a line read off a CV. Wa in place of ga (keiken wa arimasu) is fine when you mean this kind of work, at least.

script.title: Pale, then red
script.setting: A Sunday evening. Okaasan leaves a voicemail for Yuki, who lives on her own, about Yuki's little brother Kenji and his football match that day.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? okaasan da kedo.
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？お母さんだけど。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？おかあさんだけど。
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? It's Mum.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji ga ne, kyou sakkaa no shiai de kega shita no. a, daijoubu da kara, shinpai shinaide ne.
lines.ja: ケンジがね、今日サッカーの試合で怪我したの。あ、大丈夫だから、心配しないでね。
lines.kana: けんじがね、きょうさっかーのしあいでけがしたの。あ、だいじょうぶだから、しんぱいしないでね。
lines.english: Kenji got hurt in his football match today. Oh, he's fine, so don't worry.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kaette kita toki, hiza kara chi ga detete, ase mo sugoku kaitete ne.
lines.ja: 帰ってきたとき、膝から血が出てて、汗もすごくかいててね。
lines.kana: かえってきたとき、ひざからちがでてて、あせもすごくかいててね。
lines.english: When he got home, his knee was bleeding, and he was really sweaty too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kaoiro mo warukatta shi, okaasan, honto ni bikkuri shita wa.
lines.ja: 顔色も悪かったし、お母さん、ほんとにびっくりしたわ。
lines.kana: かおいろもわるかったし、おかあさん、ほんとにびっくりしたわ。
lines.english: And he looked pale, so I got quite a fright.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hidoi kega shita n ja nai no? tte kiitara, chotto chi ga deta dake da yo tte.
lines.ja: 「ひどい怪我したんじゃないの？」って聞いたら、「ちょっと血が出ただけだよ」って。
lines.kana: 「ひどいけがしたんじゃないの？」ってきいたら、「ちょっとちがでただけだよ」って。
lines.english: I asked him, "You haven't hurt yourself badly, have you?" and he said, "It just bled a bit, that's all."

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou ieba, kenji tte mukashi kara, chi ga deru to sugu kaoiro ga waruku naru no yo ne.
lines.ja: そういえば、ケンジって昔から、血が出るとすぐ顔色が悪くなるのよね。
lines.kana: そういえば、けんじってむかしから、ちがでるとすぐかおいろがわるくなるのよね。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Kenji's always been like that. The moment he bleeds, he goes pale.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, yoru ni natte, shiai o mi ni kiteta onna no ko ga, kenji no wasuremono o motte kite kureta no.
lines.ja: で、夜になって、試合を見に来てた女の子が、ケンジの忘れ物を持ってきてくれたの。
lines.kana: で、よるになって、しあいをみにきてたおんなのこが、けんじのわすれものをもってきてくれたの。
lines.english: Then in the evening, a girl who'd come to watch the match brought round something Kenji had left behind.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: soshitara kenji, kyuu ni kao ga akaku natchatte.
lines.ja: そしたらケンジ、急に顔が赤くなっちゃって。
lines.kana: そしたらけんじ、きゅうにかおがあかくなっちゃって。
lines.english: And Kenji's face suddenly went red.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hiru wa kaoiro ga warukatta noni, kondo wa kao ga akai no yo.
lines.ja: 昼は顔色が悪かったのに、今度は顔が赤いのよ。
lines.kana: ひるはかおいろがわるかったのに、こんどはかおがあかいのよ。
lines.english: At midday he'd been pale, and now his face was red!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ato de, kao akai yo, netsu aru no? tte kiitara, atsui dake da yo tte. mata ase kaiteta wa.
lines.ja: あとで、「顔赤いよ、熱あるの？」って聞いたら、「暑いだけだよ」って。また汗かいてたわ。
lines.kana: あとで、「かおあかいよ、ねつあるの？」ってきいたら、「あついだけだよ」って。またあせかいてたわ。
lines.english: Later I said, "Your face is red. Have you got a fever?" and he said, "I'm just hot." He was all sweaty again.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kega shita no mo, ano ko no mae de kakko tsuketa kara kamo ne.
lines.ja: 怪我したのも、あの子の前でかっこつけたからかもね。
lines.kana: けがしたのも、あのこのまえでかっこつけたからかもね。
lines.english: Maybe he even got hurt showing off in front of her.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji ni wa, okaasan kara kiita tte iwanaide ne. jaa ne.
lines.ja: ケンジには、お母さんから聞いたって言わないでね。じゃあね。
lines.kana: けんじには、おかあさんからきいたっていわないでね。じゃあね。
lines.english: Don't tell Kenji you heard it from me, OK? Bye.

questions.english: What's Okaasan's message about?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji hurt his knee at football and came down with a fever that evening, so he's resting.
Kenji fainted at the sight of blood during his match, and a girl had to bring him home.
Kenji got a small cut at football, and Okaasan thinks his red face that evening was about a girl, not a fever.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Kenji got hurt at his football match (kega shita), but Okaasan says he's fine. Line 5: he says it only bled a little. Lines 7-9: when a girl who'd watched the match brought round something he'd left behind, his face suddenly went red. Line 10: he says he's just hot, and in line 11 Okaasan guesses he got hurt showing off in front of her. A is wrong: Okaasan asks about a fever (line 10, netsu aru no?), but Kenji says he's just hot, and nobody says he's resting. B is wrong: Kenji went pale at the blood (lines 4 and 6), but he came home himself (line 3, kaette kita), and the girl only brought round something he'd left behind (line 7).

questions.english: You're home for the weekend with a plaster on your knee. Okaasan spots it and asks, "are, sono hiza dou shita no?" Tell her you hurt it, using kega.
questions.ja: あれ、その膝どうしたの？
questions.kana: あれ、そのひざどうしたの？
questions.romaji: are, sono hiza dou shita no?
questions.answer: Say you hurt it with kega o suru, usually as kega shita, or kega shichatta (I went and got hurt). It's natural to say how it happened: jitensha de kega shita.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, kore? kinou jitensha de kega shichatta.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、これ？昨日自転車で怪我しちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, this? I hurt it on my bike yesterday.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto kega shita dake. mou daijoubu da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと怪我しただけ。もう大丈夫だよ。
modelAnswers.english: I just hurt it a bit. It's fine now.

questions.explanation: Okaasan says Kenji kega shita at his match (line 2), asks him hidoi kega shita n ja nai no? (line 5), and guesses why he got hurt: kega shita no mo... (line 11). In Japanese an injury is something you 'do': kega o suru, even by accident, mostly heard as kega shita or kega shichatta. Itaku natta only says it started to hurt, and kizutsuita is mostly for hurt feelings. To name the place, say hiza o kega shita or hiza ni kega o shita, never two o's (not hiza o kega o shita). With your mum, casual is right.

questions.english: Okaasan asked Kenji if he'd hurt himself badly. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンジは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It just bled a bit, that's all.
choices.romaji: chotto chi ga deta dake da yo

choices.english: There was just a bit of haemorrhaging, that's all.
choices.romaji: chotto shukketsu shita dake da yo

choices.english: I just let a bit of blood out, that's all.
choices.romaji: chotto chi o dashita dake da yo

questions.explanation: Line 5: 'chotto chi ga deta dake da yo'. Japanese has no single verb for 'bleed': blood comes out, chi ga deru, the way a fever or a cough does (netsu ga deru, seki ga deru). Okaasan uses the same pair in line 3 (hiza kara chi ga detete) and line 6 (chi ga deru to). B is wrong: shukketsu suru is the medical word for bleeding. A doctor or the news would say it, but not a teenager telling his mum it's nothing. C is wrong: dasu means putting something out yourself, so chi o dashita sounds as if he made it bleed on purpose. Blood from a cut just comes out (deru).

questions.english: You've just walked in after an errand on a hot afternoon. Okaasan asks, "soto, atsukatta?" Answer using ase o kaku, and say you want a shower.
questions.ja: 外、暑かった？
questions.kana: そと、あつかった？
questions.romaji: soto, atsukatta?
questions.answer: Say you got all sweaty with ase o kaku, usually in the past: ase kaita or ase kaichatta. Then add that you want a shower (shawaa abitai).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, metcha ase kaichatta. shawaa abitai.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、めっちゃ汗かいちゃった。シャワー浴びたい。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I got so sweaty. I want a shower.

modelAnswers.romaji: atsukatta! ase kaita kara, saki ni shawaa abiru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 暑かった！汗かいたから、先にシャワー浴びるね。
modelAnswers.english: It was hot! I'm all sweaty, so I'll have a shower first.

questions.explanation: Okaasan uses it twice. Kenji came home from the match all sweaty (line 3, ase mo sugoku kaitete), and he was sweating again when she asked about his red face (line 10, mata ase kaiteta). 'Sweat' is a verb in English, but Japanese uses the noun ase with kaku, so don't say ase suru. This kaku isn't kaku 'write'. It's the same kaku as in haji o kaku (embarrass yourself). Ase ga deru (sweat comes out) also works, but ase kaita is what people usually say. With your mum, casual is right.

questions.english: Okaasan sits down at the kitchen table and says, "nanka kesa kara, chotto kibun ga warui no yo ne." She has gone pale. Tell her she looks pale, and ask if she's OK.
questions.ja: なんか今朝から、ちょっと気分が悪いのよね。
questions.kana: なんかけさから、ちょっときぶんがわるいのよね。
questions.romaji: nanka kesa kara, chotto kibun ga warui no yo ne.
questions.answer: Tell her she looks pale with kaoiro ga warui (casually kaoiro warui yo), then ask daijoubu?

modelAnswers.romaji: honto da, kaoiro warui yo. daijoubu?
modelAnswers.ja: ほんとだ、顔色悪いよ。大丈夫？
modelAnswers.english: You're right, you look pale. Are you OK?

modelAnswers.romaji: kaoiro ga warui ne. chotto yoko ni nattara?
modelAnswers.ja: 顔色が悪いね。ちょっと横になったら？
modelAnswers.english: You do look pale. Why don't you lie down for a bit?

questions.explanation: Okaasan says it about Kenji three times: kaoiro mo warukatta (line 4), sugu kaoiro ga waruku naru (line 6) and hiru wa kaoiro ga warukatta (line 9). Kaoiro is the colour of your face, and warui says it's a bad colour: pale, unwell. Kao ga shiroi would sound as if she has fair skin, and kao ga aoi is stronger (looking really ill or scared). Her kibun ga warui is how she feels inside. Kaoiro ga warui is what you can see. In casual talk ga often drops (kaoiro warui yo), and daijoubu? usually follows.

questions.english: Okaasan compares how Kenji looked at midday with how he looked in the evening, when the girl came round. What changed?
questions.ja: ケンジの顔は、どう変わりましたか？
questions.kana: けんじのかおは、どうかわりましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji no kao wa, dou kawarimashita ka?

choices.english: At midday he was red from the heat, and in the evening he went pale.
At midday he looked pale, and in the evening his face went red.
He looked pale all day, and in the evening he came down with a fever.

questions.explanation: Line 9: 'hiru wa kaoiro ga warukatta noni, kondo wa kao ga akai no yo'. Kaoiro ga warui means pale (from the blood, lines 4 and 6). Kao ga akai is a red face, which came on suddenly when the girl turned up (line 8, kyuu ni kao ga akaku natchatte). A swaps the two. C is wrong: Okaasan does ask kao akai yo, netsu aru no? (line 10), but Kenji says he's just hot, and she thinks it was about the girl (line 11).

script.title: Blossoms Twice
script.setting: A Sunday in early March at the family home. Yuki, who lives on her own, has dropped by and asks her little brother Kenji, who finishes high school this month, about the university in Hokkaido he starts at in April.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji, hokkaidou no daigaku ni hairu n da tte? nande hokkaidou ni shita no?
lines.ja: ケンジ、北海道の大学に入るんだって？なんで北海道にしたの？
lines.kana: けんじ、ほっかいどうのだいがくにはいるんだって？なんでほっかいどうにしたの？
lines.english: Kenji, I hear you're going to university in Hokkaido? Why Hokkaido?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: atsusa ni yowai kara. kotchi no natsu, mou muri.
lines.ja: 暑さに弱いから。こっちの夏、もう無理。
lines.kana: あつさによわいから。こっちのなつ、もうむり。
lines.english: 'Cause I can't take the heat. I'm done with summers here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, sore dake? maa, kenji wa mukashi kara atsusa ni yowai kedo.
lines.ja: え、それだけ？まあ、ケンジは昔から暑さに弱いけど。
lines.kana: え、それだけ？まあ、けんじはむかしからあつさによわいけど。
lines.english: What, that's it? I mean, you've always been hopeless in the heat, but still.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: asa kara semi ga naite, nerarenai shi. nanimo shinakute mo ase kaku shi.
lines.ja: 朝からセミが鳴いて、寝られないし。何もしなくても汗かくし。
lines.kana: あさからせみがないて、ねられないし。なにもしなくてもあせかくし。
lines.english: The cicadas start up first thing, so I can't sleep. And I sweat even doing nothing.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ee, semi ga naku to, natsu tte kanji de ii jan.
lines.ja: えー、セミが鳴くと、夏って感じでいいじゃん。
lines.kana: えー、せみがなくと、なつってかんじでいいじゃん。
lines.english: Aw, but when the cicadas start, it really feels like summer. I like that.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: atchi wa, semi anmari nakanai rashii yo. natsu mo sonna ni atsukunai tte.
lines.ja: あっちは、セミあんまり鳴かないらしいよ。夏もそんなに暑くないって。
lines.kana: あっちは、せみあんまりなかないらしいよ。なつもそんなにあつくないって。
lines.english: Apparently the cicadas don't go much up there. And summer's not that hot either.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: demo, fuyu wa? atchi, yuki sugoku tsumoru yo.
lines.ja: でも、冬は？あっち、雪すごく積もるよ。
lines.kana: でも、ふゆは？あっち、ゆきすごくつもるよ。
lines.english: But what about winter? The snow really piles up there.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shitteru. yuki ga tsumoru no, chotto tanoshimi.
lines.ja: 知ってる。雪が積もるの、ちょっと楽しみ。
lines.kana: しってる。ゆきがつもるの、ちょっとたのしみ。
lines.english: I know. I'm kind of looking forward to the snow piling up.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yuki wa futteru dake nara kirei da kedo, tsumoru to taihen da yo.
lines.ja: 雪は降ってるだけならきれいだけど、積もると大変だよ。
lines.kana: ゆきはふってるだけならきれいだけど、つもるとたいへんだよ。
lines.english: Snow's pretty while it's coming down, but once it settles, it's a real pain.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: daijoubu. atsusa ni wa yowai kedo, samusa ni wa yowakunai kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。暑さには弱いけど、寒さには弱くないから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。あつさにはよわいけど、さむさにはよわくないから。
lines.english: I'll be fine. I can't take the heat, but I'm OK with the cold.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uso. fuyu wa itsumo, samui samui tte, asa okirenai jan.
lines.ja: うそ。冬はいつも、寒い寒いって、朝起きれないじゃん。
lines.kana: うそ。ふゆはいつも、さむいさむいって、あさおきれないじゃん。
lines.english: Liar. Every winter you go 'it's freezing, it's freezing' and can't get out of bed.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sore to kore to wa betsu.
lines.ja: それとこれとは別。
lines.kana: それとこれとはべつ。
lines.english: That's different.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai hai. a, sou ieba, atchi tte sakura ga saku no, osoi n da yo ne?
lines.ja: はいはい。あ、そういえば、あっちって桜が咲くの、遅いんだよね？
lines.kana: はいはい。あ、そういえば、あっちってさくらがさくの、おそいんだよね？
lines.english: Sure, sure. Oh, come to think of it, the cherry blossoms come out late up there, don't they?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. netto de shirabetara, kotchi yori ikkagetsu gurai osoku saku tte.
lines.ja: うん。ネットで調べたら、こっちより一ヶ月ぐらい遅く咲くって。
lines.kana: うん。ねっとでしらべたら、こっちよりいっかげつぐらいおそくさくって。
lines.english: Yeah. I looked it up online: they come out about a month later than here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, atchi de sakura ga saitara, asobi ni iku! kotoshi wa nikai mireru ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、あっちで桜が咲いたら、遊びに行く！今年は二回見れるね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、あっちでさくらがさいたら、あそびにいく！ことしはにかいみれるね。
lines.english: Then when they come out up there, I'm coming to visit! I'll get to see them twice this year.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, kuru no? jaa, yuki ga tsumottara, tetsudai ni kite yo.
lines.ja: え、来るの？じゃあ、雪が積もったら、手伝いに来てよ。
lines.kana: え、くるの？じゃあ、ゆきがつもったら、てつだいにきてよ。
lines.english: Wait, you're coming? Then come and help me out when the snow piles up.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore wa muri. watashi, samusa ni yowai kara.
lines.ja: それは無理。私、寒さに弱いから。
lines.kana: それはむり。わたし、さむさによわいから。
lines.english: No way. I can't take the cold.

questions.english: What does Yuki decide to do?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何を決めましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなにをきめましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nani o kimemashita ka?

choices.english: Go up in winter to help Kenji when the snow piles up.
Visit Kenji when the cherry blossoms come out up there, about a month after they come out at home.
Try to talk Kenji into a university nearer home, since he's no good in the cold either.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenji is going to university in Hokkaido, partly because he can't take the heat. Lines 13-15: the cherry blossoms come out about a month later up there, so Yuki says she'll visit when they do (atchi de sakura ga saitara, asobi ni iku) and get to see them twice this year. A is wrong: Kenji asks her to come and help when the snow piles up (line 16), but she says no, because she can't take the cold herself (line 17). C is wrong: Yuki teases him about the cold (line 11), but she never tries to change his mind.

questions.english: It's early April. Kenji has moved to Hokkaido, where the cherry blossoms won't be out for weeks. He calls and asks, "sotchi, sakura dou?" (how are the blossoms there?). The ones near you are out. Tell him, using saku.
questions.ja: そっち、桜どう？
questions.kana: そっち、さくらどう？
questions.romaji: sotchi, sakura dou?
questions.answer: Say they're out with saiteru: mou saiteru yo (they're already out). Saita says they've come out, saiteru says they're out now, and mada saitenai is not out yet. Don't reach for deru: hana ga deru isn't said.

modelAnswers.romaji: mou saiteru yo. ima ga ichiban kirei.
modelAnswers.ja: もう咲いてるよ。今が一番きれい。
modelAnswers.english: They're already out. They're at their best right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: kinou saita yo. sotchi wa mada saitenai desho?
modelAnswers.ja: 昨日咲いたよ。そっちはまだ咲いてないでしょ？
modelAnswers.english: They came out yesterday. Yours aren't out yet, are they?

questions.explanation: Yuki and Kenji use saku for the blossoms in lines 13 to 15: atchi tte sakura ga saku no, osoi n da yo ne? (they come out late up there, don't they?), osoku saku tte (they come out later), and atchi de sakura ga saitara (when they come out up there). Flowers coming out is saku, and flowers that are out now are saiteru. English 'the blossoms are out' tempts deru, but hana ga deru isn't said, and hiraku (open) is for describing petals, not for chat. When the petals come down, it's chiru: mou chitchatta. In casual talk ga usually drops: sakura saita?

questions.english: It's a scorching day in August. Yuki suggests eating lunch outside: "ohiru, soto de tabenai?" Say no: you just can't take the heat. Use atsusa ni yowai.
questions.ja: お昼、外で食べない？
questions.kana: おひる、そとでたべない？
questions.romaji: ohiru, soto de tabenai?
questions.answer: Explain with atsusa ni yowai, often as atsusa ni yowai n da (the thing is, I'm no good in the heat). Keep the ni: atsusa ga yowai would mean the heat itself is weak.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, atsusa ni yowai n da. naka de tabenai?
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、暑さに弱いんだ。中で食べない？
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I can't take the heat. Can we eat inside?

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa chotto. atsusa ni yowai kara, naka ni shiyou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はちょっと。暑さに弱いから、中にしようよ。
modelAnswers.english: Not today. I'm no good in the heat, so let's eat inside.

questions.explanation: Kenji's reason for Hokkaido is atsusa ni yowai kara (line 2), Yuki agrees he always has been (line 3), and he sets it against the cold in line 10: atsusa ni wa yowai kedo, samusa ni wa yowakunai. Yuki turns it round on him at the end: samusa ni yowai kara (line 17). Yowai with ni means you can't handle something, like osake ni yowai (can't hold your drink), and with atsusa the ni stays, never ga. Atsusa and samusa are atsui and samui made into nouns with -sa. Atsui no nigate (I can't do heat) is just as everyday; the opposite is atsusa ni tsuyoi.

questions.english: Kenji complains about summers at home. What did he say about the cicadas?
questions.ja: ケンジはセミについて何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはせみについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa semi ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: the cicadas sing from first thing, so I can't sleep
choices.romaji: asa kara semi ga utatte, nerarenai shi

choices.english: the cicadas ring from first thing, so I can't sleep
choices.romaji: asa kara semi ga natte, nerarenai shi

choices.english: the cicadas call from first thing, so I can't sleep
choices.romaji: asa kara semi ga naite, nerarenai shi

questions.explanation: Line 4: asa kara semi ga naite, nerarenai shi. Insects, birds and animals all naku (鳴く), which sounds the same as naku 'cry' (泣く): semi ga naku, tori ga naku, neko ga naku. A carries the English verb over: utau is singing a song, and tori ga utau is poetry, not chat. B uses naru, which is for things that make a sound, like denwa ga naru or kaminari ga naru: animals naku, things naru. Yuki says it too (line 5: semi ga naku to, natsu tte kanji), and Kenji again in line 6 (semi anmari nakanai).

questions.english: Yuki warns Kenji about winter in Hokkaido. What does she say about the snow?
questions.ja: 北海道の冬について、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ほっかいどうのふゆについて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: hokkaidou no fuyu ni tsuite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: A lot of it builds up, and once it's lying on the ground it's hard work.
It hardly ever falls there, but when it does, it's freezing.
It falls almost every day, but it's always gone by the next morning.

questions.explanation: Line 7: atchi, yuki sugoku tsumoru yo (the snow really piles up there). Line 9: futteru dake nara kirei da kedo, tsumoru to taihen da yo (pretty while it's coming down, hard work once it settles). Furu is snow coming down; tsumoru is snow building up and staying, so yuki tsumotteru means there's snow on the ground. B is wrong: she says a lot of it piles up. C is wrong: snow that tsumoru stays put; snow melting is tokeru. Snow stuck on things, like a car, is tsuku: kuruma ni yuki ga tsuiteru.

script.title: A dog bed for the cat
script.setting: Saturday morning at the door of Yuki's small rented flat. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, turns up with a big parcel of hers that the driver took to his flat by mistake last night.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yuki-san, ohayou gozaimasu. kinou no yoru, yuki-san no nimotsu ga uchi ni todoita n desu yo. heya o machigaeta mitai de.
lines.ja: ユキさん、おはようございます。昨日の夜、ユキさんの荷物がうちに届いたんですよ。部屋を間違えたみたいで。
lines.kana: ゆきさん、おはようございます。きのうのよる、ゆきさんのにもつがうちにとどいたんですよ。へやをまちがえたみたいで。
lines.english: Good morning, Yuki-san. Your parcel came to my place last night. They must have got the wrong flat.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, yokatta! kinou zutto matteta noni, nimotsu ga todokanakute. arigatou gozaimasu.
lines.ja: あ、よかった！昨日ずっと待ってたのに、荷物が届かなくて。ありがとうございます。
lines.kana: あ、よかった！きのうずっとまってたのに、にもつがとどかなくて。ありがとうございます。
lines.english: Oh, thank goodness! I waited in all day yesterday, and it never came. Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kekkou ookii desu ne. nanika katta n desu ka?
lines.ja: けっこう大きいですね。何か買ったんですか？
lines.kana: けっこうおおきいですね。なにかかったんですか？
lines.english: It's quite big, isn't it? Did you buy something?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jitsu wa, inu no beddo na n desu. raishuu kara, inu o kau n desu.
lines.ja: 実は、犬のベッドなんです。来週から、犬を飼うんです。
lines.kana: じつは、いぬのべっどなんです。らいしゅうから、いぬをかうんです。
lines.english: It's a dog bed, actually. I'm getting a dog next week.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hee, inu desu ka. demo, koko de inu o katte mo ii n desu ka?
lines.ja: へえ、犬ですか。でも、ここで犬を飼ってもいいんですか？
lines.kana: へえ、いぬですか。でも、ここでいぬをかってもいいんですか？
lines.english: Oh, a dog! But are you allowed to keep a dog here?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai. kono heya o kariru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita.
lines.ja: はい。この部屋を借りるときに、小さい犬ならいいって言われました。
lines.kana: はい。このへやをかりるときに、ちいさいいぬならいいっていわれました。
lines.english: Yes. When I rented this place, they told me a small dog would be fine.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore wa yokatta desu ne. watashi mo mukashi, semai heya o karite, inu o katte imashita yo.
lines.ja: それはよかったですね。私も昔、狭い部屋を借りて、犬を飼っていましたよ。
lines.kana: それはよかったですね。わたしもむかし、せまいへやをかりて、いぬをかっていましたよ。
lines.english: That's good. Years ago I rented a poky little room too, and kept a dog in it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uchi mo semai heya na node, chiisai inu ni shita n desu. beddo mo, netto de chanto shirabete kara kaimashita.
lines.ja: うちも狭い部屋なので、小さい犬にしたんです。ベッドも、ネットでちゃんと調べてから買いました。
lines.kana: うちもせまいへやなので、ちいさいいぬにしたんです。べっども、ねっとでちゃんとしらべてからかいました。
lines.english: My place is tiny too, so I went for a small dog. And I looked the bed up properly online before I bought it.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sasuga desu ne. donna beddo ka, mite mitai desu ne.
lines.ja: さすがですね。どんなベッドか、見てみたいですね。
lines.kana: さすがですね。どんなべっどか、みてみたいですね。
lines.english: How thorough of you. I'd love to see what it's like.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, ima dashite mimasu ne. semai heya desu kedo, douzo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、今出してみますね。狭い部屋ですけど、どうぞ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、いまだしてみますね。せまいへやですけど、どうぞ。
lines.english: Then I'll take it out now. It's a tiny place, but come on in.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: are? yuki-san, sono beddo, sugoku ookii desu ne.
lines.ja: あれ？ユキさん、そのベッド、すごく大きいですね。
lines.kana: あれ？ゆきさん、そのべっど、すごくおおきいですね。
lines.english: Oh? Yuki-san, that bed's awfully big.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e? uso! kore, ookii inu no beddo desu. machigaete tanonjatta mitai desu.
lines.ja: え？うそ！これ、大きい犬のベッドです。間違えて頼んじゃったみたいです。
lines.kana: え？うそ！これ、おおきいいぬのべっどです。まちがえてたのんじゃったみたいです。
lines.english: What? No way! This is a bed for a big dog. I must have ordered the wrong one.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, ookii inu o kattara dou desu ka?
lines.ja: じゃあ、大きい犬を飼ったらどうですか？
lines.kana: じゃあ、おおきいいぬをかったらどうですか？
lines.english: Well then, why not get a big dog?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kono semai heya de desu ka? muri desu yo. ookii inu nara, motto hiroi heya o karinai to.
lines.ja: この狭い部屋でですか？無理ですよ。大きい犬なら、もっと広い部屋を借りないと。
lines.kana: このせまいへやでですか？むりですよ。おおきいいぬなら、もっとひろいへやをかりないと。
lines.english: In this cramped little place? No way. A big dog would mean renting somewhere roomier.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore nara, sono beddo, uchi no neko ni moratte mo ii desu ka? tama wa, ookii beddo ga daisuki na n desu.
lines.ja: それなら、そのベッド、うちの猫にもらってもいいですか？タマは、大きいベッドが大好きなんです。
lines.kana: それなら、そのべっど、うちのねこにもらってもいいですか？たまは、おおきいべっどがだいすきなんです。
lines.english: In that case, could I have that bed for my cat? Tama loves a big bed.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tama-chan ni desu ka? mochiron desu. jaa, chiisai beddo wa, inu ga kite kara, yousu o mite kaimasu ne.
lines.ja: タマちゃんにですか？もちろんです。じゃあ、小さいベッドは、犬が来てから、様子を見て買いますね。
lines.kana: たまちゃんにですか？もちろんです。じゃあ、ちいさいべっどは、いぬがきてから、ようすをみてかいますね。
lines.english: For Tama? Of course. Then I'll buy a small bed once the dog's here and I've seen how it settles in.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore ga ii desu ne. tsugi no nimotsu ga mata uchi ni todoitara, motte kimasu yo.
lines.ja: それがいいですね。次の荷物がまたうちに届いたら、持ってきますよ。
lines.kana: それがいいですね。つぎのにもつがまたうちにとどいたら、もってきますよ。
lines.english: Good idea. And if your next parcel turns up at my place again, I'll bring it round.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: The dog bed Yuki ordered for the small dog she's getting turns out to be for a big dog, so it goes to Satou-san's cat, and she'll buy a small one once the dog has come.
Yuki finds out dogs aren't allowed in her rented flat, so Satou-san offers to keep the dog at his place.
Satou-san ordered a big dog bed by mistake, so he gives it to Yuki for the small dog she's getting next week.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: Satou-san brings round Yuki's parcel, which went to his flat by mistake. It's a dog bed, because she's getting a dog next week (raishuu kara, inu o kau n desu). Lines 11-12: when she takes it out, it's a bed for a big dog, and she realises she ordered the wrong one (machigaete tanonjatta). Line 14: a big dog won't work in her cramped flat. Lines 15-16: Satou-san asks for the bed for his cat, Tama, and Yuki will buy a small one after the dog comes and she's seen how it settles in (yousu o mite). B is wrong: when Yuki rented the flat she was told a small dog would be fine (line 6), and Satou-san never offers to keep the dog. C swaps them round: it's Yuki's parcel (yuki-san no nimotsu, line 1), and the bed goes from Yuki to Satou-san's cat, not the other way.

questions.english: Satou-san asks if Yuki's allowed to keep a dog where she lives. What does she say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: When I let this flat out, they told me a small dog would be fine.
choices.romaji: kono heya o kasu toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita.

choices.english: When I hired this flat, they told me a small dog would be fine.
choices.romaji: kono heya o rentaru suru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita.

choices.english: When I rented this flat, they told me a small dog would be fine.
choices.romaji: kono heya o kariru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita.

questions.explanation: Line 6: kono heya o kariru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita. Japanese has no separate verb for renting a place: the tenant kariru (borrows), the same verb as borrowing a pen. Satou-san uses it for the poky room he had years ago (semai heya o karite, line 7), and Yuki says a big dog would mean renting somewhere roomier (motto hiroi heya o karinai to, line 14). A is wrong: kasu (lend) is the landlord's side, so heya o kasu toki would mean when she let the flat out to someone else. B is wrong: rentaru suru is for hiring things like a car or a kimono for a day, not a flat you live in.

questions.english: You've just moved into a new flat, and Kenta has come round for the first time. At the door he says, "hee, koko ga atarashii heya? haitte ii?" (Oh, so this is the new place? Can I come in?) Invite him in the modest way a host does, saying it's a small place.
questions.ja: へえ、ここが新しい部屋？入っていい？
questions.kana: へえ、ここがあたらしいへや？はいっていい？
questions.romaji: hee, koko ga atarashii heya? haitte ii?
questions.answer: Use the host's set line with semai heya: semai heya da kedo, douzo (it's a tiny place, but come in).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, semai heya da kedo, douzo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、狭い部屋だけど、どうぞ。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. It's a tiny place, but come on in.

modelAnswers.romaji: semai heya desu kedo, douzo haitte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: 狭い部屋ですけど、どうぞ入ってください。
modelAnswers.english: It's only a small place, but please, come in.

questions.explanation: Yuki says just this to Satou-san in line 10: semai heya desu kedo, douzo. It's the host's modest welcome, and a guest will often answer hiroi ne! (it's roomy!). A cramped room or flat is semai, the opposite of hiroi, as in line 14 (kono semai heya de desu ka? ... motto hiroi heya). Chiisai heya is fine for a room's size (chiisai heya ga futatsu aru), but for the cramped feeling, and in this welcome, people say semai. Kenta's a friend, so da kedo. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san. Semai tokoro da kedo, douzo is a common variant.

questions.english: Kenta shows you photos of a friend's new puppy and says, "kawaii desho? inu, suki?" (Cute, right? Do you like dogs?) You love dogs, and your family has one at home. Tell him.
questions.ja: かわいいでしょ？犬、好き？
questions.kana: かわいいでしょ？いぬ、すき？
questions.romaji: kawaii desho? inu, suki?
questions.answer: Say you love them, then say your family keeps one with inu o kau in the -teru form: uchi mo inu katteru n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daisuki! uchi mo inu katteru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大好き！うちも犬飼ってるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I love them! We've got a dog at home too.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, daisuki desu. uchi de mo inu o katte iru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、大好きです。うちでも犬を飼っているんです。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, I love them. We have a dog at home too.

questions.explanation: Keeping a pet is kau, which sounds just like kau 'buy'. Yuki uses it for the dog she's getting (raishuu kara, inu o kau n desu, line 4), and Satou-san for the dog he had years ago (inu o katte imashita, line 7). His nanika katta n desu ka? in line 3 is the other kau, 'buy', and the context keeps them apart. Having a pet is almost always in the -teru form: inu katteru. Inu o motte iru sounds like you own a dog the way you own a bag, and inu ga iru (there's a dog) also works. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Satou-san.

questions.english: Satou-san brings Yuki her parcel. What had happened to it?
questions.ja: ユキさんの荷物は、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんのにもつは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san no nimotsu wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki was out when it came last night, so the driver left it with Satou-san next door.
The driver took it to Satou-san's flat by mistake last night, so it never reached Yuki, though she'd waited in all day.
It was left outside Yuki's door last night, and Satou-san took it in so it wouldn't go missing.

questions.explanation: Line 1: kinou no yoru, yuki-san no nimotsu ga uchi ni todoita n desu yo. heya o machigaeta mitai de. Todoku means 'reach', and here the parcel reached the wrong flat. Line 2: Yuki waited in all day, but nimotsu ga todokanakute (it never reached her). Things sent to you todoku, the same verb as for letters and messages. Tsuku is for people and trains getting somewhere (eki ni tsuku), so nimotsu ga tsuita is less usual. A is wrong: Yuki was in, waiting all day (zutto matteta), and the driver got the flat wrong. C is wrong: it never got to Yuki's door. It was delivered straight to Satou-san's place (uchi ni todoita).

newWords.english: bed (inu no beddo = a dog bed)
cat (uchi no neko = my cat; Satou-san's is called Tama)

script.title: The same worry
script.setting: A quiet weekday evening at the café where Sora works part-time. Mai, a regular, has been sitting alone over her coffee looking down, so Sora comes over to her table.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: mai-san, genki nai ne. nanka nayami aru no?
lines.ja: マイさん、元気ないね。なんか悩みあるの？
lines.kana: まいさん、げんきないね。なんかなやみあるの？
lines.english: Mai, you look a bit down. Is something on your mind?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. sora-kun, ima ii? chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo.
lines.ja: うん。ソラくん、今いい？ちょっと相談があるんだけど。
lines.kana: うん。そらくん、いまいい？ちょっとそうだんがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Yeah. Sora, have you got a minute? I could use your advice on something.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii yo, ima hima da shi. boku de yokattara, soudan noru yo.
lines.ja: いいよ、今ひまだし。僕でよかったら、相談乗るよ。
lines.kana: いいよ、いまひまだし。ぼくでよかったら、そうだんのるよ。
lines.english: Sure, it's quiet right now anyway. If I can help, I'm all ears.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: arigatou. kondo no shuumatsu, yuki to kyanpu ni iku no.
lines.ja: ありがとう。今度の週末、ユキとキャンプに行くの。
lines.kana: ありがとう。こんどのしゅうまつ、ゆきときゃんぷにいくの。
lines.english: Thanks. Yuki and I are going camping this weekend.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: hee, ii ne. demo, tanoshimi ja nai no? honne itte ii yo.
lines.ja: へえ、いいね。でも、楽しみじゃないの？本音言っていいよ。
lines.kana: へえ、いいね。でも、たのしみじゃないの？ほんねいっていいよ。
lines.english: Oh, nice. But you're not looking forward to it? You can tell me how you really feel.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honne o iu to, anmari ikitakunai n da. soto de neru no, nigate de.
lines.ja: 本音を言うと、あんまり行きたくないんだ。外で寝るの、苦手で。
lines.kana: ほんねをいうと、あんまりいきたくないんだ。そとでねるの、にがてで。
lines.english: To be honest, I don't really want to go. I'm not great at sleeping outdoors.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sokka. sore, yuki-san ni itta?
lines.ja: そっか。それ、ユキさんに言った？
lines.kana: そっか。それ、ゆきさんにいった？
lines.english: I see. Have you told Yuki?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ienai yo. watashi ga mae ni, kyanpu tanoshisou tte itta kara, yuki ga keikaku tatete kureta no.
lines.ja: 言えないよ。私が前に、キャンプ楽しそうって言ったから、ユキが計画立ててくれたの。
lines.kana: いえないよ。わたしがまえに、きゃんぷたのしそうっていったから、ゆきがけいかくたててくれたの。
lines.english: I can't! I once said camping sounded fun, so Yuki went and planned it for me.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: demo, iwanai to, shuumatsu zutto soto de neru koto ni naru yo. honne, itte mitara?
lines.ja: でも、言わないと、週末ずっと外で寝ることになるよ。本音、言ってみたら？
lines.kana: でも、いわないと、しゅうまつずっとそとでねることになるよ。ほんね、いってみたら？
lines.english: But if you don't, you'll be sleeping outdoors all weekend. Why not tell her how you really feel?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou da yo ne. a, yuki kara renraku kita.
lines.ja: そうだよね。あ、ユキから連絡来た。
lines.kana: そうだよね。あ、ゆきかられんらくきた。
lines.english: You're right. Oh, a message from Yuki.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: nante?
lines.ja: なんて？
lines.kana: なんて？
lines.english: What does she say?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo. honne o iu to, kyanpu nigate na n da tte.
lines.ja: 「ちょっと相談があるんだけど。本音を言うと、キャンプ苦手なんだ」って。
lines.kana: 「ちょっとそうだんがあるんだけど。ほんねをいうと、きゃんぷにがてなんだ」って。
lines.english: "There's something I want to ask you about. To be honest, I'm not really into camping."

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, yuki-san mo onaji nayami ga atta n da!
lines.ja: え、ユキさんも同じ悩みがあったんだ！
lines.kana: え、ゆきさんもおなじなやみがあったんだ！
lines.english: What? So Yuki had the same worry!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. watashi ga ikitasou datta kara, keikaku tateta n da tte.
lines.ja: うん。私が行きたそうだったから、計画立てたんだって。
lines.kana: うん。わたしがいきたそうだったから、けいかくたてたんだって。
lines.english: Yeah. She says she only planned it because I looked like I wanted to go.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: nan da. jaa, mai-san mo yuki-san mo, ikitakunakatta n da.
lines.ja: なんだ。じゃあ、マイさんもユキさんも、行きたくなかったんだ。
lines.kana: なんだ。じゃあ、まいさんもゆきさんも、いきたくなかったんだ。
lines.english: Ha! So neither of you actually wanted to go.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou mitai. kyanpu wa chuushi ni narisou da kedo, kawari ni yuki to koko ni kuru ne.
lines.ja: そうみたい。キャンプは中止になりそうだけど、かわりにユキとここに来るね。
lines.kana: そうみたい。きゃんぷはちゅうしになりそうだけど、かわりにゆきとここにくるね。
lines.english: Looks like it. The camping trip's probably off, but I'll come here with Yuki instead.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii ne, matteru. mata nayami ga attara, itsudemo soudan ni noru yo.
lines.ja: いいね、待ってる。また悩みがあったら、いつでも相談に乗るよ。
lines.kana: いいね、まってる。またなやみがあったら、いつでもそうだんにのるよ。
lines.english: Great, I'll be here. And if anything's on your mind again, I'm always happy to listen.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: arigatou. sora-kun ni soudan ni notte moratte, yokatta.
lines.ja: ありがとう。ソラくんに相談に乗ってもらって、よかった。
lines.kana: ありがとう。そらくんにそうだんにのってもらって、よかった。
lines.english: Thanks, Sora. I'm really glad I talked it over with you.

questions.english: What happened with Mai's worry?
questions.ja: マイさんの悩みは、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんのなやみは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san no nayami wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai was afraid the camping trip would be called off, but Yuki's message says it's still on.
Mai didn't want to go camping but couldn't tell Yuki, then found out Yuki didn't want to go either.
Mai was looking forward to camping, but Yuki admitted she doesn't like it, so now Mai is disappointed.

questions.explanation: Line 6: Mai admits she doesn't really want to go (honne o iu to, anmari ikitakunai n da). Line 8: she can't tell Yuki, who planned the trip because Mai once said camping sounded fun. Lines 12-14: Yuki's message says she doesn't like camping either and only planned it because Mai seemed keen. Line 16: the trip will probably be called off (chuushi ni narisou), and they'll come to the café instead. A is wrong: Mai was dreading the trip, not afraid of losing it, and the message never says it's still on. C is wrong: Mai wasn't looking forward to it (line 6), and she ends up relieved, thanking Sora (line 18), not disappointed.

questions.english: After hearing Yuki's message, Sora says, "yuki-san mo onaji nayami ga atta n da!" What does he mean?
questions.ja: ソラくんは、何がわかりましたか？
questions.kana: そらくんは、なにがわかりましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-kun wa, nani ga wakarimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki had made other plans for the same weekend.
Yuki wants to ask Sora's advice too.
Yuki had been quietly worrying about the same thing as Mai.

questions.explanation: Line 13: nayami ga aru means having something on your mind, a problem you keep turning over, and onaji nayami is the same worry. Yuki didn't want to go camping either (line 12: honne o iu to, kyanpu nigate na n da) but kept it to herself because she thought Mai wanted to go (line 14). Sora uses the same phrase to ask what's wrong in line 1 (nanka nayami aru no?) and to offer help in line 17 (mata nayami ga attara). A mixes it up with having plans (yotei ga aru); nobody mentions other plans. B mixes it up with soudan ga aru: Yuki's message opens with chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo (line 12), but she's asking Mai, not Sora.

questions.english: How does Mai bring up her problem with Sora?
questions.ja: マイさんは、ソラくんに何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、そらくんになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, sora-kun ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: there's something I'd like your advice on
choices.romaji: chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo

choices.english: I'm happy to hear you out
give me some advice, please

questions.explanation: Line 2: Mai opens with "chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo", the everyday way to run something by a friend. The one with the problem has a soudan, and the sentence trails off on kedo so the friend can say go ahead. Yuki's message opens the same way in line 12. B is the friend's side: Sora answers with soudan noru yo in line 3, so from Mai it would mean she's offering to hear him out. C is 'give me advice' word for word. adobaisu kudasai sounds abrupt between friends, and asking someone to help you think something through is soudan, not adobaisu.

questions.english: Over dinner, your friend Kenta sighs and says, "saikin, shigoto de iroiro atte sa. chotto tsukarechatta." Offer to hear him out, using soudan ni noru.
questions.ja: 最近、仕事でいろいろあってさ。ちょっと疲れちゃった。
questions.kana: さいきん、しごとでいろいろあってさ。ちょっとつかれちゃった。
questions.romaji: saikin, shigoto de iroiro atte sa. chotto tsukarechatta.
questions.answer: Offer to listen with soudan ni noru, the way Sora does: watashi (or boku) de yokattara, soudan noru yo (if I can help, I'm all ears), or itsudemo soudan ni noru yo (I'm always here to talk).

modelAnswers.romaji: sou na n da. watashi de yokattara, soudan noru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: そうなんだ。私でよかったら、相談乗るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, really? If I can help, I'm all ears.

modelAnswers.romaji: taihen da ne. itsudemo soudan ni noru kara, nandemo itte ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 大変だね。いつでも相談に乗るから、何でも言ってね。
modelAnswers.english: That sounds rough. I'm always here to talk, so tell me anything.

questions.explanation: soudan ni noru is the friend's side. Sora offers it in line 3 (boku de yokattara, soudan noru yo) and line 17 (itsudemo soudan ni noru yo), and Mai thanks him for it in line 18 (soudan ni notte moratte, yokatta). It means hearing someone out and helping them think it through, so adobaisu suru (passing on tips) misses the point. Don't answer with soudan ga aru: that's the side with the problem, the way Mai and Yuki say it (lines 2 and 12). In casual speech the ni often drops (soudan noru yo).

questions.english: Yuki shows you a hat she's just bought: "atarashii boushi katta n da. dou? kawaii desho?" Honestly, you think it looks a bit odd. Tell her what you really think, using honne o iu.
questions.ja: 新しい帽子買ったんだ。どう？かわいいでしょ？
questions.kana: あたらしいぼうしかったんだ。どう？かわいいでしょ？
questions.romaji: atarashii boushi katta n da. dou? kawaii desho?
questions.answer: Open with honne o iu to (to be honest), the way Mai does, then say what you really think and soften it: chotto hen kamo (it might be a bit odd), or say you like her old one better.

modelAnswers.romaji: etto, honne o iu to, chotto hen kamo.
modelAnswers.ja: えっと、本音を言うと、ちょっと変かも。
modelAnswers.english: Um, to be honest, it looks a bit odd.

modelAnswers.romaji: honne o iu to, mae no boushi no hou ga suki kana.
modelAnswers.ja: 本音を言うと、前の帽子のほうが好きかな。
modelAnswers.english: Honestly? I think I like your old hat better.

questions.explanation: honne is what you really feel, behind the polite front (tatemae), and honne o iu to opens a frank admission. Mai uses it in line 6 (honne o iu to, anmari ikitakunai n da), and so does Yuki's message in line 12 (honne o iu to, kyanpu nigate na n da). Sora uses the other everyday form to invite it: honne itte ii yo (line 5) and honne, itte mitara? (line 9). Yuki's kawaii desho? is fishing for the polite answer, and that's why honne fits. shoujiki ni iu to also means 'to be honest', but it's just being frank, not dropping a polite front. Soften what comes next the way Mai does with anmari, using chotto, kamo or kana.

newWords.english: camping, a camping trip (kyanpu ni iku: go camping)

script.title: An hour to kill
script.setting: A weekday afternoon. Kenji hurt himself at football practice, so Okaasan left work early to take him to the local clinic. They've already waited a while when the receptionist says there's about another hour to go, and that they're free to wait outside.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, mada ichijikan mo kakaru no?
lines.ja: え、まだ一時間もかかるの？
lines.kana: え、まだいちじかんもかかるの？
lines.english: What? It's going to be another whole hour?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shouganai no yo. koko no sensei, hitori hitori chanto jikan kakete mite kureru kara.
lines.ja: しょうがないのよ。ここの先生、一人一人ちゃんと時間かけて診てくれるから。
lines.kana: しょうがないのよ。ここのせんせい、ひとりひとりちゃんとじかんかけてみてくれるから。
lines.english: It can't be helped. The doctor here takes his time and looks at every patient properly.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jikan kakesugi da yo. koko de ichijikan mo matsu no, muri.
lines.ja: 時間かけすぎだよ。ここで一時間も待つの、無理。
lines.kana: じかんかけすぎだよ。ここでいちじかんもまつの、むり。
lines.english: He takes way too long. No way am I waiting here a whole hour.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka.
lines.ja: じゃあ、前のカフェで時間潰そうか。
lines.kana: じゃあ、まえのかふぇでじかんつぶそうか。
lines.english: Then shall we kill time at the café across the road?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ii ne. nanika tabenagara jikan tsubusou.
lines.ja: いいね。何か食べながら時間潰そう。
lines.kana: いいね。なにかたべながらじかんつぶそう。
lines.english: Sounds good. Let's eat something while we kill time.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mou futatsume? kega shiteru noni, yoku taberu ne.
lines.ja: もう二つ目？怪我してるのに、よく食べるね。
lines.kana: もうふたつめ？けがしてるのに、よくたべるね。
lines.english: Your second one already? For someone who's hurt, you've got quite an appetite.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: datte hiru, chotto shika tabetenai n da mon. okaasan wa, shigoto daijoubu datta no?
lines.ja: だって昼、ちょっとしか食べてないんだもん。お母さんは、仕事大丈夫だったの？
lines.kana: だってひる、ちょっとしかたべてないんだもん。おかあさんは、しごとだいじょうぶだったの？
lines.english: Well, I hardly ate at lunch. Mum, was it OK to leave work?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: un. konshuu wa isogashii kedo, nantoka jikan tsukutta no.
lines.ja: うん。今週は忙しいけど、なんとか時間作ったの。
lines.kana: うん。こんしゅうはいそがしいけど、なんとかじかんつくったの。
lines.english: Yes. It's a busy week, but I managed to make time.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: itsumo shigoto bakkari de, kenji to yukkuri hanasu jikan, nakanaka torenai shi ne.
lines.ja: いつも仕事ばっかりで、ケンジとゆっくり話す時間、なかなか取れないしね。
lines.kana: いつもしごとばっかりで、けんじとゆっくりはなすじかん、なかなかとれないしね。
lines.english: I'm always working, and I hardly ever get the time to sit and talk with you.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sokka. nanka, jikan totte kurete arigatou.
lines.ja: そっか。なんか、時間取ってくれてありがとう。
lines.kana: そっか。なんか、じかんとってくれてありがとう。
lines.english: Oh. Um... thanks for making time for me.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: nani yo, kyuu ni. demo, ureshii wa.
lines.ja: 何よ、急に。でも、うれしいわ。
lines.kana: なによ、きゅうに。でも、うれしいわ。
lines.english: What's this, all of a sudden? But it makes me happy.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, demo honne iu to, kaeritai. nanka mou itakunai shi.
lines.ja: あ、でも本音言うと、帰りたい。なんかもう痛くないし。
lines.kana: あ、でもほんねいうと、かえりたい。なんかもういたくないし。
lines.english: Oh, but honestly? I want to go home. It sort of doesn't hurt any more.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dame. sekkaku jikan tsukutta n da kara, chanto sensei ni mite moratte kara kaeru no.
lines.ja: だめ。せっかく時間作ったんだから、ちゃんと先生に診てもらってから帰るの。
lines.kana: だめ。せっかくじかんつくったんだから、ちゃんとせんせいにみてもらってからかえるの。
lines.english: No. I went to the trouble of making time, so we're going home after the doctor's had a proper look.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, jaa raishuu mo kite tte iwaretara?
lines.ja: え、じゃあ来週も来てって言われたら？
lines.kana: え、じゃあらいしゅうもきてっていわれたら？
lines.english: What? Then what if he tells me to come back next week too?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: raishuu nara, mata jikan tsukureru kara daijoubu.
lines.ja: 来週なら、また時間作れるから大丈夫。
lines.kana: らいしゅうなら、またじかんつくれるからだいじょうぶ。
lines.english: Next week I can make time again, so that's fine.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jaa, mou hitotsu tabete, jikan tsubusou kana.
lines.ja: じゃあ、もう一つ食べて、時間潰そうかな。
lines.kana: じゃあ、もうひとつたべて、じかんつぶそうかな。
lines.english: OK, then maybe I'll kill some time with one more.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mada taberu no?
lines.ja: まだ食べるの？
lines.kana: まだたべるの？
lines.english: You're still eating?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. kondo wa jikan kakete, yukkuri taberu.
lines.ja: うん。今度は時間かけて、ゆっくり食べる。
lines.kana: うん。こんどはじかんかけて、ゆっくりたべる。
lines.english: Yep. This time I'll take my time and eat it slowly.

questions.english: What happens while Kenji and Okaasan wait to see the doctor?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Okaasan couldn't get away from work, so Kenji waited for the doctor on his own.
With an hour to wait, they killed time at a café. Kenji said it didn't hurt any more and wanted to go home, but Okaasan said he'd see the doctor first, since she'd made the time.
They gave up on the wait and went home, and Okaasan will make time to bring Kenji back next week.

questions.explanation: Line 1: there's still an hour to wait (mada ichijikan mo kakaru). In lines 4-5 they go to the café across the road to kill time. Line 8: Okaasan managed to make time in a busy week. In line 12 Kenji says it doesn't hurt any more and he wants to go home. In line 13 she says no: sekkaku jikan tsukutta n da kara, the doctor looks at it first. A is wrong: Okaasan is right there with him and says she made the time (line 8). C is wrong: she won't go home (line 13). Next week only comes up in case the doctor asks Kenji to come back (lines 14-15).

questions.english: Okaasan explains why the wait is so long. What does she say about the doctor?
questions.ja: お母さんは、先生について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、せんせいについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, sensei ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He spends a full hour with every patient.
He's always running late, so his patients end up waiting.
He takes his time and looks at each patient properly.

questions.explanation: Line 2: 'koko no sensei, hitori hitori chanto jikan kakete mite kureru kara'. Jikan o kakeru is choosing to put time into something, here each patient (hitori hitori), properly (chanto). Kenji grumbles jikan kakesugi da yo (line 3, he takes way too long), and at the end he'll eat his snack slowly: jikan kakete, yukkuri taberu (line 18). A mixes it up with line 1: the hour is how long the wait still takes, mada ichijikan mo kakaru, and kakaru is how long something takes. It isn't time per patient. B is wrong: nobody says he's late. The wait is long because he's thorough.

questions.english: Your manager Tanaka-san stayed after work to go through your presentation with you, even though his week is packed. When you're done, he says, "jaa, kyou wa kono gurai ni shimashou ka." Thank him for making time for you, using jikan o toru.
questions.ja: じゃあ、今日はこのぐらいにしましょうか。
questions.kana: じゃあ、きょうはこのぐらいにしましょうか。
questions.romaji: jaa, kyou wa kono gurai ni shimashou ka.
questions.answer: Thank him politely with jikan o toru: ojikan totte itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita (thank you for making time for me). To apologise for taking up his time, use the causative: ojikan torasete shimatte sumimasen.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai. kyou wa ojikan totte itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: はい。今日はお時間取っていただいて、ありがとうございました。
modelAnswers.english: Yes. Thank you for making time for me today.

modelAnswers.romaji: oisogashii tokoro, ojikan torasete shimatte sumimasen. arigatou gozaimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: お忙しいところ、お時間取らせてしまってすみません。ありがとうございました。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry to take up your time when you're so busy. Thank you.

questions.explanation: Kenji says it to Okaasan in line 10: nanka, jikan totte kurete arigatou. She has just said she hardly ever gets time to talk with him (line 9, nakanaka torenai). Jikan o toru is setting time aside, and it's the usual way to thank someone for theirs. With your manager, make it polite with o- and itadaite: ojikan totte itadaite. The apology uses the causative: ojikan torasete (making you take the time). English 'take' can mislead you, though: how long something takes is kakaru, as in mada ichijikan mo kakaru (line 1). Ojikan tsukutte itadaite would also work, if you want to stress that he squeezed you in.

questions.english: Kenta asks, "konshuu, issho ni nanika tabe ni ikanai?" Your week is packed, but next week looks better. Tell him you can make time next week.
questions.ja: 今週、一緒に何か食べに行かない？
questions.kana: こんしゅう、いっしょになにかたべにいかない？
questions.romaji: konshuu, issho ni nanika tabe ni ikanai?
questions.answer: Use jikan o tsukuru in the potential: raishuu nara jikan tsukureru yo (I can make time next week). Saying konshuu wa chotto isogashii kedo first softens the no.

modelAnswers.romaji: konshuu wa chotto isogashii kedo, raishuu nara jikan tsukureru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 今週はちょっと忙しいけど、来週なら時間作れるよ。
modelAnswers.english: This week's a bit busy, but I can make time next week.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, konshuu wa muri. raishuu nara, nantoka jikan tsukuru kara.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今週は無理。来週なら、なんとか時間作るから。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, this week's impossible. I'll find time next week somehow.

questions.explanation: Okaasan uses it three times: nantoka jikan tsukutta (line 8, she managed to make time in a busy week), sekkaku jikan tsukutta n da kara (line 13, I went to the trouble of making time) and raishuu nara, mata jikan tsukureru (line 15, I can make time again next week). 'Make time' really is tsukuru, and as in English it means squeezing time out of a full schedule. Jikan o toru (lines 9-10) is setting it aside. The potential, jikan tsukureru, is how you promise to fit someone in. With a friend, casual is right.

questions.english: There's another hour to wait. What did Okaasan suggest?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Shall we kill some time at the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka

choices.english: Shall we murder some time at the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan korosou ka

choices.english: Shall we put some time into the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan kakeyou ka

questions.explanation: Line 4: 'jaa, mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka'. Kenji answers nanika tabenagara jikan tsubusou (line 5), and later mou hitotsu tabete, jikan tsubusou kana (line 16). Killing time is tsubusu, 'squash': you squash the empty time flat. B is a word-for-word copy of 'kill time'. Korosu is for killing living things, so jikan o korosu sounds like a murder plot. C is wrong: jikan o kakeru is putting time into something on purpose, like the doctor with each patient (line 2). Here they just want to fill a wait.

script.title: The idea from the bath
script.setting: Monday afternoon at the office. On Friday, Tanaka-san asked Yuki for an idea for the next campaign, and he wants it today. Her coworker and friend Mai (Kimura-san at work) sits at the next desk.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: yuki-san, sengetsu no kyanpeen, kekka ga demashita yo. amari yokunakatta desu ne.
lines.ja: ユキさん、先月のキャンペーン、結果が出ましたよ。あまり良くなかったですね。
lines.kana: ゆきさん、せんげつのきゃんぺーん、けっかがでましたよ。あまりよくなかったですね。
lines.english: Yuki-san, last month's campaign results are in. I'm afraid they weren't very good.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. kondo koso, kekka o dashitai desu ne.
lines.ja: そうですか。今度こそ、結果を出したいですね。
lines.kana: そうですか。こんどこそ、けっかをだしたいですね。
lines.english: I see. This time I really want to get results.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kin'youbi ni tanonda aidea, kyoujuu ni onegai shimasu ne. ii aidea nara, sugu hanko o oshimasu kara.
lines.ja: 金曜日に頼んだアイデア、今日中にお願いしますね。いいアイデアなら、すぐハンコを押しますから。
lines.kana: きんようびにたのんだあいであ、きょうじゅうにおねがいしますね。いいあいであなら、すぐはんこをおしますから。
lines.english: The idea I asked you for on Friday: I'd like it by the end of today. If it's a good one, I'll put my stamp on it straight away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo. asa kara zutto atama tsukatteru noni, zenzen ii aidea ga ukabanai no.
lines.ja: マイ、ちょっと相談があるんだけど。朝からずっと頭使ってるのに、全然いいアイデアが浮かばないの。
lines.kana: まい、ちょっとそうだんがあるんだけど。あさからずっとあたまつかってるのに、ぜんぜんいいあいであがうかばないの。
lines.english: Mai, can I ask your advice? I've been racking my brains all morning, and I can't come up with a single good idea.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: atama tsukaisugi da yo. chotto yasundara?
lines.ja: 頭使いすぎだよ。ちょっと休んだら？
lines.kana: あたまつかいすぎだよ。ちょっとやすんだら？
lines.english: You're thinking too hard. Why not take a little break?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: datte, kinou ofuro de sugoku ii aidea ga ukanda noni, wasurechatta no.
lines.ja: だって、昨日お風呂ですごくいいアイデアが浮かんだのに、忘れちゃったの。
lines.kana: だって、きのうおふろですごくいいあいであがうかんだのに、わすれちゃったの。
lines.english: But last night in the bath, a really good idea came to me, and now I've forgotten it!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, memo toranakatta no? watashi wa, aidea ga ukandara, sugu memo o toru you ni shiteru yo.
lines.ja: え、メモ取らなかったの？私は、アイデアが浮かんだら、すぐメモを取るようにしてるよ。
lines.kana: え、めもとらなかったの？わたしは、あいであがうかんだら、すぐめもをとるようにしてるよ。
lines.english: What, you didn't write it down? Whenever an idea comes to me, I make a point of writing it down right away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ofuro de memo nanka toreru wake nai jan!
lines.ja: お風呂でメモなんか取れるわけないじゃん！
lines.kana: おふろでめもなんかとれるわけないじゃん！
lines.english: How am I supposed to take notes in the bath?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, chotto matte. kinou no yoru, ofuro no ato de denwa kureta yo ne?
lines.ja: あ、ちょっと待って。昨日の夜、お風呂のあとで電話くれたよね？
lines.kana: あ、ちょっとまって。きのうのよる、おふろのあとででんわくれたよね？
lines.english: Oh, hang on. Last night, you called me after your bath, didn't you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, sou datta? tsukaretete, zenzen oboetenai.
lines.ja: え、そうだった？疲れてて、全然覚えてない。
lines.kana: え、そうだった？つかれてて、ぜんぜんおぼえてない。
lines.english: Huh, did I? I was so tired, I don't remember at all.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sugoi aidea ukanda! tte itteta kara, ichiou memo totta no. hora.
lines.ja: 「すごいアイデア浮かんだ！」って言ってたから、一応メモ取ったの。ほら。
lines.kana: 「すごいあいであうかんだ！」っていってたから、いちおうめもとったの。ほら。
lines.english: You said, "I've had an amazing idea!" so I wrote it down, just in case. Look.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: etto, atarashii aji no namae o, okyakusan ni kimete morau kyanpeen. sou sou, kore!
lines.ja: えっと、新しい味の名前を、お客さんに決めてもらうキャンペーン。そうそう、これ！
lines.kana: えっと、あたらしいあじのなまえを、おきゃくさんにきめてもらうきゃんぺーん。そうそう、これ！
lines.english: Let's see: "A campaign where customers choose the name of the new flavour." Yes, yes, this is it!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kore nara, kitto tanaka-san mo hanko oshite kureru shi, kekka mo daseru yo.
lines.ja: これなら、きっと田中さんもハンコ押してくれるし、結果も出せるよ。
lines.kana: これなら、きっとたなかさんもはんこおしてくれるし、けっかもだせるよ。
lines.english: With this, I bet Tanaka-san will give it his stamp, and we'll get results too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tanaka-san, aidea motte kimashita!
lines.ja: 田中さん、アイデア持ってきました！
lines.kana: たなかさん、あいであもってきました！
lines.english: Tanaka-san, I've brought you my idea!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: omoshiroi desu ne, kore. jaa, hanko o oshimasu ne.
lines.ja: 面白いですね、これ。じゃあ、ハンコを押しますね。
lines.kana: おもしろいですね、これ。じゃあ、はんこをおしますね。
lines.english: This is interesting. All right, I'll put my stamp on it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu! jitsu wa, kimura-san ga memo o totte kureta n desu.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます！実は、木村さんがメモを取ってくれたんです。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます！じつは、きむらさんがめもをとってくれたんです。
lines.english: Thank you! Actually, Kimura-san wrote it down for me.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. futari de, kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne.
lines.ja: そうですか。二人で、今度こそ結果を出してくださいね。
lines.kana: そうですか。ふたりで、こんどこそけっかをだしてくださいね。
lines.english: I see. Then the two of you, make sure you get results this time.

questions.english: What happened with Yuki's campaign idea?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki couldn't come up with anything, so Mai gave Tanaka-san one of her own ideas, and he approved it.
Yuki forgot the idea she had in the bath, but Mai had written it down when Yuki phoned her, and Tanaka-san approved it.
Yuki remembered her bath idea after a short break, but Tanaka-san said it needed more work before he'd stamp it.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Tanaka-san wants Yuki's campaign idea by the end of the day. Line 6: a great idea came to Yuki in the bath last night, but she has forgotten it. Lines 9-11: she phoned Mai after her bath, and Mai wrote the idea down just in case. Line 15: Tanaka-san likes it and presses his hanko on it, which means he approves. A is wrong: the idea was Yuki's own. Mai only wrote it down, and Yuki tells Tanaka-san so (line 16). C is wrong: Yuki never remembers it by herself. She reads it in Mai's notes (line 12), and Tanaka-san approves it on the spot.

questions.english: At lunch, Mai hands you her phone with a game on it and says, "kore, saikin hamatteru geemu. yatte miru?" You play a round. Tell her it really makes you think.
questions.ja: これ、最近ハマってるゲーム。やってみる？
questions.kana: これ、さいきんはまってるげーむ。やってみる？
questions.romaji: kore, saikin hamatteru geemu. yatte miru?
questions.answer: Say the game makes you think with atama o tsukau, casually atama tsukau, with kekkou or metcha for 'really': kono geemu, kekkou atama tsukau ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: kono geemu, kekkou atama tsukau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: このゲーム、結構頭使うね。
modelAnswers.english: This game really makes you think.

modelAnswers.romaji: muzukashii! kore, metcha atama tsukau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 難しい！これ、めっちゃ頭使うね。
modelAnswers.english: It's hard! This really gets your brain working.

questions.explanation: Yuki has been racking her brains since the morning (line 4, asa kara zutto atama tsukatteru), and Mai tells her she's overdoing it (line 5, atama tsukaisugi da yo). A game or a job that makes you think is one that 'uses your head': atama o tsukau, in casual speech usually without o. Don't mix it up with atama ga ii (be clever), or with ki o tsukau, which means being considerate. With a friend, casual is right.

questions.english: At the end, Tanaka-san tells Yuki and Mai what he wants from them this time. What did he say?
questions.ja: 田中さんは最後に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんはさいごになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa saigo ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: This time, make sure you get results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne

choices.english: This time, please go and receive the results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o moratte kudasai ne

choices.english: This time, please take the results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o totte kudasai ne

questions.explanation: Line 17: 'futari de, kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne'. Yuki used it in line 2 (kondo koso, kekka o dashitai desu ne), and Mai in line 13 (kekka mo daseru yo). Results you achieve are something you put out yourself: kekka o dasu. In line 1 Tanaka-san used the other verb, kekka ga demashita. There the results came out by themselves, meaning they were announced. B is wrong: morau means being handed something, so kekka o morau only fits getting a results sheet. C is wrong: toru works in ten o toru (get a score) and memo o toru, but results aren't 'taken'. You deliver them with dasu.

questions.english: Tanaka-san comes to your desk and says, "raishuu no kaigi, jikan ga kawatta node, ima iimasu ne." Ask him to wait a moment while you write it down.
questions.ja: 来週の会議、時間が変わったので、今言いますね。
questions.kana: らいしゅうのかいぎ、じかんがかわったので、いまいいますね。
questions.romaji: raishuu no kaigi, jikan ga kawatta node, ima iimasu ne.
questions.answer: Ask him to wait while you take a note, with memo o toru in polite form: chotto matte kudasai, memo o torimasu. He's your manager, so stay polite.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, chotto matte kudasai. ima memo o torimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ちょっと待ってください。今メモを取ります。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, just a moment, please. I'll write it down.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, memo o torimasu node, chotto matte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、メモを取りますので、ちょっと待ってください。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, let me take a note. Just a moment, please.

questions.explanation: Mai makes a point of noting ideas down the moment they come (line 7, sugu memo o toru you ni shiteru), and she wrote Yuki's idea down during the call (line 11, ichiou memo totta). Yuki tells Tanaka-san that Kimura-san took it down for her (line 16, memo o totte kureta). As in English, you 'take' notes: memo o toru. Memo suru means the same and is just as common. A note you leave for someone is memo o nokosu. With your manager, use torimasu and matte kudasai.

questions.english: Mai says everyone wants to get Tanaka-san something for his birthday, and asks you, "nee, nani ga ii to omou?" You've thought about it, but nothing comes to mind. Tell her.
questions.ja: 田中さんの誕生日、みんなで何かあげようって。ねえ、何がいいと思う？
questions.kana: たなかさんのたんじょうび、みんなでなにかあげようって。ねえ、なにがいいとおもう？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san no tanjoubi, minna de nanika ageyou tte. nee, nani ga ii to omou?
questions.answer: Say no good idea comes to mind with aidea ga ukabu in the negative: zenzen ii aidea ukabanai. With Mai, casual is right.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, zenzen ii aidea ukabanai.
modelAnswers.ja: うーん、全然いいアイデア浮かばない。
modelAnswers.english: Hmm, I can't come up with any good ideas at all.

modelAnswers.romaji: nan darou. mada ii aidea ga ukabanai n da yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 何だろう。まだいいアイデアが浮かばないんだよね。
modelAnswers.english: Good question. No good idea has come to me yet.

questions.explanation: Yuki complains that no good idea comes to her (line 4, zenzen ii aidea ga ukabanai), though a great one came to her in the bath (line 6, ukanda). Ideas float up into your mind on their own, so the idea is the subject with ga: aidea ga ukabu, and casual speech often drops the ga. It is mostly heard in the negative, like this. Ukabu reports an idea coming, or not coming, to mind, as in sugoi aidea ukanda! (line 11). To offer an idea, 'I've got an idea!', people say ii kangae ga aru! or omoitsuita! With Mai, casual is right.

questions.english: Yuki brings her idea to Tanaka-san. What did he do?
questions.ja: 田中さんは、ユキさんのアイデアをどうしましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんは、ゆきさんのあいであをどうしましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa, yuki-san no aidea o dou shimashita ka?

choices.english: He asked Yuki to put her own seal on it first, before he read it.
He gave it a fun 'good job' stamp, like a teacher, but hasn't decided yet.
He approved it: his seal on the plan means it can go ahead.

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'omoshiroi desu ne, kore. jaa, hanko o oshimasu ne.' In a Japanese office a manager approves a plan by pressing his personal seal (hanko) on it, so this means 'yes, go ahead'. He promised it in line 3 (ii aidea nara, sugu hanko o oshimasu kara), and Mai predicted it in line 13. A is wrong: nobody asks Yuki for her own seal. B is wrong: a fun rubber stamp, like a teacher's 'well done', is a sutanpu. A hanko is a personal seal, and you press it: hanko o osu.

script.title: Just a yawn
script.setting: A Saturday night outside a concert hall. Yuki has loved a singer for ten years and has just seen her live for the first time. Her old friend Kenta came along on her spare ticket, though he'd said he didn't know any of the songs.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, sugokatta! saigo no uta, torihada tatta!
lines.ja: ああ、すごかった！最後の歌、鳥肌立った！
lines.kana: ああ、すごかった！さいごのうた、とりはだたった！
lines.english: Wow, that was amazing! The last song gave me goosebumps!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: wakaru. hora, boku mo mada torihada tatteru.
lines.ja: わかる。ほら、僕もまだ鳥肌立ってる。
lines.kana: わかる。ほら、ぼくもまだとりはだたってる。
lines.english: I know. Look, I've still got goosebumps too.
